metadata.school_name: The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

analysis.name: Anne Rea
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 130 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Maybe it's just me, but I felt as though the exams weren't testing what we knew on the subject; rather, it felt like she was just trying to trick us with lengthy word questions. Extremely condescending in personal emails. Also no cheat sheet for the test when other teachers do allow it. Take Biol 103, just not with her...

Hasn't graded most of our written assignments and our third midterm yet and it's almost LDOC. There are very few resources to study for this course. The lecture slides barely have any written notes, and the exams are heavily based on them. I wish there wasn't a character limit because I still have more to say about how horrible this class was.

Wish I could cuss. Terrible and overly nuanced; you are expected to devote to her class like a cult if you even dream of doing well. The exams are a toss-up; the mean is always low, and the questions are unrelated to the lessons we are told to pay attention to. The 5 star review is 100% from the few people Rea is actually nice to. Condescending af

She seems sweet and considerate but she really isn't. Her timing is always off, we were consistently about 10 days behind, and she often posted assignments late with very little time to finish them. She assigned four tasks over Thanksgiving break and regularly makes assignments due on wellness days or days off. Overall, not the best Bio professor.

Focuses too much on irrelevant details during the lecture. Behind schedule since FDOC. Lessons skipped or moved asynchronously to "be caught up" (we never caught up). ALWAYS last minute. Unit quizzes due less than 24 hours before the exam. Has assignments due AFTER LDOC. Modules and assignments are not posted in a timely manner.

analysis.name: Fenaba Addo
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class was extremely repetitive with the same content in every single module. Prof. Addo does NOT know how to lecture in any way shape or form. She needs to take a workshop on lecturing. The class itself was boring, tests were fine, just study the review that she posts. Application based. Our assignments were easy 100's. I skipped class a lot.

I found her class frustrating. She is condescending and fails to answer questions beyond the content of her lecture slides. The content is manageable, but lectures are poorly organized. My biggest issue with her class was the volume of tests. A policy innovation and analysis course should focus on research and writing, not multiple choice exams.

She is clearly smart but such a bad lecturer. She gets confused by her own slides, mostly just reads off them anyway, and struggles to answer student questions. She also weirdly giggles so much and it makes me so angry. Exams weren't too hard though and out of class assignments were easy 100s

I feel that some of the negative reviews of Prof. Addo are exaggerated. She is one of the most caring and supportive professors I've had at UNC. She truly wants her students to succeed, is approachable outside of class, and takes the time to explain material when you're confused. If you put in the effort, she will absolutely meet you halfway.

Professor Addo cares a lot and is knowledgable but her lectures were verbatim off the slides. She was not great at answering student questions in lecture either. 4 exams throughout the semester which was a lot but if you study the guide she gives then you should do well on them. Easy class and interesting content but unhelpful lectures.

analysis.name: Arthur Eddy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His teaching style was often disorganized and course expectations/grading criteria weren't communicated clearly. Assignments required a significant amount of work, sometimes without sufficient guidance or clarification. Lots of guest speakers. Overall, the instructor did not seem very flexible or understanding when students raised concerns.

Prof Eddy was great, very accessible, and helpful with questions. There is no rubric for any assignments, which made it sometimes difficult to understand feedback and grades. The class is boring because its a prereq, but Prof Eddy did provide good advice about the real world and had educational guest lectures.

I learned a great deal in Prof Eddy's class. He cared for all his students. There is a ton of group project which makes class fun. There were a few guest speakers from different industries that added to the class. I highly recommend his class.

I don't go here, because I'm in high school, but this guy is my godfather and I would like to mention that. He's pretty good at being a godfather, I think, but please don't let him wear suits. Otherwise someone might mistake him for Jeff Bezos and that would be bad.

This class was a bit different from my other classes, but in a good way. His class is combo of lectures, group projects and guests to speak to the class along with the main project. I learned a lot from his class.

analysis.name: Amanda Fowler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: ENGL 148. Good lecturer and engagement, can tell she has a passion for the literature. There is in class canvas discussions at the beginning that is used for participation and assume she used this in place of a student not actively speaking in class. Did this class more for fun and to retouch on reading outside main major.

For a basic Gen Ed class, it was a lot of projects and work. You have to make a podcast and create a Wiki entry. You have to watch hours of instruction just to understand how to use the software needed. I spent tons of effort on this class. It seemed like she just gave everything a 90. She was a nice teacher, it definitely could have been worse.

Professor Fowler is the most compassionate and caring professor you will ever have. Prioritizes student well-being over everything and will work with students no matter their situation. It's hard to lose your A in this class as long as you complete your feeder assignments and give good effort on your unit projects. Couldn't recommend them more.

Professor Fowler was very inconsistent with grading assignments (providing feedback), and often cancelled class last minute (or was very late). In their defense they had a lot of personal issues going on this semester, so I can't speak for their teaching under normal circumstances, but overall I learned little to nothing from this class.

Instructor Fowler was a very nice person, just not a great instructor. They would be late to many meetings and these meetings felt unprepared. However, they were very accommodating when it came to due dates and attendance. I felt my tuition was wasted, but if you want an easy class, this is the way go.

analysis.name: Jon Abramowitz
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Abramowitz was always funny during lectures. Always willing to help. You're graded on 2 midterms, a final, and a few case studies (group assignment). No grade cushioning, but exams are pretty straightforward, mostly factual and not application based. Attendance is not graded but you have to come to class since he puts very little on his slides.

The best prof I've had so far. His class is 75% exams and 25% final essay, I was hesitant about that but the tests are extremely easy if you go to class and listen. He doesn't post full lectures so attendance is a must. Super nice guy and I really enjoyed his class even though I hate psych.

Super chill professor. Nice, friendly, easily accessible. Willing to give feedback. Good lectures. Expects participation (part of your grade). Interesting lectures. Would definitely take this professor again.

Seriously the best prof I've ever taken at UNC. He's very passionate about the material and his tests reflect the lectures well. The only "complaint" I have is that he doesn't post his full ppts online, so you have to go to class to get all the info. 75% of the grade is tests & 25% final essay, so take that for what you will. 10/10 would take again

TAKE THIS CLASS: super interesting and great lectures. Some topics were more interesting than others but Abramowitz always made them enjoyable. He is a really cool guy and great teacher. The grade is based on 3 exams and 2 papers. The exams are fair if you take good notes. You can't miss any class though because he doesn't post the full slideshows.

analysis.name: Matthew Andrews
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 201 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Matt Andrews is a great person, and the lectures were interesting. However, for this class 67% of your grade is based on papers, and if you get a bad TA, as I did, you are SCREWED. I would not recommend taking a class with him if you can not pass fail it since this year he made his class significantly more difficult without the grading contract.

Best Professor OAT. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you still find yourself looking forward to his classes and actually wanting to go. Lectures are incredibly interesting and well-delivered, and it's very easy to get an A. Knew nothing about Baseball going it, and now I'm an expert on both the game's history and wider American history. 10/10 class.

One of the best classes I have had at UNC. Basketball being my favorite sport made me very excited to go to lectures, and we got to pick our grade as long as we completed the essays and attended recitation. Lots of reading if you want to understand the lectures better, but overall a very fun class for gen ed credit.

Everyone loves Prof. Andrews. I finally took one of his classes and it's easy to see why. The lectures are actually super interesting- it's like sitting down and listening to sports trivia, but then you realize you're learning history too. Graded by 7 online quizzes, 2 papers, and a final. Easy A, and super enjoyable class.

Just brilliant. Best Professor at UNC by a mile, and the content of this course makes it even better. Great lectures, easy enough assignments, just a great guy. One of the few professors that you want to listen to for 3 hours a week, and would also want to grab a beer with. What a man, what a class.

analysis.name: Antonio Rodriguez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tony is great! Lectures were engaging, good amount of info on slides but not too much. Exams were mostly vocab-based with some application questions. Homeworks were easy and the TA helped out a ton! A good amount of reading, but he goes over the important stuff in classes so attendance is a good idea. Great class and great material

Tony is an extremely nice and genuine guy and I could have done much better if I would have paid more attention and studied harder. Grading is only on two midterms, a final, and weekly homeworks but the homework is a small chunk. Found the lectures very, very information heavy and hard to pay attention to and exams hard to study for.

Textbook chapters are incredibly long and you likely won't have time to read all of them. Two midterms, a final, and homeworks are the grades in this class, and if you stumble once it's over because you need a 95 to get an A. Tony's a nice guy and the material isn't complex, but I wouldn't recommend for just a focus capacity.

Super enthusiastic about marine science. Presentations are pretty good, although not always great for individual review. Homeworks are weekly but don't take up much time each week. He can be a little disorganized, but nothing bad.

Tony is one of the sweetest human beings alive. He genuinely cares about each one of his students. I was not super interested in sed strat at first, but his excitement and teaching made me enjoy the class way more than I thought I would. I wish he taught more classes b/c I would 100% take another class with him.

analysis.name: Aubrey Snowden
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 105 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Snowden is great! Made the class really fun and entertaining. Definitely need to enjoy theatre to some extent to take this class. Sometimes lectures weren't the most entertaining, but it was fun getting to read the plays and dissect them afterwards. A lot of group work was involved. Overall a good class, great for a focus capacity.

In class Professor Snowden often seems unprepared (she doesn't create the PowerPoints she teaches from) and can be hard to work with. She based our 10% participation grade off of a few pop quizzes that most people did poorly on. Members for the group project are randomly assigned, so you there's a good chance you'll get stuck with a horrible group.
For a drama teacher, her presentational skills are lacking. No stage presence, its almost as if shes acting like a teacher, and acting poorly.

The lectures are not relevant to the midterm or final exam at all. Snowden doesn't make the powerpoints herself and doesn't seem to know what she's lecturing. The exams were straight from quizlet but also random. The one project is assigned into random groups and you are graded as a group. No curves. Don't take this class.

Class was alright, some of the plays we had to see in person were somewhat interesting but overall not too fun of a class. You could tell Snowden felt that her students didn't seem to care too much about her class and she combatted this with 8 mandatory attendance checks which were annoying.

analysis.name: Alex Foster
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr Foster is great! Super funny and charismatic, makes lectures entertaining. Goes really fast and is sometimes hard to follow. The class content is difficult but Dr Foster does a great job of preparing you for exams. Homework was unreasonably hard and couldn't do any of it without outside help. Still a good experience and great professor.

Dr. Foster is the kindest teacher! He gives out candy at review sessions and helps students as much as he can. He gives very helpful study guides for everything. The tests are very difficult, but if you study with the study guides, you will be ok. The lectures are hard to keep up with, but he is very funny. If you take this class, take it with him!

I LOVE ALEX FOSTER! He is such an amazing professor and all around guy. He teaches very well and while attendance isn't mandatory, you'll definitely miss a lot if you don't go. He's a fast talker and writer, but will slow down when asked. His midterms are very fair, but do get harder as the course goes on. He is very approachable and understanding.

To preface, I'm not the strongest math student and Prof. Foster's lectures were quite stale but you you tell he's an enthusiastic individual and passionate about math. He didn't use guided notes and would often introduce a new topic and then run through examples on the chalkboard until the end of class so don't make it a habit to miss class.

Very understanding guy, though the class does get progressively more difficult. The Edfinity homework can be very difficult and gets annoying when it's due in the middle of breaks, but does help you grasp the content. Does every lecture on the chalkboards which makes it a lot easier to learn, though sometimes methods other than his are simpler.

analysis.name: Todd Austell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 351 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Todd is the type that believes you don't have other work outside of his class. Of course you need to invest time into chem classes to do well (everyone knows that), but the time he expects you to put in isn't reasonable for anyone that is taking more than 12 hours. Love yourself and take someone else. P.s. he writes his own reviews, so watch out...

The tests are extremely difficult, and the reviews for them aren't given with a key. He asks students to "compare answers" on a forum instead of giving a key to the exams.. He's a caring professor, but his class had to have been the most difficult class I've ever taken at UNC. The final was 1/3 multiple choice with a whole section of short answer.

Todd does care about studentS; however, he doesn't care about YOU- a student. He likes to be liked by all, but is short and narcissistic when it's one-on-one. He also expects WAY MORE than a student can do in a semester and still be successful in other classes, but he doesn't care. Many useless book problems. Final was my highest grade. LOW avgs.
Well definitely a cool guy, he certainly doesn't care about the success of his students. Would not recommend taking his class.

Makes Orgo much harder than it needs to be. Controlling with note taking format, syllabus contains no scheduled list of daily activities, assignments on Mastering Chemistry are put up irregularly, making them harder to get done by the deadlines. Sometimes writes his own positive reviews on here, so beware. Not as good as he makes himself out to be.

analysis.name: Beatriz Lomas-Lozano
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is perhaps the most understanding human being known to mankind. I showed up for my interview not having realized there were sample questions on canvas, and she let me do the interview on Friday. I didn't even ask! In a world full of hate she is a shining beacon of understanding.

I thought the class was good for it being online. Obviously learning another language is challenging, but the instructor was VERY kind/open to questions and not a harsh grader at all. Assignments were a little annoying at times, but overall were very helpful for the final, which was not bad at all if you applied yourself

Those who have never taken Spanish before don't take this class or this teacher. She reads the slides and never actually teaches and the worst of all, she will only speak in Spanish never english. Half the time she doesn't even teach just tells us to read the textbook which doesn't help at all. Don't even get me started about conversating with her.

Professor Lomas is very kind and accommodating. However, the class setup isn't great even for those with prior knowledge. You'll have to teach yourself all the information, most of which isn't reviewed in class but is still on the exam.

She is very kind and approachable. If you keep up with homework and attend class, you'll do well. Midterms and exams are fair with preparation. Oral interviews and video assignments are manageable. Chapter quizzes in the Alcanza textbook are strict and don't allow retakes, so double-check answers.

analysis.name: George Baroud
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Baroud seems really intense at first but honestly he is one of the most inspirational and passionate professors I've had. I took CLAS122 for the focus capacities and loved it so much I ended up taking 241 too. Classes are action packed and I always left feeling I learned something. Readings are manageable and exams are fine.

CLAS241*. He does NOT give you the full time to take written exams. Also, it seems he wants students to give 120%, but in terms of being helpful and accommodating for students, it feels he only gives 70%. if he likes you, yay! if he doesn't, go ahead and drop.

Prof. Baroud is easily one of my favorite professors. His class was immensely difficult (300 pages of dry, dense reading each week; could not bullshit your way through exams), but his grading was fair and he forces you to grow as a thinker/reader. He's scary (and maybe a bit snarky) at first, but he is super approachable in office hours.

Don't take this class if you want to sit by, skip the readings, and hope you'll get a good grade. Professor Baroud is an amazing professor, extremely intelligent, and loves the Roman Empire. Highly recommend going to office hours, as he wants to know every student personally. If you are willing to go a little crazy, then this is the class for you.

Quite literally the most engaging and thought provoking lectures I've ever heard. He's an incredibly knowledgable and charismatic professor. Main downside of the class are the reading assignments, almost too lengthy to handle. If you show up to all the lectures, do the readings, and ask questions, you'll do well. I wish I could take CLAS122 again.

analysis.name: Tonya Balan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Balan is very fair and she makes class super welcoming for beginners to Python and Stats. Attendance is mandatory but counted only on days where there's classwork, so many skip if they know the material. Two exams which are super easy and similar to study guides. Lab session about once every 2 weeks where you work on a very simple group project.

Professor Balan was awesome. There are 2 quizzes and a final group video project. A couple things do get a little technical with some code and using the correct formulas, but if you study, you will be fine. Attendance is optional but she brought several guest speakers who were interesting to hear, so I'd suggest going. Very good experience.

Super chill and knowledgable professor. Final project was fun and just enough of a challenge. Gemini makes all labs and homework a cakewalk. Quizzes are clearly laid out beforehand with ample review material. Incredibly easy class and material is taught if you actually want to learn it. Take if you need a stats credit but don't want to learn stats.

Dr. Balan is good at making things make sense, especially if you have no expereince in computer/data science. Her class is very easy but it is just her lecturing, labs on friday are when you  get to actually interact with class material and the people in your class. Final is a group project, but watch out for quiz 2 it is harder than quiz 1.

Dr. Balan is very kind and a great professor. She makes all assignments very easy and clear. Had some guest lectures in the course which was very interesting too! As I already took other data/comp courses, it was a bit boring at times, but otherwise good content! I would definitely love to take more courses with her in the future! 5/5!

analysis.name: Burç Köstem
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I'm in one of the first classes Doctor Burç has given, and a very he's kind and engaging professor. His class is very reading-heavy with few assignments, and class discussion is suggested but not required. Lectures are interesting (if you enjoy learning about objects with cultural significance) and reading heavy.

Class has pop reading quizzes that count towards grade (10%) for accuracy. They are not hard (mult-choice), but can be tricky. Each midterm is 25% and open note. Note that second midterm is on LDOC... You are given prompts and write two short essays. It's very manageable. Final paper is 40%. He grades fairly, but he can tell if you are bs-ing him.

Burç is actually the kindest professor I have ever had. He's super passionate about what he's doing. Expect about 2-3 dense readings per week but can get away with not doing them especially if you ask questions in class. Grades were made up of two essay exams, annotations, and a finals essay.

The course code is listed wrong, it is supposed to be 412 not 312. The prof is chill and readings are mostly interesting. You're graded by three in class essays, weekly annotations plus a final project.
Really thoughtful and caring. The readings can be dense, but lectures make things clearer. Grading is fair and not a ton of busywork. If you actually show up and engage, you'll learn a lot.

analysis.name: Navin Bapat
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 109 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Navin knows what he is talking about, but you can tell how great he thinks he is by the way he speaks- with a smirk on his face. The class was fairly easy, but lectures are pointless and Bapat doesn't say anything of substance- he just poses questions and doesn't answer them and half his slides are common sense things that don't need to be there.

Lecture is completely optional, 2 midterms are take home, 2 essays, and a take home final. Because of this, the class is not hard, but I recomend going to class and taking pretty good notes, especially when you know you are going to do the essay of that week (every week there is an essay and you do 2 of them).

The way he grades his papers makes absolutely no sense. He gives you a prompt and a specific outline of how he wants the paper written, but when you follow those exact instructions he still gives you a low grade and doesn't clarify why you got that grade... the papers are 60% of overall grade in the class, making it hard to recover from the papers

This class was meh. Attendance wasn't mandatory except for recitation--and the grading felt artificial. The midterms and the final weren't difficult at all, just make sure you include stuff you learned from recitation and in class in your answers. The papers were okay, again, not hard if you include info from class. Overall not my fav poli class.

best poli sci professor. he speaks so clearly and eloquently. he truly is passionate about his work. attendance not mandatory but i made sure to go to class just to hear him speak. exams are online 10q and essay, 2 papers graded by TA. he lays everything out clearly so it is easy to do well. i HIGHLY recommend. hope i can take another class w him.

analysis.name: Carribeth Bliem
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 316 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bliem is such a sweet lady and is passionate about her work. However, the online format made this class pretty difficult. The course is entirely self-taught; you must watch a lecture and complete a warm-up, pre-class quiz, and in-class activities every time before class. I would have definitely done better had this class been in person.

Chem 101 is going to be a tough class no matter what. Bliem is one of the better chem profs imo and actually cares about you succeeding and understanding. Lectures can be boring and monotone, but I actually enjoyed them and thought she was really funny. Exams will be harder than you expect, be sure to study everything before and after class.

Gen chem is going to be hard, no matter who you take it with because the exams are made by the department. But Professor Bliem is by far the best in the department for gen chem. 102 is over 200 people, yet she will answer every single question, answer every email, and encourage you personally throughout the course if you talk to her.Take chem w her

CHEM at UNC is very difficult; however, Bliem knows her stuff and is very kind. Her lectures are very helpful for exams. I've had a year of gen chem with her, and my experience has been fine. Definitely a lot of work, but the professor for gen chem has little bearing on your grade. Just go to Chem Possible and use other outside learning materials.

Professor Bliem is very kind and funny. Chem isn't an easy subject but she is really approachable and supportive of students. I think she does a good job of explaining concepts, and I honestly enjoyed going to lectures. Bottom line for UNC intro chem is you going to have to put in the work, but there's also support systems out there.

analysis.name: Benjamin Musachio
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I could genuinely listen to Professor Musachio talk for hours. He is knowledgeable and I found his lectures effective at conveying important connections. I found it amusing that he maintains a mysterious air around his background. This was a seminar, so readings and participation were most important, but he also gave several writing assignments.

I really enjoyed Professor Musachio's class. I initially chose the class because I thought it would be easy but it was a lot of reading and required a lot of participation (speaking up in class). However, even as a stem major, it was more enjoyable than I thought. Musachio is so passionate and you can see it in his lectures. Would recommend

Professor Musachio is an excellent teacher. He's pretty traditional in his teaching methods, but makes every lecture fun and interesting. His class has A LOT of reading but it can be pretty interesting and its all important things to know. The discussions are based on the readings and he has a few quizzes, a midterm paper, and the final.

There was a lot of readings to do outside of class, which weren't always enjoyable to parse, and were mostly philosophical. However, if you enjoy reading, want to improve your critical thinking, and like big class discussions (which could sometimes get off topic), then this is a really good class to take.

Professor Musachio is overall an extremely caring and passionate professor, and very knowledgeable about many different realms of literature. The class itself wasn't too difficult, although there was a fair amount of reading. Would definitely recommend if you are interested in American literature and/or political science.

analysis.name: Vicki Chanon
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 93 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I would love to say this is an awful class to get off her waitlists lol, but Dr. Chanon is an amazing professor. She's incredibly kind and personable and learns everyone's name, and her lectures are fun to attend. This class was mainly group project focused with that taking the place of the final, which I really enjoyed. 20/10 reccomend Dr. Chanon.

I lOVE Dr. Chanon. The material in the class was somewhat hard to understand at first but I always understood it after she lectured on it. As long as you read most of the assigned textbook readings and pay attention, this class is super interesting and easy to do well in.

I love Vicki down! Super kind and cracked me up all semester. She learns everyone's names and her in-class participation is engaging and solidifies concepts. Exams are pretty straightforward, 2 homework drops, and quizzes that you can take until you get a 100. You can also miss 6 classes which is nice. Very easy class and an excellent prof.

One of my favorite professors I've had at UNC! Her lectures are very engaging including fun activities to understand the content. Her exams are very straightforward and she also offers a few extra credit opportunities. Also, one exam is dropped, and you can take the quizzes as many times as you want. I genuinely enjoyed going to her class :)

I absolutely adore Dr. Chanon! She's hilarious and gets to know every student in her class (and our lecture was definitely more than 50 people)! She's really great about posting slideshows and recordings! Number one tip is to fill out the outlines for learning checks! The lowest learning check is dropped! Homeworks are pretty easy too!

analysis.name: Thomas Chandler
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is extremely smart, but kind of goes beyond the course material to explain what can be done in further math classes (which is great for math majors, just not my thing). 2 midterms and a final, final can replace the lowest midterm. A bunch of homework sheets that are way harder than the exam questions. Super nice guy with plenty of office hours.

Chandler's a super well-organized prof with amazing lectures, and the content isn't too hard. He's definitely passionate about the class and wants everyone to learn/pass. Homeworks and practice exams aren't too difficult and prepare you well for exams. Strongly recommend taking 383 with him, it'd be a mistake not to. Also take linear algebra first!

Best math class I've ever taken! Classes are extremely structured to really make you understand the concepts, beyond just knowing the right equations/methods. Very smart guy, but explains it clearly. Office hours are extremely helpful. Weekly homeworks and midterms are only 4 questions, very similar to the practice. Definitely take him if you can!

Super engaging professor. I would only recommend you take him if you are a math major. He dives very deep into theory and as a non-math major myself I found it hard to follow. Exams are just four questions and the second one is a lot harder than the first. Very application based as well, which I enjoyed.

British, lively, and efficient at explaining concepts and clearing up confusion. He shares his lecture notes, and practice sets mirror his brief, straightforward exams. Graded by weekly HW, two midterms, and a HARD non-cumulative final that replaces your lowest midterm.

analysis.name: Mauricio Cabrera
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The GOAT. Pretty funny guy, and tries to make lectures as engaging as possible. You will definitely succeed as long as you put some effort into this class. I would definitely take him again. Tests weren't that hard too and he really goes out of his way to make sure you get the concepts. 10/10

Some of my classmates weren't big fans of Prof Cabrera -- but I liked him! While a little unorganized/inconsistent, Prof Cabrera clearly cared about his students and was a good and understanding grader. He has a great personality and elicits very interesting class discussions.

This class wasn't too bad. He cares about his students and tries his best to implement practices that help students in areas they are struggling. If you do the work and study for test you will be fine.

Great guy and really kind. The only class this semester that I actually looked forward to going to. You can tell he really cares about his students, and he always brought a chill energy to class which was really nice. Explained Spanish in a simple way which was easy for me to understand :)

As someone who hadn't taken Spanish in years but was placed into 203, Cabrera was a great professor who truly cares about the success of his students and was very lenient. He was super chill and we had fun in his class, so definitely try to take a class with him, if available.

analysis.name: Christopher Shepard
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Shepard is passionate about chemistry, and he is very kind. However, his lecture style does NOT help you better understand the material. He will start class by talking about his dogs, and we are always behind in lecture. We typically talk about material from a day or two before. You'd be better off taking 101 with another professor.

Chemistry at UNC is extremely challenging, but Shepard finds a way to make it better. He is very kind and helpful in explaining difficult topics. I will say that we often get behind in lectures, but I didn't have too much of a problem with it since you'll have everything in time for exam day. Loved him and his dogs!

Chem 101 is notoriously difficult but standardized, so it has nothing to do with the professor. Dr. Shepard is super kind and always encourages class participation. He's a great teacher and seems like he genuinely cares about students and ULs. Love hearing his dog stories and analogies!
Only went to his GPSS sessions and he's great. Doesn't make you feel bad for not understanding the content

analysis.name: Christopher Roark
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 135 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The only people who liked this class are the ones who do not care about their grades. I actually had a stroke trying to understand all the contradictory points in the materials.

Overall lectures are confusing, problem sets only minimally help solidify concepts taught in lectures, and his responses to questions on campuswire are often vague. Chill guy but not great at helping to understand material which is already difficult. Takes up time trying to be funny at least once every lecture but speeds through difficult concepts.

I learned from this class by rewatching his lectures. His lectures and homework are full of mistakes. It's the kind of mistake that confuse students. He also said the wrong things in class multiple times. For example, "Demand curve moves leftward...I mean rightward." MULTIPLE TIMES. It was a very frustrating experience.

I like this better than 420, and he's genuinely a really nice guy which makes it a lot better. It isn't super easy content, but my complaint is really just that he makes the homework sometimes unnecessarily hard. One question will be completely fine, easy even, and then the next has math so convoluted that a TI-84 can't process it. Just annoying.

Professor Roark is great! I've had him for both 420 & 425. He is generous with curves, accessible, and provides PLENTY of test prep. There are weekly assignments, but he will sometimes extend deadlines. Had an injury I was out for a month for, so he met with me via zoom to keep up. Hard content, but if you do hw will do fine. Take with Roark!

analysis.name: Carol Magee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class wasn't graded super hard and she's really nice. But unless you are really interested in the very niche topics, it's hard to feign interest in all semester and there are definitely more useful electives. Super small class so you must be engaged and present at all times, and she grades participation harshly.

Fall 2025 ARTH 453. Manageable class. Lectures were a bit redundant and was usually confused on what was being taught. Deeply appreciate Prof. Magee's drive in this class though. Grading can be a bit harsh

This was a really unique interdisciplinary class that combined art history with Feldenkrais movement lessons. Sometimes it was hard to make the link between the readings and lessons, but overall fascinating. She is definitely a tough grader—the more "meta" and detailed you can get with your analysis the better.

Dr. Magee is an expert in her field and her class was rather enjoyable, however her grading scheme is rather unforgiving and many of the grades seem arbitrary. Expectations are laid out clearly but she seemingly doesn't give out grades >95.

Graded things very last minute, didn't know my grade until the end of semester and it was sent to connect Carolina. Many times her rubric is very unclear and she takes off points for no reason very very tough grader. Participation counted a lot and needed and projects. Don't recommend this class to anyone!

analysis.name: Julia Cardwell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Good and passionate prof. Attendance is random but you could expect it'll be taken at least once a week. Lots of classwork and projects, and lectures can be super boring, but the class is really easy. You don't design maps until the final month of the semester, and for this all you do is follow her guide and watch videos on how to use GIS software.

Dr.Cardwell is great. You do HAVE to show up to class. Pop quizzes for attendance. She never makes you do the group projects at home only in class, so you have to be there. The assignments are not difficult. If you go to class and do the assignments, you will get an A. Also if you don't get a good grade on the assignments, she lets you redo it.

GEOG 370 is a hard class, and Dr. Cardwell's grading system is kind of weird. Once you understand it, though, it is pretty straightforward. If you don't understand something, Dr. Cardwell and TAs are always available outside of class and able to explain stuff in more depth.

Amazing professor, very open to feedback from students, which makes up for some disorganization. Very accessible in and outside of class, and open to helping you troubleshoot. Class consisted of a test, some labs and a final project, manageable as long as you dedicate some effort.

Dr. Cardwell is fair, clear, and engaging. I saw the world differently after her class, and I enjoyed the combination of thoughtful instruction, collaboration with others, and patience from Dr. Cardwell. I'd highly recommend her class and hope I can take another.

analysis.name: Joshua Beaver
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 303 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Allows you to drop your lowest test grade but if your overall test average is still a 50 or below, you're screwed.

An easy class is not representative of easy material, the same way a hard class is not representative of difficult material. It's clear from these reviews that despite challenging material, everyone is putting in real effort to work through it. The frustration comes from how that material is poorly translated to tests and quizzes. :(

Like poetry, this class continues to degrade any hope of redemption to the very end. I've never had a final at UNC that has felt designed to take the ENTIRE 3 hours, in a similar way to the past quizzes, just longer. A passing grade would be a blessing. They say they want us to succeed, but kick us while we're down.

So far, Dr. Beaver has been a decent professor. CHEM 101 is not an easy class but he's very energetic and wants everyone to succeed. He usually explains everything clearly and also gives you time to process and understand the chemistry problems that are done in class. As long as you continue to study consistently and do the HW you should be fine.

Verily, this course is no mere pursuit, but an odyssey of torment where only the steadfast glimpse enlightenment. The lecturer bestows knowledge in fire and fury, yet we, mere mortals, are left scorched, grasping at fleeting truths. My soul writhes beneath this incantation of madness! And yet, is not true wisdom born from suffering?

analysis.name: Katie Deaven
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class has readings, an essay, and presentation projects. Katie clearly cares about making the class interesting and informative. Grading is quite fair but the class still requires work and office hours are helpful. A lot of the work for the class comes later in the semester, so be prepared for the workload at the end.

Participation heavy. Readings are due each class, they tend to get a little long. Deadlines shift around often which may seem good at first glance, but it does get frustrating if you have a job and are calling out for important dates (presentations and such). Set up meetings in advance because office hours fill up!

I really enjoyed her teaching honestly, very enjoyable and the way that she would make the content was engaging. I would say that there was a lot of reading at times even though she tried to get the readings as short as possible. She's very engaged and passionate about the material and wants us to do the best we can in the class.

You can tell she's very passionate about what she teaches and only wants you to succeed. If you put in the work and listen in class then you'll be fine. I will say that it is homework heavy, so a good amount of readings that can be quite difficult to understand.

This is for 102 but there wasn't an option. Katie is very kind, accessible, and fun in class. Heavy emphasis on classroom discussion and participation. Easy to get B+/A-, not an easy A due to lots of reading and high expectations for understanding. I really loved this class and feel like I learned a lot about philosophy and good communication!

analysis.name: Florence Dore
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Extremely intelligent and makes interesting connections from our readings. Class discussions were engaging. Some people got by without reading the books, but I'd recommend doing them. I'm a slow reader, and some of audiobooks were 15 hours, so keeping up was hard with quick turnarounds. Need to take quality annotations, books are used in exams

Dore really is intelligent, but I often find myself leaving class dissatisfied. For every text, and every subsequent assignment, I feel Dore enters with an air about her own opinion. Her readings are always categorically "correct," and when students deviate they are met with a bad grade. I understand why some like her though, she's just not for me.

I took this class because Professor Dore spoke to my class the previous semester, and I found her to be an inspiring and engaging lecturer. The class was difficult but so rewarding, and as everything came together towards the end of the semester, I became convinced she is a genius. I highly recommend taking one of her classes and hope to again.

Sorry, but Prof Dore and this class was awful. I didn't think she was always respectful to students, and the exam she gave was SO hard. I think the average was a low C. The book she taught was hard (coming from an ENGL major). Graded harshly with a very vague rubric. By the grace of God, I got an A but it was looking like a B- for a long time.

Unless you're passionate about the South, useless class. Dore had us read "The Sound and the Fury." Don't read the book last minute, and make good annotations in the book. Buy it, don't rent. Essay grading was a bit harsh, but you'll be fine if you know the book. Other readings don't matter. She can appear condescending and cold calls.

analysis.name: David Hatcher
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is AMAZING!!!! Truly cares about his students, which you don't find much of here!!! 3 take-home assignments, which are easy A's, and he leaves you an optional question to check in with him on each one- genuinely so nice. Please take this class, David Hatcher is awesome!!!!!!!!!!!

Professor Hatch is amazing. He has no exams and very little readings/homework. Still, I learned a ton. His experience working for Duke Energy made his lectures especially interesting. He broke down big concepts in a great way, allowing me to understand concepts that I otherwise definitely wouldn't. Love him! Great guy, great teacher.

Professor Hatcher is the most caring professor you will find and wants you to come to him with questions and will always accommodate your needs. His class is mostly lectures which are sometimes hard to follow as there is not a clear outline of what the class is about. However there is very little work but a few group projects (graded fairly easy).

Highly recommend! Very easy course. Dr. Hatcher cares about his students and wants them to do well. Overall, I am not someone who cares about energy, but I learned a lot. He assigned 4 take-home assignments and 4 group projects + presentations. He definitely goes on tangents in his lectures, but participation matters in this class and was an easy A

Professor Hatcher is probably the most caring professor at UNC. Sweetest dude and really cares about what he is teaching. He is very accessible and is always willing to help! Highly recommend if you want an easy A and to have a professor who is willing to help you; classes are also very interesting.

analysis.name: Daniel Ringel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: final project is impossible and way harder than anything we're taught in the class. he's a nice guy but final project is brutal

Prof. Ringel's class was a really good intro to AI and DS in the business context. A lot of it was just high level code that was hard to understand, and we struggled a lot on our group projects. The quizzes and final were fair, but if you end up with a bad group then good luck! The CS students always carry the group, so be prepared to work if uk CS

This class is driven by group projects. What you find is that one or two people lead the entire group, often time those who care to code, while the others coast off their lead. This class is unnecessarily extra, and for a class that applies data science in the real world, i can say with experience the real world is anything then the class projects.

Daniel's COMP488 is the most popular undergrad COMP class at UNC, with 600 students sign up during pre-registration period but only 60 seats. He's knowledgeable and taught a wide range of data science techniques. He also has high expectations on the students. I still went back to his Python notebooks to solve intern tasks after the course ended

This class was really interesting. Dr. Ringel is a really cool guy with interesting lectures & life experiences. However, the group projects in this class were brutal if your team doesnt care (which mine didnt and theyre random teams) & when I brought this up to Ringel, he brushed it off. So I did all the work and everyone else took the credit.

analysis.name: Colin Wallace
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 201 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Wallace is such a beautiful light in the physics department. I can tell her really loved trains as a kid. And planets. He has a zest for physics that no one else on earth has. He lectures beautifully and in another life was a game show host. His exams are fair and he truly wants you to succeed.

Dr. Wallace is very passionate about his field, and he makes his lectures engaging. The class content is also very easy; if you have even a little bit of experience in anything STEM-related, you will do well in this class. The homework assigned is busy work but is definitely manageable. Attendance is required and can affect your grade.

There was a lot of material and a lot of graded things to keep up with outside of class like warm ups, homework, and lecture tutorials. Attendance is graded and exams were harder than anticipated just because of how much material there is. Be prepared to memorize lots of concepts, but you can tell Prof. Wallace loves what he does.

This class is so much more holistic than just aliens! Learning about atmospheres, rocks, using formulas. You'll enjoy this class if you want to a little bit of physics, chemistry, biology, math, geology, etc. Sometimes I didn't feel that his lectures prepared me for the work, but overall, he was an enjoyable, engaging professor.
I received a good grade in Collin's 115 class. My experience was filled with frustration. Wallace contributed to instruction disparities, and the way he handled student concerns was unprofessional.

analysis.name: Tyree Daye
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely loved taking this class. I learned so much about poetry. He genuinely cares about each student and wants to hear what everyone has to say. He does make you read aloud a lot, so it's kind of scary if you have social anxiety. The final was a poetry group video project, and it was fun to make.

Professor Daye is such an amazing person, and he truly cares for his students. He tried to be intimidating in the first class, but he is actually a teddy bear and someone who is knowledgeable in his criteria. Absolutely loved the workshops and I would love to take another class from him!

Professor Daye is such a kind and hilarious person. At the beginning of the semester I was nervous because he comes off slightly intimidating, but he really just wants everyone to participate. He's a lenient grader and the workload is manageable (50ish pages of poetry reading each week, one 4-5 page paper w/ presentation, and a final project)

THE ABSOLUTE BEST! This was the one class that I actually looked forward to during my week. Prof Daye is truly a caring individual that wants the best for his students and he actually checks in on his students during class. As long as you try your best and participate, grades shouldn't be a concern for you.

engl105 with prof daye was sooo easy. he just wants u to come to class & participate, & he likes talking to us about stuff other than english. sometimes hes vague about what he expects for assignments but they were all super duper easy & were not graded harshly at all!

analysis.name: Travis Day
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 87 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Day is by far one of the best professors I've ever had at UNC. He's a very enthusiastic professor and loves teaching this class, and cares a lot about his students.The final is tough, but as long as you have a good understanding of the notes provided and do any practice quizzes or redo assignments, you will be okay.

Final is weighed 50% of your grade and you cannot check your answers. Content is very useful but directions are often convoluted. 1-2 hrs of async that tbh could be 15 mins if edited down. Lots of overlap between lecture and async so its kinda boring. Grading is always quick and feedback is great. Useful and necessary class but needs some revision.

You complete assignments based on lectures recorded during COVID. It feels more like a formatting course with little real instruction rather than a high-level modeling course. There was little relevance for banking or high-level finance roles. Overall, gets you more comfortable with Excel, but a certification would have done the same.

Professor Day runs a very well structured and formatted class. His notes files are very helpful, and he is very receptive to helping you out in class. The work is a lot and is challenging at times, but if you manage your time you will be ok. I learned a ton about Excel and recommend taking this class.

Note that the final is 50% of your grade.

Professor Day is an exceptional teacher. While the material was quite dense, his methodical approach to teaching made it easy to digest the information. 

In response to the comments about the final being heavily weighted, as long as you are diligent in completing the assignments, there should be no reason for you to not do well on the exam.

analysis.name: Donovan Livingston
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I LOVE Professor Livingston!! The best guy, both inside and outside the classroom. I don't think you can choose who you get for college thriving, but if you get him, thank your lucky stars—the nicest, most caring guy ever who truly wants you to succeed. I genuinely feel better about myself every time I leave that class.

He is very kind and you can tell he loves his jobs and students. Grading criteria was unclear at some points so points would be deducted by surprised. He was not the most accessible by email, but you shouldn't need to contact him if you submit assignments and go to class.
Not MUSC 89, but MUSC 150 Intro to Hip Hop is the best class I've taken at UNC. So chill but I have learned a lot from the class. He's great and I would highly recommend you take it for FC-AESTH

Dr. Livingston is one of if not the best professor I will ever have. He is truly a great guy and is super caring for everyone that he teaches. He will talk with you after class about topics that you are interested in and genuinely wants to help in any way he can.

Dr. Livingston is the most down to earth, kind hearted, selfless professor there is. He was my first ever professor and genuinely the best one I think I will have. Very clear grading scale, a lot of emphasis on growth, and very understanding of situations students have outside the classroom.

analysis.name: Danielle James
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. James is approachable and kind and gives good lectures. She's open to all perspectives and brings a sense of humor to class. She helped me improve as a writer. The reading load is completely manageable (~25 pages a class).

Professor James is incredibly kind. I honestly learned more than I expected in. I earned an A but this required an EXTREME amount of hours and effort. I would compare this 100 level class to a 300 level course at UNC. Feedback on midterm is only available via office hours and is largely based on the “vibe” of your writing rather than a rubric.

THE HARDEST A I'VE EVER HAD. I'm a dual stem major and this was way too much for a 100-lvl class. I really enjoyed the format and lectures but the workload/grading are par with my 400-lvl core classes. I did every reading (10hrs/wk) and studied 20hrs per exam, and BARELY managed to scrape up an A. Rating isn't lower bc problem is the class not her.

Would not recommend at all. The professor is very kind and actually gives decent lectures. However, this is essentially an AP Gov/US history class with nonexistent grading criteria. Her midterm and paper grades are completely arbitrary with no clear explanation as to why she took off points. Otherwise known as "the vague B." Would avoid if possible

This NEW 100-level entry course only has 4 grades in the class: 2 papers, a midterm, and a final. There are no assignments, activities, slides, or lecture notes. Read 5-6 readings before each class. Her extremely harsh grading is only acceptable for a higher-level required class for SCLL students. I don't recommend this class at all.

analysis.name: JD Defreese
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Really nice prof. The lectures are really boring, but he really knows his stuff. Exams are trickier than you would think. I pulled out a B on the first one after starting studying the night before. There's a big group project and you're randomly assigned to groups, so as long as everyone does stuff you will be ok. Offers extra credit.

DeFreese's voice is the most monotone, boring voice ever. The content in this class is organized a little bit oddly and could be done better. It is just about a bunch of different theories you need to memorize. This class is one of worst classes I've taken at unc. Also, there is a big group project that is so busy work.

One of the worst classes I've taken at UNC. Probably the most boring professor. Focuses too much on useless group work when the room isn't even set up to work in groups. Makes the tests extra hard for no reason. This class is the reason I'm dropping the EXSS major

JD is a really good professor. He's very understanding and responds quickly to emails. He also grades really quickly. Our exam grades were released the afternoon after we took the test. Class can be challenging and instructions aren't always the clearest for the big group project. Exams are fair but not the easiest.

lots of busy work and the lectures are hard to follow, exams are hard for no reason. attendance is graded heavily and the group project that goes across the whole semester is unorganized and not easy to follow.

analysis.name: Dana Riger
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is so awesome and so interesting, especially if you want to go into therapy or counseling, or care about family dynamics in general. You do have to do the readings, however, they are generally not that bad. The grading is pretty fair, but the essays and faciliataion do take a lot of time. And there is a learning reflection every week.

One of my favorite professors I have taken a class with. She is not only so funny and caring, but so knowledgable. It is impossible to not be fully absorbed in her lectures because she makes everything so engaging. The exams are straightforward and are not meant to trick you. I studied from the exam reviews and study guide, and did well.

I definitely recommend taking EDUC 181 with Dr. Riger. Attendance is mandatory, but she is very accommodating if you email her beforehand. Her lectures are very interesting and engaging. The only reason I gave her a 4 instead of a 5 is because I think sometimes the class spent too much time "reviewing" than going deeper into content.

I cannot recommend Dana as a professor enough! Lectures were in-depth and engaging, and the content itself was fascinating. There were three exams total, and she gave study guides for all of them. Dana is caring and considerate, and easy to get a hold of. If you're thinking of taking a class with her, absolutely take it!

EDUC 181 was one of my favorite courses. Attendance is mandatory and class was mostly composed of lectures, but Dana's a great professor and definitely prepares you for exams (she's also hilarious). There's a good amount of homework, but grading is pretty lenient and there's lots of extra credit opportunities.

analysis.name: Eleonora Magomedova
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: An amazing teacher who genuinely cares about her students. She will always take the time to meet with you outside of class if you need help, and she is a very lenient grader. The exams are not very difficult and if you ask for extra credit she will always give you something to do.

Russian Department Legend. She is super sweet, caring, and funny. Participation is a must, and her lectures are engaging. She simply wants all of her students to learn the Russian language. All the resources are available, and she provides excellent feedback. As long as you show up, participate, and do your work, you'll succeed.

Truly my favorite professor I've had at UNC, will do anything and everything to help you succeed in her class. She's so funny and makes me really look forward to coming to her class and I literally structured my entire schedule next semester so I can take 204 with her

She's great at making the class engaging and really cares about each person's success. She will call you if you're falling behind/haven't been in class. A lot less talking in class than McGarry's class and harder to get an A. Still lots of small group work in class. Very funny
Simply the GOAT of the Russian department at UNC. The best lecturer there is, with a nice sense of humor. She is joyful and passionate about what she teaches.

analysis.name: Elad Sherf
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Elad is a cheerful teacher, and the class is fairly enjoyable, but he crams WAY too much work into one weekend and gives you absolutely no feedback. Also wish the activities were a bit more creative since it's a creativity class (maybe a real-life Shark Tank as a team assignment). Overall, it was nice, but causes a ton of burnout and lacks support.

Nice person, but assigned an infeasible amount of work and relies on a group project format that simply doesn't work the majority of the time. Also is constantly interrupting his own students. Do not take this weekend class, and this is coming from someone who's taken almost all of the KF weekend classes.

Great weekend class. Interesting lectures and enjoyable activities made the weekend fly by. Fair amount of material to read in preparation for each day, but not unbearable by any means. If you need a weekend class, take this one

Elad is a good person and is engaging in class, but the amount of work he expects to be completed in such a short time is crazy. His grading criteria is extremely tough, he grades on tiers and for large assignments he will not give anyone higher than a 90.

Took creative thinking over the weekend. He's super engaging and makes the day go by faster. Only complaint is that the class is more like 9-9 than 9-5, but the grind is worth it and the material is fun. Worth it.

analysis.name: Elisa Pieri
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Pieri clearly has no interest in teaching and her class reflects that. Your grade is 100% exams. She doesn't provide resources. No learning objectives, no class schedule, no practice problems, she doesn't post her notes, her lectures are objectively boring, she has difficulty explaining topics, and she often makes mistakes in her lectures.

Pieri lectured verbatim from the Atkins textbook, so if you read before class, you'll be fine. Problem was she didn't give us reading assignments or have a schedule for what she'd be lecturing on, so I had to guess. Lectures were not engaging at all. No class curve, but no homework & she dropped the lowest midterm. Office hours were very helpful.

Do not take her, grade is 100% exams. Gives no practice problems except 1 practice midterm which is different than the content on the exam. Just derives equations from the textbook. Doesn't explain anything well.

Dr. Pieri was very nice and will make you tea/coffee in 1-on-1 office hours. She tried relating the material to real world implications which was cool due to how abstract thermo usually is. Her classes are 100% lectures and derivations from the textbook, so we didn't really get to do much problem-solving which I would've preferred. Exams are fair.
Learned PChem and how to make pasta. 5 stars, would recommend

analysis.name: Evyatar Marienberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class was a lot of work, but its very easy. Takes a lot of time but all grades are easy As. If you put a little effort into studying, the tests (1 midterm 1 final, both writing) are pretty easy. Would reccomend only taking this class if you are genuinely interested in the topic, as you'll be learning a lot about it and spending a lot of time on it.

(Fall 2025) Loved this class. Marienberg can be a bit of a character (in a good way!). Absolutely hilarious guy, great stories, and still gets you immersed in the content. Grading was very easy: mostly completion-based, and what wasn't was fine if you skimmed the reading and paid attention. Loved the course and professor. Will take him again.

Not sure why the ratings are so low, I had a great experience with Professor Marienberg. He's very understanding and his lectures were very engaging. There is often a good amount of reading per week and a discussion post or quiz for every class. The midterm and final were relatively easy as long as you studied the concepts and reading material.

Nice man, though he was difficult to reach. Class content consists of readings and discussion posts due every class which, if done well, will take multiple hours each. The lectures are basically a recap of these. Exams contain very specific knowledge, but if you actually do the readings (and not just put them in ChatGBT), they're very manageable.

Dr. Evyatar has a wealth of knowledge and shares it enthusiastically. He's honestly a funny guy and shows videos in class, along with bringing in prayer shawls. Classwork is easy, you just write a discussion post before each class based on the readings.

analysis.name: Nita Eskew
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I've had bad experiences with gen chem at UNC, but having taken CHEM 261 and CHEM 262 w/ Dr. Eskew, she made orgo not as bad as everyone made it seem. She offered us all the resources to succeed, and having attended her office hours, she is very accommodating and always willing to help. If I had to take orgo again, I would do it again w/ Dr. Eskew

Best CHEM prof at UNC!!! She is very caring and has a sense of humor. She is also very kind and explains everything clearly and patiently, like your grandma. The 2nd exam was difficult but I know it wasn't written by her. Her exams were the easiest orgo exams I've taken! Take her orgo she's the best!

Prof Eskew was supposed to teach my class all semester, but randomly took off for the first month. I had Prof Zurcher, and she was amazing. Then Eskew came back and my grade tanked. She's just such a boring lecturer, and she doesn't explain anything. When people ask questions, she doesn;t actually answer them and just moves on.

Dr. Eskew was very kind and approachable, often making an effort to connect with students in class despite it being a large lecture. Her slides were well put together, and she explained things clearly. Exams are tough, but that is to be expected from orgo. Just do the homework and practice problems, and you should be fine. Best orgo professor!

Dr. Eskew cares about teaching the content and walks around the class from time to time to answer questions. Exams are difficult but fair, with very few curve balls (Looking at those energy diagram questions). Overall, a great teacher, and I highly recommend her for orgo. Watch Chad's Prep 2x speed before the lecture for an A.

analysis.name: Eric Youngstrom
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The title of this class was very misleading. Rather than doing archival research, we used pre-existing small datasets to learn the basics of the programming language R. Most of the lecture was given over to personal stories, and the rest was on basic coding.
Great professor! Highly recommended for any psyc majors. Especially individuals considering graduate school

Incredible professor. Had the absolute pleasure of having him as my Developmental Psychopathology prof at KU and he was honestly out of this world. Super kind to students, fair exams, engaging lectures, and gives lots of insight into the research world of psychology. Would leap at the opportunity to work with him again if i ever got the chance.

Dr. Y told us this would be taught like a graduate-level class, but definitely not. Very lecture-heavy. However, Dr. Y is a great lecturer! He's an incredibly funny professor (lots of in-class demonstrations of concepts) & is always available to answer questions. Did a great job transitioning to online. Bonus: Two quiz grades replaced by the final.

Dr. Y is AMAZING! He is the best professor I have had at UNC. He really cares about his students and you to succeed. It is possible to get an A if you work hard and show you are putting effort into the class.  I would highly recommend taking this class. His lectures are entertaining and he has you apply what you've learned to cases from his clinic.

analysis.name: Dorothy Espelage
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING PROFESSOR! Being in Dorothy's class was incredible. She would tell many funny stories and is relatable, especially because she knows what students go through while in college. If you're lucky enough, she'll bring her dog George to class some days! Easy class in general, reading quizzes and midterm + final paper. TAKE THIS CLASS WHILE AT UNC

She's a great and lenient professor! Loves to talk, easy A. Weekly journal (one page). 1-2 question quizzes, usually true or false, with 2 attempts. Very low stakes class. One group presentation. She's very funny, does random activities for the classes like yoga, rock painting.

Overall, amazing amazing professor. I also engaged with her class and cares about what she is doing. Nothing too hard in her class, just a final campaign/presentation, but it's in a group and very fun to do. Dorothy is hilarious and would always enjoy being in her class.
Easiest class you will take at UNC. Easy ahh workload. Take this class

She is AMAZING! The class is not challenging, and the content is honestly so interesting. 2 simple exams as long as you pay attention in class. One group project and one final paper. Dr. Espelage is super passionate and one of the most hilarious people you will ever meet. I highly recommend taking any class offered by her!

analysis.name: Juan Carlos Gonzalez Espitia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had Juan Carlos for SPAN 363, disease in hispanic lit. He is indisputably the goat. Good amount of readings and 2 weekly forum posts + journaling, but readings are reasonable + very interesting. Class discussion is the core of this class so you must come prepared. The discussions are fantastic though, JC is an amazing lecturer. Take this class!

Juan Carlos is by far one of the best professors that I've had at UNC. I had him for SPAN 260 and SPAN 373. Although he uses old Spanish texts, he makes them very relatable to current events on campus/in our personal lives. He also isn't afraid to talk about sensitive topics. Furthermore, he encourages participation in Spanish which is helpful.

I can't speak for semester classes, but I took him over the summer and he had daily reading quizzes that were worth 40% of the final grade, which seemed a little absurd (one screw-up and your grade is in serious jeopardy). Takes off points needlessly sometimes on assignments, but he's also very passionate and lively, and a cool person.

Juan Carlos has been my favorite Spanish professor at UNC so far! He is very clearly passionate about the subject matter and leads engaging discussions. His energy is unmatched and I looked forward to every class! He creates an environment where it is easy to participate and contribute to the discussion, even if your Spanish isn't always correct.

I loved JC! He cared so much about the material and subject matter and the class was super fun. I also appreciated how he was not a strict grader and cared more about the content of responses on homework as opposed to proper grammar.

analysis.name: Tim Flood
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The irony of a Communications professor with unclear communication is hard to ignore. Guidelines were confusing, course materials were confusing, and feedback was minimal — and again, confusing — leaving you no real way to improve. He proudly claimed to be a tough grader. I left more confused than I entered. Would not recommend.

I don't understand his criteria for giving students a certain grade. His assignment instructions are never clear, and going to office hours doesn't help you out. It's perplexing how a student is expected to succeed without clear instruction. The way he grades is incredibly harsh. You can bank on this class lowering your GPA.

If you can take any course at the business school, make sure it is not with Tim Flood. He is the most arbitrary grade I have ever encountered. This is a group consensus. While he presents the assignments as manageable, he grades with little feedback and a lack of standardization. Save yourself.
Genuinely struggled to understand what was expected throughout this entire course. Materials were unclear, and the grading felt disconnected from any clear rubric. Get another professor for 401.

analysis.name: Sandra  Martinez Franco
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Martinez Franco is such a sweetie and clearly loves her students. She does grade somewhat harshly (I'm always getting A-s and never As :C ) and you have either a quiz or in-class essay to write every week, but she doesn't assign homework so it cancels out. Attendance is mandatory, but class is easy to go to.
