This is the hardest class I've ever taken. Dr Franco is a very nice person. But she only speaks in Spanish. This makes it extremely difficult to understand what is going on in class. Also isn't helpful for understanding the material when confused or lost. It was her first year at UNC, so Ill give her some slack. But I wouldn't do that again.

I was very intimidated by taking Spanish 203 in college as everyone was advising me to take Spanish online through community college instead, but Professor Martinez Franco is so kind, patient, and makes everything easy to understand. I feel like I learned more from her class than from five semesters of Spanish in high school.

Such a nice and caring professor. She really wants everyone to do well in the course and generally grades pretty easy. I am horrible at spanish and still passed 203 with B+ which was mostly due to sandra being my teacher. Great professor would highly recommend after hearing how hard spanish can be at UNC.

Ive heard nightmares about Spanish at UNC but Profe Martinez-franco was super sweet and did the best she could to make the content as understandable as possible. It's important to remember that for most of the stuff, she doesn't control what she has to assign us, it's the department.

analysis.name: Na Fan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Fan Laoshi grades harshly, but she is fair, kind, and has a great sense of humor. You will get at least a B as long as you put in the effort. I had about 2-4 hrs of homework every week, and an hour of studying. Don't take this class if you aren't conversational in Chinese. Hit the anki flashcards for every vocab quiz, and you will be fine.

fan laoshi and this class can be intimidating at first (esp if you can't speak fluently/read/write at all like me) but my improvement has been insane. she is very funny and understanding. lots of hw and vocab words to learn in a short amount of time, but if you put the work in you'll be fine. 2 oral presentations (generous grading imo)

she is understanding but there is so. much. work. like we would learn 50+ words in one class and have the vocab quiz the next. her rubrics can be a little vague so don't be afraid to ask because she is pretty lenient on some project deadlines and explains things well. fan laoshi also encourages group discussions so be open to that!

Fan Laoshi is a great instructor for Chinese 111. She explains concepts clearly and is very patient when answering questions. She encourages group discussions, which makes the class more engaging and helps with speaking practice. Overall, I learned a lot and would definitely recommend her.

Fan Laoshi is so invested in seeing each one of her students succeed and learn. She is very accommodating and understanding and gives amazing feedback to help you improve. She also pushes her students to do better!

analysis.name: Fan Yao
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor is very supportive and approachable. He is easy to reach outside class, office hours are helpful, and he patiently clarifies any questions.The course is challenging, but he makes it manageable. Homework is flexible and helps learning, and midterm grading is lenient.Overall, a great instructor and you will learn a lot. Highly recommend

Had for STOR 565. Homeworks can be challenging and are assigned monthly  but graded very lenient. Tests much easier than homework and also graded lenient. Decent lecturer but very inaccessible outside of class.
Took him for 323 and 565, free A.

analysis.name: Helene De Fays
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I learned a ton in this class, improving both my grasp of history and the Spanish language. I found the workload reasonable, and the final group project was really creative and actually fun. De Fays was kind and a super interesting lecturer as well; she's very well versed in the subject matter. I would highly recommend this class!

De Fays is very nice but can seem a bit intimidating at first. Classes involve a lot of participation and group work, but is very helpful to improve Spanish. Midterms and final are difficult, but doable if you study. Challenging class, but would recommend De Fays.

Profe De Fays is so kind, funny, and caring. She explains concepts pretty well, and she also makes class sort of conversational, which makes it easier to learn (though my class did have 7 people). There is a decent amount of online homework, but it's not awful. The final research paper could had more instruction, but she wanted us to succeed.

I took Spanish 101 last semester, and, while being very likeable, it seemed like she was impatient/uninterested with teaching us beginners new material. She covered subjects too fast and did not seem sympathetic to beginner problems. She was very funny and pleasant to be in class with, though, and i ended with a B+ in the class.

She is nice but didn't really seem to care about us. After I went to her with a personal issue and asked for some leniency with missing a few classes due to a family medical issue, she seemed understanding and said that since I let her know it was an "excused absence" but then gave me a low participation grade.

analysis.name: Jade Fostvedt
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of, if not the best professor I've had in college. I learned a ton in this class and had fun doing so. This course was also not overly-demanding at all and I enjoyed it even though synthetic chemistry is not my field of interest within chemistry. Definitely take a class with Dr. Fostvedt if you can.

Best wet lab I've taken at UNC. To my knowledge, Dr. Fostvedt is the only lab instructor that actually releases the grading criteria used for evaluating each assignment. This course is 100x better than it used to be, and the pigment synthesis is actually pretty fun. Group research project at the end of the course with a poster presentation & paper.

Fostvedt is hands down the best chemistry professor at UNC. Shes so kind, good at teaching, and approachable. So reasonable with grades and classwork and takes feedback from students fullheartedly. An angel sent down to bring a little light to the hell that is the UNC chem department. If youre a chem major or need to take a chem class PLZ TAKE HER

Hands down my favorite chem professor so far (junior chem major). I love Dr Fostvedt so much. She cares about your learning, is kind, and is very accessible. She also wants you to succeed and do your best. Dr. Fostvedt will meet you where you are and try to help you every step of the way. Truly a wonderful human being--her kindness is contagious.

She is such a great person and great lecturer. She is open to feedback and is very passionate about her subject. By far the best chem prof I've had so far (chem major). She writes very fair exams and gives an extra credit question at the end of the midterms and final. There is also an opportunity to memorize the periodic table for a grade boost.

analysis.name: Mario Giacomazzo
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 158 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Doctor Mario is a real beauty. By far the best professor I've had at UNC. Took him at 8am M-W-F, but I did not regret it. He is super funny during lectures and knows how to crack a joke. Exams are easy and most of the class normally gets a B or higher. There is normally homework on Web Assign after each class, but its easy. Mario is a real homie.

Dr. Mario is hands down one of the best professors I've had at UNC. The class is both very entertaining and pertinent to the data science field. He is also very accessible outside of class and cares about his students. He makes his class suitable for both advanced programmers and people with little experience. I would take any class he offers!

AVOID AT ALL COSTS... Mario is undoubtedly the worst. He will tell you to read the textbook, but not have the same material on exams, ridicule you, and waste your time. If Mario only curves to "fix the mistakes in his teaching," but there is a 20% curve, how can he claim that he's a decent professor? Nightmare professor for an introductory course.

Hilarious but extremely egotistical and conceited. Don't take this class if you've never taken stats before, but if you have, you'll be fine. Generous with curves mostly because he values his reputation more than your life. Lectures are relaxed but full of tangents, so little gets done. Gives zero insight on exams, so studying feels like a gamble.

horrible experience. 0 study material given outside of notes outlines. Exams are MCQ but are worded so poorly and designed to confuse you and are NOTHING like the homeworks. Midterm 1 is fine, Midterm 2 was universally so TERRIBLE that we had a 20 (!!!) percent curve. Says it was unfair but says that now that we've seen it, it is fair for final????

analysis.name: Gabor Pataki
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 117 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Listen to me, save yourself now and do not take this class with Gabor. Although he does seem to care about his students, he gives three midterms that are roughy 7 free response questions each with little to no partial credit. The home works are easy and the practice exams he gives are simple but neither resemble any of the questions on the exams.

Dr Pataki is an AMAZING professor. I didn't want to take his class at first because of his poor reviews on here but don't let that fool you! He teaches comprehensively so that EVERYBODY understands and he just really wants you to learn and feel confident with the material. His class isn't too hard and he's very willing to help. TAKE THIS CLASS!

Gabor is the worst professor I've ever had. He is rude to students and is inept at answering questions. He is unable to explain even the simplest of concepts well and uses an arbitrary extra credit coupon system. A real jerk, make sure to do his way of calculus or you're screwed. If you haven't taken Calc before, you need an outside tutor.

Gabor Pataki massages your brain to think outside the box, iykyk. He cares lots about his students, and it shows during his lectures. If your bad at math this class is pretty easy, just put in some work and you will be fine. He does have an accent, but worry about his handwriting more. He's also pretty funny too, in a mathematical way.

The fact that he has an A- grade is one of the most absurd things I have ever seen. His grading is the most ridiculous things ever and I truly suggest getting out of this class before you even enroll in it.  Pataki's way or the high way. Also do not let him learn your name because he will constantly call you out in class. AVOID GABOR PATAKI!!!!!!!!

analysis.name: Grigory Terlov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Greg isn't bad but his lectures are disorganized i.e he doesn't provide notes but its bc he teaches from the textbook so j look at that. The key to being successful in this class is going to office hours. His lectures are theoretical so it is really helpful to go to office hours to get help applying concepts from lecture. Hard, but def manageable!

while the homework is manageable most of the time, it doesn't really feel like the lecture material applies to it. his lectures are a bit unorganized because he often jumps in without telling us what section of the text he's working from. no example numbers from text. he does all of his notes in chalk, so write fast and never be absent.

His lectures don't really make sense as he tends to go on tangents about random things. When asked what he refers to in the textbook, he says to pay attention in class. This class is already hard as it is and other than offering office hours which don't really help imo, he doesn't do anything outside of that. Would not take :(

Lectures are hard to follow due to the fast pace. The professor pauses for questions, but most students seem too unsure to ask, so it doesn't help much. Concepts move on before they fully sink in. Slowing down and spending more time reinforcing key ideas would make the class more effective.

Greg is a super nice professor but for an intro course the class is difficult, especially if you are not good at math. He gives past exams for you to study but he make mistakes on the answer key which makes it hard if you are already confused. Tests are a big portion of grade and are graded very strictly, he does give extra credit and curves exams.

analysis.name: Melissa Geil
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: 401 is already a pretty weirdly structured course. Professor Geil makes it pretty manageable and in most of the other courses the feedback kind of seems arbitrary; hers is more concrete and very easy to implement if you read through it, grades a bit harshly but I was never upset about my grades in the course. 10/10 would recommend for 401

I took ENGL 105i - Writing in Business with Dr. Geil and it was a wonderful experience. I thought the class was very useful and I developed writing skills relevant to my future career. We also had a mock Shark Tank presentation, which was actually quite fun to work on. Learned a lot from Dr. Geil, guest presenters she brought in and my classmates.

Take everything she teaches. She's funny and really knows her stuff. She pushed both papers back almost two weeks, and held extensive reviews for the midterm and final. Weekly quizzes are a great way to bolster your grade, and she drops the lowest one. She was always available for help with papers, and she'll even send promising sources your way.

Dr. Geil is a very nice professor and her class is very relaxed.  It was all basically discussing the books we read and taking basic reading quizzes on them.  However, her grading for papers was very difficult and her grading criteria is sometimes vague.  The papers are a majority of your grade so her difficult grading makes it hard to get an A.

Dr. Geil was so helpful and she was so entertaining. She kept her demeanor friendly and she was a bit quirky. She grades strictly, but fairly. The course was incredibly interesting and she was the primary reason for keeping it interesting as Shakespeare is sometimes difficult to grasp. I would absolutely recommend taking her class if you can.

analysis.name: Karen  Guzzo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So Free. Literally Take notes and do ur work for a guaranteed A. ZERO flexibility on missing assignments or turning in late tho, so if you do that even once you might be cooked.
This was my favorite class I have taken this semester! She is a great professor and I recommend everyone take this class.

Dr. Guzzo is such an amazing woman and professor. Genuinely hilarious, cares about the subject, and tests are very straightforward and easy if you go to class. If you need to take Soci 101, take it with her for sure. Hardest part of the class is remembering to do the reading responses.

She is one of the best professors I have had at UNC. Her lectures are very information heavy but it you pay attention and take notes then everything is easy for her exams. She knows how to keep people engaged and is very funny. Def recommend her for everyone!!!

Allow me the honor of telling you how AMAZING Professor Guzzo was. Funny, intriguing, and passionate, Professor Guzzo was always available and open during class. Her slideshows were easy to follow and informative, the readings were chill, and the hardest parts were the reading response papers, which you could easily forget about.

analysis.name: Gwendolyn Schwinke
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Schwinke was incredibly kind! When reading her reviews I was a bit scared as I am generally a sensitive person, but she did her best to make everyone feel as comfortable as possible. There were many opportunities to collaborate with my classmates, which I feel added to the good energy. I will be taking her again for voice training 2! :)

Professor Gwendolyn was the kindest and most supportive professor I had during my four years of college. The coursework was manageable, consisting of just three short projects (a poem, a speech, and a monologue) throughout the entire semester. All works are done in class. You'll get an A as long as you attend class.

I have no clue why Professor Schwinke has low reviews. She is an excellent teacher who provides an energetic approach to sort of "black and white" topics. This class is not difficult at all. She is a tough grader but if you follow the rubrics for the essays you have nothing to worry about!

Gwendolyn is divisive. Some people found her fun, others found her condescending and stressful. Be prepared for her to call on you and kind of pick on you in class. Again, some found it funny, others would get upset. It's an easy class but a strange one! This review is for 154, Performer's Awareness (wasn't available as a class code.)

Super kind and energetic!! This is a theatre class so PARTICIPATE. Don't be afraid to be/act silly during class -- both your grade and speaking ability will improve if you go along with it. Take this class !!!!!

analysis.name: Amanuel Gebremichael
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I really liked Professor Gebremichael's lectures and the group discussions! If you aren't comfortable speaking in front of the class, you may not score well in participation though. The material is very interesting and he often incorporated current politics into class. The exams were difficult but curved very generously (15% curve on the midterm).

I enjoyed Prof. AG's sense of humor and how much he cared about our individual opinions in class discussions. Compared to other poli prof.'s, he is definitely more difficult. The class is graded on 3 five questions quizzes, a midterm, and the final. If you don't do well on all of the quizzes, it'll be very difficult to get your grade up. He curves!

Prof Gebremichael is down to earth and engaging during his lectures. We had very interesting discussions and his quizzes were super easy. Don't underestimate the tests though, they are pretty hard and have a detailed written portion. The exams were based on the lectures, so I never did the reading and did just fine. Definitely take this class!

Professor Gebremichael was awesome. I had him for my African American Economics and Inequality FYS, and he had great content, excellent and funny lectures, and was an overall great professor. His grading is stricter for the final presentation and paper, but he gives you more than enough notice to complete them well in advance.

POLI 100 is a very introductory class and is very lecture heavy, so it can get a little boring. I did think Dr. Gebremichael did a good job trying to spice things up by incorporating current events. Attendance is mandatory and there is one midterm, one essay, 3 quizzes, and a final. Grading is very fair, and the class is really just not that hard.

analysis.name: Jennifer Gates-Foster
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 100 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gates-Foster was knowledgeable about her field but could come off as arrogant/disrespectful. IDST-190 was painful. Up to 60-page readings and 5-question 10-minute quizzes before every class, & the midterm was awful. Assuming they even keep Triple-Is around after this semester, do yourself a favor by trusting these reviews, and don't take this one.

Dr. Gates-Foster is clearly very knowledgeable about Roman history and archaeology, and she seemed very nice. However, I found the lectures to be somewhat repetitive. Grading was fair, and was half determined by her and half by a TA. Turn in the work and read at least some of the required readings and you'll be fine.

If you have to take a Triple-I, DO NOT DO BORDERS AND BOUNDARIES!! Not even if you like history or the Middle East, do not take it. While Gates isn't a bad lecturer, she can be quite condescending. There is a quiz before every class and you are expected to read long passages before them. AVOID THIS CLASS.

This is one of the worst gen eds you can take. If Borders and Boundaries please do not take the class. The class is lecture heavy and involves a quiz due before every class. Also, the professors half the time repeat material from previously lectures that is identical to previous lectures.

She cares about every little detail and there are so many readings that make no sense and tests that are graded on the smallest details. Would not recommend this course (borders and boundaries). Honestly take any other IDST triple I course for gen eds.

analysis.name: Harvey Seim
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Seim is always ready to help if you are willing to ask. With around 8 homework assignments and the rest tests determining your grade, it can be difficult to bring up what you have because barely anything is given to you. Quite challenging tests because you need to remember very specific numbers. Lectures and slides are decent, but helpful.

Dr. Seim is SUPER kind and wants us to succeed. I am a biology major (took this as allied science) and HIGHLY recommend. Tests are straight from class and a study guide is provided. Homework is slightly difficult sometimes, but it's made by the TA. Content is interesting and I have learned a lot!

He is super nice and super invested in what he teaches. I learned a lot of interesting material. "Weekly" homework is easy, and tests are very straightforward. If you study the study guide and attend class the exams will be easy. The lectures sometimes felt like they were dragging or long, but overall easy class with a very nice professor.

Dr. Seim is SO sweet and his class was very interesting. I am an EMES major so that's why I found it fun, the lab is even better. Make a quizlet of the study guides and as long as you know the answers you will be fine. Take the homeworks seriously because they weigh a lot.

Prof. Seim is a good lecturer and he is really knowledgeable. The TA grades most of the work and helps make the homework and tests. Most of the testing material is pulled from the homework and the free textbook.

analysis.name: Hugo Mendez
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 68 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took this class for an interesting, and relatively simple introductory focus capacity. It has not been what I was expecting. The tests are graded ridiculously harsh. I was talking to a friend with a different TA and they were getting 2 points off for things that I got 5 points taken off of. Just very frustrating

Doesn't teach anything from the textbook that he wrote, but still tests all vocabulary from it. Exams are way too difficult and harshly graded for an introductory level class. Spent more time studying for this class than for any of my biology or math classes, it was unnecessarily time consuming and difficult

If you get the opportunity to take a class with Dr. Mendez, take it! He made going to a 9am easy. His lectures are entertaining. He is also an incredibly kind professor and wants to see his students succeed. Now, the class is quite test heavy with three exams making up 68% of your grade. However, he gives a detailed study guide that is cumulative.

Prof. Mendez was one of my favorite professors I have ever had at UNC. He kept lectures engaging, attendance was mandatory but he made them fun. Workload was one 6-8 sentence reflection from each class and one 8-10 sentence paragraph from a prompt a week. Exams were very fair and study guide was super helpful. LOVED this class and this professor!

Great professor and cares a lot about the material! Unbiased, and easily accessible. Definitions on tests can be oddly specific and meant to trick you, but everything is in the slides from class. Made attendance required halfway through the semester because everyone stopped showing up. Hard to bring your grade back up if you do bad on a midterm.

analysis.name: Kelli Holt
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 58 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Holt was wonderful and so caring for all her students. The class is very chill and she makes it lively with class discussions and activities. Gave us extensions on over half of the assignments without us even asking. Gave insightful and encouraging feedback on all assignments. I always looked forward to this class, can't recommend her enough!

even if your interest in law is small, take this class!! prof. holt is so kind and an easy professor. we were only graded on a few assignments and she gave us extensions on half of them. for the assignments that she did grade, she gave very insightful comments on how to improve for the next assignment. loved the environment of class and the prof!

Actually the most amazing teacher, so caring and such a fun class. If you don't like talking, then don't take the class, but everyone in the class got so comfortable with each other, and it was just such a fun class, and I learned a lot. If you are into law, take this class. You get to learn so much about argumentation & just a great class overall!

She is one of the funniest professors, she talks about funny personal situations. She does care about her students and wants you to succeed. There are three main assignments, and the class is not difficult. If you like to talk, then this class is for you. The warm-up discussions took most of the class, which was fun.

Professor Holt is AWESOME. She makes the class so fun and is super easy. We only had two major assignments, and the work was interesting and fun. You'll have the chance to either work in groups or alone, whatever you prefer. Seriously consider taking her to fill in any of your focus capacities - she's the best!

analysis.name: Hilary Lithgow
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lithgow focuses on students' improvement. She will sit down and provide as much feedback and guidance as needed. Classes were very participation-driven and focused on students sharing and discussing their thoughts on readings. She gives extensions and is understanding of extenuating circumstances.

Dr. L is the BEST! Although her ENGL 105i class comes with a relatively heavy workload (assignments every two days), it really pushes me to work hard on my writing. As long as you put in the effort on your essays, you're guaranteed to get a great grade. Her feedback is incredibly detailed and helpful. HIGHLY RECOMMEND if you really wanna learn

Do NOT take this class if you want to get your papers back on time, she STARTED grading half of the assignments we were given a week after LDOC, so you will have no clue what your grades are going to be. Even though she seems to really care about you and your success, it is ridiculous and I will never be taking another class with her.

This was one of the most difficult/rewarding things I've ever done-I definitely hated this class at times but I know I can write a good research paper now-She really wants you to get it and will meet outside class until you feel confident with your writing skills-The assignments feel redundant at times but theyre worth it for the dedicated student.

This is my second Lithgow class, and honestly, I'd take one of her classes every semester if I could. She is so sweet and goes above and beyond to get you helpful feedback to help you improve. This class isn't an easy breezy ENGL 105, but you learn SO much and it prepares you to write like a college student. 110% recommend.

analysis.name: Robin Horton
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: . Imagine you are in a boxing ring with Mike Tyson ( in his prime) and he bit your ear off. Imagine you are playing football, and all the sudden you get ran over by a 300lb lineman. Imagine you are at a baseball game, and when you look away, a bat hits you in the face. These are things I would rather have happen to me than take a class with Horton

It seems like she pretends to be really nice in class but it feels so, SO fake. This class feels like college thriving-level basic material but somehow worse. Made me cry when she pointed out my mistakes on an assignment that I failed and passive aggressively said "this is definitely one of the more...interesting ones I've seen..."

Robin can come across as patronizing, but many reviews feel exaggerated. Attendance is strict (only 1 absence) and she enforces rules on phones and punctuality, though you can request to switch sections up to 3 times. The work is easy, less than an hour a week, and you can do other homework if no one comes to tutoring. Overall not bad for 3 cred PF

I just completed EDUC387 with Horton . If you asked me to swim in shark-infested waters or take another class with her, I would chose the former. If you asked me to fight a grizzly bear or take this class again, I would choose the former. These are not difficult decisions. Neither should yours be when registering.

Robin will open up the class for questions but if you actually ask she seems to be irritated and gives a condescending answer. She was highly passive aggressive both during and outside of class. The lectures are just bullet points of the readings which I actually found interesting, but this was a lot of work for a pass-fail class.

analysis.name: Sherick Hughes
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Hughes seems like a sweet guy, but he should not be teaching a course. For a class with assigned group seating and heavily weighted attendance, we learned nothing. We had one class on hits, misses, and false alarms and one class on debiasing strategies, and learned nothing else. He would say a word and then ramble on about something irrelevant.

Truly got so bored during his lectures, he doesn't teach anything he just rambles on about his life that has nothing to do with the course work. All of the assignment are easy but being there for attendance is miserable. The final makes no sense because you don't learn anything all semester so get ready to teach yourself. nice guy bad teacher

He talked very much. I loved the TA, Katie, but I feel like Dr. Hughes wasn't talking about course material. He posted the syllabus a few days late, rarely responded to emails, and took a while to get to a point he was trying to make. His rubrics didn't make any sense, and even the TA didn't know what it meant half the time.

Professor Hughes is an overall great dude. However, there isn't much teaching that goes on in the class, no quizzes, just the final and project-based work. The TA is absolutely amazing! She is caring and flexible. She would make a great professor. Make sure to attend every class because attendance is weighed HEAVILY!!!!

This class is extremely unorganized. If you like clear grading, rubrics, syllabi, and structure, this is not for you. This class is not hard but you don't learn much. We have only had 2 or 3 lectures and even those are hard to follow along with. He has not shown up 3 times with no email. I strongly advise taking a different leadership course.

analysis.name: Jeffrey Hoopes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: his quizzes can be rough so just pay attention and you'll do well. a really funny professor and very passionate about tax probably the most interesting class i took at the b-school

I bombed first exam, hence the grade. Not an easy class but not hard either. Great lecturer and nice guy. Daily quizes that are just common knowledge, basically his way of taking attendence. Easy HW's, exams are similar to practice exam.

Dr. Hoopes is an absolute gem of the KF department, and I was so lucky to take his class. The 407 pre-req is entirely optional, and the energy he brings to class every day is the only reason why my trip to KF was worth it. The content is super interesting, and he's always flexible to talk about anything related to the class. Would take again 100%.

Jeff is probably the most passionate professor I have had in college. While it is true that taxes may not be the most appealing subject, his lectures are great and easy to understand. He calls exams "celebrations." As long as you keep up with the content, he will make sure you succeed.

I had Prof Hoopes for Taxes & Business Strategy. He's really funny, but the lectures were a bit boring (it's a tax class, what do you expect). He was great about answering questions, especially in office hours. I'd recommend this class because of him, but the subject itself would probably be really dull if you're not into tax or corporate finance.

analysis.name: Henry Veggian
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 56 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Most entertaining class ever. Henry listens to his students extremely carefully, and takes careful measures so everyone is satisfied with due dates. In addition to being a great professor, he is a hilarious person. Personality is often lost in gen-ed classes, but NOT in his. He is an amazing storyteller and keeps students engaged with the content.

Henry is awesome. You will find yourself captivated by a long-winded fantastic story that initially seems completely irrelevant, but somehow at the end, every single time, he pulls the story to relate perfectly to what we are learning about in class. You will write in this class, but primarily only on topics that you are interested in.

He cares a lot about his students and makes a point to listen to them - changed homeworks or syllabus to fit what we thought was better, I've never met a professor like that. Definitely a lot of reading and movies to watch but most of them are fun. Does go on tangents and seems to get a little lost in his own head but he's funny.

Took feedback and added plenty of space between readings and films from big-name auteurs. The few texts he assigned were long but worthwhile for those interested in film adaptation theory. Two 5-page papers and weekly blog posts. Went on tangents, but always had great insight in setting up cultural and historical context.

I found him to be a very laid-back and thoughtful professor. Others say he is full of himself, but I think he simply likes to offer his perspective on the topics in the class. He's an interesting guy, and his discussions always held my attention. He's clearly very knowledgeable in his field, and he makes an effort to get to know his students.

analysis.name: Serenella Iovino
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Iovino is very knowledgable and passionate about her lectures. Her assignments are straightforward. Sometimes, she becomes a bit too passionate and takes over the discussion, giving students less time to speak. She's also not afraid to question students on their research on a topic, so be prepared to defend why your information is relevant.

Pr. Iovino is so sweet and caring, and this class is an easy A. She is very passionate about the material and will sometimes dominate the class time but overall I didn't ever stress about this class. She is also very accessible if you are ill or have to miss class for any reason. Would def recommend if you need to fulfill the gen ed.

Iovino cares about each of her students. She is super passionate about the subject and it shows. Sometimes this passion causes her to overtake a conversation and not let students speak, but overall she's amazing. She is not afraid to question a student's information or presentation, so be prepared to defend the information you chose to add
Class rocked. She was very kind and fun.

Prof Iovino is super nice and genuinely cares about her job and you. However, I feel like she doesn't read the room well sometimes and kinda just talks for hours. She's also not afraid to interrupt you while you're presenting/talking, but not in a rude way though. Overall, this class is a free A.

analysis.name: Iuliia  Fokina
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Fokina is truly the kindest professor I've had the pleasure of learning from. I know so many people who can say the same about her kindness and genius. She understands time constraints and the under load of an undergraduate, which not many professors do. Above all though, she teaches with compassion and intention. I highly recommend taking her.

I honestly don't know why other people dislike her, she is truly such a good professor, who when you ask for clarification will help you understand complex concepts better. She is really funny and always made attending class enjoyable. Definetly would take her for 225, HW is not that bad and exams are pretty fair.

She was fine and a funny lecturer, a lot of the material/hw/slides did seem written by chat gpt which is a little disheartening but the class was pretty easy and exams weren't too hard if you practiced with the poll everywhere questions. HW load is light and attendance policy is forgiving
Dr. Fokina is so nice and funny. She likes for students to participate, so don't be afraid to! She is a super fair grader, so just show up and pay attention to lectures, and you'll be golden!

Only reason why I got a good grade in this class because I studied on my own. Her slides are not clear and very hard to study from, especially if you miss a class. She also just does not teach effectively and is bad at explaining so it's not really of use to go to class anyway. Would not recommend taking it with Fokina

analysis.name: Ivan Cherednik
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Math62H is ridiculously easy to get an A. Material is impossible to understand, but the final is take home and the projects are easy after help from the GRC. Homework is graded but not factored into final grade unless it helps your grade. Ivan is so smart it is mind boggling, however his accent and random trains of thought make it tough to learn in

He was a very tough grader. There was extra credit options on tests, but that was for a reason. Tests were so difficult that he had to give us the built in curve or else everyone in the class would have failed. The positive reviews are from the .1% of students who spend hours upon hours just studying for this one class. DO NOT TAKE!

Professor Cherednik was a nice and funny professor. He has an extremely thick Russian accent that can take a while to understand. He is too smart to teach a class such as MATH231. Had a weird grading scale that ended up making a lot of people have their final exam as 80% of the final grade. Overall, I would recommend with someone else if possible!

Do not take this course unless it is required. The professor has a very strong Russian accent, which makes lectures difficult to understand. On the first day, I was completely lost and could not follow what he said. However, he reviews material for the midterms except the first take-home exam. Later midterms usually have about four questions total.

Dr. Cherednik is a kind and caring professor. Unfortunately, he has a super thick Russian accent, so learning discrete mathematics from him is a challenge. He is very clear about what to prepare for the exams and is very understanding. The class, especially the homework, is complex, but he makes himself accessible and his notes are helpful.

analysis.name: Isabella Hinks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 80 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The lectures are very informative and she explains things very well especially if you are new to the topic. At first I did very poorly on the quizzes but after I went to tutoring with the TAs I did way better on the quizzes. I recommend going to tutoring right when you see yourself struggling and recommend it a bit more the office hours.

I came into this class with 0 coding experience and struggled to grasp the content often. However, the resources provided by the CS department are crazy. There is tutoring and office hours almost every single day (Sundays too!). 

Dr. Hinks is great, and she truly did everything (including omitting the late submission penalties) to help our grades.

she clearly wants everyone to do well in this class. turning EXs in before due date gets extra credit at the end of the semester, most missed quiz Qs often dropped, takes the time to explain things well. lectures can be a bit boring if you already know the content, but she is so nice and helpful! this class is so easy if you just put the time in

She is a wonderful professor and explains things very clearly. This class is hard so once you start to see yourself struggling on quizzes take advantage of the tutoring (this is what I did and it truly helped me). At first, I got 60s on the quizzes and after going to the tutoring with the TAs my scores went up to 80s/90s!

Class is well organized. But, if you've never coded, I think Dr Hinks is not the best teacher. Lecture slides are very high level w/ few examples covered in class. Quizzes are short so if you miss 1 section, its tough to do well. I found other resources to learn the content. She did adjust the final quiz/exam weights, which helped grades a lot.

analysis.name: irina kruchinina
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: If you are a stem major and don't have the mindset for creative thinking, unfortunately this is not the professor for you. Dr. I is very abstract and creative with her thought processes. To others, her guidelines appear to be vague and complex, but she wants to give you ideas and creative freedom. She is very caring and passionate.

her speech is very difficult to understand, and on top of the fact that the concepts are all very abstract makes her lectures very confusing. jumps between topics too quickly. the details of the performance requirements are usually incredibly vague and not fully explained until very close to the due date. take this class with literally anyone else.

Dr. I appears to be very caring and kind. However, I was very confused by her lectures. There are 3 major performances, but your TA gives good feedback on how to improve. This class was a nice brain break for me as a STEM major. I still didn't mind the class and would recommend it.

Gave multiple assignments over university mandated holidays, unclear assignment guidelines, excessive homework for a 100 level course. Currently have an A but not worth the effort. Professor is difficult to reach. TAs were the only saving grace for this course

Her lectures can be very boring and convoluted, and she also has a thick accent which can make understanding her a bit difficult, especially in the mornings. Otherwise, you can tell she's very into performance and analysis and if you are too she'd be a great professor.

analysis.name: Iris Fitzsimmons Christensen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Profe is amazing! Class is interesting, and she always engages with students. There is a LOT of homework and vocabulary in class, but the Spanish department assigns that, not her. Midterms and finals are difficult due to the amount of material covered, but profe always helped us with what to study. Go to her office hours as well!

Spanish at UNC is hard, but I would definitely recommend taking 105 with Iris! She's super accessible outside of class and genuinely wants her students to succeed! Be prepared to learn A LOT of content, but as long as you start studying for exams early, you can succeed in this class!
She's a very good teacher and explains tough spanish concepts very well. Her in class activities were always fun, and I've always felt prepared for the tests.

analysis.name: Inger Brodey
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would rather retake Gen Chem, pull out my anterior cerebral artery, and lasso a bear with it than take this class again. Expected full-length novels in a week and acted like we only had her class. Gives zero feedback on assignments but continues to grade extremely harshly.

Dr. Brodey was very kind, and invited the class over to her house for dinner a couple times. She was nice to talk to, and I enjoyed the class a lot. She offered good feedback on essays when asked. However, the workload was definitely overwhelming at times. We consistently read 150 pages of dense reading for each class, or watched long movies.

professor brodey is knowlegeable, kind, and accessible. lots of reading, but to be expected for an english seminar, and definitely manageable. her grading criteria could be a bit unclear at times but she's always open to explaining! she even invited us over to her house for dinner, she's super sweet.

Professor Brodey is very kind and passionate, but the workload is overwhelming. Full novels in under a week and long films in one night made the class feel unrealistic with other commitments. Creative final project, but I wouldn't recommend unless you have lots of free time.

As a Jane Austen fanatic, I was very disappointed. I feel like we did 85% of the teaching. We had group presentations where we taught parts of adaptations or extra readings. Also, lots of group discussion. We read 8 books, so you had 150+ pages due every class, which was impossible. No rubrics for anything. Brodey was very sweet, though.

analysis.name: Imran Rizvi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Rizvi is a very talented researcher and clearly has a lot of passion for the material he teaches. While his lectures sometimes seem a little out of order or repetitive, he covers most of the material he says he will at the start of the year, and his exams are very fair. One of the most passionate and easy to talk to professors.
Dr Rizvi is obviously very knowledgeable and incredibly passionate. He is my favorite BME professor I have had!

Dr. Rizvi is very knowledgeable about the subject. My main issue with the class is the lab reports, about half of them being full-length. I recommend going to office hours while doing them as the TA's will always find some points to deduct otherwise. Exams (including the final) are not bad, study diagrams and lecture slides and you're good.

I really enjoyed this class. He is very knowledgable and truly cares about the class's understanding. The only issue is that the class is somewhat disorganized with timing of assignments, and grading for labs doesn't seem standardized with TA's. If you don't pay attention, read the textbook instead. Tests are not impactful, and an A is 95+, not 93.
The best. He really organizes the class to ensure student's success. Truly passionate about the subject,  one of my favorite professors at UNC.

analysis.name: Patrick Harrison
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 207 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Believe these reviews, Professor Harrison is amazing. I am not a psych major, but I was still able to gain a lot from this course. It strongly helped that Professor Harrison always cared about his students and their comprehension of the material. If you're like me and simply in need of a research and discovery class, I highly recommend this course.

Professor Harrison is kind and accomodating, and this course is super helpful for writing. The course involves a semester-long research paper which is broken up into sections, and there are clear rubrics to follow for each. Take notes during class to make studying for the final easier, as the final is open note!  Attendance is through PollEv.

Phenomenal professor! Very passionate about the topics in class! The class itself is very draining in the sense of the semester is spent writing a research paper. Don't procrastinate and you'll do great! If you do, you'll be fine! To me, the content of the class was kind of dull, but it's centered on research, so it's expected. Definitely take it!

Dr. Harrison is genuinely one of the best professors I have ever taken a class with. He is so kind and truly cares about what he is teaching and how well his students are doing. It is clear that he wants the best for his students and will do what he can to make the class easier/more accessible. If you have the opportunity to take his class, DO IT!!

Dr. Harrison is a great guy and wants everyone to succeed. No question is stupid to him. The course involves a semester-long research paper, but it's broken up into manageable sections. You are given everything you need to do well (examples, outlines, rubric, data, etc). Attendance was only counted for the first week or so.

analysis.name: Isaac Unah
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Unah's a researcher, not a teacher. Late to every class, very unorganized, & falls way behind on schedule. He had an obsession with teaching us regression analysis (not in class description). The little amount he did teach, he was repetitive & didn't prepare us for the research paper or exam. We didn't learn for a month once. Wouldn't recommend.

You live by the test, you die by the test. I wish this class had more opportunities for students to demonstrate their knowledge on the law and court precedent. Instead 70% of the grade goes to two online tests with large multiple-choice sections. Unah is a very nice guy, but the laxity was too much. Class would begin far-later than scheduled.

Great professor, is engaging, and passionate about what he teaches.  He is a lenient grader, lets you know what is going to be on the quizzes, and he pushed the midterm back 3 times because the class begged him to.  He is a bit disorganized which makes it hard to prepare before the class. He did show up to the final late because of Canvas issues.

Dr Unah is a great professor. I think people need to give professors some grace. Unah is funny and caring. Definitely go to office hours and get to know him. He also has a lot of connections. If you're interested in law, take this. Easy A class - one midterm, 6 quizzes (drops lowest 2), a partner paper, and final. Exams are online which is nice

I love Dr. Unah! His style is not going to be for everyone, as you can tell from other reviews. However, if you can get past his high level of disorganization, his classes are really enjoyable. He has so much passion for his discipline, loves talking to students who are interested in law school, and is just a great guy overall. Would recommend!

analysis.name: Joseph Telegen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is very passionate about teaching; however, his methods are not for everyone. He is very dramatic and at times a bit disorganized. He has a lot of tics that might annoy some people. While his train of thought is often heading to an insightful and interesting place, it sometimes gets lost on the way there.  Super easy grader.

Joe is really nice, and very accessible outside of class if you need help. This class is great if you want an easy A and enjoy talking about pop culture. He does go on a lot of tangents and I didn't really leave the class feeling like I'd learned much about writing though.

By far the easiest A I got all semester. He goes on a lot of tangents, but I tended to find them pretty interesting. If you're an English major or particularly care about learning about the field, maybe choose a different professor, since there were some days we straight up just watched TV shows in class that vaguely related to course content

Joe was an amazing professor and I would love to take his class again. You can tell he loves rhetorical analysis. He does bring up the TV show Succession quite a bit, as well as Kanye West, Taylor Swift, and Elon Musk. He is very accessible outside of class time, and he makes sure you know where and how to find him.

Joe is a nice guy, but rambles about unrelated stuff for most of class and frequently goes off track so I didn't get much out of his lectures. He is very friendly and tries to connect to students, but goes over the top sometimes. Almost all in-class work is group work, but rarely is it productive. He is a lenient grader and is very accessible.

analysis.name: John Noonan
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Noonan is a truly a kind person, making an effort to remember your name and make 231 really entertaining than most sections. But most of us agree that he tends to ramble about things that aren't important to the curriculum at hand. the ULAs in recitation were def better at teaching than he was in general. also poll everywhere is used for attendance

Dr. Noonan is lots of fun! Teaching style could definitely be improved, but he's engaging and silly, and answers specific questions pretty well. I leaned HEAVILY on the ULAs in the class to actual learn material and prepare for tests... probably would've failed without them. Overall fun, but you're left to learn a lot of material on your own.

great guy and really funny in class. We did sometimes speed through lectures, but I felt like he still did a good job explaining things. There was also a lot of time doing practice problems, so I generally felt ready for the midterms. He also made sure you were prepared for what would be on the tests. underrated professor for sure

Honestly, a very nice and funny guy, is pretty accessible outside of class too. But, he expected us to know a lot of things and may not exactly be the best professor in terms of teaching. Good thing is, he makes the tests pretty easy compared to the other Calc 3 classes. I'd recommend teaching yourself a lot outside of lectures.

Professor Noonan is a great example of great person, somewhat lackluster teacher imo. He is lively and brings good energy to his classroom. However, his teaching is not my cup of tea. The material that is on exams is very different from what's practiced on homework/class. It was often "figure it out" with not much else for help. I felt unprepared.

analysis.name: Justin Nolan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This was the easiest class that I have ever taken at UNC. While class is optional attendance, he is very excited about the subject material making his lectures pretty engaging. Two papers and two online take home exams are the only grades in the class, but they are graded easily. Recitation is chill and gets out early. Take this class!!
Justin is a nice person and a good teacher, but beware of the 13 in-person quizzes!

I liked this class! I didn't come to lecture often (optional attendance), but the lectures were interesting sometimes. Graded by two 5-page papers, a midterm, and a final. Good gen ed option to consider! I recommend going to recitations. Our midterm and final were taken at home. He's also really chill, used to be a high school teacher.

("City and Regional Planning" not "Architecture") Very funny, down to Earth, and kind. Fast-paced lectures. Detailed PPTs. Not much HW. Papers: 2x20% | Midterm: 25% | Final: 25% | Recitation Participation: 10%. Easy grading on papers. Vocab-oriented exams (there are hundreds of vocab terms so studying takes a long time). Good choice for a Gen-Ed.

Information heavy slides make it so that purchasing the textbook isn't even necessary (like I don't recommend spending your money). Professor Nolan is a great guy but the lectures themselves are extremely fast-paced and monotonous. Your only grades in the class are two papers, a midterm and final but are all relatively easy.

analysis.name: Jason Roberts
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were not productive as he would just repeat the textbook and go off on random tangents. Test average for the first exam was a 63% and he blamed the class for not paying attention during lectures.  If you really want to succeed in this class, then you would have to read all of the chapters assigned in the textbook--which mind you, is a lot.

I honestly learned more in recitation than in lecture. He is not very engaging and can sometimes come off rude. First exam had a 63% average in the class and did not suggest any changes on his end to help our performance. There is definitely a way to do well in this class, but it requires a lot of effort outside of class.

For a first year seminar, class was difficult for no reason. Graded by a few things, so messing up on the exams doesn't help your grade. You never really know what to expect on the exams, so they were difficult. Not reading heavy but lectures are boring. Professor is nice but any other first year seminar would be easier.

would only really take this class if you are a political science major. i took this for the gen-ed credit and had a hard time. lectures are boring, Roberts moves through material super quick, and tests are relatively hard. you def can do well, but it requires A LOT of studying/work.

Class average on the first exam was a 63 and blamed it on us for not memorizing extremely obscure details. Class lectures are boring and unengaging and he often stops lectures to call people out for small talk.

analysis.name: Kathryn Reissner
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took 418 this semester. Dr. Reissner is very kind and loves to know her students! Her lectures are entertaining and very fascinating, and she loves answering questions. Tests were fair and were exactly what was mentioned in class, and her slides are very helpful. I would love to take another class with her.
I took 418. She's super funny, lectures are engaging, exams are fair and not many other assignments. Her grading is good, nothing to complain, I would definitely take her again

Dr. Reissner was one of my favorite professors at UNC. You could tell how passionate she was about the content of the class and it made lectures so exciting. NSCI320 in general was such an interesting class, and she made accomodations for every student and truly cared about our well-being throughout the semester. She wants everyone to succeed!

Dr. Reissner is absolutely amazing! Her depth of knowledge in the subject makes her lectures very dense and informative. She is very good at explaining the material and always answers questions! Although the material is difficult, she really wants her students to do well! My favorite class ever at UNC- it inspired me to be pre-pharm! Amazing class!

Reissner is the sweetest person and amazing teacher. However, her tests are tricky because there is so much information and little guidance. Same goes with her papers-you never get a score back and have no idea how you did.

analysis.name: Justin Sawon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I can tell he knows a lot about math, but he doesn't seem to particularly like teaching it. Puts minimal effort into his lectures, teaches very fast. I was better off just reading the textbook. But he did do homework questions in class & was semi-helpful in office hours. Midterms were really easy, but 20% each, and the final is 45%.

I really appreciated his accessibility and personality, but his lectures were often somewhat difficult to follow. While the midterms were fairly easy, it left me relatively unprepared for the final. If you're okay with putting in extra hours to learn material yourself, you'll be okay; however, make sure you're extremely thorough.

Tests were all very fair and not difficult if you put in the effort to study. Unfortunately, Sawon definitely lacked enthusiasm towards class and his lectures were often hard to follow. I appreciated him going over homework problems in class. Exams make up pretty much the entirety of your grade, so be aware of that before taking it with Sawon.

Sawon has the harshest grading policy of any 233 prof at UNC—90% of your grade is based on exams. No midterm replacement, little weight on homework or recitation. Other profs give more free points. The course itself is easy, but take someone else if you want a lighter grading policy.

Dr. Sawon is very nice and clearly knows a lot. HOWEVER he doesn't curve anything, doesn't drop a single thing, and exams are almost 90% of the final grade. Cannot stress enough how frustrating this class was.

analysis.name: Katelyn Smith
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
I had her for Data Literacy Lab, so it doesn't really matter but I found that she was condescending towards students (not only me) and did not have the very basic level of knowledge that is needed for teaching Data Literacy Lab.

Was rude in answering reasonable questions and unable to help with basic tech. issues when it was needed.

Great, easy-going professor. The Data Lit Lab is asynchronous and you can even skip up to 2 of the in-person classes if you do the module make-up work afterwards. Pretty simple assignments and she's a super lenient grader. As long you are aware of what's happening throughout the semester, this was a great class to take with her!

Prof Smith is a lovely person, and it's clear she genuinely cares about her students and wants them to do well. Class is very easy for the most part, and there are only six in-person meetings and you are allowed to skip up to two of them.

This class is pretty silly and I don't think it should be required, but since you do have to take it, you should take it with Prof Smith. She graded quickly and fairly and she was always kind in class.

Profe Smith is amazing! Intro to Yucatan Mayan is so interesting and an overall easy class! I'm taking this as a Spanish minor elective and she is very respectful, considerate, she is flexible, and if you put in effort you will do well. Study for maybe an hour or two a week and you're golden.

analysis.name: Xiangjia Kong
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures were not very helpful as he would just copy examples from the textbook onto the board and expects us to know everything. Even though he was a pretty nice guy, I would NOT recommend taking him for discrete. Classes are very disorganized, and you are honestly better off self-learning. The homework's were also graded pretty harshly.

I took in Spring 2025, and I believe it was his first time teaching. He was not very confident at the front of the room, and he could be somewhat condescending at times. He was late to his own office hours and at times wouldn't show up. He grades the homework strict but drops the lowest 2, and the class was curved. I would avoid taking it with him.

Lectures can be a little dry sometimes, and the time would be better spent going over textbook yourself at certain points in the class. The class can be pretty hard but eventually becomes pretty easy. It was also pretty hard to do well on the homework assignments. He's a genuine guy despite that, and made sure we know how to write good proofs.

Nice guy, horrible teacher. Unorganized lectures, unclear expectations of students, no resources for success. HARSH grader - doesn't accept certain proofs even if they're correct in the textbook. Was late multiple times to his own office hours. DO NOT TAKE DISCRETE WITH HIM. but he is willing to work with students.

He was an okay professor for discrete, but sometimes seemed confused on what he was teaching or by simple questions students asked. A very tough grader and doesn't accept methods other than what was taught in class (even if its in the textbook/still correct). Office hours are slightly helpful for explanations.

analysis.name: Mike Kris
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is a wonderful prof, and it's a privilege to have the opportunity to take lessons with him. He's genuinely interested in his students' lives, not just within, but outside of music, too. He wants to see everyone succeed, and his teaching methods and life advice will do just that. He's the prof I hope most to stay in contact with after graduating.

He is genuinely one of the best teachers/professors I've ever had in all of my schooling career.  He consistently pushes students to be better without being rude about it.  He is very knowledgable but never talks down to his students.
His teaching methods are superior. I feel very comfortable learning from him and he is super knowledgable. Easily one of the most valuable music professors employed at the school.
Great teacher! Very clear and caring!

analysis.name: Kaki Ryan
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Kaki was amazing. 311 is a tough class, but she made the class very easy imo. 6 quizzes worth 8% each (all very similar to the worksheets you're given for HW), 6 Worksheets worth 20%, 5 labs worth 20% (designing circuits), and 1 final exam worth 12%. She dropped lowest 2 quiz grades for your final too, and always gave extra points on her quizzes.

Kaki is my angel. Her lectures are kind of boring, but the slides are clear and descriptive enough that I was able to get >90 on every quiz except quiz 6 without too much studying. Quiz 6 was the assembly quiz and we were a little rushed content-wise, but she had a generous curve. Final was the easiest final I've ever taken in a CS class

Kaki is very kind, but her lectures can be more confusing than self-studying. As a newer professor, her lectures are still developing. The quizzes are harder than her practice questions, though she offers a small curve. no midterm, 48% on 6 quizzes, 12% final, 20% hw,  20% coding hw, 2 quizzes can be replaced by the final grade

i honestly was so scared of 311 before taking it but it was my favorite class this semester. i took 435 w/ her too, she structured them both similarly -- lots of quizzes, labs, practice problems (in class, worksheets for credit). 435 just had a project too, which was fun. and the TAs were amazing!!
Very nice person, class is not difficult at all, a lot of partial credit given on exams

analysis.name: Shahar Kovalsky
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I think Shahar is a great professor but only for the more advanced math lectures. This was his first time teaching MATH 231 and it does show. If I needed to take another more advanced math class I would definitely take it with him. Just not Calculus 1.

He always uses the excuse of having a lot of classes to teach and being very busy to not fulfill the necessary duties of instructor, such as providing support to students in need of special assistance, which he basically completely ignores. It's basically impossible to reach out to him by email. Don't want to take any classes with him anymore.

He did not perform his duties as instructor at all. He never puts himself in others' shoes. When students are in great need of help, he always chooses to ignore it, which is such a blow to the students. He is indeed kind to this course, but he is definitely not an understanding and caring prof.

Could not recommend him more for MATH231. He is hilarious and genuinely cares about his students. His exams are fair, and he will actually answer your questions thoroughly if you are confused about anything. Edfinity homeworks during the week and quizzes, with 2 midterms and a final. The final can replace the lowest exam, and he gives extra credit!

The best thing to happen to the UNC math department. Keeps lectures clear and entertaining, makes sure he takes every measure for students to understand the content. This course content shouldn't be too difficult, and it seems like other professors overcomplicate. Hoping I get to take another class with Shahar.

analysis.name: Heather Lee
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr Lee is a nice lady & responsive to emails. While the the class looked interesting (food+history), it has been super boring. We've spent a lot of time digging through library archives, have daily difficult quizzes, and tons of essays. Really slow grader so you have no idea where you stand. No tech allowed in class & all readings must be printed.

Prof Lee is a sweet lady who cares a lot about her class; however, she is completely and entirely unorganized. She changes assignments, class expectations, and even the syllabus as a whole on a nearly class by class basis, making it extremely difficult to keep up. Her course had so much potential to be great and was unfortunately a major let-down.

Am I taking a 100 level class or a 500 level class?? Only one midterm that consists of mainly open ended questions which are graded VERY HARSHLY. Almost weekly quizzes that you don't have time to finish and are designed to trip you up. I had high hopes for this class because Asian American history isn't taught enough but I can't wait to be done.

Seminars with Professor Lee are a ton of fun, she keeps everyone engaged and interested. There is a graded assignment every class, so do the short readings and participate in conversation. She is also amazing about letting students make up work if they missed class. She's very kind, but deserves respect, so don't confuse her kindness with weakness.

Professor Lee is so passionate about what she teaches, and she made sure to guide our discussions and encourage us to share our perspectives. The course content and readings were very interesting, and Professor Lee was knowledgeable about all aspects of the course. She was always smiling and happy to talk after class, I highly recommend!

analysis.name: Victoria Le-Sweatman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Victoria leaves extremely ambiguous and rather unnecessary comments on the assignments in this class. She repeatedly claims to not understand concepts that had been laid out throughout the assignment, and needed constant re-clarification to reduce the loss of points. It is hard to understand what she's looking for because it is constantly changing.

Attendance is very important, and you have to participate and talk each recitation. Her feedback for assignments is very vague but it is clear she is looking for something very specific which she does not always tell you. Once you understand what she wants the recitations are easier, but she doesn't make this very easily known.

Recitation instructor. RMP reviews had me worried, but she was a fair grader with exams and weekly participation (80% for showing up, full points for speaking at least once). She also created a great classroom environment by leading discussions on sensitive topics.

This is for COMM 450. She will give you grades well below what you should have gotten. She has no rubrics and incredibly vague guidelines for assignments. She will give little tangible feedback and the difference between getting an 85 or 78 is completely unknown. If it is possible, avoid this professor.

I took this course online, and to be as tough as a grader that she is, she gives ZERO feedback. I technically ended with an 87, but thankfully the final grade was curved. These assignments were dreadful and so unrewarding to get no help or feedback. I would not have done well on my final essay if it weren't for her not being the one to grade it.

analysis.name: Christian Lentz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Lentz was a good professor and was available to help with course content. The material was fairly easy, but expectations for the quiz, midterm, and final were unclear, and his advice focused on big-picture themes, while the tests asked about specific details. The papers lacked rubrics, which can impact your grade.

Content isn't hard, but grading is vague and based on just a few assignments with no real guidance. Despite full participation and strong work, I got a B+. Prof disappears for multiple lectures (trips to Singapore, etc.), returns feedback too late, and doesn't put in any grades until they are finalized (likely to avoid receiving complaints).

Professor Lentz makes class enjoyable and really encourages class participation. There are no tests, and very few quizzes, so the majority of your grade comes from papers. If you are a superb writer, then you will be fine, but otherwise, he is a very strict grader and isn't all too  clear on what exactly makes a paper a great paper in his eyes.

Great lecturer, I was very engaged even in a longer T/TH block. He expects you to read but he also covers important topics from the readings during lecture. 2 group presentations (can't pick group); some had issue with lack of detail in his rubrics/instructions. He gives off the impression that he wants us to succeed. Sometimes takes roll.

I had Dr. Lentz in spring 25. Coursework was light but I would not take this to fulfill a focus capacity. He had no grading criteria or rubrics, so that allowed TAs to grade arbitrarily. When I asked for specific feedback and which criteria I had points docked from, my TA gave vague answers and was adamant that her grading was correct.

analysis.name: Lexi Toufas
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Hands down, one of my favorite professors ever. To describe Professor Toufas is to call her incredible and intentional. Despite having her ENGL 105 at 8 a.m, her charm, attitude, and care for students made me excited to come to class. And on top of that, she's actually hilarious. 110% take a class with Professor Toufas, you will never regret it. :)

Legit the best professor ever!! She truly cares about students' well-being and will work with you if you have questions/concerns. She is an easy grader and gives clear instructions for what is expected. Her lectures were kinda boring but they were manageable.

Lexi was amazing. If you want an easy 105 class while still learning something I 100 recommend her. She is very sweet and understanding and only wants the best for her students.
