There is no homework only the projects that you work on throughout the class, and you have a week to finish each section. Easy class, great professor.
Lexi is such an amazing professor! Please take English 105 with her if you can, she is so sweet and just wants all her students to do well. Great class, never stressful, couldn't recommend enough.
The BEST English 105 professor!! If you can take this class with her please do! She was always making sure we weren't stressed, and had lots of accommodations.

analysis.name: Laura Ott

review_highlights.comment: Refuses to provide a copy of lecture slides, so half the class is scrambling to write down content instead of listening to what she's saying. Exam questions do not test on knowledge of content but instead are written to trick us. Median on the first midterm was a 74 AFTER 10 bonus points were added and 7 questions dropped (out of 27). Dr. Opp fr

Dr. Ott wants you to think she cares. However, that is only true for a select few. Very passive aggressive, not willing to answer questions, not widely accessible outside class, and relies heavily on peer mentors. Beware of "select all" questions with no partial credit and no low stakes practice for tests. Dr. Ott? More like "Dr. Opp."

Dr. Ott is one of the most condescending professors that I have had the unfortunate displeasure of taking a class with. The information of the class was bearable but whenever you need something from her, it always seems like she is talking down on you. If you have the chance to take a class with her, do yourself a favor and don't.

The course content itself is not hard to understand as a whole. However, Dr. Ott teaches the concepts in a nonlinear way that is hard to understand if you don't reorder it yourself. GRQs were a waste of time and lectures could be confusing at times. Pay attention to the lecture slides when studying. She is getting rid of cheat sheets soon - beware.

Does not seem to care about students. Extremely condescending, makes the class more difficult then it needs to be and also takes her bad mood out on students. Content is not difficult, exams are not necessarily hard but they are clearly meant to trick you rather than assess your actual understanding. Voice is really annoying.

analysis.name: Josefa Lindquist
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This lady stinks. She runs all the SPAN105 classes and is not lenient at all. She wants everyone to get a B I think. Also, there's way too much work. I swear even for a 4 credit hour class. I had average Spanish experience before and thought I could ride it out and I was so wrong. Just don't take Spanish as a language so you can avoid her regime

Dr. Lindquist is absolutely amazing and you should definitely take a class with her any chance you get. She is very nice, funny, and eager to teach you about Spanish. Not only does she do a good job teaching the material, but she also interacts with students in a fun and enjoyable way. She genuinely wants to see her students succeed.

LOTS of working in pairs! I had concerns about taking it with her being the 105 coordinator, but it meant she could be much more flexible. Very kind and willing to help. Unlimited tries on online hw, so if you want you can end with a 100 for hw grade. Besides that, 3 tests and a final, a cool project at the Ackland, participation points, etc.

I loved Dr. Lindquist and she's not the issue herself, but the SPAN 105 curriculum, which she creates (she's the head of the department). This class took SO much studying and there was SO much homework to where I stopped learning because I had to look up answers to have time for other classes. Just take at a community college I beg of you!!!

IMMACULATE PROFESSOR! Get ready to be called on, but she's always willing to help you get a better understanding. Daily homework can pile up, but it's honestly super easy. Her class was very enjoyable! Very hilarious and personable! If you take this class, take it with Lindquist! She's also the dept. head, so she'll make sure you know everything!

analysis.name: Jeannie Loeb
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 349 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Everyone loves Loeb, but I personally didn't think she was the best. The tests are borderline insanely hard while could be remedied by having a test on 2 chapters instead of 3 or 4. She's not bad, but not good.

Loved Professor Loeb's class! Attendance is required, but her lectures are so interesting and easy to sit through. Definitely take good notes from the textbook and lecture, but it's easy to get an A. Readings and quizzes are due before lecture. 3 exams, 1 non-cumulative final and lowest exam is dropped. Highly recommend!
contradicts textbooks, lectures are not good, lecture slides are bad, not accessible outside of class, tests are crazy unfair

Lectures the majority of the time but her humor keeps the energy up, you have opportunity for bonus every class.  Homework single spaced 1 page papers are not terrible & help you learn the material better.  TA's are top resource for clarification.  Top suggestion: go to office hours after exams & write down questions, many repeated on final!

She changed our syllabus 3 weeks into the class and made all exams closed notes. I feel as though it is of a very unprofessional and irresponsible nature to make such drastic changes to the syllabus after the drop/add period has concluded because it leaves students in a difficult position to adapt to such changes on the fly.

analysis.name: Stephanie Mahin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Avoid at all costs! Has no clear grading criteria, and just basically assigns a B to any work you turn in. Doesn't provide any guidance - just expects you to know what she is expecting. Also is disrespectful to students, and spends all class talking about all the "experience" she has in the field.

No matter how hard you try or how little you try on each paper you will get a B. She told us on the first day of class that a B in her class is an A in any other class, which is wild because some people are taking Biomedical Engineering and getting A's and we are struggling to get an A in a class about writing different types of emails.

This absolute queen. I am baffled at how negative the reviews are - I adored Professor Mahin and this class! The lessons shifted based on current events, and the activities were engaging. And to people dissing her for mentioning she won Emmys, I would say she didn't mention it enough because I think that's really awesome.

I would avoid taking 401 with Mahin if possible. Her grading is very arbitrary and her feedback is insincere as she is often just copying and pasting stuff from one students assignment to the next. It was also supposed to be a fully in person class and she moved many classes to Zoom taking away from the classroom experience.
Dr. Mahin was an incredible professor with amazing connections, many of which she brought to class to speak. She's a tough grader, but you can tell it's because she wants you to be successful.

analysis.name: Robert McDonough
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 178 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: You could know every concept in depth and study profusely and still struggle with the exams, which make up 70% of your grade. I have never gotten anything below an A in my life and I near failed some of his tests. Lectures were interesting and I learned a lot. Tests on concepts we never practiced. Sent me straight to my therapist twice. Don't take.

The one takeaway I have for this course is to lower my expectations before checking canvas. He prides himself on class averages being below 60%. The only things this class has taught me are to humble myself and that i'll never be prepared enough for his exams. This class is unnecessarily hard and he refuses to acknowledge it. King of gaslighting.

Robert is honestly one of the worst professors I've had here. The exams are virtually impossible and he likes his averages to be in the 60s. He makes TONS of mistakes on exams which causes grading to be delayed and overall confusion. You might as well guess on the short answers because he never explains how to do them. Good luck if you have him.

It's as bad as they say. McDonough's exams are impossible. I can't count how many times we have been interrupted mid-exam because of multiple errors and typos on them. Spends more time worrying about cheating than teaching the material or checking his exams for errors, which are 70% of your grade, and the average is a 66%. Avoid at ALL COSTS.

Professor McDonough is very enthusiastic about the material but his exams are unnecessarily complicated. I found the multiple choice sections to be a joke, while the short answers were very difficult solely due to poor wording rather than students lack of understanding of the material. Also, he just pisses me off sometimes.

analysis.name: Matthew Weidenfeld
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Such an amazing and smart teacher. He genuinely cares about his students and doesn't grade harshly at all. Very engaging lectures and the simulation portion of the class if not too hard. The quizs are easy and sometimes even done in groups, exams are challenging but if you pay attention in class then you will be good. Take this class!!
Very nice and funny but extremely disorganized and difficult to reach outside of class. Respect him a lot as a person, but I do not recommend taking a class with him simply because of these issues.

This class was so much fun and I would highly recommend you take it! It consisted of a speech, 6 quizzes (one dropped), 3 tests, participation, and a final discussion (10%) of grade. As long as you read the required pages listed in the study guide you will do well on the quizzes/tests, overall very fun class and a great way to get the theory credit

He does a great job teaching and making topics understandable. As a non-poli major (took for the gen-ed credit) I found this course interesting and digestible, with a reasonable amount of work for a gen-ed.

The Reacting to History format was engaging and fun, using a historical character to do a deep dive on different parts of political history. Mr. Weidenfeld was not often available over email/outside of class and the organization of the class was not great. Most of the benefit I got was from group collaboration and challenging my perspective.

analysis.name: Mark McCombs
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 250 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Mark McCombs is possibly the most down to earth faculty member you will find in UNC's math department. He's really accessible outside of class and is pretty hilarious. I made a D on my first test, but was able to pick up my grade to B. You should definitely check out his office, it's awesome.

McCombs is a nice person, but an inadequate teacher. He repeatedly canceled class hours or minutes before the beginning of the class and did not finish teaching us all of the units necessary for the final. If you have the option to take this class with a different professor, DO IT.

Not sure what most of these reviews are on about. Although he is a great person, his lectures are incredibly confusing. You can barely hear him, he goes on long tangents on unimportant topics, and he generally makes no sense. Although his midterms can be easier than other sections, this just means the common final will be atrocious for you.

Mccombs is a very kind person. I found his lectures to be pretty unhelpful, so I skipped a lot. The best part of the class are the MyLab assignments; they allow multiple attempts, so I ended up teaching most of the course content to myself. PREPARE TO TEACH YOURSELF EVERYTHING.

This man did not know this subject. He's probably great at other math concepts that he teaches, but he even said in lecture that he does not know this subject, and he has no idea what its purpose serves. I could go on, but I feel bad, he's a nice guy but for the love of GOD he should not teach this course.

analysis.name: Niklaus Steiner
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Steiner is the BEST professor at UNC. This is not an easy class, and he makes you very aware of that at the beginning of the semester. You can definitely get an A in this class, as long as you do the readings and think deeply about the concepts. This is the most impactful class I've taken at UNC.

Dr. Steiner is great and really knowledgeable on the topics he teaches on. He genuinely cares about his students as people and wants to see them learn. Most of his grades are from essays, which he grades with a pretty high standard though. If you want an easy A, then he's not for you. But, if you want to learn, then definitely go with Dr Steiner!

Prof. Steiner is an amazing teacher, would definitely recommend taking a class with him! He's caring and passionate about the subject. It is a discussion based class, so come prepared. There is a lot of reading and material so definitely make sure to do it. The majority of the grade was in-class essays, with several small reflections and quizzes.

AMAZING class. Learned so much from Steiner and will actually apply it to real life. Lots of readings, but don't skip them because it will be evident in your work. Short reading quizzes and minimal cold calling, so come to class prepared. Group paper and 2 in-class essays for midterm and final. Do the work, be thoughtful, and you will be rewarded!

Prof. Steiner is a great guy. Gives good advice & clear feedback on writing. 

3 in-class essays & a group paper make up most of the grades, he also gives a lot of reading quizzes. Do the readings thoroughly & take lots of notes. Lots of writing, best tips are to cut the fluff & write a strong introduction. Participate in discussions & be present.

analysis.name: Briana Nave
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class has so much random rigor it's not even funny. We've had many guest speakers, all have been more engaging than her. Lesson plan assignment in particular has been nail in coffin in terms of unneccessary work. She should not be teaching this class. Great interesting subject, terrible professor and course structure. Mick A is only good TA.

Decent person, horrible lecturer. Talks condescending at times, gives a lot of tedious assignments that takes up more time than my actual major classes and didn't really feel fun or were related to the course. SOME of the TAs are unhelpful and didn't give good feedback. Made us get a textbook that we barely used. Don't take this class with her.

Absolute waste of time and energy. The grading in this class is a joke. The TAs themself don't even know what they're doing. They take off points for things that are never mentioned in the rubric for assignments. Ms. Nave speaks to her students condescendingly as if undergraduates don't know what they're doing. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Nave was okay, lecture was boring. Getting a good TA was gambling, only Mick A. knew what they were doing. I lost all interest in this class due to the constant passive aggressiveness from a certain TA and how all assignments were just busy work. Don't take this class.

Professor Bri talks to the class in an off-putting way and calls people out for not paying attention. She is very easy to contact, lectures are easy to follow, but assignments are long and tedious. Do not get me started on the TA's. Multiple people, including myself have been graded unnecessarily harshly by a TA, and in some cases they're wrong.

analysis.name: Neal Caren
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 95 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a funny professor, BUT you will be swamped with work. So many things are going on at the same time in this class (assignment wise) that it's overwhelming. You have a lot of reading to do, a lot of acting out to do, and a lot of group projects. This class is NOT an easy "A."

This was one of my most favorite classes I've taken at UNC. While you do have to put work in in reading, getting to know your character, and writing and memorizing speeches, this class truly helps you become a better public speaker. There is no judgement and the more you engage with the material and design of the class, the more fun it is.

Professor Caren is an amazing professor with such a welcoming personality. I took this course to fulfill my minor, and it was a great class with wonderful people in it as well. We have speeches to give, but the process leading up to the speeches is structured so well that you truly shouldn't feel scared. Take his class, you'll love it!

This guy goes out of his way to make studying for exams as easy as possible and hands out extra credit. Really a nice and hardworking professor. The research applications (8 per class, lowest score dropped) are kind of a lot of work but not difficult or heavily graded.

Gonna keep this short and simple. Prof Caren is the best teacher possible for SOCI101 and if he teaches it, take him. Projects are basically graded for completion and exams are pretty straightforward and if they weren't he gives us points back. Barely studied and got near-100.

analysis.name: Nadia Yaqub
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Proffesor Yaqub put together interesting readings, but was not a great lecturer. She often goes off topic and doesn't get into the meat of her lecture. She also will try and keep you after class is over to continue her lecture if she got off topic. I wish she was a better lecturer because what she has to say is often very interesting.

These classes are not easy, it is very reading heavy and she is a harsh grader. But she really cares about students and is very understanding of any outside circumstances you might have, which can't always be said for other proffessors at UNC. I was very grateful that she was so understanding.

I really enjoyed the class. Dr. Yaqub is very knowledgeable and approaches the subject very well. She is a little disorganized, and the class is reading heavy, especially for the first two exams. Other than that, I enjoyed the class and learned a lot.

This class is really not that bad. It's interesting and I learned a lot. That being said, Nadia was not a good lecturer. She's clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches, but she just doesn't do a good job teaching to such a large body of students. Students should know that her unit focuses on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

Literally the most boring lecturer I have ever had the pain of listening to. Nobody pays attention or cares about the class and she is droning on continually for the entire class. Class is not hard and she is not a hard grader, just a ton of reading and a soul-suckingly boring class.

analysis.name: Natasha Parikh
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 129 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: super nice, class was rly easy, poll everywhere everyday, labs every week for completion, assignments every week for accuracy but super easy and using jamovi. take home quizzes, midterm and final. uses piazza for participation

She was wonderful. The course was structured where you watch lectures before class and do some compression questions (but that should take about an hour at most). In class we do review, poll everywhere, and work on assignments, which is really nice because you can get a lot of help from both Dr Parikh and the ULAs/IAs. Overall a great course!!!

Amazing Professor! She made retaking stats an enjoyable experience. The one downside I had with her is that she often would respond to emails very late, and many times she wouldn't even respond. But, it was not an issue as she was very welcoming and always had time before or after class to speak. I would recommend taking a class with her!

She is a great person! But on top of that this is the best class I have taken. The lectures are actually interesting and all test are take home and open note including the midterm and final. The only thing that you are not guaranteed to get an 100 on is the in class assignment but those don't really impact your grade. Take this easiest A.

Prof. Parikh is a great professor! 210 content was a bit dull just because it's statistics focused, but she made it as interesting as it can be. Easy A! Labs are automatic 100s as long as you try, and assignments are pretty easy. I liked how detailed instructions were provided. Overall, take it with Prof. Parikh.

analysis.name: Kristin Ondrak
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 125 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Class is half async/online, half in person. Learning the content is entirely on you. It is hard to hold yourself accountable, but your grade will reflect the work you put into it. She clearly outlines exam content and the exams are fair. She's really nice and an engaging lecturer. You don't need to buy Visible Body, but it was very helpful.

Ondrak is nice and not a bad professor, but I'm leaving the bad review because there's no reason that this class should only meet one day a week and have the other day be asynchronous. Do not take this class if you need structure to hold yourself accountable for work and studying. Class was already only one day and still canceled numerous times.

This class is half async/online, half in person. This helps because learning the content is entirely on you to put in the work outside of class to memorize everything. She clearly outlines everything you need to know, and the exams are fair. She is also very nice and makes class engaging. Also, you don't necessarily need to buy Visible Body.

Ondrak was a good instructor considering the class size. Her exams are pretty straightforward, and do not try to trick you in any way. The class is extremely dense and there is so much to memorize. It was a difficult class, but she tried her best to make the class as supportive as possible. I would recommend Ondrak.

Exams were strictly memorization based but there is just A LOT of material in each exam. She is super helpful and wants you to talk to her if you need help, never be scared to reach out. There are small homework assignments and quizzes that are weekly/biweekly, if you do all of those it is a great grade boost.

analysis.name: Max Owre
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 64 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Just don't take this class. Dr. Owre simply makes the class much harder than it needs to be by assigning lots of work. I'm generally very interested in History but couldn't engage at all with his lectures, especially since he refuses to teach in chronological order and answers at least 95% of questions with "I don't know, you should look that up."

I am someone who loves all of my history classes. However, this was unlike any course I have taken prior (of which there are many). Grand total of 2 assignments graded by LDOC, insanely tough grader (free write exams - 45 min only), and unclear grading criteria. I literally had nightmares about these exams and almost didn't make it out alive.

Max gets so disorganized that it's hard to understand the point of the lectures. He gives no context for a lot of it, ultimately making it hard to understand for a beginning history class. All of the grades are based on the TA's, so you better hope you get a good one. I felt like getting an 'A' was practically impossible, even while going to hours.

I feel set up for failure in this class. I want to stay on top of the readings, but he doesn't post them for class ahead of time or even for weeks after the fact. Also, engaged activity reports  dumb. I go to every class and recitation, but still think the best possible grade I can get is a B. I feel like I work so hard but it doesn't even matter.

I wanted to like Max and this class but I just couldn't. His lectures are overly verbose and since he slacks on posting the readings, I was constantly confused about the material. It is obvious that his other job, exec. director of Carolina Public Humanities, is his priority and he doesn't make enough time to be an organized/effective professor.

analysis.name: Todd Ochoa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Todd was a enthusiastic lecturer but sometimes did not explain the material in the readings well. There were lots of readings in this class - some of them were very dense. My TA broke down the material into manageable chunks that Todd lacked in lecture. Only 2 papers but weekly small writing assignments. Very low stress!

Passionate and caring professor. The small group oriented lessons implemented for this semester were a miss (especially if you're anxious speaking in a massive class hall). Class attendance is graded but may be *ahem* bypassed relatively easily with the check-in beacon system. Lots of homework is assigned, but was ungraded and therefore optional.

Awesome professor. Really knows what he's talking about is my favorite type of nerd/geek. He really does make the class engaging and provides nice discussions in class. There is a lot of material you need to read, however Ochoa does clarify ideas and concepts from them in his lectures. I would highly suggest taking this professor.
Lots of reading and writing and the contents feel super boring and dense. Plus, this class has high threshold (95%) for getting an A. Take this class if you truly enjoy religion.

Ochoa is one of the best professors I've had at UNC. Lectures were amazing and extremely interesting, class was fun and interactive. He makes very deep topics about religion and society very accessible to people of all backgrounds. I'm a CS major and Todd made me want to add a RELI minor. Not that hard if you just do the work and skim the readings.

analysis.name: Mariana Olvera-Cravioto
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It's undeniable she is a great person passionate about the subject and accessible outside the classroom. However I would not recommend taking this if you don't have background in stats or math. The lectures are extremely confusing and require you to know the material beforehand. Hardest tests ever. If you take 435 with her good luck you'll need it.

Lower averages than other sections. Failed several of her students. Insufficient prep materials for the exams. No recorded lectures. Exams were much more challenging than other sections. Homeworks take a ridiculous amount of time to complete. Professor has been falsely represented in her ratings. You've been warned. No curves when over half fail...

I had her for 435 and 445. I really struggled through 435 and her lectures started getting pretty confusing, but shes still an amazing prof and person. I'm half way through 445 right now and I do think it's a lot easier than 435 and I am enjoying my second class with her a lot more than my first.

To be honest I did not know what to expect with a 400 level class called Introduction to Probability but it was like two weeks of introduction. PSA that you need to do calculus in this course and I spent like 14 hours a week on this class. Go to class and do extra practice problems because honestly understanding the question is half the battle.

Professor Olvera is a genius and she is extremely well spoken when it comes to statistics; however, that does not take away from how difficult this material is. If you fall behind, it is almost impossible to catch up. I respect her so much as a professor and it is clear that she wants her students to learn, but be prepared to fight for your grade.

analysis.name: Mike O’Sullivan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O'Sullivan is my favorite lecturer at UNC. He is passionate and pretty funny, although self-deprecating at times. I liked learning how history is still very relevant today in stuff like politics. Few assignments, and most are completion/effort. There is a lot of reading, but take the time to go thru everything to ace the midterm and final.

Professor O'Sullivan gave detailed lectures and made sure to show every side of the various historical debates that we covered throughout the course. He provides good feedback on writing for history and is willing to talk and answer questions outside of class in general. He is very smart but also very down-to-earth, and kind to students.

Heavy on the reading, but very entertaining lectures, talks as if he is telling a story and is easy to learn from. Easily accessible outside class, very kind and very understanding. Encourages people with no outside knowledge to take the class. Highly recommend.

Hard to take notes on his lectures, it's a LOT in a short class period. Very story telling adjacent, so he's fun to listen to if you enjoy the topics. Amusing, very caring, chill professor. Very understanding. Graded on midterm paper and final paper, and a few reader response. Lots of reading and one group presentation.

Professor O'Sullivan is so nice! The course is easy overall: 3 reader responses, a map quiz, a mid-term, and a final exam. Don't stress if you are struggling, go to his office hours and he's always willing to help. This course is reading heavy and quite fast paced, so make sure you do your readings or else you'll feel lost in class

analysis.name: Barbara Osborne
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Overall, a good professor but the class material is boring, it's based around a lot of readings and court cases, so she can only make it so interesting. The quizzes online for each chapter can be difficult but are not too hard if you go to class and pay attention. Quizzes could probably be done w/o going to class but would definitely be harder.

I took her EXSS326 summer class and she rocks. She's really funny and gets to know all her students really well. She tells personal stories related to the law that are actually interesting, and she will help you out if you're ever confused or having trouble with anything. Participation is a big part of her class.

You will not regret taking Professor Osborne! She is hands down one of the best professors I have ever had the privilege of taking. I highly recommend her course and she will always do whatever it takes to make you successful in the course. She definitely cares about her students. The course has challenging aspects of it as it is a law class.

I loved Prof. Osborne! Truly caring for her students. Her 326 class is graded 85% on open-book, open note quizzes and 15% class participation, so doing well on the quizzes really matters. I was having trouble with the quizzes for the first part of the semester and started emailing her specific quiz questions and it saved my grade. So helpful!
Not an easy course, but with 100% online quizzes you can do well on them. Attendance is optional and overall just boring lectures.

analysis.name: Michal Osterweil
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 77 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. O is odd, but I do recommend her because she'll change the way you look at the world forever. This class can be frustrating at times in the way that's like those tiktoks where the girl is like "when a man has a thought I had when I was 7," but don't take it to heart if she comes off as patronizing because she really does just want you to learn.

Dr. O is a genuinely good person who cares about the class, her students, and the content. This being said, the class is semi-disorganized and can be redundant. Lots of reading, but you only really need to do it if you're doing the reading responses. Pretty liberal and not very open to other perspectives, so prepare accordingly. Go to office hours!

Dr. O is a great professor! The class itself was honestly not too bad, you just have to keep up with some readings (and you can honestly get away with not doing a lot of them). The tests were mostly short response with some multiple choice, but Dr. O and the TAs grade pretty leniently. Overall, fun and straightforward class!

We meditated before each class, which was kind of cool in my opinion. The course material is interesting and progressive, if you're into that stuff. The papers and exams were graded very leniently. If you can showcase within them that you did the readings / kept up with class, you will do very well. Attendance is not mandatory, but I recommend it.

Dr. Osterweil's class was definitely the most unique I've ever taken really - it is obvious she cares about the material very deeply and really gets you thinking. Even though the class could've been a bit more organized and straightforward, I really enjoyed the energy and knowledge she brought to the course. She's also very kind, open, and driven.

analysis.name: Timothy Ott
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Attendance played a big role in grading. Students were often asked to upload photos, which were then used to track attendance. The class felt quite boring, relied heavily on cold calling, and the slides were very amateur and could be much better. Overall, grades seemed to be based more on attendance than on actual learning or engagement.

Long cases and a quiz required for every lecture, were just a large amount of time and super exhausting. Ott is a good lecturer, however, the final project (which is a presentation) is a large amount of time and the average for the final project was a 75. I felt like it was hard to know what he was looking for since the TA graded our quizzes

I personally like Prof Ott, but know others who didn't. He's a tough grader, good lecturer and a nice guy. This course is based on 9 case studies with quizzes on each and a final group project. Grade-wise, it's 30% - Participation, 40% - Quizzes, 30% - Group Project. This class has a lot of reading, and if you do it, you'll do well.

analysis.name: Zlatko Plese
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Zlatko is truly an inspirational professor and someone who knows how to keep students engaged. The class had lotssss of reading but it was mostly very interesting. Really nice professor and a challenging, rewarding course

Z-Man is amazing. He keeps you engaged in all of his lectures and is super funny. He really expects you to talk and answer his questions but if you do the reading then it's not hard. I would take him again in a heart beat
It has been 4 years since I have graduated, and I still have respect for the man. His class was one of the most memorable for me in my career at Carolina.

Z-man is a great man and scholar, but an awful teacher. His disorganized teaching style, combined with the esoteric/incomprehensible subject material makes for an absolutely baffling class. He doesn't post grades until the last week, gives rubrics for nothing, and will never assign anything normally on canvas -- only through announcements.

one of the meanest professors I've ever had. one of my best friends & I took this class together, and she got low-key persecuted the whole class by the professor. He was unbelievably rude to her & conveyed no respect over emails. He will say criticisms in the most unnecessarily condescending ways. also, 0 structure, no curves, & interrupts you.

analysis.name: Shane Peterson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Peterson is an amazing guy and really cares about what he is teaching. I took him for his game studies class and I really enjoyed it. I am NOT a gamer but the class was still very easy. It's mainly group projects and essays, but every assignment was done step-by-step. We also always had a long time to do each assignment. I would take him.

His grading doesn't go by points, so everything in Canvas was just shown as "completed" meaning you don't know what grade you have in the class until the semesters over. Still, he's really nice and makes games studies interesting. If you wanna play some games, try to take his class.

He's nice enough, but can be a bit annoying. It all depends on what type of person you are, but sometimes I found his humor to be a bit off and it made it hard to take him seriously. He is a passionate guy, and his lectures were fine but nothing special. I wouldn't say never take him, but if the millennial humor style annoys you maybe avoid it.

Peterson, himself, is fine. His lectures are nothing special but he clearly knows his information. His assignments are not enjoyable nor are they helpful. The class itself is difficult and a poor representation of UNC's classes. The class is extremely difficult to recover from if receiving even a 70 on anything so I do not suggest.

IDST118 is a very boring and semi-difficult triple-I, but unexpectedly, I enjoyed Peterson's lectures the most. His assignments are usually rhetoric and analysis-based, so if you know how to write those assignments will help your grade in the class. His content is easy for quiz questions too.

analysis.name: Oluremi Abayomi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 115 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Beware of this class! It is insanely challenging for an intro-level course. There are no HW/lab drops or curves. You could be on your deathbed and Dr Remi still would not give you an extension. Never answers emails and talks down to you during office hours and when asking questions in class. Goes indepth on easy concepts, but breezes by hard ones.

This class and Professor Abayomi's teaching was not very intuitive for someone who doesn't have any coding/limited stats experience. It isn't necessarily extremely challenging, but I would recommend taking this class when you have a lot of time to rewatch Abayomi's lectures and dedicate to the labs. He is funny and friendly, but pretty strict

The class itself is useful, but the grading was unnecessarily nit-picky. The professor was egotistical and unwilling to answer any questions or provide any sort of help. They spoke with an air of superiority and disrespect that I've never received from any other human being. I've never cried so much over a class. Do not take this class.

This class is just a cheap knockoff of UC Berkeley's Data8—he's stealing their work word by word and claims it as his own. At times he would switch the states from CA to NC to not make it as obvious. If you want to get a feel of how the class would be I encourage you to look it up, and practice. You'll pass the class with flying colors!

Dr. Remi was a very thorough teacher but was very condescending as a professor. He had very little patience and was rude to students on occasion. While his lectures were thorough, he spent a lot of time explaining simple concepts that everyone already knew.

analysis.name: Pello Huesa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is one of the most personable, funny, and caring professors I have ever met. He is a tough grader, but he is always understanding and gives great feedback to improve. The way he acts out words sometimes is so funny. He always tries to be a good professor, and he does great. I would take this class ten times over, he's so great.

Professor Huesa is super nice and explains class content very well. The class requires a good amount of effort and studying, but it's not too overwhelming. Class is very interactive, so I definitely recommend making it to as many classes as you can and participating a lot. He is also very accommodating and understanding if you have any issues.

This professor refuses to take into account that his students are learning a new language. He grades as if we are fluent... and we are not. For the spanish major we have to have 261, and despite my love for learning spanish, I would NEVER take this class with him again - i don;t even know if Spanish is for me anymore because of him. DO NOT DO IT!!!

He is the worst grader I have ever had at UNC. He takes off points in almost every single sentence, but when you try to talk to him he doesn't tell you how your fluency can be improved. He will make you laugh in class, but cry every night. Worst professor at the UNC spanish department, if you ask me, and I've had almost 8 professors at this point.

Insane amount of homework, very harsh grader. He's a good lecturer, I had him twice but he was a lot harsher for this class. I would not take this class with him if I had known. Also seems to cater to native speakers so fair warning. He's very approachable and nice but as a professor I would not recommend to a friend.

analysis.name: Tony  Patterson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great and engaging professor, but meh class (very boring material at times). All classes he teaches are graded by a total of 100 points, so just make sure to be on top of assignments. Exams are online and are pretty easy. Be careful about letting the little points missed add up and tank your grade, as it happened to multiple students.

Tony is the goat! He is so fun, a great professor, and really knowledgeable about the subject he teaches! He wants all students to succeed and is so caring. The class environment is super chill and he makes it enjoyable to go to. I would take him over and over again if I could! The work is super easy as well, guaranteed A!

Dr. Patterson is wonderful and gave me a lot of opportunities within the Sport Admin realm. I have test anxiety so I struggled on the midterm (which is to account for my A-), but if that's not a huge issue for you, the tests aren't hard, you just HAVE to read the textbook.

Very very easy class I took over the summer. Do the work and read the assigned chapters, you're guaranteed an A. I highly recommend anyone who needs it for a gen ed or just as an elective to boost gpa. Would take any class this man teaches if I need for credit or have room for extra classes to boost my gpa. A great class

Dr. Patterson is a very kind and understanding man. With my tough schedule this semester, this class was a breath of fresh air every day. This class was not hard at all and if you do your work you are pretty much guaranteed a good grade.  Dr. Patterson is very easygoing and you can tell he cares about his students.

analysis.name: David Parr
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Parr is one of the best professors I have had at UNC - he is very caring, and genuinely just wants his students to learn. This is really exemplified with his 'unique' grading scale he has in place - it makes the class less stressful because it's a lot easier to get an A and you can focus more on course content and work than fighting over points

Really good grading scheme that made it low-stakes and extremely easy to get an A. If you get an 80% cumulative avg b/w the 2 exams, complete 8/9 assignments, complete 3 small projects, and deliver 1 presentation, you will be guaranteed an A in the class basically. As a teacher, Dr. Parr is accessible and really understands how to teach new coders.

Dr. Parr is the goat. The grading criteria are clear, and he prioritizes the students' learning over exams. With how the class is set up, getting an "A" is achievable as long as you're not lazy. All the resources are there, and the lectures are engaging. Dr. Parr is a cool professor who is willing to help a student learn and grow in the class.

LOVE DR.PARR! Took both 215 and 370 with him. You definitely need to learn the concepts because you need to code yourself in the assignments, but 90% of them you copy and paste from his example. His exams come straight from the assessments. Definitely an easy A, but you need to put a little work in. Please be nice and engage in class- he cares.

This class is an easy A IF you do the work. The final project was interesting, the final exam was easy if you come to class throughout the semester, and the lectures were straightforward. I respect Dr. Parr immensely for emphasizing learning over grades in today's academic system. I actually remember everything I learned in this class!

analysis.name: Roxana Perez-Mendez
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: -extremely unclear due dates -no sakai use -no updated grade  everyone was terrified of failing -inconsistent expectations for attendance and participation -no clear guidelines for any projects -helpful critiques

She's an accomplished artist and has made some great work but admittedly doesn't want to teach and this blasé attitude is evident in her lack of syllabi, unclear instructions, non-existent due dates, and spotty class attendance. As a one-on-one advisor, she can be very helpful. Unfortunately, she is the only sculpture professor at UNC.

Gave very vague instruction and would often change up what she wanted from you. Never ask her for advice on a project because she will most likely dismiss all of it and tell you you did the entire thing wrong. The class material would be interesting, but lectures drag on and are boring. Some of the projects were fun.

It has been a week since LDOC, and she has not submitted any grades so far. When you ask for feedback on a project, she is very vague and not helpful. There are better first-year seminars than this course. It is very lecture-heavy and boring when not completing projects. The professor is kind, but does not grade on time.
this professor was not kind or understanding, nor accommodating. class was incredibly boring too.

analysis.name: Angela Pratt
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is mainly centered around a group project with different assignments throughout the semester. The groups are random so be ready to make up for your groups lack or work. She is a pretty tough grader. 1 midterm and 1 final, both are allowed a 1 page cheat sheet which really helps (its straight from textbook). Most classes are optional!

Dr. Pratt is an excellent support system to get you through this class. She is very compassionate, and genuinely wants her students to succeed. EXSS 493 is hard no matter which way you cut it (reaching the required hours is the hard part) but she gives very good feedback and is generally very understanding about any issues you might come across.

Pratt is extremely kind in person, but is also an extremely stingy, tough grader. The course is group project heavy (all randomly assigned groups), so be prepared to put in overtime to make up for others' lack of work. Exams are straight from the book and can be challenging, but not impossible, as she allows a note page while you take it.

Would not recommend, only take her if it's a last resort. Takes off way too many unnecessary points, grades way too hard, it's like she grades papers how she wants to see them, and doesn't understand that she can't grade by her biases. Like papers are subjective, keep your opinions to yourself??

Dr. Pratt is knowledge about her topics and is a nice person, I found it difficult to engage in her lectures and she is a relatively tough grader in comparison to my other exss classes. The group projects are easy but grades were not released which was frustrating. A few extra credit ops– take advantage Read the textbook chapters or fail the exams

analysis.name: Yue Qiu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Qiu does not explain concepts in class: he reads straight from the PowerPoints. He doesn't even try, even if students ask him to write out explanations in class. Stay away, if possible. I do not know why he is teaching intro physics as he does not seem to care whatsoever.

This is for PHYS115 but I agree this guy needs to take a public speaking class before he can lecture.  I can't imagine him teaching his own class don't take him if you don't want to raise your cortisol levels.

This is actually for Phys 115. I cannot hear Qiu, he just reads off the slides and WHISPERS. He doesnt explain anything or write anything to solve it he just talks. Please avoid him, you will not learn.

Professor Qiu struggled to read the slideshows, which made understanding difficult physics topics even harder. In fact, I got a better grade in 118 than 114 just because of how bad professor Qiu was. He also never answers questions, always seems nervous to lecture, and seems so out of touch with his students. if you have a class with him, DROP IT.

Just don't. It's clear he's very nervous up there and I feel bad for the guy, but you literally can't hear a word of what he says. And I sit near the front of the lecture hall. He's someone who may be too smart for his own good. It's much more productive to watch the YouTube lectures from 2020 during class and follow along with poll everywhere.

analysis.name: Qing Gong
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Gong was a great professor because she actually put effort into teaching rather than the flipped classroom style of some other econ classes. Problems challenged us and really tested our understanding of the material without being "trick questions." I loved this class and thought it was relevant to contemporary policy problems.

Dr. Gong is one of the best econ professors I've had. You can clearly tell that she is passionate about the subject, and mentions real life applications. If you're confused on anything, Dr. Gong will clarify everything during office hours. The class isn't as easy as some claim, and you do have to put in effort.

I LOVED her. She doesn't try to trick you at all and gives you everything you need to succeed. Exams are extremely similar to problem sets and hw. She is always there to help if anything is needed and such a nice person. Can't speak highly enough about her!! 100% take this as an Econ elective.

Dr. Gong is a really great professor and lenient grader. She really wants you to do well which is uncommon in UNC Econ. Best professor I have had in UNC Econ not because I did well but she is so passionate about teaching. This is good to see and something that UNC Econ needs more of.

Professor Gong was one of the kindest professors I have ever had. She is very accessible outside of class and she genuinely wants to help you succeed. The class consists of short homework assignments and one group project that you work on throughout the semester. I cannot recommend this class and Professor Gong enough. Take this class if you can!!

analysis.name: Roberto Quercia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enrolled in PLAN363 for a free A, and I wish I hadn't abused this class as much as I did (attendance-wise). He is genuinely so kind and clearly cares about what he is presenting. Please make sure to go to his classes, he teaches very valuable information that I wish I didn't take for granted. Highly recommend!

He is very unclear in his lectures about the topics that we actually need to know. Also..what a snooze fest., and he doesn't know how to work technology AT ALL. If you want the class for somewhat easy credit then sure, take the class, but don't expect to come out of it knowing anything useful about personal finance that you can't find online.
Very easy class if you want an A, The lectures can get a tad boring but again, it's easy and you could get an A just zoning out in lectures and reading the slides later.

TA's did majority of grading and gave good feedback, class was not hard at all, although the lectures could be boring at times.  Quizzes came straight from the slides as well as the final, which was online.  Pretty useful class and information.  Final questions were pulled from quizzes

Very easy class, good easy A. There is a financial plan that TAs grade, my year the TA's were very nice. There are 2 "true/false" questions every class to make sure you're present. Those were kind of annoying but you can find the answer pretty easily. The quizzes were 10 questions (there were 3) those were also pretty easy. Final was online.

analysis.name: Qi Zhang
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a sweet person who cares about students and someone who likes to see you truly understand and learn from class content. This is the most diverse class I have every took with people coming from all kinds of backgrounds and ages. 10/10 would recommend!

Dr. Qi is an amazing professor, who offers great and enjoyable experience to students in class. He does excellent jobs to help students understand the concepts and develop programming skills with hands-on exercises. He is ready to give feedback and cares about your performance. I would definitely take his other classes if any.

I absolutely loved Prof. Zhang! He is such a nice, caring, and considerate guy. Definitely one of the best professors I had at UNC, and I will for sure take his class again. He gives really good lectures. Do not hesitate to take his class, it's an easy A, I promise.

I enjoyed this class & Qi's teaching; it was one of my top 3 at UNC. He often gave extensions and was great with partial credit for late work. There were times in class where he didn't give us answers, but after he hinted that the question was on the midterm! Attendance & group work are important, but I'd def take another class with Qi

Taking Geog 567 with Dr Qi was a honor. I left this class with more knowledge, super cool projects, and the desire to learn more. Dr Qi went out of his way to make sure I was learning and understanding the material. He would encourage me and I never felt stupid. I wish I could take all my classes with him.

analysis.name: Qi Sun
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The worst math professor I've had. His lectures are extremely difficult to understand and follow. It's much easier to understand the course by just reading the textbook, but since he does some proofs in lecture only and won't publish those notes, you still have to go to class. He did not curve any midterms despite a plurality of students failing.

I took MATH566 with him. HARDEST B- OF MY LIFE. I did all the homework, read through the textbook multiple times, and took great notes, and still ended up with a 70 avg on the midterms (he doesn't curve btw). I missed ONE CLASS the whole semester, and missed one proof (not in the textbook) that he then made 20% of a whole exam grade. DO NOT TAKE

The worst professor I have ever had. In addition to everything else that has been said, he simply doesn't care about teaching. I went to his OH 30 minutes before they ended, and right after I knocked on his door, he proceeded to pack up his things and leave while ignoring me. Impossible to reach over email. Didn't curve midterms. Don't take!

Not a great lecturer, hard to understand and kinda just teaches from the textbook but these reviews are unnecessarily harsh. Sun is a bro. Nice guy, pretty chill dude, helps students as much as he can while preserving reasonable course standards. Small quizzes instead of HW, easy exams with no trick questions (usually just copies of book problems).

The worst professor I have ever had at UNC. Exams were strictly based on textbook proofs, homework questions, or proofs in lecture. Lecture notes not given and textbook gave computational algorithms while our exams were by hand. Mostly a kind person to talk to but can be rather condescending when trying to learn and ask questions. Never take.

analysis.name: Wei Quan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: overwhelming emphasis on research, neglect teaching responsibilities. The pressure to publish papers and secure funding often overshadows commitment to delivering engaging and high-quality lessons.  Adopt a dismissive or authoritarian attitude towards students, which discourages open dialogue and critical thinking in the classroom.
Wei needs to improve his  expression skills, probably because his mother tongue is not English, and sometimes I can't fully understand what Wei wants to express in class.

I took the German summer course online, and unfortunately, I found the experience quite frustrating. While I understand the challenges of teaching virtually, I felt that the instructor was not well-prepared for the online format. The instructions were often unclear, and communication lacked consistency.
Won't recommend this course for beginners
Very bad attitude and arrogant

analysis.name: Andreas Quist
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Quist is pretty chill for M130 He knows his stuff but sometimes he speeds through it. If you don't get smth,hit him up during office hours.He gives good feedback if you actually ask for it. His lectures can get kinda dry, like my skin (i have eczema), but if you stay focused, you'll be good. Hes a prof who cares & knows what he's talking about

Professor Andreas isn't the best professor for math 130. He does have very good "teaching" skills and doesn't know how to explain the content well. However if you are able to go to office hours and have one on one time he does go into more depth about a concept. To do well on the exams just go over study guides prior to. He repeats questions.

Andreas is not a very good teacher. He goes through the information way too fast. He shows it and does not explain methods. If you ask a question during lecture you will end up more confused. Andreas also missed and canceled many lectures in the middle of fall. Our class asked for him to postpone the test or review more and he said no.

He missed a lot of classes during the middle of the semester which made it really hard to understand the material and do well. The tests are very hard but he gives a ton of partial credit. He is never available outside of class and doesn't respond to emails, ever, no matter what. I would definitely take another teacher for the course.

Professor Quist wasn't a great teacher; he would miss classes and he was new to teaching so most lectures were confusing. I didn't even really pay attention during lectures, I just did the pre-class work and studied well before the exams. But he did offer extra credit on tests and made good study guides for the exams.

analysis.name: Brenda Quinones-Ayala
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Quinones-Ayala was an absolute joy to have as a professor. So caring, enthusiastic, and engaging with her students. Spanish 203 is a hard class, but she was very encouraging if you ever made mistakes and would explain them in a very understandable way. Some of her grading took a long time but I can't even care because of how amazing she was.

Funny and bubbly- Brenda is my favorite out of all instructors I've had thus far at UNC.  She's caring, passionate, personable, and truly understands the Spanish language (as she is a native Puerto Rican.)   I went to office hours for help on a paper & she not only worked through my paper with me, but also asked about my interests and future plans.

Dr. QA was extremely kind, caring, enthusiastic, understanding, and accommodating. I am not the best Spanish speaker but was able to get through this class because I made an effort. If you care, you will do fine because she cares! A great option (if not one of the best) for 203.

Genuinely one of the best professors I have encountered during my time at UNC. Take her class if you can, while SPAN203 can be difficult, she will do anything to support you and make learning Spanish fun and accessible.

There is a lot of pressure to be conversationally perfect, and if you aren't you will pay for it. Professor QA can be very nitpicky about some grammar topics and completely lenient in others. The textbook is mostly useless, easy assignments rather than content. Don't take this class to learn, take this class if you know Spanish and want the credit.

analysis.name: Tine Rassalle
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: For Ohio Wesleyan University; Hebrew Bible class. Her class is difficult, but it was one of the most rewarding classes I have taken. She is also incredibly kind and understanding, allows late work when needed. Didn't use textbook, still passed. If you're willing to buckle down and study, take good notes, and write fast, then definitely recommend.

This is for Ohio Wesleyan's REL111 class, Dr. Rassalle Lectures for the whole 1 hour and 20 minute class period, and is rarely interactive with the class with activities. 2 page essay duefor every class, and readings that can possibly take up to 3-4 hours to complete each class. Midterms are so much information it is nearly impossible. Do not take

Tine is great! Responds to emails super quickly (even after 5pm on weekends) and was very understanding and kind. Course material is DENSE and you will write a ton of mini papers (one 500-word essay or three 100-word essays every other day). Quizzes were easy but exams were near impossible & very detailed. Also didn't like not having weekends off.

Tine was a great teacher. She handled the online class format really well, and she was readily available via Sakai message or email. She was obviously super interested in the subject she was teaching, and she made the material interesting and engaging. Because of her class, I'm taking another religion course this semester. Take her class!

I was worried about taking an online class at UNC because I have hear they could be disorganized, but Tine has made this class so easy to follow. She is really on top of communication, gives you all the resources you need to succeed, and really cares about students. She is very passionate and you will get an A if you put in the effort.

analysis.name: Quoc Tran-Dinh
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 52 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Tran-Dinh, in both his first year of teaching and first year in the country, graded strictly, and rapport with students was nonexistent. He seems like a very nice man, but lectures were confusing, and office hours confused concepts further. Definitely the hardest professor for STOR 113. Hopefully his teaching will improve with experience.
Class itself is very boring, but he gives extra credit opportunities and curves a lot

415 is a very boring class compared to others in the statistics major. Quoc is an okay professor, but implements strange curves and refuses to give back points when his TAs make grading mistakes. Lots of tedious homework that isn't always relevant to what is tested. But overall, relatively fair class

Quoc taught a new course and, considering the difficulty in balancing a new course, did a great job designing it. He adjusted the pace of the course when he realized we were struggling and provided sufficient feedback on assignments. The tests and quizzes were very difficult, but he curved appropriately. Reasonably understanding if you reach out.

This class is essentially applied calculus. I never took calc in high school so I found this class to be extremely difficult (If you're familiar with calc you should be fine). Quoc is a nice man but it can be difficult to understand his lectures, and I usually regretted attending them because I'd have to teach myself the material at home anyways.

analysis.name: Timothy Ryan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Genuinely my hardest class as a PRE MED. Tougher grader than the chem department. All exams are open note, yet I never made higher than a 62. He will assign 50-70 pages of readings A DAY and will pop quiz you or call on you so watch out. He has no grading criteria or rubric and is just rude about you not understanding content other needing help.

I took POLI 100H with TJR and it was honestly the most frustrating class. He told the class that he “doesn't give A's." Others reached out to me because they felt I was being singled out during conversations. I never explicitly shared my political views, but it sometimes felt like certain perspectives were treated less favorably in discussion.

Timothy Ryan is the worst professor I have ever had. He provided little feedback and EXTREMELY unfair grades on the few papers and exams we had. His grading is very inconsistent–he took points off my work for things that he did not for other students. He is VERY stuck up. Go ahead TJR, attach your "Course Evaluations" - they just prove my point.

TJR might be the worst professor on the east coast. He grades based on an algorithm that he does not share with students. Only about eight assignments/exams for the whole class and he provides little support and when combined with his extremely harsh grading, this is a hard class to get a good grade. Please, DO NOT take this class. It really sucks.

Dr Ryan might be the most stuck-up and pretentious person I have ever met. He is wholly in love with himself. He grades holistically and makes up grading criteria as he goes along. When you go to office hours, he only answers in riddles. I would rather stick my hand in a cheese grater than ever take another class with Dr Ryan again.

analysis.name: Ryan Urquhart
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The other reviews aren't wrong, he definitely gets cross with the class sometimes. However, he did a good job of putting us in an entrepreneurial mindset and I got more out of this class than I was expecting. He also offered to write us a LoR for grad school which was unprecedented. Was he my favorite prof? No, but he far exceeded my expectations.

Amazing professor. If you're struggling in this class, it's not on him it's on you. He's tough, blunt, and expects you to act like an adult. People who complain are just soft and not ready for real expectations. If you can "handle" honesty and want to actually learn, take his class. Highly recommend.

I read the comments and had some apprehension coming into the class. I was amazed about how the comments were totally wrong. I'm a Jr and many of the ppl were Sr. who were complaining. All you had to do was come to class, complete the assignments. He was always available to meet via zoom, b4 or after class. Don't pay attn to the crybaby comments

Dr. Urquhart is a great prof who won't shy away from sharing his real-world experience with the class. Teaching-wise, he's very direct and has been using the same assignments since forever, so there are clear expectations. However, since the semester project is a group one, you better pray for good teammates. Good class and great portfolio booster.

This class was a huge waste of time. I heard that 382 with other professors is actually really helpful but I feel like I didn't learn anything. he was not clear at all on what he wanted and graded harshly. Didn't learn much he seems like a nice guy but takes himself too serious and doesn't teach any material. You have to cheat on quizzes due to ts

analysis.name: Saiful Tamim
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Wonderful professor, gives clear explanation for all concepts. Cares about his students, very accommodating. Class is not difficult if you engage with the material, do the homework, and practice problems. There is nothing on exams that is not covered in class; very straightforward, I got a 100% on every exam. Lowest exam grade replaced w/final.

Truthfully, I did not enjoy a single class period of his. We either had boring lectures where I regretted showing up or times he didn't even show up... I spent most of the time teaching myself the material. He doesn't respond quickly to emails, provides little feedback, and overall, is just disorderly. Fair tests were the only good thing.

Saiful is a great lecturer and teaches 383 very well. It can be fast if you aren't well-rooted in previous math classes, but it is still doable. He is nice, pretty funny, and considerate. It is best to go over lecture notes and provided worksheets to study for his midterms and finals. The tests are hard and worth a lot of your grade, study.

Lectures are a little fast and he assumes you know stuff that he hasn't taught often. Seems like he would be a great prof for higher level math but not the best for the basics. Exams are very fair and cover the same kinds of problems that we did in class. Lowest midterm gets replaced by the final.

Great for a math prof. Got an A. Let us replace our lowest test score with our final if it was higher. TONS of resources available for outside of class (i.e. practice problems, so if you do all of the practice you'll do well on exams). Never puts anything on the exams that we haven't covered in class with practice problems or in previous exams.

analysis.name: Steve May
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor May is an amazing lecturer, people have a "just get it done" attitude in this class, and it is unfortunate. He makes difficult concepts easy to understand. He is extremely accessible outside of class, I once emailed him about the lecture slides, and he got back to me within the hour with the slides from that chapter and the one after.

Hereallycaresabout the topic butsometimes overexplainedwhatsomethingmeantmaking it a bit confusing. He hosted review sessions before the midterm and final as well as giving us a list of the topics that were going to appear. Youhavetoread a lot, but I gotawaywithnotbyjustpayingattentionto the lecturesandtakingnotesbecausehetalks about the readings.

I really enjoyed his lectures. He was pretty engaging and made confusing theories and concepts relatable and easy to understand. There is a good amount of reading and notes but I highly recommend doing them. Overall the class was pretty straightforward and a good start for the comm major.

I think I lost brain cells during his lectures. Better off doing poppers. 2 essays, midterm, and final exam= entirety of your graded work. Very easy and only requires common sense; no reading of textbook is necessary. The recitations felt like I was at summer camp. Cannot believe this is a required college-level class, a 10-year-old could pass it.

He is knowledgeable and passionate about his teachings. Fairly easy class, note taking during lectures can be important as there is not much info on the slides to look back on. The nights before the midterm and final he hosted exam reviews which was very helpful as it was an opportunity to ask any questions we had which he would answer in detail.

analysis.name: Timothy Marr
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof Marr is a nice guy, but his class is very unorganized and very hard to follow. No guidelines for essays; he grades based on his opinion. Huge final project as well as midterm and final. There's a reason there are seats open in class.

Professor Marr is incredibly intelligent and is knowledgeable about the lecture topics. However, the lectures can sometimes be boring and he rambles so for the final I recommend rewatching the recorded classes. Also, some assignments come out of no where and that feels overwhelming. He is a sweet guy but holds a higher standard than most100classes.

While Prof. Marr is one of the sweetest professors I've had, the structure of this class made it difficult for me to enjoy. Super interesting concepts even if he is a bit long-winded. I didn't mind that but ALL of his assignments have lengthy, vague instructions with high expectations of content. I was constantly asking my TA for clarification.

Unrealistic reading expectations (150 pages between Monday and Wednesday), along with vague assignment criteria. Very high expectations for a gen-ed. Classes were boring and very repetitive. Also, he cares a lot about participation so get ready to be cold called if you don't like speaking up (or don't do readings like me & most ppl in the class).

Has an unreasonable amount of reading due during the week, with very little actual directions on how to complete the annotations on them, and when to do them by. Lectures are impossible to take notes on because he just will put up one slide and ramble on for minutes on end. Other students and the TA's rarely had an idea about what was going on.

analysis.name: Uffe Bergeton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr Bergeton clearly cares a lot about the content but his lectures were not very captivating as someone who didn't already have a passion for the topic. I did enjoy the freedom in the final paper which allowed me to dive into really any aspect of Qin and Han history/culture. If you already know you love the topic, you'll enjoy this more than I did.

He definitely knows what he's talking about, but is terrible at teaching a simplified version of it. He goes off on really long unrelated tangents and is generally confusing. Definitely go to office hours because he is picky. Not to mention, he is white but claims to be "Chinese" as a result of marrying a Chinese woman.

There are quite a lot of readings, but they all relate in a way and most of the readings are online. 2 essays, one being the midterm, and the final being a 10pg paper along with a 5 min presentation. He is a very generous grader and the lectures were pretty interesting. He holds office hours for essay critique so you can score better on the essays.
hard course but he is a nice guy.the materials are hard though, i don't know the stories in the slides even though I'm a Chinese

His lecture is dry and boring. He wants participation but belittles students' opinions that don't align with his. He has a very Euro-centric view on eastern history and culture. He often suggests that because a student doesn't speak English natively, they aren't good at writing in English. But he does give extensions for papers.

analysis.name: Elaine Townsend Utin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING! Elaine is a true gem and I would HIGHLY recommend anyone to take her class. It is full of so much helpful and important information and she has passion behind everything she does. She is also super compassionate, and understanding of the chaos that was 2020. She held plenty of spaces for healing and for growth in combination with learning.
