As an Education Professor Elaine really knows how to effectively foster a nurturing learning environment where everybody feels heard and respected. She is sweet and fun and lights up every class with her bright attitude and passion for what she teaches. She may honestly be too good for the classes she teaches. She takes radical pedagogy seriously.

Profe is amazing and a true gem at UNC. Her class is so interesting and a must take for any Latine person at UNC. It is a great class to explore your own identity and understand the world around you. Profe creates a safe space for people to be vulnerable and honest about their experiences. You really begin to feel at home in class.

analysis.name: James Umbanhowar
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Terrible.  Not even worth going to class.  I started reading the book before the class lectures and I started to think I could have taught the class better than he did.  He stutters a lot and spends the vast majority of the time talking about simple concepts and completely avoids the nitty-gritty details.  I also hated his voice.
Absolutely terrible.  Lectures made 0 sense. The recitations are the only thing that  saved me from failing

It is true that his lectures are a little vague and he speaks really fast but there is a lot information that he has to cover in a small amount of time. He tries his best to be helpful and make the class interesting and overall is not a bad professor. The class is tough but the exams are not impossible and the curve is usually pretty good.

Umbanhowar's lectures are worthless. He stands up there and discusses vague examples and graphs, and doesn't have a clear point. It's better to just read the textbook to understand the material. The tests aren't too hard and are curved ALOT because everyone does poorly. I would stay away from him and his poor ecology teachings.

You definitely need to have a good understanding of stats to take this class (and understand it). You can get by with all of the assignments by going to office hours and simply doing the assignments (those are 80% of the grade and no exams), but you won't really understand it without a baseline understanding of stats.

analysis.name: Peter Uhlenberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall his class is very enjoyable, he makes the class very interesting. Although the class might seem very easy watch out! His exams are very detailed you have to really know it all. A lot of reading, in the book and articles he assigns. Overall I liked him

analysis.name: Melissa Venegas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Profesora Venegas was a great professor! She's super caring and made classes enjoyable. The SPAN 261 curriculum (at least when I took it in fall 2024) was standardized between all of the professors, so I can't really say anything about the course itself that applies to just her. I'd definitely take a class with her again though!

She is the most caring and understanding teacher I have ever had! There's homework for most class days but it doesn't take long at all. One midterm and one final exam and a project. I would highly recommend taking span 267 with her. She is not a harsh grader at all and gives helpful feedback.

She seems nice, but I was having a tough time understanding the concepts, and when I approached her during office hours, she refused to help. She also grades very strictly and gives few and unhelpful comments. The class as a whole is set up awfully, but that's the department's fault.

Professor Venegas clearly cared about the content shown in class in context to our heritages as students. She is super bubbly and provides a comfortable environment to discuss perspectives on the material provided. Gonna miss her and mis compañeros!

Professora Venegas is a wonderful lecturer and a great Spanish teacher!! She is very sweet and understanding so never hesitate to go and talk to her. Her grading is also pretty chill and she will help you as much as she can. There's a lot of in-class participation and quite a few quizzes but just pay attention to deadlines and you'll be good.

analysis.name: Pablo Vega
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Pablo is an incredible teacher. I took this class fall of 2024, and he canceled class a lot - this has since changed in later classes. For the final project, we recorded and mixed a live performance, and we only had 2 analysis papers and 2 music projects, plus 2 quizzes. He takes a while to return grades but pushing back our due dates as a 'sorry'.

The classes were not organized very well. His feedback on assignments was often limited to only 2 words. Assignments should have been more hands on instead of watching him read off a doc for an hour. Obvious this is just a paycheck for him, but an easy grader.

Professor Vega is extremely knowledgable. can't really teach. I could have learned so much from him except that we barely got through any material. Cancelled class all the time, didn't grade anything till the last week, but did give feedback on assignments.
Pablo is absolutely the best professor! Super awesome and so gifted!

Pablo was super nice and the class work was not super hard. There was an online quiz that i missed as I had work and it brought my grade down to a B- from and A. I was not allowed to take it with a penalty or anything, just lost the points. This was frustrating as the class was not supposed to hurt my gpa and inevitably did.

analysis.name: Beril Ulku-Steiner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Had a phony and fake nice personality in lecture but if you approached her one on one, she was inflexible both in her availability and in her willingness to help outside of class. She assigns an case study paper with vague and unclear parameters and expectations, and she has questions on the test from videos we watched in class weeks earlier. SUCK!

Dr. U-S will come to class every day cheery and smiley but DONT LET IT FOOL YOU. It is mandatory to go to class even though the way you will learn the material is purely through reading - she does not help. She will assign a group project and about 11 pg paper but don't count on a good grade, she'll rip you on both no doubt. Tests are ok if you stu

She smiles a lot; don't let it fool you.  Instructions for things are completely unclear.  EXTREMELY harsh grader, tests on things that we never talked about in class.  Scope of information way too large.  Extremely picky.  She was late to every meeting I had with her (meetings that she required), didn't show up, or just postponed them last minute.

Although she was a bubbly professor at 8 AM, I learned very quickly that turns into a very condescending demeanor. She grades incredibly tough and does not give good feedback. It's really disappointing considering how much I was looking forward to this class. The lectures were mandatory but not helpful, pretty much taught myself all the material.

If you can avoid taking Professor US for Abnormal Psyc (or any class), then PLEASE DO. Horrible professor. Ridiculous grader. The group project and accompanying paper was a complete joke, as she graded unfairly, extremely harsh and her rubric was unclear. Don't let the happy demeanor fool you. Also, 1 unexcused abstence failing attendance grade.

analysis.name: Krysten Voelkner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Krysten was awesome. Her class is environmentally focused, which is not usually something I would enjoy focusing on, but she ran it so well that I ended up liking it a lot. She encourages discussions/debate in class (especially materialism vs. idealism). If you are a reasonably strong writer, you will have zero issues and appreciate the discussions

Krysten is such a unique and interesting professor to have. She really just cares about you becoming a better writer, without making you jump through hoops. She is very clear on what she is looking for and will let you resubmit papers for a regrade if you are not happy. I think most people in this class will end with an A.

She was great, very approachable, an excellent choice for ENGL105. The class will be environmentally focused, even if you're taking a specific concentration of the class like humanities. I found her grading to be very lenient, everything I turned in was an easy A.

She is great. She's super down-to-earth, gives no tests, and pretty much grades all projections/essays on completion(I ended with a 100.0), as long as you put effort and follow her instructions. She focuses a lot on plants from various perspectives to teach class, so if you find that boring, she may not be for you, but definitely extremely easy A.
Her Engl105 is focused around environmental studies, which usually bores me to death, but she kept things interesting. If you're a competent writer you'll be absolutely find with her.

analysis.name: Maharshi Vyas
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Vyas is a really cool guy overall. His lectures are interesting and it's clear that he is very knowledgable about the subjects. I took this class for an FC and it actually expanded my POV on a subject I wouldn't have otherwise studies. Prof. Vyas is great and this class is not stressful, a nice break from harder classes. 100% take again.

He is one of my favorite professors I've ever had! He's a super kind person and very clearly extremely knowledgeable on what he is teaching, and passionate about it. However, he still gives students ample time to discuss topics on their own, which is probably my favorite aspect of the class. His class Reli 388  isn't very work heavy either!

Honestly an amazing professor. One in class test that is graded well and showcases what one truly took from the class material. He is extremely accessible outside of class and so caring. Truly knows the content and welcomes differing ideas and opinions. I recommend taking his course(s) and if I can, I will again.

M. Vyas is a great professor! Super engaging during office hours and cares about his students ability to succeed. Had a small class cohort this semester but he's looking for new students to join and I would def encourage you to do so! His RELI 388 class has FC Global/Ethics and there's only one SHORT midterm exam. The rest is fun projects, etc.

If you are interested in learning more about Hinduism and Hindus as a diaspora I recommend RELI 281. We learned many interesting things about their history/religion/culture and how communities adapt to new settings. Prof. Maharshi is very nice, a fair grader, and all you need to do is read the material and participate to earn a good grade.

analysis.name: Vladas Pipiras
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor Pipiras was great. Although teaching seems very fast paced content coverage was excellent.
If you do put time in you will definitely get an A . Extremely easy tests and if the entire class is not doing good in it he reduces 0.5 points instead of 1 point for every wrong question. Very easy going grader .
Recommended for everyone.

Professor Pipiras is excellent and easy to communicate with! Sets clear grading criteria, has well-prepared documents, and gives moderately hard midterms. STOR 120 is not a very challenging class and you get what you pay for.

If you're thinking of taking STOR 120 over STOR 155, I would take 155 instead if you have little to no coding experience. Weekly labs and homeworks take about 2-3 hrs each. His lectures consist of him doing the code and you copying it down but fairly quick. He is a nice guy but overall goes quickly and lots of homework.
Professor Pipiras is very kind and understanding. He uploads a lot of useful material on Canvas for students to use. The class is well-planned.

This is a good class. It is a little difficult for those without much coding experience. However, the professor makes it easy to learn and as long as you are being diligent and learning, it's great. Grading is pretty chill and a lot of boosts come in later on. Prof. Pipiras is decently lenient on grading tests which helps a lot.

analysis.name: Margaret Wiener
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
She's very nice & understanding. I got sick and couldn't get a university-approved absence,  but she totally came through for me and sent me the work & didn't count the attendance against me. There are a lot of pre-class readings.
She's very knowledgeable in her field, but she is a little strange (isn't everyone in the anth department though?)

This professor knows her stuff, but be prepared to work harder than ever. She is exacting and very particular regarding papers she assigns. Her edits are so extensive that you will wonder if she even thought you understood the assignment, and that is for an A paper! However, I learned more from her than from any other prof at UNC.

Miserable. Grading criteria unclear, when she doesn't like your stuff she will let you know in the most rude and condescending way ever. 
Avoid this class at all costs. also it's boring

Very sweet/caring professor. You can skim readings. As a first year seminar, this is many students' first anthropology class so at first it seems she believes that she's "always right", but she really intends to challenge the way you think. Particular about grading, but learn her language, ask questions, participate, and you'll do really well.

Assigns multiple readings due at the start of each class. It was so much reading that after the first week, no students did it. We did group discussions on the reading and then she would lecture and it was so boring. The entire semester you work on steps to your final research paper and she grades each of them HARSHLY. Take a different FYS.

analysis.name: Herica Valladares
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: No required attendance in lecture unless you are worried about missing the notes. She is knowledgeable about her field and is an amazing class if you are interested in classics. As a non-history major got kinda boring. Easy grades, graded by a few in class writings, 2 papers, a midterm and a final. Midterm and final are nothing to stress over.

I loved this class. It was so incredibly chill; they just want you to learn. They send all test material out beforehand. Valladares was so kind. Her lectures could be a little boring, but it wasn't her fault; it's just that it was a Tu/Th class, and it loses your attention at some point. Overall, would definitely recommend for an easy gen ed.

She was very sweet and very passionate about Pompeii. Very easy tests and assignments, just make sure to put some effort into the 2 essays. Almost completely homework free, and prioritizes your learning over your grade. Unexpectedly interesting, easy, and professor Valladares is awesome. I would recommend this class to anyone

Had I known what this class would entail I never would have taken it. Your entire grade relies on two midterms and a final. Furthermore, Prof. V began to remove student's access to helpful study material (lecture videos) midway through the semester. Grading also takes a really long time, so I never really knew where I stood in the class.
Attendance isn't mandatory but such an easy class if you go. 6 participation in class writing assignments, a midterm, final, and a few essays. She's very understanding, highly recommend.

analysis.name: Carson Watlington
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is a nice person, but takes the class too seriously. Lots of homework and lots of essays, she is a hard grader. She does help and point you in the right direction, but save yourself the time and take a different teacher for ENGL-105, a lot of easier teachers out there.

This class definitely had a lot more work than some of my other friends with English 105 teachers that grade easier, but Professor Watlington tells you exactly what you need to get a good grade for each assignment and it's not too hard to get an A. She's very kind and creates a good vibe in the classroom. Good teacher!

Professor Watlington is very caring and the units of the class are interesting and give students room to explore their fields/interests. Her grading can be a little tough, but I still definitely recommend her.

Watlington graded tough but fair. Her feedback was very constructive and her rubrics were extremely clear making it easy to get good grades. She is passionate and knowledgeable about the subject matter and challenges you to become a better writer in a caring way and is accessible outside of class. I would recommend her for ENGL 105.
I was actually in ENG 205 but option wasn't there. Save yourself and do not take her. She is a tough grader. She seems excited about teaching but she also seems to be on a power trip

analysis.name: Daniel Westreich
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Although this professor has wonderful research, his teaching style was inadequate for the average graduate student. It was very hard for both PhD students and MPH students to understand the professor. This was NOT an intro class; it was more rigorous than that. Be prepared like your life depends on it.
he teaches a graduate level class, and does an amazing job at it. love the subject, and love the class.

This is not an intro to epidemiology; it is a PhD-level course, and it's taught like a philosophy class. It is very hard to understand. Personally, I think it should be an elective and what MPH students take for the intro to epidemiology.

analysis.name: William McCance
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mr. McCance is a nice guy- but if you want to learn stats, I would suggest taking a different professor. He uses the chalkboard- often with illegible writing. His lectures are not well planned, often reads slides off his phone. I basically taught myself the entire course. Exams curved 20-30% because so many people fail. UNC stop making TA's teach.

Easy class if you have previous experience with stats, but lectures were extremely boring and hard to pay attention to. Exams were medium difficulty but get insanely curved, so its hard to get a bad grade in this class. Also takes forever to grade exams. Only allowed to miss 2 classes before attendance deduction. Prof is funny sometimes though.

took forever on grading midterms. made office hours at 7pm to find out our midterm grades and didn't show. he barely posts study material for the midterms. lectures are terrible and he says intuitively a lot lol. he never answers emails even though he says to email him. he cancels class a lot (says he's sick tbf). this class made me WANT to do hw

barely homework, and tests aren't impossible, but he doesn't show up (idk how else to say it) for the last two weeks of school he cancelled basically every class because he was sick to be fair but he didn't even hold zoom or offer alternative ways to learn the material. He doesn't answer emails and is inconsistent w being present at office hours

Canceled classes the last weeks of the semester, gave us our midterm back days before the exam. Notes were all over the place and he would sometimes get his own problems wrong when writing them down. The homework was inconsistent and I had to teach myself most of the material in the class. He does heavily curve the exams though.

analysis.name: Bryn Werley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: CHEM 101 is standardized but Werley does a good job of getting through the topics.  She is very concise, gets the point across, and consistent every lecture. She was very engaging for an 8 am class and would start the morning with a cat picture or a meme. Sit in the front where you can ask questions during practice problems.

Even though I am having to retake CHEM 101, that is not a reflection of Professor Werley. She is incredibly encouraging and kind. I constantly find myself remembering things she said during lecture that are finally clicking now. Professor Werley truly cares about her students, and I am very grateful to have had her as a professor.

no matter what Chem101 class you take they are all the same. Werley was more on track with lesson plans, but she often rushed through it. If this is your first time taking chem ever (i never took chem in hs ) UNC chem is really hard.... I got weeded out! Read, go to tutoring, dont cheat on smartworks. The actual exam is 2x harder than the practice.

It isn't the professor that is hard, but rather the content and class itself. A fast paced class, and heavy on content. Tests are extremely challenging, and weigh heavy into your grade. It is nice to have a recitation to talk things through. Professor was easily accessible and willing to meet outside of class time to go over study habits, etc.

Chem 101 is a standardized course, so it doesn't matter which professor you take, but Werley is pretty good. In her lectures, she often goes into detail and asks for questions from people. Chem 101 is a hard course - I recommend finding another student who has already taken the course and asking for advice on studying, you're going to need it.

analysis.name: Ross White
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. White was a difficult professor, but if you are serious about poetry, he makes your writing GOOD, really makes you think more broadly than you might have coming out of an intro/intermediate classes. He is almost clairvoyant when he prescribes you individual readings, and he will make your poetry better with his challenges.

ENGL 259 is an improvisation class that fulfills my GE requirement and the screenwriting track. The class is fun and low-pressure. We practice improv in class and write weekly journals. There is no midterm or final. We have two formal theatre performances, and you can learn a lot from performing in public and developing comedy-writing skills.

He's so caring about us as people and our growth. Accessible outside class. He will push you HARD but it's worth it. Be ready for a lot of work, but know it's not pointless and all very thoughtfully designed. Great guy willing to go to bat for anyone, and well respected

Prof White takes your work very seriously and expects that you will too, but if you work with him your writing WILL improve a great deal. This class was a LOT of work but it hardly felt like work, it was all edifying and will stretch you in the best way. If you're willing to put in the effort to learn and grow, Prof White is a fabulous instructor.

The workload is hefty, but it never feels like busywork. Prof White makes it clear that he cares about you as an individual and your personal artistic growth. His feedback is sooo helpful (def go to his office hours!) and he has definitely helped me to become a better poet! I would 1000% take a class with him again, and you should too!

analysis.name: Danny Wu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Wu was fantastic, engaging, & informative. I learned a lot, and would absolutely take another course with him. There were only about 3 assignments total, and the semester focused on building final projects, making the end manageable. He cares deeply about his students and creates a collaborative environment. Highly recommend INLS 382!

I learned a lot and really want to take time the amount of effort Professor Wu took to make sure his students learned the topics in the most meaningful way. Always went above and beyond and really a gem of the INLS department!

Danny is such a caring professor. The course is graded based on three short homework assignments and a multiple-choice final, for which he provides the correct answers beforehand so students can study.

analysis.name: Xinyun Liu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Liu is a very great lecturer who explains thing pretty well. His midterms and individual part for the final exam are easy. The common part of final exam is kinda challenging... but Dr. Liu's easy individual part really makes up for my bad grade in the common part. He is very accessible and really cares for the students. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Professor Liu was great. I loved watching him get progressively covered in chalk throughout the lectures. 

Seriously though, Professor Liu is a great guy and his lectures cover enough content so reading the textbook is unnecessary. My only note is that there can sometimes be a slight language barrier when asking questions.

Professor Liu is very caring and understanding. I struggled a bit for the exams but if you show up to class, pay attention, and start studying early you'll be fine. 
His lectures are great and really clear, and you can tell he cares about the subject and the class. Great professor, choose him!

Dr. Liu is a GREAT prof. He rescheduled two exams to fit classes needs, includes extra credit, and has great lectures. He is hilarious, and very good at explaining concepts. Highly recommend taking. If you pay attention, you will get an A.

Xinyun is a good time! Never read the textbook and was able to get all necessary content from lecture which typically ended early for time to ask questions about HW (or eat lunch early lol). He's funny in class and cares a lot. I can't recommend him more.

analysis.name: Xinlin Ma
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's just professional and cares about students. She made things more flexible for students even during a hard time. I got more feedback than I expected as a junior. I will say take her class again!

She's the nicest professor I've ever met at UNC! She hopes students can learn from the course and makes the course as easy as possible. The topic is interesting and we have lots of case study about different worldwide cities, such as Chicago, Beijing, etc. She is very reachable after class. I will definitely take her class again.

She was always available to help and had the best, most welcoming attitude. She tried to make learning the material fun and enjoyable, and I believe she succeeded. One of the best professors I have ever had. She cares so much about her students and her field.

She cared about her students and was very enthusiastic about teaching. Attendance was not taken and the class was graded by 7 short open-note quizzes, a presentation, two papers, and a final. All were very easy.
She's very kind and sweet, and always willing to help her students with anything.

analysis.name: Xingyu Cheng
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: It was clear that he had not taught for long, as he struggled a lot early on. His teaching got better over time, and he has office hours sections where he will sit and explain material to you. The first midterm was incredibly easy. The second midterm was a lot harder, but still chill if you study hard. Final is demonic, but he curves accordingly.

I left this class most days understanding the material! He starts with easier content and then builds on it so we have the foundation to understand harder concepts. Some proofs can be a little abstract, but lots of practice can help you be prepared for tests. His study guides were helpful but looking up other practices can be helpful.

Tiger is a really funny and patient professor! He is very approachable and wants all students to do well in his class, but sometimes his explanations were hard to follow. Reading the textbook is optional, but I would highly recommend reading it + doing the practice problems if you want to do well in the class!

Office hours and in-class questions were available and very helpful. The second midterm and final were more challenging than the first test, but he curved generously at the end. The textbook aligns well with the course material and is a useful reference

At the begining of this class he did not really know how to teach well, but as the class went on he got better. There are 3 exams, homework due usually every Wednesday and a final. On exam 2 and exam 3  we got opportunities for extra credit which are the harder exams that really helped my grade. If you pay attention to lectures you will be fine.

analysis.name: Jennifer Weinberg-Wolf

review_highlights.comment: Literally do not take this class if you are trying to get ur create credit or anything, it may say meant for non physics majors but this was a pain and I would pay to have never taken this class. Would not recommend to anyone, egregious workload and midterms graded very harshly

DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE A NON-PHYSICS MAJOR AND JUST NEED AN IDEA CREDIT. I wish I would've listened to the 1 star reviews. Insane amount of work, exams are unnecessarily hard, labs are stupid, and lectures only scratch the service level of understanding. Spare yourself unless you want your semester to revolve around an INTRO LEVEL CLASS!!

I think Dr.W is very nice but I hated this class so much so I highly recommend dropping it! It was interesting for a bit but really not worth all of the assignments and labs that occur outside of class. She would give us equations without teaching us how to use them. I don't think you should take this class for a FC credit; don't tank that GPA.

This class caused me so much stress. As someone who has taken physics classes, this was the biggest mistake of my life and ruined my gpa and mental health. I am having nightmares about the clock I had to build. As someone who works hard to maintain his stem GPA do not take this class RUN AWAY. this is not worth it at all take something else.

If you want to take this class solely to fulfill the FC-Create requirement, please reconsider. There's an ungodly amount of homework & labs. There's interesting demonstrations during lecture but the focus on concepts for exams was considerably less, attending SI session and doing lots of extra studying is really the only way to get by on the exams.

analysis.name: Yuqian Xu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She's a really good prof, the material is fairly easy and up until the final its pretty fair. The final was painful also she puts in grades extremely fast (same day we took the final) the final was really hard so just prep for that. I did not hence the grade (had an A all sem)

Yuqian is a great teacher and person, but I disagree with other reviews. Class is extremely test-heavy and the final was surprisingly difficult compared to other exams and course sections. Final dropped my final grade 3 thirds of a letter grade.

Dr. Xu truly cares about her students! She teaches at a very fast pace so we always get out of class early. She's very eager to answer questions and make sure students are successful. She also is open to helping students in non-class related things

Professor Xu is a fun and engaging professor. Her class covers all the content you need to know and I felt I had everything I needed to thrive. Class consists of problem sets, 2 midterms, a final, and a group project. the final was the hardest part of the class, but overall, I enjoyed this course and would take Professor Xu again.
Everything is extremely fair, give feedback real quick. I am not a math person, but I did better than I thought in this class. My favorite professor!

analysis.name: Xiaoming Liu
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Xiaoming is a kind professor who is very passionate about what she teaches. She is slightly disorganized, and slow with grading, but she makes it relatively easy for students to succeed. She doesn't take attendance, and it's not necessary to come to every class.

Xiaoming as a person is a really nice lady but as a teacher, leaves much to be desired. Attendance isn't mandatory so only about 40% of the class shows up on a regular basis. I attended every class but didn't get much out of it. I wondered "why am I here?" The slides are boring and can be accessed online. Not a terrible class but needs improvement.

Xiaoming is extremely sweet and approachable. She understands that it is an intro level class that most people are taking for gen ed credit and even tells you that reading the textbook is not necessary. Her only grades are two midterms, the finals, and participation so it is essential you study for tests, but overall not a hard class.

Xiaoming is a sweetheart. She is really kind and you can tell she wants her students to understand and love geology the way that she does. With that being said, I found it difficult to pay attention in this class, for whatever reason. The material is not terribly difficult to understand, so take some notes and you should be fine.

Very structured and clear-cut class. Xiaoming is a wonderful person and she teaches the material very well. I'd highly recommend for students to take this class whether they are interested in geology or just trying to fulfill a Gen-Ed. Take caution though- you will have to study the lecture slides hard to get an A.

analysis.name: Ximena  Bustamante-Marin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Though Dr. Marin may seem strict, she is genuinely really nice! Class content is difficult and requires a lot of memorization to be prepared on tests, so definitely do not study last min! But it is really interesting to learn if you are interested in nutrition. Her office hours were pretty helpful to go over exams or any content related questions!

So much to say, so little words. Lectures were a waste of time, she reads directly off the slides and still finds a way to tell us inaccurate information (takes a true genius to do that). Dont bother asking questions because she wont answer them. Pros - she's funny and sarcastic, really appeals to my sense of humor. My advice, dont take this class.

Dr. Bustamante-Marin is a GENIUS in the field and is very knowledgeable. She's the sweetest person if you take the time to actually talk to her. That said, she is a tough grader with exams with tricky wording (which she will not give points back on), and omg the lectures are so fast with sometimes 100s of slides. you learn a lot! DONT CRAM!!

I really like her as a person, she was very approachable and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. However, lectures were pretty uninspiring and the tests were horrendously written. Good news is about half of the questions on her exams are free points, but the others were often very ambiguous and did not focus on core concepts.

Her lectures are boring. They only go over a small part of the assigned readings, so you are basically teaching yourself. If you read the chapters you could skip the lectures. Exams are hard. Multiple select questions. For example, the choices would be A; B; C; A & B; or A , B, & C. Over half of the test consist of question in this format.

analysis.name: Claire Yang
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Instructions so unclear, lots of reading, very boring lectures and is kind of condescending to students. If you need this class, you can survive it, but I would not take it if I didn't have to.

Overall, this was an ok class. Almost all classes were just straight lecture without any engagement, which makes it hard to actually learn the material, but if that's your cup of tea then this class is fine. There was often pretty ambiguous grading criteria on what was wanted for assignments, which just took trial and error to figure out.

Super important in her field, very knowledgeable, but lectures can be a bit dry. Try not to take this class early in the morning if possible. Grading criteria for papers is a bit unclear, but if you are willing to go to office hours to ask that could help. Lots and lots of articles to read.

analysis.name: Xiangying Huang
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof Huang moves very quickly and has had me lost in confusion since day 1 of the class. Her homework assignments often cover nothing done in class and as such I cannot practice what I learned. The class is graded 80% on multiple choice tests, but with no practice questions, I'm often lost on what to study. She is nice, but her class is very hard.

Her lectures are not helpful when it comes to homework and exams. Exams are multiple choice and do not properly test knowledge of the course (almost impossible to adequately study for). She talks more about the philosophy of statistics and goes through difficult proofs during class rather than covering necessary material that is tested on.

Although friendly, professor Huang's lectures are impossible to keep up with. One week she says she is uploading her notes and the next she says she has stopped. Exams are multiple choice but extremely difficult to understand. Her lectures include maybe 1 or 2 examples while the rest is just her doing proofs that aren't helpful.

Goes through the material as if everyone in the class has already seen it and just needs a quick glance to understand the topics. Does complicated proofs in class; homework and exams are unrelated and difficult. Unless you have already taken STOR 435 and know all the material, this is a terrible professor to have to start learning it.

She spends most of the class time doing proofs rather than providing examples to explain the concepts. She moves extremely fast and barely explains difficult concepts.Two tests that are 12 question MC, which make up a significant portion (40%) of the overall grade. The final (40% of your grade) is a a MC test w/ no partial credit.

analysis.name: Yinghsuan Chao
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
Having exams worth 70% of your grade is unreasonable when lectures are unclear, the slides are filled with AI and memes, and the textbook offers little support. The exams don't reflect what's taught.

She is kind and accessible outside of class, but I don't think that makes up for what you'd get out of it.

she probably isnt bad for Econ 101 b/c the content is straightforward, but she is not equipped to be teaching Econ 420 at all. she seems nice but she cannot answer questions clearly and her lectures rarely stay on topic. the exams are not bad if you use outside resources, but in general her lectures offer little help with understanding the content.

She is the sweetest lady, don't get me wrong. But she can't teach. Most of her slides are AI memes and she deviates so much from the content. She doesn't grade the homeworks till more than a month after it is submitted.
What you are taught in class is NOT what you are presented with in the exam. And you're not allowed to ask questions on the exam..

The majority of the slides were AI generated pictures of herself or random AI pictures/memes. The lectures were not very helpful and most of the learning is done outside of class. I think she's really nice and knowledgeable about economics, but it didn't really feel like a whole lot of teaching was going on.

For the Econ 420 class, the lecture is ok, but not very clear. The exam is long and difficult. The exam time is less than 75 minutes, which is too rushed for students to finish in time. Although she curves a lot on the exam, it still makes students feel unprepared for the class. However, Professor Chao is a very nice person, caring about students.

analysis.name: Zachary Yukio Kerr
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kerr is supportive and encouraging throughout the senior honors thesis process, and challenges you in the best way. Feedback is detailed and helpful, and time is always made to talk about challenges. Dr. Kerr clearly cares about student success as expectations are clear, communication is consistent, and support is always there. Highly rewarding

Dr. Kerr is one of the rare professors on campus who considers the fact that his students are people with lives outside of his class. He is very willing to be flexible as long as you are willing to demonstrate you are putting in effort to the class. Makes an otherwise really boring topic and 8 am class really enjoyable. I would highly recommend.

If you have the chance to take a class with Professor Kerr, take it. He is a phenomenal professor who is so understanding when it comes to his students and is willing to do whatever to help them out. He is so funny and makes going to class at 8 am worth it. You will not regret taking a class with him.

Honest and understanding of students lives outside of classes, especially for a one credit course. Take this class with him if you can, it seemed he was able to be more flexible with the material than other professors because he helped create the course. Met six times throughout the semester, with biweekly online work and a final group project

Zack understood that the class was only a single credit hour, and only had us do what was necessary to learn the content. I had to meet with him for help with my final project, and I mentioned that I was looking for some good study spots on campus. He took the time after our meeting to send me a list of his favorite places to get work done.

analysis.name: Bryan Yackulic
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I've ever had!! He is so incredibly kind, really cares about his students, and makes a point of getting to know you. If you have the option, TAKE IT WITH HIM!
Dr. Yackulic was great at keeping us in the loop with Honors Carolina events and resources and has some super interesting anecdotes of his own.

Professor Yackulic is amazing! He really cares for his students and gives great advice for freshman to use for their future college careers. Easy class, only five assignments total and a very easy final exam but class is pass or fail. Kayden Hunt is also an amazing TA!

Dr. Y is a walking W. He's interesting, funny, caring, & inspirational. HNRS 101 is EXTREMELY easy: it has 6 simple assignments total & is graded on a P/F basis. There are a lot of resources you get exposed to, and the material can really help orient yourself at UNC. Just attend class, do your small, easy assignments, and you're done!
This is a very easy pass/fail class and Dr. Yackulic is a very kind and understanding professor.

analysis.name: Yaakov Ariel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ariel is fantastic! His classes can be hard to follow and he interrupts presentations. BUT! He is a wealth of knowledge and I have never had a professor be more complimentary and supportive of my passion. He can take a joke, is willing to be (respectfully) challenged by students, and brought food to share at the beginning of class. He is great!

Dr. Ariel veered away from the syllabus to say the least. There was a required reading of at least one novel, usually more per class.  The readings were dense, the videos were boring, he was confusing, not to mention the 12 pg term paper. I would not recommend. He was also HATEFUL if you ever had to miss a class, even if you were sick.

I LOVED this class. Favorite professor and favorite class and i'm about to graduate. I would take any class he teaches. It's not hard if you try and are thoughtful. I really enjoyed the topics and Dr. Ariel always brought snacks, which was super kind. For the class, we got to visit churches and write about our experiences visiting them.

Great professor. Provided clear expectations for exams and opportunities to help prepare the class. Would highly recommend any class with Dr. Ariel. Honestly, a gem of a human. 

The topic of 242 (New Religious Movements) was unlike anything else I've ever learned and broadened my understanding of other faith communities.
Great professor, gets to know his students, very personable. Would recommend him to anyone.

analysis.name: Muxin Zhang
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: All your homeworks and 100s of practice problems given are exactly like the exam. Lectures are explained really well and if you cant figure it out studios are just practice sessions and have amazing explanations. Just try and you'll do well. Plus she is so chill for labs. Literally gave me free credit when I needed it.

Prof. Zhang was my studio instructor for PHYS 118, and she was absolutely amazing. She was insanely good at answering questions and would always help you in any way she could. She was the course coordinator this semester, so she did not lecture for the full class. There is not a studio instructor I would rather have. Wholeheartedly recommend!

I had Prof Zhang for my Physics 118 studio and she was amazing. The class was very difficult but she explained everything in a clear and engaging way so it all made sense. The canvas was very helpful and she was always willing to walk you though any problems both in class and in office hours.

SHE IS THE BEST!!! She is super accessible, especially in office hours, and explains concepts extremely well. This class definitely requires some hard work, especially if you've never been in a college-level physics course before, but if you use your resources it is definitely doable.

Phy118 is hard and a fair amount of work, but completely doable. Course was organized really well. Dr. Zhang was my studio instructor, and she did a great job reinforcing difficult concepts taught in lecture. Class isn't super test heavy, either.

analysis.name: Eva Zhao
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: One of the worst MEJO professors. She gave NO FEEDBACK. Doesn't believe in giving 100s. She told us we did great but the max she gave someone was a 94. This isn't supposed to be a difficult class, but is when she doesn't give any feedback other than a good job, and quickly goes through the slides. We have only done group work all year. DO NOT TAKE!

I would recommend taking ad/pr research with Eva. She is super nice and accessible and is very passionate about research. She is willing to help you and the class is very manageable (with little assignments). Just participate in class!
Take this class with this professor if you want to feel terrible about yourself and want to have your work picked apart to shreds. AKA don't take it.

She is sweet and cares about learning, but definitely made this class much more stressful than it needed to be. Was not super clear on assignment and grading guidelines and graded them very harshly. Assigned a lot of work week to week and gave a final presentation in addition to a very challenging final. I'd find another professor for this course.

Eva is clearly very smart, but she has a hard time communicating her ideas and knowledge to the class. She constantly contradicted herself in class and had to second-guess herself on many things. I don't know if this was her first time teaching MEJO 379 and she just needed a semester under her belt, but I will just say she did not make it easy.

analysis.name: Yaron Shemer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you're taking it for the Gen-Ed, be aware that it's a decent amount of work, & unless you're really interested in film, you probably won't enjoy it. Dr. Shemer is very caring and a generous grader, but lectures can be mind-numbing. If you do the readings, watch the films, and participate, you WILL get an A, but don't expect a fun class.

Dr. Shemer's lectures are interesting. If you don't know a lot about Jerusalem, sometimes it can be difficult to follow some of the concepts he talks about, but he's always willing to answer questions and clarify when needed. Great person!

Seems like a nice guy but I dreaded going to class. Drones on and on and I had a hard time following. On tests and essays he wanted me to parrot back what he taught, didn't appreciate me putting in my own perspective on things. A deep dive into Middle Eastern Cinema, but I came out of it still not understanding why that was important.

Assigns ridiculous amounts of reading, especially for a 100 level class. I've been in college for years and have never had to do this much reading. He is a very good lecturer and encourages his students to think and discuss the themes found in the reading, though you will mostly be discussing that at recitation if you're in a large lecture class.

Yaron is a great guy and is clearly passionate about the subject matter. Attendance is mandatory and participation is recommended since lectures are discussion based. Reading for every class that is a bit dry but I would recommend doing it since he asks for opinions. 4-5 papers graded fairly easily. Straight-forward final. Some extra credit.

analysis.name: Danielle Zurcher
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zurcher was a fantastic professor for Chem 261! Her lectures were clear and easy to understand as long as you prepared before class (Mastering and review textbook OR videos). Her exams were challenging but fair. Nothing came out of left field. Everything was from somewhere in the notes or clicker questions. I'd highly recommend her.
Zurcher is new to UNC and she is great. Very clear, very accessible, and funny at times. Definitely a solid choice for orgo-- not as experienced as Crimmins, but she is a good professor.

I was skeptical of taking her class at first but am happy I did. She cares a lot about her students success and actually listens & acts on the feedback she receives which I feel many professors don't do. She offered extra credit and a slight curve. Orgo is not an easy class, but her enthusiasm during lecture and organization helps. Solid professor!

Dr. Zurcher was one of the best science teachers I've had. Her lectures are clear, concise, and well-structured. She's also a very cheerful, easy going person, and is always ready to help. Org. Chem is a difficult class, but she managed to make it very enjoyable. Her tests are harder than class material but doable if you stay on top of things.

Professor Zurcher was very clear with what knowledge was required and there were a lot of resources provided to ensure that you learned. One issue was that a lot of the material was not taught with the concepts behind them, so it required memorization. However due to her enthusiasm and clear teaching style, I would definitely recommend her.

analysis.name: Zachary Nimchuk

Otherwise, the only other grades are a semester long group project and the "final exam" which is a prompt that you get ahead of time and can prepare. Definitely recommend this class.

Dr. Nimchuk has been by far the best biology professor I've ever had at UNC. This course was my absolute favorite this semester and I always looked forward to sitting in lecture. He is very knowledgable with the CRISPR-CAS9 system and has so much insight to provide. Everyone should take this class and witness how marvelous Dr. Nimchuk is!

The best professor I've had at UNC. Very clear on his expectations and willing to explain difficult concepts. The class material was interesting for people interested in genetics and molecular biology. If you read and understand the papers, you will do well.

Loved Dr. Z! His lectures were engaging and entertaining to learn from. He sent out a weekly email that outlined the class we had that week and showed how much he cared about us. This was a 1-credit seminar, but he's teaching a full course on CRISPR next semester which I would highly recommend!

Great professor and person. Very knowledgeable on the subject matter and cares about the students. Seems as though he wants students to succeed and learn from his class. I highly recommend his course on CRISPR if you're a science major and interested in genetics. Final project was a lot of fun.

analysis.name: Zachary  Fisher

Amazing person!! I loved Dr. Fisher. He is the nicest person ever, and extremely helpful. Everyone in our class which was small loved him. He is a great professor, and if I had someone as a PI or something, he would be it. Dope professor, easy lectures, amazing materials :)

Zoe is great. She is super understanding of people learning french for the first time, and she it a pretty easy grader. Super approachable, but do the nightly homework or your grade will be knocked.

Love herrr. She's so sweet and just wants to help in any way she can. She's very flexible too - I had a cold and she let me retake a quiz a few days later. Participation matters, but that's expected in a language class.

Zoe was a very fair grader and gave good, helpful feedback on the daily homework, as well as quizzes. She lived in Paris for an extended period of time so she is very familiar with how native French is spoken. She is also very friendly and easily approachable. I highly recommend Zoe for French 101.
too informal and unprofessional but very approachable

analysis.name: Lillian Zwemer

Instead, she schedules two sessions to 'view' your exam, which I have never been able to go to due to class/work conflicts. Avoid her class at all costs.

Several common phrases used in Lilian Zwemer's lecture:

"Let me see bababa...... So this uhhhh [insert structure here]'s function is uhhhh let me check my notes..... Oh yes! [Insert function here]"

"Mea Culpa, andioop, I made a mistake in my lecture the correct [insert] should be[insert]"

analysis.name: Adi Nester
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Nester is very nice and enthusiastic about what she teaches. She really cares about students understanding the materials. The lectures were very informative and engaging and the class discussions were interesting. Homework assignments were straightforward and most of the time she gave the answers already in class before we had to submit.

Dr. Nester was a very kind and understanding professor. She assigned lots of extremely lengthy readings which were the only things covered in lecture. Her exams were what you make of them, she is very clear with what will be on the exam, you just have to make sure to prepare for them well because she is a tough grader in my opinion.

I enjoyed this class! You can tell Nester is very passionate about the subjects, which sometimes led to going over time with lectures and getting off schedule. She really wants to help her students, she gave plenty of feedback on assignments and offered extra credit. She can be a little bit of a tough grader, but is clear with her expectations.

The class was very interesting and the lectures were well-organized with really helpful slides that made studying for the exams much more manageable. Prof. Nester is very nice and accommodating. She encouraged participation in class and gave a lot of helpful feedback on the homework assignments.

Professor Nester's class was wonderful. We read engaging texts from diverse perspectives, creating a rich and meaningful learning experience. Discussions were consistently thoughtful and in-depth. Exams were fair, and she clearly reviewed key material and how to prepare. Highly recommended.

analysis.name: Adrienne Erickcek

Dr. Erickcek is amazing, this class made me switch my major to astrophysics! Fantastic class, lectures, and professor. The homework can be difficult but is totally manageable if you start on time. Having python experience can be helpful.

She is an exceptional teacher, her lectures are so thorough and well-planned. She is so helpful if you make it obvious that you're trying to understand. She is really nice, gave good feedback on all assignments, but the material is vast and she doesn't give exam practice problems. So it is difficult to study for those exams.
The best physics teacher I've ever had.

analysis.name: Adam Harris

Listen. College Thriving is a really annoying class. However, he really did his best with the material provided to him.

analysis.name: Adam Price

Sounds super light, but gets tedious.

I enjoyed having Adam as the instructor a lot. I thought he was very knowledgeable on the subjective of creative writing and was incredibly passionate. The class itself is easy, particularly weighted on your submission of your own 10 page short story. He's very sarcastic, but I find him to be hilarious. I recommend!

Funny, smart, charismatic guy. This was one of my favorite classes at UNC. You read a short story before every class, then discuss it in class. You have a 10-15 page short fiction story (basically about anything you want) due at a certain point in the semester, where it gets workshopped in class. Chill A, cool subject, if you're taking 130 take him

Adam was an amazing professor and his class was very straight forward. You have small readings with short writing assignments before each class and then one final long story that you get to create. Show up to class, participate every now and then, and listen to feedback from your draft and you will get an easy A.

Adam was a super nice teacher and made the class feel very open for constructive criticism. My only complaint with him was his "Do Not" list for writing, but with the way he structured the class it never became an issue. He was flexible as well.

analysis.name: Adlai Lang

Super easy grader, and a B is the lowest you can get if you complete all the work.
He's very chill and super kind. Just make sure to turn in the homework on time and you'll get an A. Also, go to his office hours, he is very knowledgeable on classics (lowkey cool)!

An amazing teacher and my favorite professor this semester. Every assignment we did was marked based on completion. I loved how his areas of expertise (I believe it was Latin or Roman linguistics) seeped into the way he taught class. What you learn and get out of this class is based on what you put into it. There was one group project.

Prof. Lang is a great choice for ENGL 105I (Natural Sciences). The writing assignments were all interesting and relevant. They're caring and will work with you on deadlines if you communicate. Prof. Lang was caring, kind, well-organized, and overall a really great teacher. Assignments were fairly easy but engaging and had lots of room for creative touches. Good incorporation of individual and personal work. Engaging lectures. Grade was mostly completion and attendance. Would highly recommend taking his class.

analysis.name: Adam Versenyi

Adam Versenyi is very good at illuminating the meanings of the most obscure dramatic texts, however, he can be a bit boring at times. No extra credit, 2 papers and a final exam which is also a paper.
Adam's class was alright overall. A lot of readings, but that didn't make it too hard to get a good grade. Strap in for the final project, though.

analysis.name: Amy Adkins

The best professor to take 205 with. This class is so difficult but professor adkins made it easier to understand. She offers quiz corrections which saved my grade. Very caring and has multiple officer hours that you should go to. Cannot stress enough how much I enjoyed having her as a professor coming from someone who didn't do good in physics 1.

Pretty average professor, statics isn't an easy class but is doable with Prof Adkins and a good bit of effort. She allows you to do test corrections for 50% points back on tests which is super helpful gradewise and for understanding the concepts. Dr. Adkins is a great professor. She's funny and very generous with grades (students can get half points back on midterms with corrections). She also does a great job of keeping the class relatively low-stress while still helping students learn a lot. I would absolutely take another class with her in the future.

Dr. Adkins is a phenomenal professor for an intro engineering course. The format of her exams allowed for test corrections which was incredibly helpful when learning the difficult content. I cannot say enough good things about the organization of this course and its format, it was really easy to follow new material and get help from the textbook.

Loved this class. Abelardo is such a great professor and he cares so much about what he teaches. I took this for a Gen Ed credit but honestly found this to be a super interesting class. He is very lenient with grading, he just wants you to learn. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

Dr. Abelardo is by far one of the best professors I have gotten to experience at this school. He is excited about teaching and his enthusiasm makes the course interesting and insightful. analysis.name: Abel Munoz-Hermoso

review_highlights.comment: To start, I had him for 355 (no option to select that on RMP) Abel is my favorite UNC profesor, this is the second class I've taken with him and 355 has been my favorite class by far. Reasonable workload, he is flexible, he is hilarious, class feels like a conversation, he made the entire class friends and I would talk to any of them outside10/10

Chill and understanding professor. Cares more about participation than perfection, make an effort to speak up in class and it'll go far, even if your Spanish isn't great. Communicate issues or a desire for an extension and he'll make it work for you, if he can tell that you care about the class.

I loved this man, very happy and go lucky, makes funny jokes. He makes class engaging and gives you a lot of freedom when it comes to your written work. Not a tough grader but expects participation in class. You can tell he has a passion for Spanish, teaching does not feel like a chore to him, cares about your learning. Reopened homeworks for me.

i really enjoyed abel and took him for both 204 and 261. attendance and participation are key for him but if you make a good impression at the start and he likes you, he basically guarantees you an A. 204 was mega chill, 261 was a pain due to all the busy work.

This guy is the goat. I took him and can honestly say he was one of the best Spanish teachers I have ever had. If you are a student you need to take him (like trust me). His lectures were fun, although the content is hard he makes it fun to learn, and really wants to see you succeed as a Spanish speaker and in the class.

analysis.name: Abigail Panter
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Dr. P is really awesome. She cares very deeply about her students and her class is not hard at all. I had no tests. She is an easy grader and wants you to do well (very flexible with deadlines). However, her lectures can be very long and all over the place. It's fine because no tests means you don't need to be fully attentive and can space off.

Dr. P is amazing and one of the best teachers I had this semester. She is always available during office hours and always checks in on students. The classwork is useful and not too difficult, with only a few hours of work outside of class each week. No exams.
You can tell that Dr. Panter actually cares about her students and she makes her classes enjoyable. She wants students to succeed and if you put effort in and participate you will do well.

Dr. Panter is the most caring professor I've ever had. She really cares about each individual student and always takes the time to ask you how you're doing. She is SUPER enthusiastic about statistics. She's kind of a perfectionist, but always has a positive attitude. I'm definitely going to keep in touch with her after this class!

Dr. Panter is a wonderful woman and professor. She is so sweet and is always concerned with how people are doing as individuals, not just their performance as students. She is not always clear and doesn't always answer e-mails but she is brilliant and more than willing to help you with anything you could ask for.

analysis.name: Abbie Smith-Ryan

Massively regret taking this class with such a disorganized professor. ASR has very unclear grading criteria and is very late on communication. This class was very interesting and I enjoyed learning a lot of the topics we covered. She also was very good to answer questions and really encouraged us to participate during class. The quizzes were pretty hard and it was really unclear what we needed to know to prepare. Also was quite condescending when you were called out and answered wrong.

analysis.name: Andy Ackerman

Concepts are hard but Andy was helpful in OH. Virtually no material to help you study for exams and HW questions did not always relate to class / exams. Great lecturer and educator in general. Looked forward to class.

Not sure why the MATH186 ratings are so bad, I guess you guys didn't study. Class is super hard, but Andy's a great professor and really accessible outside class. Doesn't give much material for exam prep, but class problems and reviews outside of class are very representative of what the exam looks like. Work is hard but doable, very fun class.
Horrible. Grading is harsh. Does not drop lowest midterm. Grading unclear. Don't take.
Does not care for your grade. The hardest professor to take for stats at Lafayette.

analysis.name: Achsah Dorsey

*ANTHRO 364*
I loved this class. Dr. Dorsey teaches us about professional development as an Anthropologist, and I still use the notes I took in her class to this day.

Professor Dorsey was one of the best professors I had at UMass. She makes learning content fun and super interesting. I have a lot of respect for her. Take a class with her! You'll learn so much without being overwhelmed, and she's always willing to help if you need it.

Achsah was my TA for this class, and it was a pretty TA heavy class (meaning they did all the grading and that's who you actually interacted with in recitation). I enjoyed her a lot! She's really nice and has a pleasant personality, and she got to know us all by name. She isn't an easy grader, but it's nothing insane. Solid choice overall
Dr. Dorsey is a great lecturer and a very kind professor. I would highly recommend her classes, especially Anthropology 313 (Nutritional Anthropology).

analysis.name: Rafael Acosta Morales

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed SPAN344 (not 373 344 wasn't an option). This course was chill & insightful. Sometimes it was hard do all readings. Professor wasn't perfect (a bit unorganized... FYI to ppl who get stressed over that lol) BUT he was really flexible and understanding throughout the class which is rare in the ROML department. 8.5/10 class would take again!

This was probably my favorite class at UNC. I usually struggle with participating but the prof is so knowledgeable and funny I felt really comfortable! Class always felt incredibly dull which is surprising considering the class was about fiction writing (one of the most entertaining forms of writing). Excited to see how he structures future classes, he has the passion.

analysis.name: Michael Acosta

review_highlights.comment: Mike Acosta is an incredible teacher. Class is never boring and he actually cares about each student. He has a wealth of knowledge and shares it in an understandable way. What a guy. Easily the best professor I've had at UNC. Acosta cares so much about his students. The man has lived three different lives and has countless hilarious stories he loves to share. He was by far the best professor I have EVER had at this school. I am a premed stem student and I took this class as my sanity class and it was the best decision. I enjoyed this class so much because of Dr. Acosta. The content and the class were enjoyable but it was Dr. Acosta who brought the class to life.

Dr. Acosta has been the best professor I've had at UNC thus far. He is so funny and actually cares about us as students, which you don't see from the other professors at UNC. The lectures were so funny and he related it to screenwriting, which allowed me to learn in a way that I haven't in any other class in my life.

Greatest class I've ever taken. Most classes are just him telling stories about his life -- which is super interesting. The class is like an interactive stand-up comedy show that gives you a super easy A for very little work. (VERY little)

analysis.name: Jeff Ackermann

Jeff is a super nice guy and his lectures (that you definitely don't have to attend) are funny. However, his tests are not written by him so they don't relate well to what he lectures on in class. This is a tough class mostly because the professor doesn't know what he's talking about. He is good at teaching the specific material, but he lacks basic knowledge of topics taught in ECON 101.

analysis.name: Neel Ahuja

review_highlights.comment: Class was not the best. The professor also made me feel uncomfortable. Like, my eyes are up here.

The papers are the main part of the class. They were slightly difficult because they were on such odd topics I was not used to writing on. Overall, the class was really good. Discussions were very interesting and you read good documents and novels. I would definitely take this class again.

Great FYS - delved into a lot of interesting topics. Extremely discussion-heavy. You get as much out of it as you put in, learning and grade-wise. Besides being a cool guy, he will save your life if you need any help at all with your papers so go see him! Grading's a bit unclear but he seems to notice effort and it reflects. Got an A.

Neel is a super nice guy who is very knowledgable about Caribbean literature. That said, when it is time to write the multiple 7-page papers, you will end up in his office hours and he will save you. He doesn't grade easy and expects you to have it together when you come to class. Participation is key in this class. I would take it again though!

Mr. Ahuja taught the most interesting freshman seminar I could've imagined. He was clear and the work was SO manageable, he was understanding and encouraged us to participate (very necessary!). But overall it was such a great class and there aren't many assignments- barely even did the readings. Take his class!

analysis.name: Shawn Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: This class was awesome. Dr. Ahmed was super layed back and the entire course reflected that. Your grades off of 2 midterms and 1 final (not cumulative) and 2 group presentations. It's very much show up do the work and an A is almost guaranteed. I don't think anyone got under a 80 on any exam or presentation.

This class was very easy in comparison to other bio courses. All midterms and final was take home and were graded very fairly with clear feedback. Only two group presentations and you get to choose your groups. Overall, I highly recommend this class to help boost your science GPA.
Great prof, never showed up to class and only showed up when it was my turn to present. Take home test and finals. He also records lectures and host it on zoom. Easy BIOL 400+ class!!!

I actually took 546, but it was an easy class, as long as you take enough notes to understand the material, all you have to do to succeed is rewatch the lectures and write down what he says with your understanding on the open note tests. This man does not tip servers when he goes to restaurants.

analysis.name: Andrew Ackerman

review_highlights.comment: Very available outside of class which is great however he is not very accommodating for extenuating circumstances. Amazing lecturer and explained concepts really well. You can tell he really cares about his students and teaching. Not hard but you'll have to put in some effort for an A

Andy is a great and caring person who answered every single question with much consideration and patience. If Andy has managed to keep me, a graduating senior in an 8AM class, then you know he's done something right. His enthusiasm in each lecture makes the most boring topics engaging. Fantastic lecturer, always energetic and engaging. You can tell he is truly passionate about the material and teaching it to his students. I know many other STAN majors who are interested in this class.

The workload isn't tough and it's easy to end with a good grade, but the best part is listening to two great data science minds work through problems in lecture. Stan was a very kind and considerate professor however was not the best lecturer. The lectures were mainly watching professors code and follow along without a lot of explanation as to why things were done. This course would be much easier if you have an understanding of programming beforehand, however is not impossible without any.

A fantastic professor and cool guy. He taught this semester tag-team with Dr. Krishnamurthy, and both were great! The course is very well designed. Lectures are helpful but not required if you read the book. Course is easy not in the sense that it's a joke but that you'll know how to code by the time it's done. Highly recommend!

Professor Ahalt taught this class with Professor Krishnamurthy, and I loved it. For me, the workload in this class was very manageable. Both professors were extremely understanding of students struggling with mental health and other issues that kept them from completing work. I would highly, highly recommend this course.

analysis.name: Katherine Aha

Enjoyed her POLI 236 class. Interesting topic--lectures are sometimes a bit long, but grading criteria and exams are straightforward.

Terrible lectures. Overall, the class wasn't too bad, but I didn't learn much from her teaching style. The projects are straightforward and generally enjoyable, so getting a good grade isn't hard.

lectures can get boring sometimes and are a lot of information with barely any words on slideshows, have to actually attend lectures to do well on quizzes. instructor really cares about what she talks about and i found the lecture content to be super interesting and cool to learn about!

Aaron was a gem!! I am a senior and took his Algorithms & Society class with little to no experience with interpreting data and he made sure that even the hardest readings were made understandable. analysis.name: Aalyia Sadruddin

Wellesley - ANTH 101 Really kind prof! Very accessible and inspiring/global with her viewpoint. Wants everyone to succeed and provides the means to do so. If you get the chance, take a class with her!

She's teaching at Wellesley now and I took her class last semester. Learned so much in her class, best professor I couldve ever ask for in college. I'd be thankful in my life to have Dr. Sadruddin.

Dr. Sadruddin is the BEST! The course structure is weekly readings and an easy-going class discussion about them. There are several writing assignments, but she grades fairly and provides amazing feedback. She WANTS you to succeed and to love med anth as much as she does. She is energetic and passionate. There is not a class I would recommend more.

analysis.name: Ron Alterovitz
