2) Go to CHEMPossible

I would say Anna Curtis is one of the best Chem 101 lecturers. She seems to really care about the subject matter and is enthusiastic while teaching, without being too overboard. Although chem 101 is a flipped classroom format which can be somewhat difficult, I feel like she addresses all difficult content and allows time for questions always.

analysis.name: Caitlin Andrews-Lee
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best polisci professor! So passionate about her work and super engaging. Almost too smart for us, so sometimes we leave her hanging when she asks us questions in class. Overall, highly recommend her class! 2 exams, 3 in-class writing assignments, and a final policy simulation. Meet with her in office hours if you want her to explain/help review.

This course deals with Latin American politics, and it is clear that Professor Andrews-Lee is extremely knowledgeable about this topic. I also found it highly beneficial to speak with her during her office hours when I needed clarification on the course. She will suggest scheduling appointments so keep that in mind if you plan on speaking with her.

Professor Andrews-Lee clearly cares for her students and their wellbeing both inside and outside of class. Lenient on attendance if you are sick, but make sure to show up as much as you can, as the exams are directly based on lecture slides and conversations held in class. Exams were easy if you studied the way she said. Lots of reading.

Prof Andrews-Lee is such a knowledgable professor on comparative politics and one of the nicest professors I've ever had. She truly wants her students to succeed and the assignments she chose for class are interesting. The midterms and finals are not too difficult and she makes her lectures really engaging! I would definitely recommend her class.

Prof. Andrews-Lee is one of the most kind and caring professors I've had. She is so great at making the material easily digestible. If I had any questions I found she was more than willing to answer them during office hours and over email, and often went the extra mile to help. If you review the slides before exams you should easily ace them.

analysis.name: Ana Silva Campo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She cares deeply about her students and is invested in our growth as people. Class is thoughtfully designed and really interesting. She took us to see Wilson Library's archives which was really cool. Great first-year seminar––interesting and fun but not overly difficult

She lectures very clearly. She grades written responses clearly and fairly, although there isn't a set rubric. Group presentations are fairly simple and she's very encouraging and respectful with her feedback. You are expected to do the readings, annotate, and participate in class.
Great professor! Overall, she teaches very clearly and connects topics well. She gives good feedback on all assignments. Very calm environment with her!

I took LTAM314 with her. It was ok, wouldnt recommend. Topics felt random & irrelevant to modern law. It's graded by maybe 6 things total, so doing bad/ok on one of 2 in-class assignments will knock ur grade down bad. Most ppl didnt read before coming to class but plz do! Even if you like law like me, just take something else there's better classes

Prof. Silva was a delight to have as a professor. She was very kind and I loved that she incorporated different methods of getting participation points for people who may not have been comfortable speaking in front of the class. I loved the readings, and it's clear that she has a passion for the subject. One of my favorite classes of all time.

analysis.name: Andrew Walker
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Only reason I wouldn't take again is becuase no one really seems that interested, so he lectures for a long time. Otherwise, easy exams, short writing assignments, and he is very accessible outside of class. I think he should just teach higher level classes and not a 100-level class, maybe he would get more engagement.

Great professor, I loved his LTAM 101 class. Expect to have 20-45 page readings per class, but the lectures broke down all of the denser, more complex concepts into something that anyone can understand, so it truly wasn't bad at all. Definitely would recommend taking his class!

Dr. Walker is an incredibly nice guy and cares a lot about his students. He is newer as a prof but has his stuff together way more than any other prof I had this sem. He makes learning fun and approachable. Don't hesitate to take one of his classes
He gives students opportunities to come to their own conclusions, help them learn how to work collaboratively, would recommend this class and teacher to anyone interested in the subject

analysis.name: Jocelyn Aksin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Aksin is fantastic! Very nice and understanding, easy grader, and my favorite professor at UNC so far. I never felt like I had to be perfect to answer questions, and she never made learning feel like a chore. Some homework outside of class, but never anything crazy. Overall, very happy with Dr. Aksin, and am excited to take 204 with her!

My German made leaps and bounds under Dr.Askin. She learned German in middle school and as a result better understands the many struggles people learning German experience. She's able to break down complex German topics and make it easy to understand. Also very understanding, clearly hates to grade and doesn't put a lot of emphasis on it.

This is for GSLL 89 FYS. Dr. Aksin is amazing!!! She picks the most interesting literature/movies and gives fantastic lectures on super interesting topics. We think about language in a totally new way, and she has unique perspectives because of her background in Germany and Turkey. Highly recommend her seminar, and getting to know her as a person!

THIS IS FOR 203. Great professor, her lectures make learning a language easier, totally understanding and flexible, The entire class taught in German but makes sure to keep students in the loop and focused. Grading structure is favorable and encourages you to just come to class and learn. Would recommend to anyone trying to learn German

This seminar was really fun - small class size and pretty much all grades were very creative assignments (presentations and essays). Dr. Aksin speaks with no accent, and she does a lot to keep class topics interesting. This was the best type of environment to learn German in, and my favorite out of all of the German courses I've taken here so far.

analysis.name: Akaa Ayangeakaa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The TA teaches, grades and creates homework for the lab section. Professor simply gives the recitation lecture. In those lectures he is a slow speaker, does not get through all the material in a timely manner. He is also a poor communicator outside of the classroom. He once forgot to tell us about an assignment and then tried to blame us.

Lecture plus supplemeting with textbook make the material clear and manageable. Fun lecturer and engages with students. Grades exams rather strictly, (i.e., you want textbook work) but is very lenient when it comes to getting points back. Akaa wants you to succeed, and he was very forgiving with final rounding. Put in the work and you will do well!

I took 281L with Dr. Ayangeakaa, and again I found that he was a caring professor that only wanted the class to learn and succeed. Homework sets are a little disorganized and can be long, but the lectures are well-structured and clear, and include examples to work as a class or in small groups. Tests are fair and he prepares you well with examples.

Great professor. The midterm exams were both a bit disorganized, but he was honest and fair when grading them. Doesn't take attendance traditionally, but gives pop quizzes throughout the semester as a substitute. Overall very understanding and a funny guy in lecture.

He's a very decent professor. He's a funny guy and clearly knows what he is talking about, and he expects that from you as well. If you put in the work, you'll do just fine. Only reason I didn't get an A is because I was lazy.

analysis.name: Akram Al-Turk
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Akram is a really cool guy that knows a lot about subject matter. The class is pretty laid back and free-flowing and he tries to help the class seems to not be able to grasp a concept. The class isn't SUPER easy, but considering that all the tests are open-note, take-home tests, you should be able to get a solid grade as long as you put in the time

Akram was well-liked by everyone in SOCI 133. He does a great job facilitating discussion and connecting material on a grand scale. The class is consistently interesting, and Akram is always willing to make time to help students that needed it. Students learn not only about political trends on an abstract level, but also perform data analysis.

Best instructor I have ever had. Very understanding during pandemic. Listened to what the students had to say about their situations & really took that into consideration. Not a hard grader at all as long as you follow the rubrics he provides. Lack of pressure in this class really allowed me to learn a lot. Textbook/readings are provided for free.

EE's tend to be lots of work but I found the amount of reading and writing required for this course outside of class to be hard to keep up with, especially when you're spending about 3 hours a week volunteering for the course and not getting any additional credit for it. Disorganized, but a reasonable prof who will work with you.
Seriously the nicest guy. You can tell he really cares about his students and he's super easy going.

analysis.name: Patrick Akos
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tough grader Not much to grade Lots of paper/book to read Pop quizzes

A class that you get out what you put in. Akos is reading heavy and this takes a lot of time but it helps you understand class comments. Stickler on grading (points taken off easily) but a cool guy and fun professor.
Professor critically grades. There are group based projects and if you are in a bad group you suffer. Will not move you grade up even if half a point away from a higher grade. Overall bad experience.

Akos is easily the best professor I've had at UNC! He is a tough grader though!!!!!! If you say one thing off or wrong, that's half a point off of something you can only get 3 points on. He truly cares about his students and commits to the material he is teaching. Wouldn't call this an easy A class, more like an easy B. Love Akos, not his grading!!
Unfair grader, does not bump your grade even if half a point from next letter grade.

analysis.name: John Akin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class consists of multiple guest speakers who lecture about boring things. There's a huge final group project and too many readings. The class is super boring and you don't learn anything useful.
If you don't pass this class, you're not alive.

analysis.name: Akilah Swinton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class wasn't that hard. Just had to go to take class take the notes that she wanted you to know. Read textbook and get a general idea of whats going on. Not too bad other wise.
Very nice and very helpful professor.  We did a lot of group assignments which were sometimes a little elementary but the class is really easy.
She seemed to really care about us understanding the material and doing well in the class. I really liked the videos and guest speakers.

analysis.name: Heather Apple
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Heather is incredible! She is the best professor I have had at UNC. She provides feedback in every class and encourages us to produce our best work. Additionally, she is a creative genius, always coming up with ideas on the spot. A true professor of practice. Thanks to her facilitation, our class became friends. TAKE HER and cherish your time.

Heather was awesome! She is so cool and kind and her industry experience makes her an awesome resource. Assignments were easy and graded generously. You're required to stand up and present your work almost every day, but it was never intimidating and was just an opportunity to get detailed feedback. Definitely take her if you can!

I could not recommend Heather more. Class is primarily presentation-based, but she gives super in-depth, constructive feedback. Lots of guest speakers and practical, real-world advice. I learned so much from Heather and I wish she taught more classes because I would absolutely take more with her.

analysis.name: April Munroe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: All hail April Munroe. She is such a nice and caring ENGL105 professor. She made the class fun and interesting. She was a very relaxed grader and made it very hard to get below an A lol. I am a STEM kid and hated English but she made me love going to her class.
April is amazing! She's very nice, her class is fun and easy. You do a lot of work in groups with a lot of independence. Very little homework, and a pretty lenient grader. Take her class!!!

April is such a caring teacher. She is always understanding of students needs and the pressures of being a student. She uses a very creative connection between literature/writing and conspiracy theories to make the class interesting and educational. Although there were more assignments than expected, I enjoyed doing them as we chose the topics.

This class was pretty chill and super easy. It's pretty much like a book club. 2 papers based on analysis of your chosen book. Midterm was super easy, she gave us the test the class before. Final exam was to make a playlist on another book of our choice. Don't even have to talk in class, just read books you plan on doing papers and final on.

Pretty standard class. Four papers. Very heavily discussion based. Really thought provoking class about mystery novels and conspiracy theories. One of the better and more fun classes I have taken at UNC. Pretty easy to get a good grade too. Didn't read all the books but will still probably make an A.

analysis.name: Apurba Chakraborty
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This guy is the man. Is very approachable and friendly and wants you to succeed in his classes rather than perform poorly. The presentation you have to do forces you out of your comfort zone and helps you learn about the psychology behind legislature and political issues and bias present today. 10 page paper but makes it an interesting task.

This guy really wants his students to succeed, and while he won't tolerate slacking, he definitely strives to allow everyone to get an A if they are willing to work. Participation matters, but he does a great job of explaining the readings, so just skimming them works. One ten-page paper, but no other homework.

Professor Chakraborty is great. He's not an absurdly hard grader like most of the Poli profs I've had. You can tell he really cares about his students and honestly just wants you to learn something. Definitely a solid choice.

analysis.name: April Lawson
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's one of the most understanding and sweetest professors at UNC. I was hesitant to take this class because I had an interest in creative writing but I wasn't entirely sure if I'd succeed in the class. Lawson makes it a great experience and supports you through any issues you have.

April is not only one of the nicest English professors I've ever had but also one of the most creative and considerate. One ten page paper and daily pop quizzes for ENGL 130. Class discussions are always riveting and her paper feedback is so thoughtful. Definitely take a creative writing class with her if you get the chance.

April is super nice and chill - the class is very laid back and not difficult if you do the reading (which arent demanding or difficult but are necessary). There are daily quizzes on the readings, and a final short story. A good class to take 'for fun'.
omg so talented, please stay @ unc forever

analysis.name: Amanda DelVecchia
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed this class and ultimately learned a lot, but the class did feel disorganized at times. The Canvas page was confusing and work was returned weeks/months after we turned it in. However, for someone interested in GIS, I would recommend this class, as it covered a lot, and Professor Delvecchia was very  helpful and accessible outside of class

Gave many basic assignments, did them all well. Graded 2 months after assigned, I got 7/9 8/12 etc. Couldn't change my strategy for doing those because it was end of year. She gave surprise grade # of perusall comments we made. Never told us to write comments on all but 2. Got a 14/30 on it dropped my grade by 7% got me a B. Super unfair ridiculous

Dr. DelVecchia is sweet but her class is disorganized and her grading criteria is unclear. There's no way to know what she will decide deduct points for in written assignments. 591 needs a recitation to justify the amount of labs. The pacing and structure is nonexistent, and she is unavailable outside of her office hour.

Dr. DelVecchia is the best professor at UNC hands down! She genuinely cares for her students and wants to help them achieve their goals. She will work with you to find what you want to do then help you figure out how to get there. I haven't has a professor as influential as Dr. DelVecchia in my four years at UNC
wouldnt take again. Lectures were hard to follow. Everyone completed activities at a different pace. Grading criteria for quizzes was unclear. Not enough guidance

analysis.name: Amy Chambless
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I absolutely adore Professor Chambless. She is a fantastic professor. In-class time is typically spent practicing skills, so I would recommend taking time to read/take notes on the assigned textbook pages so the content doesn't sneak up on you for the test. Grades fairly and generously, and always gives clear feedback. Take ITAL 101 with her!

She's very participation heavy, which makes sense with an introductory language course. She's always happy to help and offer office hours, extra practice, and support when students ask for it. She's very patient and encouraging, the class is a very welcoming environment.

I highly recommend Dr.Chambless for Ital 101 and 102; she is an amazing lecturer and has a lot of empathy towards her students. She grades fairly and provides plenty of feedback, as well as resources, to help you improve your Italian. She is very knowledgeable about the textbook content and is always available to meet with students.
She was really nice and really made sure the students understood the material. I slacked off pretty bad and failed the first 2 test but she worked with me and I ended up doing ok. Don't fall behind.

She is very friendly and encouraging! Classes have a lot of fun activities to encourage constant learning.  There are short quizzes (vocab or the grammar concept you are learning), but they are easy and only count for 5% of your overall grade. There are also assignments w/each unit to record a conversation about a certain topic with a partner.

analysis.name: Mandy Cooper
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took the class in Fall of 2025. Class was TA-graded, but Dr. Cooper structures it well and doesn't set expectations terribly high. Show up, follow along, and you're in a solid spot to get a good grade. Course was mainly surface-level, though definitely more covered than your typical person would know. Lectures weren't boring or overly interesting.

As a person, Professor Cooper is amazing. She truly cares about us as students, even in a large class. The way she set up the midterm and final was great. However, my TA who graded all my essays was unfair and difficult in grading considering it's a gen-ed. The lectures also weren't the most engaging although she is very passionate about her work.

Dr. Cooper is very knowledgable! She is passionate about what she teaches and is easy to talk to and encourages group discussions. Your TA will be grading everything so I would say to make sure to go to both their office hours as well as Dr.Cooper's if you feel like you should have had higher scoring/asking how to improve for future assignments.

The lectures could get a little long, esp if you're familiar with US history already, but Dr. Cooper was super cool and knowledgable, regardless. Her assignments are very clear, but you are being graded by a TA who can be inconsistent and give little feedback due to the volume of papers. office hours and the writing center can help you do well!

Cooper is super nice and caring. Lectures were very hit or miss imo; some were super interesting, and others felt like a chore. Lots of writing but graded pretty easily (may have been specific to my TA). No tests at all and offers a ton of extra credit; pretty easy A overall, but there are definitely more interesting gen-ed history classes.

analysis.name: Angela  Ambrosio
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Angela is one of the best Spanish professors that I have ever had. She is an extremely fair grader but also provides good feedback. She made each class fun and not boring, even when using slides to teach. She is hilarious and always made class feel like a welcoming place, and she gives you lots of practice to prepare you for the tests and final.

Angela is so sweet and entertaining, but she genuinely wants to you to learn and understand topics in class. I never once dreaded going to her class. Participation is required and recorded throughout the semester, so try to answer questions frequently even if your not 100% sure. Definitely take Angela's class if you have the opportunity.
Very doable SPAN 105 class. She was kind and graded fairly, and class was genuinly fun to attend. Participation does matter a lot, so keep that in mind.

analysis.name: Ami Ward
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: ** EMES 101L** she is the best. checks off your labs! she understands you are taking this lab for the credit. Took her at 8am bc of how much you want to take her lab time.
Great TA. She was very helpful and understanding. Reviewed necessary material and explained the labs thoroughly. Would recommend.

For EMES 101. Ami was the TA for this class, and I'm not completely sure she knew what she was doing. She didn't answer a lot of questions thoroughly and was not always available for office hours (consistently rescheduled them) or in class. Nice person though.
Easy class. Amy is great with giving feed back. Not a hard class just turn in stuff in time and review notes.
Such an amazing TA! Very helpful during office hours!

analysis.name: Amalia Ashley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ashley is wonderful! We had a group book club project, which was really interesting and something I haven't seen before in a class at UNC yet. She clearly cares about her students and makes sure everyone feels comfortable and safe. Her feedback on assignments is great, and she tells you exactly what to fix and why you got points off.

*wgst 340* Professor Ashley's decent. You can tell she cares about the material. LOTS of reading and weekly journals that are pretty tedious and boring. The material was interesting if you are interested in the topic l. Has barely graded all semester so no idea what my grade will be. Service learning for apples was the best part of the class!

If you are interested in the content you will love this class. class is split into lecture, activity, and discussion. You can miss 3 of each. She covers a wide range of topics and truly wants you to enjoy the class. Exams are online with clear feedback for how to improve. One of my favorite WGST classes at UNC!

I loved Dr.Ashley's class. super interesting but you def have to do the readings. She had a lecture, activity, discussion setup for her MWF class which I really enjoyed. Had to read a book for a book club but it was engaging and not overly strenuous. You will learn a lot and should get an A if you do your work and participate.
*WGST 270 Women and Sport. Good lectures and discussion about modern topics. I have no interest in sports but learned a lot from this class.

analysis.name: Aria Tsoulouhas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took RELI-101 with professor Tsoulouhas this semester and it ended up being by far my favorite course I took. Prof. Tsoulouhas is very kind and displays a good knowledge of subject matters present in the course. She is not difficult to reach outside of class and you can tell student success is a priority. I would take class again with her.

RELI 101 ended up being one of my favorite classes I've ever taken at UNC. Professor Tsoulouhas gives amazing lectures and makes complicated ideas easy to understand with real-world case studies. I would definitely take a class with her again!

An interesting course. I learned a lot while investing a reasonable amount of time. Discussions were also worthwhile. Quick aside: Students at a school as prestigious as this one shouldn't lash out because the professor prohibits plagiarism, or because they assign college-level amounts of reading. It makes us all look bad and devalues our degrees.
Professor Tsoulouhas is very organized with her Canvas being extremely accessible and all of her rubrics/deadlines being very clear. This class has a lot of group work and class discussions.
Be prepared to read.. Make sure you cite every quote. Not a fun class

analysis.name: Arunima Bhattacharya
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I actually love her. She's genuinely so smart, and this is a hard class, so I'm aware of the challenging content. But still, her lectures were great, and she stopped for questions a lot. The first midterm was definitely not easy, but she was generous with grading and made the second one easier. She's a very responsible teacher.

Dr. Bhattacharya was an amazing lecturer despite the abstractness of a lot of the concepts in real analysis. The subject was hard, but she was very fair and generous with grading, along with guidance outside of class during office hours or by email. Incredibly hard class, but she made it more tolerable.

The first exam average was 51%, which isn't unusual for MATH 521, but grading has been pretty unclear. We were only told a "nonuniform curve" will reduce the number of students who fail, leaving many students completely unsure how they will be affected by a curve. Lectures are generally good but often feel a bit rushed.
Amazing lecturer, she explained difficult topics super well. 521 was definitely a learning curve as it was different from other math classes I'd taken before but she made it easier to adapt.

This was a very tough class. Prof Bhattacharya is nice and understanding, but often did not explain class concepts fully, and homeworks were unreasonably hard. I learned more from my recitation TA. The final was near impossible, with the class average being an F. the class was curved a full letter grade at the end. I don't recommend this class.

analysis.name: John Arnold
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Arnold reignited my passion for creating art. Although I hadn't taken an organized class since early high school, I was able to produce detailed drawings I was proud of by the end of the semester because of Professor Arnold's guidance and encouragement. I truly believe any student under his instruction is capable of immense growth.

This was the last class I took to finish my degree and I was so happy! Mr. Arnold was great at teaching the fundamentals of drawing. He got us out of our heads about perfectionism. I gained a lot of skills in this class than I have in past art classes. Bonus, he plays great music in class during drawing time! Highly recommend!!

He is very clear in his guidelines but is also very flexible and willing to work with you. He teaches the basics but encourages self-exploration of the topics. There is no textbook, and there are also no tests, just two portfolios made up of classwork and a final project. Very good class for improving your fundamentals and learning technique.

Phenomenal instructor! Incredibly kind and cares about your individual success and growth. He's easily accessible and makes his expectations incredibly clear. He makes learning the basics of drawing fun and interesting and gives amazing feedback.

analysis.name: Ariannah Kubli
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Take her! Absolutely amazing she really cares for her students and it is very easy to earn an A if you turn everything in on time. She uses grading contracts so if you meet all the requirements you can get the grade you desire. Super nice, projects are engaging and she provides clear and constructive feedback.

Professor Kubli is kind. She was always accessible and willing to help. It is clear that she cares about her students. The projects were not too hard and you got to choose what you wanted to write about for all of them. The class is contract grading, so if you do the work and go to class you will get an A.

She is the best. I hope she stays a teacher because she has enthusiasm and the smarts to back it up. Such an easy class and not too easy where it was boring. If you're checking rate my prof. to see if she's a good teacher, the million 5/5 reviews should tell you YES

She is amazing and super flexible whenever you need her to be. very very easy and straight forward class but also super interesting. The class is what you want it to be because every project is very personalized and targeted to your interests. HIGHLY recommend her!

I definitely recommend Ms. Kubli for ENGL 105. The assignments for the class are actually interesting and she is a super fair grader. She's also very forgiving if you need an extension or extra help for an assignment.

analysis.name: Alaina Garland
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 422 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Unless you want to learn random facts, such as the length of fruit fly's stuff or the debates around religion and evolution, do not take this course. Dr. Garland chooses to spend time on minor details that do not appear on the test, and thus does not effectively teach the class. Do not take BIO 101 with Dr. Garland. Save yourself the trouble.

I've never made one of these so you the fact that I had to take time to make this should be a warning. She has NO business teaching at the undergraduate level. If she taught Intro to ABCs I would not take it with her. I've had elementary teachers that are more capable of teaching than her. She is by far the WORST professor I have ever come across.

For starters, I hate this class. I took AP and honors Bio in high school and got As and then get a 36 on the first test. I would study for hours and the questions on the test did not make any sense what so ever. STAY CLEAR if you do not want to tank your GPA. She wastes time making a seating chart for a 400 person class instead of teaching.

Dr. Garland is such a sweetheart but you should steer clear of this course. The exams are harder than the material is to understand. And the lectures are fluffy and unhelpful. I'm hoping to be premed and this course made me genuinely reconsider whether I was fit for it. Do yourself a favor and take any other Professor. It's not worth the trouble.

Dr. Garland wastes a lot of lecture time going over useless information including but not limited to preaching about career goals. Tests are very tricky and seem to test test taking ability more rather than knowledge. Lecture lowkey useless, but she's definitely caring. Just not a great prof. Get ready to study and read the textbook.

analysis.name: Valentina Arismendi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is great, and I would definitely recommend her. This class is centered around Figma and the basics of UX/UI, and she does a great job of teaching both. She is not a tough grader but gives great feedback, no matter what grade you get.

Val is a great teacher, and I found her lectures to be informative. She is very available and graduated not long ago from UNC, which makes her more relatable and fun than other professors. I enjoyed the guest speakers she brought to class, and she is more than qualified to teach this class. I would highly recommend taking any class with Val.

Said it was her first semester teaching and it kinf of showed. Good class overall and really learned a lot but it was a bit disorganized at times. Gave a lot of time in class to work on projects. It was online so not my most memorable but Val made UX easy and seems like shed have good connections if you want to go into that field.

analysis.name: Arne Kalleberg
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Kalleberg is the goat. He is a caring guy and is very knowledgeable in sociology. He is an expert in the field and very well respected around campus and nationwide. If you can take a class with him, jump on it. Do what is asked, which is not much, and you will make an A. 5/5 class.

Dr. Kalleberg is the goat. He is an expert in his field, very laid back, and a very caring guy. Absolutely take his class if you can. Do what he asks, which is not overwhelming, and you will succeed. 5/5 class and 5/5 prof.

Class was interesting and engaging, and super easy. If you're not doing well you're not trying. He mostly stands out for how he is as a person! He really cares about his students and makes an effort to know everyone. He's not the most tech savvy, so we spent a lot of classes with him on the phone with its, but we laughed it off! HIGHLY recommend

I LOVE ARNE. Would regularly drag myself out of bed only to see him. Love his cutie NY accent, made me feel like I was back home. Content was easy. Lectures were not super heavy. He's just a sweetheart and I love him.

Was a decent lecturer. Course content was pretty simple and easy to understand. Multiple short readings, but not too much to handle. Laughed when a student asked about extra credit... but overall was alright.

analysis.name: Benjamin Arbuckle
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 50 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Sitting in on Arbuckle's lectures is like story time for the class.  His enthusiasm and excitement for teaching the material rubs off on you, and this is being written by a science major & minor student.  Exams are easy to study for as long as you put in effort the night before or so & listen to the lectures generally.  GREAT class for gened reqs!

Best class ever! There were no midterms or finals. One 5 page paper in the middle of the semester, but not difficult if you don't leave it to the last minute. Professor Arbuckle is understanding and kind. While his lectures were not required, they were very interesting and worth your time to attend. Would 100% take a class with Arbuckle again.

Minimal feedback given throughout the class, didn't grade any assignment until the day before grades were due. Very unclear final essay rubric and if you don't write in the exact style he is looking for, you will not do well. But you wouldn't know what that style is, because he doesn't grade anything or give feedback throughout the class.

kind, very interesting, understanding prof. easy A. 1 paper due in the middle of the year making it possible to actually be interested in the content. you get downgraded if you use AI but are given the (optional) chance to revise the paper at the end of the sem. this was good incentive to be more ambitious with the work resulting in an A.

Amazing class!! Professor Arbuckle is so nice and caring. He is accessible at all times of the day and often answers emails very quickly. He answers any and all questions. Professor Arbuckle's lectures are very interesting and sometimes showed images about his archaeology experience which was incredible to see first hand.

analysis.name: Ashton Rooney
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ashton Rooney encourages students to participate in Spanish, and he grew my confidence. He doesn't care if you aren't proficient, as long as you try. He is lenient with grading, even though he does have to follow the Span 203 grading guidelines. His class is engaging, fun, and educational. If you are nervous to take Span 203, definitely take his.

One of the best profs I've had. He genuinely cares and doesn't expect perfection, just effort. I hadn't taken Spanish in four years, but Ashton helped us learn and stay engaged. He doesn't control the class structure, but he makes the most of it. The tests are tough. Prep and do VHL early. I am not the best at Spanish and still managed an A-.

I came into this class super scared because I hadn't taken Spanish since my freshman year of high school. However, Ashton made it such a supportive and fun environment, and I ended up doing great on all the exams, essays, etc., because he focused on building our confidence.

analysis.name: Sudhanshu Ashu Handa
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Love ashu!! Very willing to help outside of class, lots of jokes throughout lecture to keep us engaged, and lots of step by step help to make sure we are really following what we are doing! TAs were great as well. Loved the treats ashu brought in (though wish we got to try his brownie recipe). If you can take a Class with ashu, do it!

Professor Ashu is an amazing. He's incredibly engaging, bakes cookies for his students, is clearly passionate about the material, and makes his expectations/what we need to know for exams very clear. If you attend the lectures, utilize your recitation TA's and their office hours, and take good notes you won't have a problem in this class!

Ashu is super nice—he brought us cookies/cupcakes and even gifts when he traveled for research. The class itself isn't super hard, and the curves were also really generous. As long as you come to the class, do the problem sets, and attend review sessions, you will do fine. Favorite class & professor—definitely + highly recommended!!!

Professor Ashu is a really caring professor (he baked us treats often and got us gifts when he travelled)! He doesn't provide powerpoints for his class, so attending his classes would be really helpful. And the exams are hard and he's tough grader, but his exam grades and the overall grades are curved generously, so it's not too bad.
TA Laraib Kamal has anger issues.

analysis.name: Idris Assani
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Before taking this class I loved calculus. It was so frustrating taking his tests because they were nothing like the homework assignments or the problems in the book. That isn't even the worst of it. He doesn't give partial credit although he says he does. You could spend 20 minutes working one test problem and make a small mistake towards the end
Avoid at all cost! GPA killer.
GOAT of a professor. Super awesome guy and really cares about the material and about his students. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! He will help you. Super great guy, really recommend.

Prof Assani cares about his students. His lectures make 521 like learning a new way of thinking. Go to office hours and ask for help, he wants you to succeed, so he will help. My sole complaint was the disparity in difficulty between this year's final and the material we had seen all semester/last year's final, but he does challenge you to think.

Professor Assani is incredibly intelligent. You'll understand that after hearing his first lecture. But not all intelligent people are great professors. Professor Assani rushes through tons of materials in one lecture each week, leaving the other day purely for quizzes. You'll more than likely be relying on online resources to learn the material.

analysis.name: Ashok Krishnamurthy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I know some foreign professors are bad, this one is NOT. He just came from Ohio and taught this semester's 116 kind of tag-team with Dr. Ahalt. Both were extremely helpful and practical. Assignments were well-designed and they were flexible on dates. Lectures were good, not required. I highly recommend Dr. Krishnamurthy for any level class!

COMP 116 is tough no matter what but Ashok is by far the best option. He's funny and a patient lecturer. His extra-credit/take-home policy for midterms are way fairer than Majikes' and honestly saved my grade. He also offers a ton of options for extra-credit integrated into the assignments/worksheets and he doesn't take attendance. Really cool dude

Ashok is such an amazing professor. Though I'm not sure why he is teaching, because he is a research professor and that's his main focus. Regardless, he is very caring and will curve exams based on the class average He also lets you fix your midterms, and your correction is 70% of the midterm's final grade. Overall, and easy class and a great prof

This class is definitely a bit different than most other classes in that learning is HIGHLY dependent on you doing the assignments and understanding the mechanism behind it. That being said, the class is pretty chill and Dr. Krishnamurthy definitely goes over a lot of useful, fun, and interesting material in the class. It's manageable.

Ashok was a very kind and considerate professor however was not the best lecturer. The lectures were mainly watching professors code and follow along without a lot of explanation as to why things were done. This course would be much easier if you have an understanding of programming beforehand, however is not impossible without any.

analysis.name: Asya Passinsky
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I've heard Philosophy at UNC is pretty tough, but Prof. Passinsky made the class as interesting as she could and she brought in philosophers to talk with us. The daily amount of work is not actually that bad, but the papers are crucial. She doesn't give specific criteria but if you make your paper topic specific and overly clear you'll be fine.

Since this is a philosophy class, your grade will heavily depend on participation and papers. If you are not a good writer, I would NOT recommend taking this class because one bad grade on a paper can cause you to fail. It would have been extremely helpful if the professor looked over rough drafts since two papers were over half our grade.

Professor Passinksy is really intelligent and she puts a lot of effort into her classes and gives her students opportunities to actually talk to the philosophers we discuss in class. She is a tough grader but she is available in office hours to talk about your paper before submitting. If you're not a good writer, skip this class.

I loved Dr P's class so much I decided to minor in philosophy. She seems cold at first but she's just like that. If you reach out to her she's super nice and the course itself is super interesting. If you have a chance to take her classes definitely do, it's rewarding but not crazy hard.

analysis.name: Ellen Atterbury
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Ellen is an amazing professor who makes it easy for students to succeed. She makes expectations clear with rubrics and grading criteria, and is a very fair grader. She leaves great feedback and resources for students to learn and improve. The exams were pretty easy and projects and in-class activities were fun and engaging. Overall great class!

Not sure how anyone could rate Professor Atterbury low, she is great! The class is pretty standardized for projects/tests but Atterbury prepares you well and encourages in-class group discussion which is super helpful if you actually want to learn the language. Midterms and final were easy if you just study a couple days before.

(Spanish 204) This class is pretty standardized for quizzes/tests and assignments but Professor Atterbury was super understanding all semester long and gave helpful feedback on assignments without being overly harsh. Make sure to talk in class and do your readings and you'll be fine!

I didn't like her as much as other reviews. What made me mad is nothing was assigned in Canvas with specific dates so it was easy to forget due dates. Attendance is mandatory and you have to participate everyday.
She was really amazing, we always know the expectations. She makes the class fun and educational!!

analysis.name: Atiya Husain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Atiya knows how to be engaging with her students and gives many examples to ensure that you understand a topic. She made complicated theories seem like elementary school with ease. She is always calm, cool, and confident. Highly recommend

Great Professor overall, took her in the 2024 winter term, and her lectures were truly engaging. There's something admirable about her, from the way she speaks so eloquently, to how she engages with the class by eliciting introspection into our consciousness. And she also situates her lectures in real-life contexts for better understanding. 10/10

Atiya is a great teacher and her lectures are very interesting. She does a great job of relaying the material in a clear way. There are 3 take home tests, each worth 20%, and an in-class final also worth 20%. She gives pop quizzes on the reading almost every class, but they trickled out at the end. The readings are all online, no textbook required!

analysis.name: David Attewell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's the sweetest guy, always asking for feedback on where he can improve as a professor. Lectures are interesting and the grading system is extremely fair, consisting of a presentation, two 5-page papers, a final, participation and 3 pop quizzes. Very open to giving feedback during office hours and encourages class discussions on relevant matters.

David Attewell was my favorite professor during my first semester at UNC! His lectures were engaging, he values class participation, and he truly makes an effort to get to know his students. You have a few assignments throughout the semester but his grading criteria is clear. He is absolutely brilliant and I could not recommend him more strongly!

David is one of my favorite professors at UNC. He's young which makes his lectures more interesting because he thinks about current events and relates to his students. He's a lenient grader and SUPER caring about his students and the quality of his teaching. Just make sure you are participating in class and doing the readings. 10/10 recommend.

I absolutely love David! He is so knowledgable, approachable, and caring . He explains concept well, but lectures can be dry. Fair grader on papers and no midterms! There are 3 pop quizzes (easy) but just on the readings so if you read you'll do good. I would do everything I could to take Attewell's class.

Professor Attewell is very knowledgable in his field and lectures with confidence. His lectures and powerpoint slides make politics easy to learn and he has made learning super accessible to non-political students. Highly recommend, be sure to take notes of his slides and read the case studies.

analysis.name: Ava Geenen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: PHIL 140: Very nice prof. but class can get dull. Worksheets give good overview of papers but the subject matter is really confusing, especially for your first philosophy class. Half of class stopped attending. Papers are hard but if you go to office hours and the writing center you can totally do well. If you love philosophy, you will 100% enjoy.

Ava is a great professor. She understands the material extremely well and, more importantly, can explain it well. Her readings were thoughtfully chosen and refreshingly contemporary compared to many introductory-level philosophy courses at UNC. Additionally, her unit quizzes required meaningful engagement with the texts, which helped learning.

Ava was caring and accommodated for everyone's needs in terms of feedback and giving extensions. Lots of tough reading but she explained it well in class. Lecture and participation heavy, you will be expected to speak at least 2x a class for a good participation grade.

PHIL140 was an awful experience. The class material felt like a giant circle leading back to the same discussion and topic we had on the first day of class. Paper grading was harsh for the class, and the lectures were very discussion-based, yet dull. Half the class stopped showing up throughout the semester, if that says anything.

This course was fairly difficult for an introductory class and contained a lot of reading and lectures. Professor Geenen was always willing to help outside of class and had some interesting lectures. The material was pretty comprehensive as well.

analysis.name: Ashley Anderson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 122 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Great class and professor overall, but didn't love the communication between professor and I. She's very nice but unavailable. I showed up to her office hours once, waited an hour and a half just to find out that she was in Europe and didn't notify her students. This was a week before finals. But everything other than that about the class was fine.

Professor Anderson is disgustingly and dangerously educated. She makes lectures engaging and is very knowledgeable in pretty much everything she talks about. Attendance is required. There's weekly quizzes with five questions and two papers, along with the midterm and final that make up your grade. She challenges you, but an A is possible!

I took POLI 130 with her, and she was pretty great! Informative lectures, clearly knows her subject matter, and encourages class participation. Readings are the main homework, and are necessary to know for the midterm and final. Additionally, I would recommend checking the lecture handouts for the key terms, because those will also be on the tests.

no one cares that she went to Stanford and Harvard. this is a 100-level class. she's unaccommodating: i had to take weekly quizzes while hospitalized. grading feels TA-dependent, As are rare (94 = A, no rounding). i was docked for recitation participation despite university excused absences. not an easy A, and she acts like it's your only class.

Super interesting lecture and class material. Anderson is incredibly knowledgeable. None of the assignments are very difficult; however, almost impossible to get an A, given 80% of your grade comes from just 4 assignments (2 papers and a written midterm and final / have to really crush the papers) + extra credit assignments were really dumb imo.

analysis.name: Sage Aviles
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Spanish was such a hard class due to the way it was taught. Genuinely did not feel comfortable speaking Spanish in class due to how rude they were, and expected us to know more than is generally expected out of 101 students. Do not take this with them if you can avoid it, and always go off the rubric instead of what is said in class or posted.

Prof Aviles made an effort to make lectures engaging by making jeopardy and other review games (that are not required by the 102 director), but they are VERY passive-aggressive. Make sure you participate, they will plummet your participation grade if you are not being VERY active. Also, just generally rude and laughs at struggling students

Lectures weren't engaging and lecture materials came directly from the textbook. She would basically just repeat everything we've already read with a few in-class activities here and there, which was overall not very helpful. Don't take this class if you can help it.

analysis.name: Avi-Dan Santo
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof and class are so incredibly boring. Prof. Santo's lectures consist entirely of him reading off slides with way too many words on them. Not a lot of assignments and they're not inherently difficult, but they are graded harshly. Didn't learn anything from this class and I wouldn't recommend it, huge waste of time. Dropped COMM major bc of this.

Very easy but very boring. Slides were just many bullet points on a blank screen although he tries his best to make it more interesting. Participation is the majority of your grade, and you have no actual exams just papers.

Good professor but super wordy and long winded. He was nice and clearly spoken, but kinda weirded me out sometimes. He had guest lectures all the time. Not a hard class at all, but be prepared to listen to boring lectures.

analysis.name: Lorna Avilés
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Aviles is hands down the best professor I have had at UNC so far. Although speaking in a different language can be daunting, she encourages practice and genuinely cares about whether or not you are learning. Participation matters to stay engaged, but class would fly by, as she's a great teacher and not a boring lecturer. TAKE HER CLASS!!!

Professor Aviles is amazing. Her lectures are interesting and engaging and she doesn't take herself too seriously. Her course load is made to challenge you and help you succeed (if you put in the work). She returns graded work so so fast. Seriously, she is the kind of professor that makes you happy you paid for college. Take her class.

Don't let other reviews fool you, this is NOT an easy A class. There are a handful of grammar quizzes throughout the semester that can tank your grade, the in-class essays that can be graded somewhat tough in terms of grammar, and the examsare fairly graded, but you have to study and be familar with the content.

I took prof Avilés for span 344 and loved it! You will spend a lot of class time discussing readings, the lesson, etc with peers and I feel it really improved my speaking skills in a chill environment. The papers aren't hard and you can often take them in your own direction to keep it fresh. There is a group presentation but it isn't hard. Take it!

One of the best professors I have had. She grades SO quickly (got my final exam grade back 6 minutes after the grading period had ended). She gives great feedback and does a good job of keeping everyone on track. There is a good amount of weekly homework, but its worth it and is helpful in understanding the class material. Really awesome Prof.

analysis.name: Ava Stone
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I do not know what these ratings are talking about when she is described as "passive aggressive" . Believe me, she is anything but passive aggressive. She wants you to succeed. She wants you to participate in class and if you are wrong she will gently nudge you in the right direction. She gave lots of extra credit opportunities and is very helpful

I did not like this class, the structure and lecture style of this course were awful making it hard to learn. She was passive-aggressive to students and she really didn't "teach". I would not recommend this class at all. I took 101 with another teacher who was amazing so this class was a disappointment. She is also not a native speaker.

She's not the best, but not the worst. The class itself isn't too hard so who your instructor is doesn't matter too much. I don't think she's a native Italian speaker though, which has it's downsides.

Ava is extremely nice, and caries her warm demeanor throughout her lessons and lectures. She urges students to participate in class, which facilitates great camaraderie between classmates, and is always understanding to any issues that may arise and responds well to motivated students who demonstrate effort in her class.

Ava is really nice. Her class can be difficult but she recognizes effort and is really nice when you're struggling. The IPAs are really clear and easy to do well on but the tests are a little more difficult. Overall, she's a good teacher and I would def take 102 by her if she taught it.

analysis.name: Avery Wilson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great professor for a summer class, really made sure that everyone understood the material and took time to help during class. Shortened some of the homework and was willing to give people some more time as needed to complete it. Very accessible and willing to work with you so that you understood the concepts clearly. Exams were similar to lecture.

He was a nice guy but he did not really teach the course material well. Lectures were not mandatory and I went to them at first, but it just felt like a waste of my time. We spent half of class just sitting silently in break-out rooms, and I could barely tell what was going on when he was teaching. I ended up teaching myself with the lesson videos.
Wilson was very harsh with his grading and did not teach the material well. You have to work on your own outside of class to get a decent grade.

Generally a good professor and a nice guy. He isn't the greatest lecturer but he records them and provides lectures from other professors so it's pretty easy to learn the material on your own. Tests and the final are weighted fairly heavily but they are a lot like the problems you do in class. Not a super easy class but manageable.

I really enjoyed having Professor Wilson for Math 130. He is extremely approachable, and often pauses lecture to encourage students to ask questions and clear up confusion. As long as you pay attention in class and put in the work outside of class, I couldn't see how anyone would leave this professor a less than stellar review!

analysis.name: Etna Avalos Molina
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's great. Gives awesome feedback and grades tough, but fairly. Do the online assignments, write the essays, and do your best and you'll be fine. She really just wants her students to make an effort. Try your best and you'll be fine!!!!

Most of class is just doing activities in the textbook and speaking Spanish with other students, so preparing for class is pretty easy but participation is important. Not a lot of homework given. Her most important thing is that you put in the effort. She doesn't expect you to be fluent. Doesn't give very good feedback on writing/presentations.

Loved her as a professor. She's so funny and while the material wasn't all that interesting to me, I still enjoyed her class. She was a fair grader when it came to essays (got a 95 and 92 on them). Her exams were a little difficult but as long as you study you'll be fine.
She is really nice and definitely tries to spice up her lectures. You use the textbook everyday in class and just go through all of the activities. Not a lot of homework assigned.
She is a very kind person but is sometimes hard to reach outside of class. Sometimes is unclear about what to do, but is still a good professor.

analysis.name: Laurence Avery
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Avery is one of the best professors in the history of the college.   12 years later I still think about his courses.   Thorough knowledge of subject matter but always accessible, Avery defines what a scholar and professor should strive for. He's the best.  Willing to help you understand the material but pushes you to be your be best.   A+++
Nice guy, and the class isn't bad if you pay attention and take notes. Very helpful if you need it, though he does seem to play favorites sometimes.
Nice guy. Clear, knowledgable, definately old school.

analysis.name: Aubrey Lewis
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: French 105 is a VERY difficult class, especially if you have only taken HS French. Aubrey was very caring and gave great feedback. I learned a lot about French in this class, but again, French is hard. If you are interested in French, Aubrey is great, but if this is for credit, take it at community college.
This is a hard class, but Professor Lewis grades fairly. She's very sweet and doesn't cold call.

tbh I think the problem with fren105 is the class itself, not the professor, but the model just felt a lot like she wasn't doing much teaching, and we had to just figure everything out on our own outside of class bc that's how fren105 is set up. the online textbook is not very helpful, either. duolingo was my best friend. she's very nice, though.

Aubrey is first and foremost a sweetheart. She does her best to make class engaging, but overall this course sucks. It's not her fault though, she's a TA who is stuck doing what UNC has decided Fren105 should do. The textbook sucks too. It's not unreasonable in terms of what you're expected to know, so while you have to self-teach, it's not awful

The problem is really mainly just the structure of FREN105, Aubrey is really nice but the structure of the class means there isn't much opportunity for her to teach, its very self-taught and the textbook was kind of weird. There are a lot of different grades though so it's not only based on tests/quizzes.

analysis.name: Aubrey Hart
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Aubrey is a great professor. He cares a lot about his students and is very willing to work with you. Language isn't always easy but he made it interesting and I learned a lot from the course. Highly recommend Italian for completing the language requirement.

I had Aubrey for 102, he was an amazing professor. He was very passionate about the language, and his passion really helped my passion for Italian grow as well. He was very helpful during class and office hours, and he is extremely patient. He also speaks Italian at a moderate pace that is very easy to follow. One of my favorite professors at UNC.

I was taught by Aubrey for ITAL 101 & 102. He is an amazing Italian professor! He is a current grad student, and he is really passionate about teaching. He makes learning accessible and fun, and he is very understanding of the fact that we are still learning and will likely make mistakes. I would definitely recommend taking a class with him!

Mr. Hart is a phenomenal person and teacher! I had him for both ITAL-101 and ITAL-102, and overall, the Italian department at UNC is AMAZING! Aubrey is a great teacher and is super encouraging and understanding. For sure, I would recommend taking any ITAL courses with him.
I had Aubrey for 102 and he was great! he cares a lot about his students and makes sure you know it's ok to make mistakes and not be perfect. I would gladly take a class with Aubrey again!

analysis.name: Audra Wormald
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It a short course with lots of information packed in. She grades a bit harshly and did accuse me of using AI to fully complete an assignment, although she encourages AI usage, so that was a bit weird. She seems judgemental, but she is open to conversation and will explain topics to you if you need extra help. Speak often in class (like everyday)!

Every class was invigorating -- heavily discussion/participation based and the best learning experience I've had at KF. Wormald was engaging and guided the conversation flow but let student voices shine. You'll have to work for it, but an A is highly doable. Definitely recommend.

I actually really enjoyed the course content and thought she was nice but kinda judgemental and it is really reading heavy, cases were fine and easy to do well on the quizes. Group projects were annoying and some of the grading doesn't make sense, same with soem of the assignments. SO make sure you look at all the files and canva pages.
Professor Wormald cares about her students. She and I had a great conversation after class that she mentioned to me later through the course. She encourages responsible use of AI.

Audura is terrible. The class is miserable but she is the only professor that teaches this mandatory class. It might be impossible to get an A in this class. She dropped everyone's participation so much. I talked in every class, didn't miss one, and still got screwed. The group project grades were so harsh. Worst prof I've had in Kenan Flagler.

analysis.name: Audrey Sachleben
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She really cares about her students, and her lectures are always informative. The readings she gives are not too long and are really the only weekly homework you get. The overall structure of the class was great, and the tests only had things you covered in class and weren't too difficult. She gives great feedback and is super nice. Would recommend

Audrey is an amazing professor! Her lectures were awesome and I was never bored in this class. You can tell that she also really cares about all her students' opinions, which makes the simulations engaging. She gives great feedback on papers, too, and is very accessible for office hours. I would 100% take a course taught by Audrey again.

Audrey was a great instructor for this class. It was extremely straightforward and she did her best to make sure both her lectures and simulations were engaging. She is not a tough grader, as long as you put in the work, and she really values participation. I would absolutely recommend Audrey for any future classes!

analysis.name: Aurora Yu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Yu is incredible! She's passionate about what she teaches and Existentialism is one of my favorite classes I've taken in my time at UNC. Highly recommend!

Aurora is kind and accomodating, but I would NOT recommend taking her for logic. Each hw assignment worth 5% of grade and harshly graded. No structure during class and no slides/notes to look back on. Textbook is confusing and doesn't get explained in class. Some extra credit opportunities but has minimal impact. Class felt tangential and unhelpful

Aurora is a HUGE fan of 17th and 18th Century philosophy, and I am not. That said, I think Aurora is one of the better instructors I've had at UNC. She provides thoughtful discussion questions with every lecture. 100% recommend taking PHIL 210 (Ancient Greek), PHIL 220 (17th and 18th Century), and/or PHIL 224 (Existential) with her.

Aurora is great. Several of my peers aren't pumped on the course content, but they all admit they have reading/discussing philosophy, so take that with a grain of salt. Put effort into the readings. Pay attention in class. Think out loud, even if your thoughts feel stupid. Aurora created a great class culture.

analysis.name: Aubrey Leary
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is an absolute nightmare. Avoid at literally all costs.

Aubrey was a great math 130 instructor! She's kind, funny, and knowledgeable. Our class often did practice with problems harder than any exam questions we had, which is honestly appreciated. Any complaints I have are not her fault and more so to do with the course coordination/structure. Get ready to work, but it is overall manageable.

Take this class at a CC. Aubrey was flexible, but I did not understand her teaching strategy and basically taught myself for the entire semester. Classes consisted of her reading through notes and learning catalytic. A Lot of material to cover. Exams gave little room for error and created/graded by all TA's. HW was outdated/took hours.

As far as math goes, Professor Leary tried her best to make the material understandable and clear. She was great at giving time for questions and answers, as well as for students to learn and practice on their own time during lectures.
This was the most poorly run class of my life. Terrible, just terrible.

analysis.name: Cemil Aydin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 37 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: One of the easiest classes that you can take at UNC. Cemil himself isn't very involved in the grading; the grades you receive are completely down to the TA (mine was pretty nice). You seriously don't need to show up for class though and there isn't much homework.

Weekly writing assignments that are around 400 words, but the readings with it are very long and dense. Decent lecturer but goes on a few tangents. Gives out points for discussion and attendance, so show up or communicate (he was pretty flexible if you told him why you were out). Midterm was an essay, final was a take home exam and in person essay

Had a really good time in this class. Prof was very kind funny and entertaining, he is very knowledgable and is always going into interesting tangents he picked up from his years of research that tie into the class. Not a harsh grader at all and is very understanding. I took him for History 538 The Middle East and the West learned a lot Recommend!

There is weekly assignments averaging around 400 words and lengthy readings with them. The TA grades most of your work and at times can be very particular on what his is looking for. Unless you want to learn about the Ottoman empire, I would not take this class.

Dr. Aydin was absolutely amazing, and this was my favorite class this semester. He is incredibly knowledgeable and offers an important and different perspective on many historical events. This course ties in with many current-day events, wars, and disputes. Note: there is a lot of reading, but 50% of your grade is recitation, highly recommend it!

analysis.name: Jeffrey Ayers
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: fantastic teacher/lecturer, has review sessions and tons of practice posted before the midterms/final. super helpful during office hours. discrete is a hard class, the first midterm is often misleading and the course piles up by the end. only concern id say is that you don't know grading scale until end of semester.

Considering this is an advanced math class, Jeff made the class as painless as possible. Even though we meet only twice a week, Jeff does his best to teach all the material in lectures to avoid outside reading (you will most likely be reading anyway). It's bittersweet that he is graduating this December, as he will no longer be teaching.
Discrete is a tough class regardless but Jeff made it manageable. He was accessible outside of class and was as helpful as possible.

He's a grad student, so there's not much I can really say other than he's just okay at teaching. First half of the class is MATH 110 review, but the second half is rough, and I don't think he was prepared. I'd take him again, but only if I had to.

Ayers was amazing! He curved the tests that the majority of the class did bad on (20 points usually). He provided us with exam reviews before every exam which were extremely helpful. He is an amazing prof that wants us to succeed. However, the final was HARD. I had a B+ going into the final and ended up with a B- in the class even after the curve.

analysis.name: Cemil Aydin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Aydin is a GREAT professor. He is so passionate about what he teaches and is very caring. Class is pretty lecture heavy and there is a lot of reading, but material is super interesting and he is a very fair grader with reasonable expectations. I highly recommend.

Professor Aydin was the most understanding professor out of both semesters of online classes. He's very passionate about his work which focuses around decolonization and every class was fun to attend. 10/10 would recommend taking a class with him!
Cemil is a good lecturer and he cares about his students, I took a class I had little to no background in and he made it incredibly interesting. Would highly recommend taking if you are into history.

analysis.name: Lindsay Ayling
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Ayling has been one of my favorite professors at UNC so far. Very knowledgable about the subject area and makes the topic interesting for students.
