SO SO caring and accessible outside of class-- she really wants students to succeed. Would absolutely take another class with her.
Very knowledgeable about the subject matter, very kind and understanding, and overall great prof. Readings are pretty dense though.
She's a wonderful teacher and would absolutely take a class from her again.

analysis.name: Karen Auerbach
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 63 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You can tell that she is very smart but her lectures are terrible. She is very hard to follow and I often walk away from class not being able to tell you one thing I learned.  There is an absurd amount of reading for an introductory course and the grading on papers/tests is harsh. I would not recommend this class to anybody!

This class was dreadful. Each lecture felt like a stream of consciousness and she never got to the point. She was very disorganized and her teaching style was very ineffective. The amount of reading was ridiculous, for example: an entire book and four primary sources as a night of reading wouldn't be out of the norm. Avoid at all costs.

Professor Auerbach is very caring and knowledgable, but the class is boring. The readings each night were very long and rarely talked about in class. She was very nice, but goes through the slides very fast and the slides barely have any actually notes to look back on. Guidelines for midterm and final were clearly posted before, which was nice.

She is kind and was gracious to me when I was struggling, giving me extensions and hearing me out. She appreciates participation and will notice if you are active. The lectures are a hectic and hard to follow, but you can still do well if you can't pay that close attention to the material. Final was not hard; what was on it was what was expected.

Everything said about this professor is true. While she is very kind and knowledgable about this topic, she is equally unorganized and her lectures are very hectic. Her quizzes are specific and detailed, make sure you truly understand the readings with dates/minor details before taking them. im halfway through the sem & only have one grade put in

analysis.name: Ayana Younge
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Younge is super nice, upbeat, and willing to help. The class material for Busi405 is commonly seen as common sense, but she finds a way to make it interesting through class activities and games. The tests are a little long and will push you to work a little more quickly than normal, but the classes tend to performs well. Homework is minimal.

Shes awesome. Show up to class and youll do very well in the class. She genuinely cares how youre doing and was willing to move assignments around based around how we were doing. Tests will push you for time, but getting 90% on them padded with all the homeworks will give you a pretty easy A
Super nice professor. Always had interesting exercises and brought lots of energy to class. The tests were insanely long and difficult for no reason.

analysis.name: Azza Ben Youssef
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Azza is such a light spirit who makes learning french enjoyable. She has a sense of humor which is refreshing in a classroom environment and she grades very fairly if anything she tries to give you as much credit as she can within reason. The course covers a lot of material, but she makes sure to go over specifically what we will be tested on.

She is such a kind, supportive, and funny instructor. She treats each student with respect despite different levels. She also explains cultural and relevant background info. She is just funny and seems to really enjoy teaching. Make sure you do the pre work. She is a fair grader. Participation matters and will help you succeed.

ABY was one of the nicest professors I've had. She speaks very fast but she has a true passion for teaching french and ensuring that we understand everything. I would definitely take another class with her.

Professor Youssef is by far the better of the two french professors I have had at UNC. She is much easier in grading and is sassy which I think is super funny. She is also super accommodating with grading (I forgot to submit half of a HW assignment and she gave me full credit for it). Overall, her class was the best french class I have taken.

Azza is the best professor I have ever had. She encourages everyone to speak in French each class and I can testify that this has improved my French so much. She is very graceful correcting us when we make mistakes so we learn but are not afraid to mess up. She wants everyone to learn and succeed and knows how to help us do so!

analysis.name: Amanda Aziz
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Amanda was a good professor. Her lectures were very informative and she cared a lot about students' well-being. However, her criteria weren't always clear when it came to grading papers. I often got feedback that I didn't follow the prompt when I would address everything in the prompt. The class was easy, but don't expect to ace the papers.

Amanda said at the beginning of the semester that she wanted this to be a class that you could put on a temporary back burner in times of stress or difficulty. She values her students' physical and mental wellbeing above all else, which is clear in her easily approachable demeanor and ability to accommodate each student in their unique situation.

Amanda is one of the best instructors I have met at UNC. She tried to make everything easier and more convenient to her students. She could explain some confusing concepts very well. She is always very patient and very responsive to emails. The short answer format of the midterm and final is not easy, but overall I enjoyed taking the course.

I loved POLI 215 with Prof Aziz! She is always available via emails or at her online office hours. Although the course was async and there were lectures 3x a week, she kept them pretty short (25-30min) and always asked us for ways to make class better. She was very accommodating and she's a great person! 10/10 would recommend

Amazing professor and person! She cares about her students mental, physical health and wellbeing. I learned so much about myself and about how groups function within society in her class. I would highly recommend her.

analysis.name: Barbara Entwisle
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Her tests are incredibly difficult, and large portions of your grade rely on group projects. I HATE the way she organizes her canvas. Arguably the most engaging and easy to understand class of the semester was the day our TA taught the lesson. Also 2 points are taken off your semester grade for every class you miss starting day one. Good otherwise.

Prof. Entwisle is nice, but she will get mad if ur on ur phone. The class is okay, basically one big group project the whole semester and the grading criteria for it is unclear, and if u miss a class its 2 pts off ur overall grade. It was not hard to get a B+ or an A, but only take this if ur interested in the subject, or ur gonna be really bored.

2 tests, 4 individual assignments, and 4 group assignments ending with the final research project. Tests were moderately difficult; use flashcards for vocab and practice quizzes for question style. Focused mostly on application. No final, just comment on other projects. Great instructor, super experienced and friendly if you showed you cared.

Barbara is VERY knowledgeable, but she occasionally was condescending when speaking to students. Her feedback was great and fair, but sometimes grading was harsh. Overall not bad, but I wouldn't choose to take her again.

Barbara is amazing and clearly knows what she's talking about. The class was pretty easy, there were clear rubrics for everything, and you learn a lot about research processes. Exams were a bit tricky with vague study guides, but its fine cause you can ace everything else. Lots of group work, so depending on your group you may have more work.

analysis.name: Rachel Baum
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Decent professor for a decent class, very much focused on developing industry knowledge and applications for the insurance/risk market. Show up, generally express interest, and you'll get an A if you don't screw up the assignments. Much more valuable for the guest speakers than the lectures. Dr. Baum has a lot of connections and wants us to learn.

Rachel is such an amazing professor. Super knowledgeable in insurance. She will connect you with so many industry people, and help get internships set up. She is a legend. DATA540 is really easy, but the final project was unnecessarily confusing. The part of the class with Steve Bennett was really tedious and boring though.

Super simple and easy to understand interesting assignments, no exams, straight forward lectures, tons of guest lectures from the insurance industry, and I left the class feeling like I learned a good deal. One of my favorite classes here

She taught this class for the new risk management minor, and she is so amazing. For a first time teacher she is so good at explaining things, the class is engaging, the material is interesting, and her and Prof Bennett bring in a ton of guest lecturers. Cannot recc this class enough.

analysis.name: Shelby Baez
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best EXSS class I have taken at UNC! Exams are very similar to the study guides, and we were given the prompts to the final exam question a week before. Loved her lectures as they were interesting and engaging.
Best EXSS class I have taken. Take this class if you can.

I took Professor Baez the first year she offered EXSS 581, I loved the assignments, and she was clear about what she wanted. The content was interesting and if you have a psychology background, it's cool to see topics and how they play a role in sports injuries.

analysis.name: JJ Bauer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Please do not take this class if you are looking for an easy gen ed. I worked so incredibly hard for the B+ that I go. Professor Bauer is kind, but her lectures are incredibly disorganized and the amount of material included on midterms is insane. Get ready to study and memorize your heart out if you take this class.

Very difficult considering it is an introductory level class. Her lectures go incredibly fast and are very disorganized to the point where I had to reorganize all my notes after every lecture. Midterms and exams are written only and require very dense knowledge about the structures covered and memorization of terms, dates, and architects.

This class was a lot of fun! I think this class is one that you can take regardless of your level of interest in film, because the movies were all very good and the lectures were extremely interesting! Just get ready to write a few papers, but overall the work is very manageable and the professor is so nice and accommodating!

JJ is one of the best professors I've had at UNC so far. This was a rough semester, but JJ's class was a bright spot. I'm not an art major and have never been the creative type, but the material in the lectures was pretty interesting and she is good at grasping students' attention. Great class and great prof
This is a great professor and a great course to take some time here at UNC. Made learning more about the art styles in movies very entertaining and had good commentary on the aspects of movies.

analysis.name: Brandon Bayne
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The class itself wasn't that much work: 10 discussion posts and replies, 2 quizzes, 1 midterm paper and a final project. But Bayne had no rubrics, barely any guidelines for assignments, and grading was random and subjective. He also didn't grade the majority of our assignments until the last week of class which was stressful and frustrating.

This was my favorite course so far at Carolina. It made me reflect on my own faith and consider ways we could be doing better. Professor Bayne is super knowledgeable about both Christianity and Native history. Sometimes it was tough to confront so many difficult moments, but he always gave us helpful context and led creative group discussions.

this class was a gen ed for me but i loved this class. prof and TA are awesome and i learned a lot. not a lot of hw for the class, probably an 1-2 each week but readings are required and they do notebook checks. exams were easy and theres xtra assignments to pad out ur grade. overall a super nice guy who wants to see students succeed!

I LOVED this class and the teacher. He is a great lecturer and I was never bored in his class. He is very clear on his assignments and exams. If you put in the work, this is a very easy class to get an A in. he gives and adequate amount of work. There is a lot of readings but they are enjoyable. He also made us food for the exam.

Dr. Bayne and Carla were amazing this semester. The classroom environment is very engaging and interesting, and both are very caring. As long as you pay attention and study the exam guides, an A is nearly guaranteed. The best professor and TA duo I have had at UNC so far.

analysis.name: Cecilia  Benninger
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. B was definitely one of the best professors I have had at UNC! She always keeps her lecturing super concise and engaging. She brings a lot of real-world and personal experiences to her class and would start every class by talking about news and sports going on in the world. I would 100% take her for MEJO-153 if you can!

One of my favorite professors I've had at Hussman!!! She is so funny and really cares about her students. Final project is a series of social media posts about a research topic and is not hard as long as you don't wait to the last minute. Take her for MEJO 153, you will not regret it.

If you are looking for a more hardcore journalist perspective that 153 is typically notorious for, this may not be the class for you. The class was comprised of a variety of smaller assignments that included interviews and answering questions from the textbook, and was extremely manageable. If you want to complete 153 with an A, take Benninger.
If you're looking to take Mejo 153 take it with professor Benninger. She is super down to earth and genuinely cares about her students and wants to see them succeed. Literally goated.

Dr. B is the best professor to take Mejo 153 with! She is super funny and genuinely cares about her students. We only took one test (mini quiz) the whole semester and our final was a social media project of our choice. She does not try to trick students at all. Big class discussions were a regular thing though, so have something to share.

analysis.name: Benjamin Meier
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 105 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Professor Meier is WAAAAY overqualified to be teaching undergraduates and yet it is his passion. His intellect, dedication, and endless wit shows in his lectures and especially during office hours. There's a lot of reading, and you're expected to participate. Yes it is a lot of work, but global health policy is not easy in the classroom or beyond.

Okay, yes, this class was difficult for me because I wasn't used to high-level readings. However, I would still highly recommend taking it- especially if you're interested at all in health policy. If you're not, it might be a little more than you bargained for, but if you are, having Professor Meier will be invaluable and you will learn SO MUCH.

Meier is absolutely amazing. The class requires reading and participation, but if you put in effort you will do fine. He is so passionate and knowledgeable and a true gem. He cares that you learn but he also cares about your growth and wellbeing. Meier is someone that I can trust and go to for advice. He is a professor that genuinely cares.
Incredible, inspiring professor. However, this seminar is very reading heavy, which can be difficult if global health policy isn't your true passion. Definitely still worth taking a class with Meier!

Dr. Meier is great. His lectures, full of cynicism, humor, and well timed musical references will engage you and cause you to see the world in a new way. Yes, there is a lot of reading and mandatory attendance. Yes, the class is hard. But honestly, if you put effort in, an A is more than possible. Take the class, it will make you a better person.

analysis.name: Benjamin Romero Salado
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Salado is so nice, and I would definitely recommend him for 203! Since 203 is standardized across all sections/professors, he doesn't have much leeway in the structure of the class, but he still does his best to make it as fun as possible. He encourages as much talking in class as possible and genuinely wants you to succeed.

I would recommend him for anyone taking 203! He was fun and entertaining during class and a pretty lenient grader in my opinion. Like most Spanish classes there's lots of online homework and they're pretty strict on due takes so keep up with it! Participation is also of course important but Benjamín made me super feel comfortable speaking in class.

Definitely take 203 with Benjamín if you can! Truly one of the most caring and fun professors I've had, always super supportive and approachable and really cares about everyone. He made sure we were all prepared for the exams and grades fairly, and I always felt comfortable speaking in class which was great in a class with participation grades.

Loved this class and this professor! He is very kind and provides good feedback, and is very fair. 261 is going to be a lot of work with whoever you take it with, but Benjamin makes the class enjoyable and I have learned so much from this class. Participate in class and attend office hours, and you'll be just fine! Can't recommend his class enough

If you are taking Spanish 203, take it with Dr. Romero Salado. He is a kind, caring individual who cares about all of his students and knows them well on a first-name basis. He is funny and everyone looks forward to seeing him. He is engaging and is a great example of an excellent professor.

analysis.name: Bella Randle
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: i absolutely adored poli130 with her! she's a very good teacher and her lectures are very engaging and she definitely knows what she's talking about. not an easy a and there's reading due for every class with quizzes but the reading helps and if you do it you won't struggle.

Bella is an amazing professor! Poli-130 was by far my favorite class this semester. She made the class engaging, but there are readings due every class, with weekly quizzes. Some of the readings are pretty long and our final project was fairly difficult. Not an easy A, but Bella makes up for it with her awesome lectures and love for the class!

Definitely have to put in effort to get good results. Good lecturer and engaging. Does a great job of keeping up with the syllabus and all readings are available on Canvas so nothing to buy. Lots of quizzes but always straightforward w/ no trick questions. Kind and approachable. Loved Bella!
Very sweet and fair grader. The subject is interesting and she leaves space in the syllabus to discuss whatever the class wants to.

She was my TA for Professor Anderson's POLI 130 course. She was helpful going over information and condensing the material to help students better understand the readings. There were 2 absences available for the recitation. Overall great TA/Professor and person. She is really understanding and nice!

analysis.name: Teressa Bergland
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 99 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: As others have said, her exams are quite long.  However, she has recognized that the exams weren't completely fair and offered revisions worth half credit back.  Her lectures are pretty good and she's very accessible via office hours.  Homework is pretty light.  She's not perfect but def way better than some  of the other stor profs here.

these reviews are way too harsh... there are professors genuinely so much worse than her, and they still have a better rating. it seemed like she struggled a lot with anxiety and felt disorganized often times, but she was passionate and tried her best. her exams were very hard, as the other comments suggest, but it was not anything impossible.

Rated her 2 (not 1) bc she does genuinely have a passion and it shows in her good lectures. HOWEVER, she is not meant to be a professor. Harsh/rigid grading and closed-note tests aren't sensible for a coding class, and tests (that she made) not graded for 1-2 months. She tries to do too much then penalizes the students when she finds out she can't.

SHE IS A GOOD TEACHER. People need to chill on her because she is genuinely good at her job, but she teaches a hard class so people are bound to get bad grades. She does her best, and while it takes her a long time to grade, she is very generous with extra credit. You are going to struggle in this class if you dont like STATS, but she does her best

I do not understand other reviews. Is she the best professor? No, but she's a fine one. It's clear that she's adjusting to teaching here, but, her exams were quite fair. You'll struggle if you don't show up to class/study, but you'll do fine if you pay attention. Not an easy A, but you'll get a good grade if you show up and put in a little effort.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Brunk
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I took the honors section of chem430 and loved it. We did a capstone project and got to present our work at the Undergraduate Research Symposium. I was able to learn new how to work with data and even apply some of what I did to my own research! It was hard at first but I learned a lot about myself and team science. This was my fav class at UNC.

Dr. Brunk is kind and clearly cares about her students. She is very busy, as most research faculty are but she answers questions when you bring them to lecture. The flipped classroom can be an adjustment, but it reflects med school style learning. Biochem is challenging (DUH). Homework load is heavy-it helps and can be a grade saver for exams

This class was really hard but really good. It changed my view of medicine and it changed what I want to do with my life. I love the real world applications and learning how to work with data. I loved the lectures on precision medicine and things that are really happening in science.

Took Brunk because Hogan's section was full - worst mistake ever. My friends in Hogan's section had a walk in the park compared to what Brunk put our class through. Prone to mistakes in videos/lecture, very confusing explanations when asked for clarification (which I had to ask at office hours bc she never responded to my emails!), tricky exams.

She is rarely available and actively makes it harder for you to find help. She doesn't let you email her so you can only get help from the TAs. I had to have my final exam rescheduled and she refused to help me out. Keep in mind it was an EXTREMELY easy fix. Don't expect any notes or videos to be posted, and her modules don't match with the exams.

analysis.name: Shankar Bhamidi
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Definitely in the top 2 STEM professors I've had at UNC. STOR 435 is very hard material but he is hilarious and great at explaining the material, and there are many office hours every week.

Highly recommend taking him for 435! Very fair exams and grading, and he allowed us to use a cheat sheet on the final. The hws take a while, but the exams were all variations of hw or practice exam problems. He's also very accessible outside of class and explains difficult concepts in 435 well. Definitely would have done much worse if not for him.

Professor Bhamidi is an excellent professor and cares deeply about the success of his students. On multiple occasions I was able to meet with him outside of his scheduled office hours because I had class during his office hours. He curved the grades at end of semester. Also a funny lecturing that makes a hard class more enjoyable.

The best professor I have had at UNC so far. He is inspiring, intelligent (and great at explaining), clear with what he expects on homework and exams, and is readily available to respond to questions. Also has a good sense of humor.

Shankar is incredible! STOR 435 is a very hard class, but he explains things so well and makes the course as straightforward and clear as possible, and the exams are very fair. Lots of homework, but they are very helpful. He is also hilarious.

analysis.name: Reema Bhattacharya
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof accused me of plagiarizing the final despite having no evidence and threatened to fail me if I didn't respond in a day (during finals). Obviously I didn't cheat and was able to prove it. Make sure to keep a record of all of your work. If you are looking to spend hours on assignments just to be accused of cheating, then this class is for you.

The class structure and course site were convoluted. The course is simply a laundry list of links to articles and videos with little "teaching". For this professor's section of the course, there were eight assignments, a midterm, and a final. None of which helped me learn substantially. Recommend avoiding.

INLS 490 is one of the most valuable classes that makes me feel more prepared for the job market.  Despite the fact that I am not a technical person, Professor Bhattacharya went out of her way to encourage me. You truly get what you put into it. The final project was creating a training; although we had to self-learn the software, it was worth it!

INLS 490 - Reema was accessible outside of class, however, I feel like she did not care for us at all. Her instructions were so confusing and she would contradict things she said. She would also change up her idea of projects after I had already submitted them. She is just all over the place. Overall, I can't say I learned much but it was easy

taking inls 490, the learning design class. she gives off this superiority attitude where she feels like she's better than everyone else. her feedback are short and not helpful. she doesn't seem to care about her students. her modules are full of spelling errors, which show how little effort she put in and she don't care. 

avoid this class

analysis.name: Kanika Bhalla
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I love Prof. Bhalla for reason that she focuses on learning real stuff than just grades. How can one not be fascinated to attend a class where a professor shows stand up comedies to facilitate language learning! She's super cool, I could approach her like a friend, she talks to students in their language by giving reference to Instagram memes, etc.

Kanikaji is an alright professor but there have been many times where she does not show grace to her students. She is not extremely forgiving and the way that she grades is rather harmful -- in the sense that she takes points off like nobody's business. She is fair in class but expects a lot of participation -- talking once a class is not enough.

One of the best professors I have taken classes with so far. She is really understanding and tries to make students comfortable with the teaching materials. I would love to take class with her again and have enrolled with her course in the next semester. I am super excited!
Wish she could stay at UNC longer! Loved her classes. Always used to look forward to see her in class!

analysis.name: Andreley Bjelland
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: outstanding instructor at TCU who genuinely cares about her students and their success. She makes the material easy to understand and is always available to help. The class itself is very easy and a great option for an elective or a less stressful semester. Highly recommend!

Ms. Bjelland was an amazing teacher with the most chill class. There is not much homework and most of the work you finish in class. Couple projects over the semester but she helps so much and makes them fairly easy. 100% recommend taking this class you wont regret it.

Dr Bjelland has the chillest and most engaging class. Some quizzes and discussions to do in class, but she's willing to help with all of those as long as you ask her. Tests aren't that hard also. Really caring and passionate about her work and her students
Dr. B was my favorite professor this semester, hands down. She was so caring, funny, and always helped me when I needed it. Four projects, but all are very straightforward. TAKE HER!!
So easy its not even funny. She grades projects a little weird but other than that the class was perfect.

analysis.name: Susan Bickford
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The grading scale is difficult, but it's not impossible to get an A. There are 8 quizzes; two are dropped. You essentially need near-perfect scores on the remaining six, but she tells you what the questions will be in advance. The best advice for this class is to go to office hours for your papers to talk about them well in advance of the deadline.

She reduces grades when your interpretation is different than hers, even if you provide textual evidence. The class itself is insightful, though I don't think it reaches a philosophical level. The class material is philosophical but how we approach them is not. Grading is too tough and reading&writing is too much for a 200-level class.

Approaches philosophical materials in a strange way, mixing high school-level Engl, Philosophy, Polisci, and Classics but lacks depth in any. Extremely tough grader, focusing on trivial details. Avoid 270 if you dislike being disciplined - only by rewriting papers to her exact suggestions will you earn a decent grade. Tokens make little sense.

She's awesome, the only thing that sucks is her grading scale. It's almost impossible to get an A. She is so caring, engaging, etc. I thought I was going to hate everything about this class and I didn't, I actually kind of loved it. Seriously my ONLY issue is the grading scale, you have to get a perfect grade on almost everything to get an A.

Professor Bickford is kind and knowledgable but her class is TOUGH. She's a very harsh grader and expects expert knowledge from her students. The amount of work that you have to do is not comparable to the grade you will get - it is next to impossible to get an A. If your GPA is important to you, take another political philosophy class for credit.

analysis.name: Jackson  Bittick
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Jackson is an AMAZING professor. He explains concepts clearly and obviously wants his students to learn and succeed. Very accessible and helpful office hours. Mandatory in-person group discussion posts every class, but basically graded for correctness. 4x papers that were super fun to write. Very lenient grader, just not many points to lose.

Down to earth and offers extensions. Reading before class, and then the next 2 classes, you spend time discussing and analyzing the argument presented. In each class, you turn in answers for participation credit. There are 4 papers and a final exam. In each paper, you argue against one philosopher in the unit. He gives amazing, detailed feedback!

Jackson picked some really interesting papers for us to discuss this year! I learned a great deal about ongoing issues surrounding AI, as well as more general Philosophy topics! He was pretty strict on the papers, but it was worth it in the end with an easy final exam. Jackson is a fun, young professor and I enjoyed taking his class!

analysis.name: Elizabeth McLaughlin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 441 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: do not trust her, she wont give any partial credit EVEN when you deserve it! i self studied everything for the final and ended up doing well ONLY because of that

While very knowledgeable and willing to answer questions, the professor's teaching style was rushed and felt unfit for students learning brand new content. The homework was very hard and not useful for tests. However, the TAs and ULA were super helpful.

Dr. McLaughlin doesn't follow lesson plans or the syllabus schedule. She puts little effort into teaching, but has intentionally harder exams than other professors and refuses leniency (i.e. dropping the lowest midterm) unlike other professors. She is passive-aggressive about people not coming to class, even though she knows her lectures are bad.

Heard shes great for Math-232+ but do not. DO NOT take her for math-231. Shes horrible at teaching the material and KNOWS it and makes the exams insanely hard that even TAs have trouble explaining the material. Told TAs to "grade harshly" to spite students that didn't come to class. Go to another profs lectures to learn. Take exams when needed.

After taking AP Calc and MATH130, I had a fair understanding of the topics, but after Mclaughlin, I have never been more confused about calc. After having near-perfect attendance for the first two midterms, I decided it was a waste of time to continue attending. She makes new notes for each class period and has not followed her posted curriculum.

analysis.name: Brian Billman
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 119 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Professor Billman makes a rather boring subject, interesting.... going into the class I was expecting it to be a rather dry, difficult topic, but his lecture style keeps you engaged. The lectures are VERY important however, as they comprise most of the exams... definitely recommend!

I like his personality, but he tends to go off on a rant during lecture. I also find it hard to pinpoint exactly what I should be focusing on while I study. Going to class is a must. He uploads his ppts, but they don't go into much detail and are mostly pictures.

The lectures were very dry and included him talking for 75 min with pictures on the slides. Paying attention the whole time was almost impossible. The exams were very difficult, multiple choice with an essay question. The two recitation essays were not bad, they are what probably saved my grade. I would not recommend taking this class for a gen ed.

Took this class as my friends as an 'easy A'. Easy A's do not exist here, you're gonna have to put work in to get the grade you want. You gotta go to class, pay attention, and study. If you do that, you'll get a good grade, but don't think it's gonna be a joke of a class you can take as a filler. Class is fun and interesting.

I found his lectures to be pretty interesting since a lot were about personal work he did down in Peru. Quite an easy class if you put in work for the essays and keep engaged. Would definitely take him again I love his sense of humor.

analysis.name: Lucia Binotti
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lucia is very kind and a great lecturer! I wasn't sure what to expect from this class but I ended up learning a lot, she made the material very interesting. As long as you participate thoughtfully, this is a wonderful class

Binotti goes with the flow, willing to change assignments if students are busy, and also passionate about Spanish literature. Participation, a group project, 5 small papers, and a final paper made up the whole grade. She is very friendly; loves when students participate (20% of grade) and share their knowledge of the few required readings/tv shows

Binotti is so energetic and fun in her lectures that they aren't boring; however, you do need to show up in order to get a good grade. There is LOTS of reading for her class but honestly you don't have to read it all. The only grades are participation and the occasional paper, which she grades very fairly and they are based on the lectures.

Oi if you have the option to take Lucia's digital spanish 260 course TAKE IT. It is much easier than regular span 260 and a lot more laid back and fun. I thought it was an easy A;  the end of year project can be a little demanding but it's a fair balance because you don't have to do very much during the year. Also it's an EE credit :O

The professor is very unorganized. The homework is not clearly explained and the assignments are very vague. She will call on you frequently and will be condesending if you do not know the answer. Everything is done digitally and she doesnt even know how to work it. I would not recommend this course unless you are a native speaker.

analysis.name: Raphael Birya
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Amazing professor, but I wished he had given better instructions for assignments mainly the final paper. He encourages everyone to participate in discussions read the articles and watch the videos.  He does give extra credit if you attend all his lectures and submit all your assignments!

very understanding teacher and cares about connecting with his students. all he asks is that you participate in class because it is primarily discussion based. even if you don't know the answer he only asks that you try and say something. very easy class, tests fair, homework is always very easy. love professor birya he's so nice and such a king
I would love to eat BIRYAni with him.

Dr. Birya is a kind and interesting professor with great stories. However, grading guidelines are unclear and there are often confusing typos on exams. An A is a 95. Fair amount of dense readings. Usually there would be a 10+ page paper and textbook chapter to read for each class. Come to every class, as participation matters a lot for your grade!

Such an annoying class if I'm being honest. When asked for information on the exam all his responses consist of are 'Do not worry' and 'You will be fine'. Provides a tremendous amount of reading and work for an introductory class. I do not recommend taking him as this class mainly just memorization. The exams wanted you to remember specific quotes.

analysis.name: Gary Biglaiser
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Gary teaches the class as an honors class, uses poorly developed slides, and threatens to beat us with a stick. Homework accounts for 10% of your grade. The TAs do not understand the assignments/problems,the homework is completely irrelevant to the exams. The TAs would say "I do not expect any of you to get this right, I barely understand it."

Jawn was a grind, bank on riding the curve. Slides were never useful (majority of class). If he does a problem on the board though, it might be on an exam. Useful things: recitation, finding book answers online for hw problems and learning from those, old exams, review sessions. Dude also definitely has adhd

I heard a lot of complaints about the class before I took him, which surprises me in hindsight because I didn't have any problems with him. He explained the material well, answered questions well, had simulations and review sessions after class for students, and was a fair grader. Decent class, relatively exams. Says "suppose" a lot.

Gary is a VERY nice guy. However, he taught us like we were phD students and I took nothing away from this class. All lectures were power points and there was 0 practice(besides extra textbook questions which were unhelpful). Help in the aide center was not helpful in any way either. If you want to learn 410 or even get a good grade, do NOT take.

Great guy, bad teacher. Very disorganized slides, few examples, mostly explained math but not how to apply it, still you had to go to class or you'd be completely lost (attendance not mandatory). HW assignments are only worth 10% but very long and only 1 problem picked at random is graded. 90% of grade is exams. Very arrogant TA, as clueless as us.

analysis.name: Codey Bills
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Codey is great. The issue is the formatting of this class. There are only so many assignments so your grade is a reflection of how harshly you are graded on the final assignments which are worth a majority of your grade. Codey is helpful and teaches the class material well. He is hilarious and makes the class go smoothly. Harsh grader, though.

Codey is amazing. He's so funny and very easygoing. He is happy to help and meet after class anytime. For the COMM 113 speeches specifically, he's a tough grader, but if you put in the effort and show you care you will do fine.

He's a real gem in the communications department. He is very knowledgeable on the topics he teaches and makes very abstract concepts easy to understand using references and lingo that students use. He is happy to explain any topic multiple times until it sticks. His anecdotes are always random but funny and do not drag on.

he was my TA for COMM120, definitely chillest of the TAs. gave us 100s just for turning most things in and wasn't nitpicky about other grading. usually late and sometimes cancels recitation, funny guy and doesn't expect you to be overly prepared (because he definitely isn't!) sweet guy

Great guy and very approachable. He made everyone feel as comfortable as possible when speaking. Gave back detailed feedback and was very encouraging. He is kindhearted and understanding. I would definitely recommend if you want to get an easy A with a kind and constructive professor.

analysis.name: Gary Birdsong
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you've ever asked yourself any of the following questions, you must take this class: 1. How much weed do I have to smoke to become a homosexual? 2. Is Obama really a man, or a gay-terrorist-devil? 3. Where can I find a source of condemnation in my daily scheduel today? In summary, Professor Birdsong is what it feels like to chew 5 gum.

Passionate about the subject, though sometimes gets off topic. Known to repeat his point several times per lesson. He's a big devil's advocate and loves to contradict his students. You can skip buying the book with this one; he references one or two passages, but completely dismisses the rest of it.
Easily one of the best professors on campus. Easy discussion-based class, very passionate and very informative.

Very clear syllabus and grading criteria. Gary makes the do's and don't's of the class known right off the bat. He usually has them written right up on his signs for clarity. Despite his passion for teaching, I have failed this class. I'm still a bisexual atheist. Gary provided no feedback but to "roast in Hell". I'll see you there Gary!

Gary was my favorite teacher at UNC, and I'm pretty sure I learned the most from him. And unlike a lot of UNC professors, he never minded answering even the dumbest of questions and never shied away from controversy. Yes I failed his class and am certainly going to hell, but I'll be there with the rest of my Tar Heel friends. God Bless you, Gary.

analysis.name: Pauline Blaimont
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Blaimont was pretty great. I genuinely enjoyed her lectures and was interested in the content even though I am not a Bio major. Just try not to miss any homework or quizzes because she won't let you make anything up unless you get hit by a car or something. Overall pretty epic teacher.

Dr. Blaimont was amazing! This class had a lot of content and work, but her lectures and teaching style always prepared me. Her exams were difficult in the right ways, testing things in an understandable manner from lectures and work. 220 had a lot of content, but I feel like she made it as manageable as possible. Take her if you have the chance!

Dr. Blaimont was probably the best 220 professor ever. I was so terrified for this class and she was the nicest person ever. Her lectures were clear and engaging, and didn't mind explaining something slowly in class when I asked for help. Office hours are great, exams are fair, and she is hilarious! Don't miss the chance to take a class with her!

Blaimont is an amazing professor. She is very kind, very enthusiastic about the subject (she is young and relatively new), and very straightforward about what she wants from her students. She is also very accessible outside of class for questions, help, and anything else. 100% the best option to take for 220!

God-tier of a professor. Definitely take Dr. Blaimont for BIOL 220! Very fair exams and grading on assignments. Patient on answering questions. I wish she would answer questions more directly, but she is already doing an amazing job for her 1st semester at UNC! Study the ppt and journal club, then you will be fine!

analysis.name: Sarah Bloesch
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If you're taking this for a Gen-ed, I recommend! She was very nice and the class was pretty easy. Lectures could be kinda boring and readings were long, but she went over them. She gives a clear study guide over the midterm, 3 essays with clear rubrics, and weekly reading quizzes. Just wish the TA gave more feedback on assignments.

Super caring professor! Easy class, just don't be rude and occasionally add something to conversations. The tests were pretty easy, essay-style but she gives you some possible prompt beforehand so you can prepare. Recitations were basically just a rant sesh about the current state of feminism and women so honestly super fun class
She makes the lectures interesting and is very understanding as long as you communicate. Love her as a professor, I highly recommend!

I enjoyed this class Professor Bloesch is great and very knowledgeable. She prepares you very well for all the assignments she expects of you. There is a lot of reading but you can get away without doing it because she goes over it during class. There is a recitation which is mandatory but not too much work overall.

Professor Sarah Bloesch is an outstanding educator! Her Sexuality and Salvation class in Women and Gender Studies was engaging, thought-provoking, and eye-opening. She fosters an inclusive environment and encourages deep discussions on complex topics. Her teaching style is clear, passionate, and approachable. One of the best professors I've had!

analysis.name: Blake Faulkner
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Teaches nothing but the will to die. I CANNOT STRESS ENOUGH NOT TO TAKE HIS CLASSES. Unapproachable and rude. I consistently felt as though he was teaching a lot of nothing, then expecting an unattainable amount of work and careful thought with no content.
biased grader takes his hatred for life out on his students because he had an affair and a child and lost his pastor job at a church.

By far the worst learning experience I've ever had. He does not communicate very well (kind of ironic considering what he teaches), he does not seem to care about students. This man should not be allowed to teach anything except what not to do as a teacher.

Would not recommend. Blake was a hard grader and did not provide helpful feedback. We had three papers and a midterm and we didn't get our grades until the week of the final (the final is today and I still do not have my midterm grade). Not responsive to emails. Very snarky and rude overall. Probably should not become a professor if he gets his PHD

Such a rude and cocky teacher for a 100 level class. Extremely tough grader. If you want to inquire about a bad grade, you have to formulate an argument as to why he should regrade, if the argument is deemed illogical or is wrong he will not respond to your email, will not remade, and "reserves the right" to give you a lower grade.

analysis.name: Kerry Bloom
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very smart researcher. Absolutely horrible professor. Doesn't give feedback. Doesn't teach anything. DO NOT TAKE. YOU WILL REGRET. DO NOT TAKE. YOU WILL REGRET.
Do not take this class with this professor, whatever you do do not take this class. Exams are hard and are overly graded. This class is worse than Orgo.
Absolutely horrible. Worst class I've taken at UNC

Take home exams- as long as you go to office hours, he will help you get an A on all of them. As long as you participate in class every so often, you will do fine. Definitely a bias grader, helps if he likes you and you seem interested. Going to office hours is enough to get an A in the class.

The MTs and finals are open note, collaborative, and Prof Bloom will help you out if you go to office hours. His main thing is that you show up to class (he doesn't take attendance, but he notices who is there), ask questions, and pay attention.

analysis.name: Sarah Blanton
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: professor blanton was so knowledgable and passionate about spanish and clearly cared about helping her students succeed! she gave great feedback and was always kind when redirecting students during class and on assignments! the workload was completely manageable and she was a very fair grader! i would recommend her to anyone taking spanish!!

Professor Blanton is a great instructor who truly cares about her students. The class was challenging for me since languages aren't my strength, but if you already know some Spanish, it should feel manageable. The assignments are easy, but the exams are tougher, so regular studying is helpful.

Professor Blanton is sweet and very helpful. I enjoyed her class even though I didn't know it was all online originally. Most of the work is done in the Alcanza textbook, while classes were spent reviewing and practicing the material. Would definitely take a class with her again!

I love Ms. Blanton. She is so kind and really cares about her students. I was afraid I would not learn much since it was an online class but Ms. Blanton made the zooms very interactive and easy to learn from. I learned a lot and I definitely recommend.

I would definitely take Span 100 with her again—she was so kind and the perfect teacher for learning a new language. Even if I made mistakes during my speaking exams, she was generous with grading as long as I stayed in Spanish.

analysis.name: Dennis Blair
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: super tough grader. Did extra credit papers and still got a bad grade because all he counts is the finals. Assigns way too much reading.

Not many chances to learn from a practitioner like the Admiral. He clearly puts a lot of time into his syllabus and lectures, and you won't hear stories like his from just any PWAD/POLI prof. Practical final paper, loves to support his students (rec letters, connections, etc.), and incredibly knowledgable. If you read & participate, you're all set.

Professor Blair is a brilliant man. He doesn't take attendance and rarely quizzes on readings, but it'd be a huge loss to neglect either. He's also glad to help his students professionally, his tips and reference letter being immensely valuable as a former admiral, DNI, and a talented professor. So make an effort, learn a lot, and ask for advice!
The Professor is a very intelligent man. His lecture style does leave much to be desired however. If you don't like reading do not take this course.

analysis.name: Taylor Blankenship
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I feel lucky to have had Taylor for 187. She brought real-world experience from her career into class and was accessible whenever we had questions. Her grading criteria are clear, she's funny, and she made web design seem less scary. The JavaScript section kicked my butt, but if you show you tried you'll be okay.

Taylor is such a caring and kind human, but she isn't the best teacher. A lot of times when asking questions and being confused, she would seem equally as confused and almost act as if you should know the answer. If you take this course, Google and ChatGPT will probably be your best friend.

I really enjoyed my time in this class. This was her second semester teaching this course, but she really values her students. Coming into class every day was a joy as she often makes funny comments throughout her lectures. I highly recommend taking 187 with her!

analysis.name: J Troy Blackburn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The other prof for this class is easier, but this class was my favorite for the semester. Blackburn is an amazing lecturer, he is genuinely interested in making sure you understand the material and is down for any questions. He moved a test because it was on the same day as an anatomy exam too, he wants to give everyone the best shot they have.

The class is only lectures that weren't very detailed and very hard to learn from. You have to listen to his lecturing to understand the content, so if you miss a class or don't take notes for a class, you're going to be very lost. The class is also only made up of tests and quizzes, so if you flunk one, your grade is done for.

He was alright. I wish there were more assignments other than the tests and quizzes because they make up your whole grade. Never communicates via Canvas or Outlook and never updated the syllabus (which was crazy because he changed the dates of almost all the tests). He's very nice but if there is ever another section take it with someone else.

I did not enjoy this class, even as someone interested in physiology and neuroscience. Blackburn was incredibly lecture heavy, a big departure from other professors I've had in EXSS. Your grade is 3 tests (90%) and 3 quizzes (10%). I got A's on the MC parts of exams and quizzes and failed the short answer because of how vague the questions were.

He's a really nice guy. He's willing to work with you and in class he gives great examples to help you understand. Hes funny. Looks like a Doogie Howser and Ryan Secrest love-child, but in a cute way. Go to class and pay attention and you will be fine. Ask questions if you got to, he's willing to help!

analysis.name: Pamela Bond
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Bond made learning a joy. She is by far the most kind and energizing professor that I have experienced. She always showed up to class with a smile and was the highlight of my day. Her assignments consisted of reflective essays, designing our own sustainable fashion piece, etc. I learned a lot and had a bunch of fun in the process!

Professor Bond is the best teacher I have had at UNC so far. She genuinely cares for all her students and she gives you the confidence to participate. She is hilarious and  I always leave class feeling so much better than I did walking in. All the assignments are easy but interesting and you learn so much from her style of teaching!

Pamela Bond is such an incredible teacher and even better person. She's super understanding and clearly cares more about you learning than busy work. Would recommend you take her classes, but if you do, please give her the respect and attention she deserves!! Top tier teacher!

Professor Bond is probably one of the (if not the) best teacher I have ever had. Not only will you leave her class laughing, but you also feel as if you have a genuine friendship with her. Her lectures are very interesting and taught in a very entertaining way. You will not regret taking her class.

Professor Bond was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. She was so caring and made class so engaging and fun. She genuinely sparked interest and inspired me every single day. I cannot emphasize enough how awesome she is and how awesome this class is. Shes truly the best.

analysis.name: Paul Blom
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's a solid professor and a decent person. While nobody loves ENGL105, his section is good. You learn how to write. I'll leave it up to y'all whether you think it's appropriate for a student at an elite school like UNC to complain about being required to attend class and do simple assignments. To me, this is anti-intellectual and very dumb.

Super nice guy and good class overall. He made lots or resources available and taught helpful foundational writing skills. My one complaint is that he takes a while to grade. He clearly cares a lot about teaching and puts a lot of effort into the class to make it engaging. I highly recommend his class for English 105!

I love Professor Paul! He is so sweet, and you can tell he is a genuinely good human being. The only things I would comment on are that he takes a very long time to grade, and his lectures are also boring at times. However, his expectations are clear, and he tries to be as engaging as possible. Take him if possible!!

Every single day you have a homework assignment. So if its a M/W/F class you have to read something for each of those day and post a discussion post (three to four questions to answer). All of those readings will also be on the final. SO be ready to read. Also he is a very slow grader. Although caring about his students I would not recommend.

Cares about his students and will understand if you ever need an extension. However, missing one class reduces your grade by a point, and if you come in late, he'll give you a .75/1. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities to fix that, though. A discussion post is due before every class, and he assigns both a final project and an exam.

analysis.name: Tanner Bourne
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Tanner is genuinely my king. Do whatever is humanly possible to have him as your professor. He's super nice and funny and he makes class very engaging. Participation matters and he rarely gives out 100s, but he really wants his students to succeed so he's super lenient with deadlines and partial credit.

(I was in SPAN261)

Tanner is a very easy professor. He's friendly, hilarious, and gives great feedback on your assignments. He is a bit harsh on grading and likes to give out 90s a lot, so your grade can drop to a B easily. In class, there's homework assignments pretty much every night, but they aren't too hard. He does grade participation.

Take this man if you get him, honestly probably for whatever course he is teaching. Super caring and chill. Was very lenient when it came to turning things in a little late and honestly just there to see you succeed. Just participate in class! I hadn't taken a whole lot of spanish before but I felt fine and learned a lot in the end

Very passionate about languages and teaching! Makes class fun and is a chill grader. Slow grader for bigger assignments, but will always give you an extension to make up for it. Participate in class and turn in textbook homework on time and you'll be fine.

I LOVED Tanner! He made lectures exciting and funny, which made learning feel so much more engaging. He was always willing to help and would ask if we wanted to redirect the class to areas we struggled with to make sure we did well on quizzes and exams. I genuinely felt supported throughout the course. Highly recommend! Office hours are great too.

analysis.name: Lois Boynton
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great, great professor. She's funny, discussions are interesting, and the readings are minimal (and interesting). I don't know why people say this class is so hard, it's really not as long as you put in the same amount of effort you would any other class. (It's easy not to because it seems like such easy material, but she's a tough grader).

She is a super sweet professor. She is easy to have a conversation with. My only complaint is it is nearly impossible to make anything higher than 90. I have gotten maybe 2 grades over 90, and heard this is common for other students. We don't do much in class, but from what we do it is an interesting and engaging class.

Dr. Boynton is so sweet and funny! The content can be a little boring at times, but she always managed to make us smile during class. Daily in-class group assignments were pretty easy and useful. Sometimes, she can be a tough grader, but she genuinely cares about her students and loves her job.

Lois is so funny and gives entertaining lectures. Cares about her students and is accessible outside of class! Can be a tough grader at times but she cares about her students succeeding, especially in a 100 level class.

I want to love Dr. B, but I am not happy with the experience I had this past semester. She uses her lecture time as a standup comedy hour. She is hilarious, but I learned approximately 25 percent of what I wanted to learn. My classmates and I agreed that we were teaching ourselves by the end of the semester. Take 141 with someone else.

analysis.name: Andrea Bohlman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Andrea is fantastic. I would happily take another class with her. I would also give her a 5 if this class wasn't pure fluff. This is more beneficial than music history? The curriculum is disjointed nonsense and the final project was a show and tell of everyone's musical interests. I think music conservatories would laugh if they observed MUSC270.

Dr. Bohlman clearly has a passion and interest in her lectures. She looks forward to participation, reading over the short assignments, and gives great feedback on the midterm. She takes students' workloads into account when scheduling her big deadlines/midterm, clearly showing empathy for her students.

I beg the UNC Music department to do away with this new curriculum. Dr. Bohlman was fantastic and clear but the material she was given to work with was nearly nonexistent. This course caused multiple people to DROP the music major because they have decided to stop teaching anything useful. The dumbing down of the music major at UNC is sad to see.

The main issue with this course was the course itself, not the professor. Bohlman is a zealous, involved professor who will help you with anything-- academic or personal. That said, I didn't learn a lot in this course. The lectures tended to be all over the place and slightly unrelated to each other. Homework is not required, tho assigned.

Andrea is alright; no more, no less. Similar to my experience with her MUSC 120, we learned absolute nonsense the whole semester. We basically studied music through unguided interpretation. Andrea has a knack for calling on students but not really caring for their responses & for giving unclear essay criteria, but overall this class is an easy A.

analysis.name: Lori Boyer
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The most disorganized professor I've ever had. Already have had multiple assignments with due dates that weren't properly communicated or adjusted, even though she said they'd be moved. She's super entertaining, caring, and a fun person, but for someone teaching business communications, you'd think she would communicate more.

I honestly did not know how to rate Dr. Boyer; she's an incredible person who deeply cares for her students and is extremely reasonable. However, she is disorganized and often very behind in getting back grades to students, and in this particular class, grades are very harshly-like all other 401 professors. I would recommend taking it with her!

Difficult to get an A, A- didn't require much effort, but that's honestly just BUSI 401. Discussion based class with lots of small group work and in-class activities that aren't graded. Assignments were applicable and didn't take too long. They're graded harshly, but again that's just 401. Interesting lecturer, and I actually enjoyed going to class

She's funny and makes classes engaging. Hard to get an A, her grading criteria is very unclear at times and the feedback is not great either - sometimes even contradictory. 401 kinda sucks in general, so among the options I think she's one of the best to at least have a fun time. Just accept you will prob get an A- even if you try really hard.

Boyer's cool and a great lecturer who made class engaging. That being said, she is so nitpicky when it comes to grading. You can clearly do everything on the rubric but she'll take off ten points for no reason. I guess that's just 401. Also all her assignments are written/graded by AI which is pretty annoying since it leads to unclear guidelines.

analysis.name: Greg Bocchino
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Greg is great, I heavily recommend this class for anyone even slightly interested in public health! We just met once a week briefly on zoom with mandatory attendance, but Dr. Greg is very understanding and offers alternative options if something comes up for you. The only grade is the final paper and he wasn't a tough grader at all.
Attendance is graded; just come and listen. Only 1 essay is graded at the end of the course. Gives you directions for every paragraph that needs to be on there.
super chill class. once a week class online and attendance was mandatory. had to have camera on. only assignment was a 800 word paper. learned a lot about how to get a health career.

This class that introduces you to every public health field out there. It is a pass/fail class with only one essay due at the end of the semester. The guest speakers would each come one per week to talk about their specialty and answer any burning questions you have on career choices. Dr. Bocchino is a great resource for future Grad level planning.

Professor Bocchino was definitely the best professor I've had at UNC this far. His class is very chill as your whole grade is made up of attendance and your final paper. Very interesting content wise and you learn a lot from the guest speakers. I would definitely recommend this class

analysis.name: Karen Booth
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Do not take a class with Dr. Booth. She is unorganized, has very inconsistent and random deadlines ex. 4:15, and unclear grading policies. She randomly canceled class and added assignments at the last minute. This would not be such an issue but she was inconsiderate of student's needs, even if there were issues with tech or health (in a pandemic).

Do not take this class. Dr. Booth uses lectures not to challenge students, but to find students who validate her own world view. The course does have very interesting readings, but you can do them in your free time. She is also incredibly trans-exclusive and has disorganized lectures. She is not willing to explain confusing course assignments.

Not impressed at all. Class "discussions" entailed her calling on different people until she got the answer she wanted. She is very self-righteous & actively shut me down when I tried to bring up trans health issues in a sexual health class. Reading materials were interesting but I would suggest reading them on your own time.

All you do is sit in a circle and discuss the readings, and all she does is shut down conversation and make people feel like they said something "wrong." by halfway through the semester we all just sat in a silent, tense circle because everyone was too afraid to talk. Really interesting readings though, I did learn a lot from them.

Do not take a class with Karen. She has impossibly high standards for participation, and her grading is incredibly subjective. She WILL give you a bad grade if she doesn't like you. These "subjective" grades make up 80% of your total grade. You can participate everyday and still get an 80% for participation for no reason. Such a subjective grader!

analysis.name: Jennifer Boittin
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I wouldn't recommend this class as a GenEd. Professor Boittin is fine, but lectures are slow and lack clear slides. Grading depends heavily on your TA and often feels subjective, with little feedback. Attendance is a major component of your grade, and participation doesn't guarantee an A.

Boittin's lectures are bone-dry, rambling, random, and occasionally border on offensive. My biggest gripe was our unit on terrorism, which Boittin devoted to justifying why the radical beliefs of those who murdered hundreds in Paris and Nice were not to blame for the events, but rather some abstract failing of European society. Just disappointing.

Meh! That probably sums the class up well. Began interesting, but lost its intrigue as time went on. She is very knowledgable, yet this is quickly offset by her lackluster voice and seemingly disorganized lecture topics. Assignments were given at random and quizzes felt devoid of any lecture material. The recitations surprisingly saved this class.

No clear grading rubric. Quizzes were short answer style with little time to complete them. Feedback from TA's on quizzes would tell you to "add more detail" when you only had 10 minutes to handwrite an answer making it almost impossible to do so. Grade was essentially up to your TA. Unreasonably hard for a 100 level course. Would not recommend.

Professor Boittin is a nice person and an engaging lecturer. My issue with the class lies more in her TA's. I was graded very harshly on
few assignments and was not given a clear rubric or instructions on how to improve. Participation makes up a large component of the grade and despite attending and participating full credit is not promised

analysis.name: Ben Bolling
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: (Writing in Law) Super easy grader with rubrics to follow. Available for questions. Manageable/concise assignments, a few group projects, open note quizzes. Extremely thorough feedback. Nearly everything he says is funny. Slightly slow grading but many opportunities for revision. Not prelaw but no regrets on taking this course.

Just straight up mean and condescending, easily offended. Took a student outside mid-class and I could hear him yelling. unclear assignments & class is a lot of work. assignments build on ones before which wouldn't be so bad if he could actually grade anything so u knew what was going on. when he does grade comments come back clearly ai generated.

Ben is a very engaging teacher and gives helpful and detailed feedback on every assignment. He's also a pretty easy grader. He took a long time to grade on some assignments, but it was understandable due to various uncontrollable complications throughout the semester. By far my favorite professor this semester. Don't listen to the review bombers.

Ben is an amazing professor and an amazing person. I thoroughly enjoyed taking Writing in Law and I learned so much from him. A couple group projects and every unit was structured. Definitely more difficult than a regular 105, but so worth it if you are considering law (also worth it if you aren't). Prepare for a busy schedule but a great class!

Dr. Bolling is a great professor who is extremely willing to work with students, field questions, and provide clear rubrics and guidelines for course material. His Writing in Law class is great at teaching students about the importance of consistency and brevity in writing, and I found the course material manageable to keep up with.

analysis.name: Bruno Estigarribia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Class is only graded by 2 exams and a participation grade, but Bruno makes it as easy as possible. He is very passionate about linguistics and wants us to talk to him in class (will cold call). No course schedule, just occasional reading homework to keep us engaged. Attendance is important, and he is sure to explain concepts clearly in class.

He is a very passionate teacher but very strict. Make sure you go to office hours. No computers/phones/ipads allowed in class-- all hand written. The class was also quite difficult for being an introductory course.
Lit teacher played Roblox all class and leveled up in adopt me hella take his class for an easy A
great class took it with the fellas and day traded the whole time I put bruno onto forex

Forensic linguistics, new course. Bruno is scary, but honestly the sweetest. Mad respect he's so smart. The homework is hard but if you start early and ask he'll help you. There's hw every class but he only requires 5 graded, you can ask for an excuse if you ask ahead of time no questions asked. My 1st class with him, dunno what he's like in person

analysis.name: Brian Brew
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Hes a Goat. Always made it so fun to show up and as a student who is the type to sit in the back and be on there phone I was front row always paying attention to him. He does expect effort, but with how engaging his teaching is its impossible not to put in effort. Chill grader, genuinely funny guy, and great political takes. Made me want an A

Incredible professor with true passion and inspiration for his students. Gave so much grace when I struggled due to personal reasons and let me take the midterm a week late.
