Such an incredible professor, take his classes!!!! So funny and attendance isn't graded (but it's important unless u look at the notes) No electronics but so interesting.

brian was a pretty easy grader. one 10-12 page paper, a midterm, a final, and a couple of assignments that required you to go to office hours for a bit. he was pretty nice but he did go on random rants about primaries where he screamed for like 5 mins. there are lots of readings but you can just skim them enough to write the discussion posts
He is a great professor that is easily reached outside of class and cares about the success of his students. I highly recommend you take a class of his if possible.

Brian is pretty great. He clearly loves political science, and that is shown in his lectures. He isn't a very harsh grader, and if you are interested in political science, you will enjoy his lectures. POLI 208 had two papers, a midterm and a final exam, and none of them were too difficult. It's a good class to learn in and not worry about grades!

analysis.name: John Bruno
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: My favorite professor so far at UNC. His exam was so easy and was straight from the study guide. His lectures were interesting and he sometimes brought his dog to class. This course is taught with two other professors and he by far was the easiest one.

This is one of the best professor's I have ever had, he really cares about his students and is very passionate and knowledgeable about this course and topics. Definitely take this class, very easy and super interesting.

Dr. Bruno was by far my favorite lecturer on the FoF teaching team. His lectures were insightful and easy to follow, and he always brings his dog Mr. Lizard to class when he teaches. He gives an in-depth synopsis of the fishing industry and the fraud within it. He is also accessible outside of class and offers advice who show the initiative to ask.

Dr. Bruno was the best professor in FoF. He made lectures very interesting and was always knowledgable on what he was doing. Hes funny and is always very kind to the students. FoF as a class wasn't too hard but the quizzes were very detailed so I reccommend at least reviewing before. Everything else was graded easily, including the final paper.

One of the best professor ever met! He really supports and wants student to learn how to do research and understand sustainability related topics. Grade is not a concern for this class (he's grading fairly and  leniently) but understanding science & research is the goal.

analysis.name: Brett Whalen
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 87 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Nice professor but unnecessarily tough grader with difficult exams. Not an easy gen ed. Don't take unless you really like medieval history.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor who LOVES what he does and is always happy to give feedback on essays. The class was very interesting and discussion based, but NOT an easy A seminar. We watched a movie and read documents weekly outside of class. Part of your grade is from participation in discussions/group presentations and essays.

So many old, boring movies. Watched about 10 films, no color, silent, 3 hours long, and some in other languages, and most were not great. Had to read a chapter a week that barely related to move. There is a big group project, so hope for good group. MUST PARTICIPATE.
Dr. Whalen is obviously incredibly passionate about the Medieval period and his students. Interacting with him is an excellent way to improve the uniqueness of his class.

Dr. Whalen is a great professor. He really knows his stuff and is very excited to be teaching it. He structures the class so it does not burden you too much. However, the assignments do not have clear grading criteria. Overall, a great class though and I would definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Steven Buzinski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Huge group project. Exams contain very specific questions from reading and the reading is really long. Very likely to get bad grades on exams if haven't taken psychology in high school or haven't read textbook very very thoroughly which will take tons of time.

He's a pretty good professor. Probably not my favorite, but he's an approachable person. Definitely eye-candy and great to listen to, but sometimes I'd be a little confused at the concepts he would explain. We had probably 4 guest lecturers (3 TA's) which really influenced Test 2 badly for me (multiple perspectives). Overall, I'd recommend.

Dr. Buzinski? Oh you mean the GOAT. Second time taking one of his classes and honestly they should let him teach everything. He is an incredible lecturer who makes class fun and clearly cares about his students. Upon first glance it can look like a lot of assignments but I promise they are not bad at all. Exams are super fair as well.

Professor Buzinski is an amazing teacher, and his lectures were super interesting. Grades are 3 exams, online learning quizzes, and a semester long project. The exams are straightforward; if you attend every class, you should do well. The course-long project is clear and approachable, broken up accross the semester. Overall, an enjoyable class!

Half of the course lectures were for lectures, other half were for project work. Super slow at getting grades back but all assignments were easy. Four exams, drop lowest score. Structure of class forces spaced studying, which makes exam prep easier later on. Can be flaky/slow over email, so get questions/requests in as early as you can. Nice guy.

analysis.name: Becky Butler
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The class was mainly focused on Dr. Butler going through slideshows and discussing readings in groups. It's not the most organized, but as long as you somewhat pay attention, the class wasn't hard. If you commit some time to the readings or oral histories, getting an A is very doable. That said, you could get away with skimming the readings.

If you're looking for an easy or filler class, do not take this course. It is graded on around six different components, making it more demanding than expected. Dr. Butler is a good person, but the lectures and assignment details were very unorganized. The exams were also poorly structured and much longer than they should have been.
Do not take this course if you're just looking for an easy filler. Dr. Butler is very kind, but the lectures are often unorganized and the exams are much longer than they need to be.

There are a decent amount of readings. There is a group interview, and a final paper along with a 10min presentation. There are only 2-3 homework assignments, and there were about 3-4 tests, all being online, including the final. The class was decently heavy on participation but it was always fun and usually was discussing the reading with someone.
Really great professor. Very accessible. LOTS of work. You will discuss the readings in class, so you have to actually do them. Learned a lot though.

analysis.name: Mindy Buchanan-King
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Mindy was an amazing professor who genuinely cares about her students. She is super lenient on attendance although participation does impact your grade. You get 3 unexcused absences. There are open note quizzes with extra credit for the readings that are super easy in addition to 2 papers in place of exams. Class is discussion based.

Mrs. King was a great professor and genuinely a really nice person. She gave very helpful feedback and allowed for resubmissions, which made the class both useful and pretty easy. Overall, it was a solid class and Mrs. King was a good prof to take 105 with.

I took Mrs. King for English 123 and she was amazing. She was very understanding and is willing to work with you if you have outside issues. The class was comprised of  discussions, weekly open note quizzes (and a midterm and final paper ( no exam). It was a very engaging class, just be ready to read so you can engage in active discussion
Really cares about her students. Put the work in and you'll go far.

Professor King is a very interesting instructor. She is very accomodating when it comes to deadlines and is passionate about her work. She follows a contract grading system which alleviates lots of stress. The projects were interesting and easy to get a good grade on as long as you put in a decent effort. Would definitely recommend her class!

analysis.name: Bud Kauffman
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you're taking Arabic at UNC, take a class with Ustaaz Bud. He is by far the best professor I've had here. Despite having the class 4 times a week, first thing in the morning, I looked forward to it every time. He is so engaging and encourages you to speak and practice as much as possible. He's accessible out of class for general life advice too.

He is a really good teacher, he made a really tough language seem super doable and was very uplifting. He is really smart and gives little side anecdotes about roots of words and stuff which makes the classes interesting and less mundane.

I took 102 with Bud three years ago. I was dealing with significant mental health challenges, and had 40+ assignments that were late. I communicated this with Bud, and he accommodated me to his fullest capacity, and I passed. Now I'm about to graduate, and I still remember his kindness. His class is challenging no doubt, but worth taking.

I entered the class with absolutely no knowledge of the language and came out of it pretty confident and with a good understanding of a lot of content. He is an amazing teacher and improved my freshman year's first semester. There is a lot of work, I usually felt as though all I did was the work for this class but it is so worth it.

Oh Bud. Just an interesting man. He is really an enigma. I have been with him for multiple Arabics and I still feel as if I don't know anything about him. Anyway he is a great teacher and a great person! He cares about everyone, always makes class fun, and is really understanding. He puts his foot down for grading and missed work when appropriate.

analysis.name: Marcus Bull
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Would not take this class again if given the chance. He is extremely inaccessible outside of class and not accommodating at all. Lectures for over an hour with no visuals, no notes, nothing but talking at you. Extremely strict about everything. It feels like he doesn't respect students or even want us in the class, teaching us seems like a chore.
very supportative of students! go to his office hours and he will love you. amazing professor. be prepared to read and talk in class

This class caused me more stress than all my other classes combined. The lectures were unhelpful, full of vague, disconnected information and random pictures that you have to memorize for the tests. While he says history is not about memorizing facts, the test questions are very specific. The papers are difficult and time consuming. Not an easy A!

Professor Bull gives amazing lectures, but you're grade in his class hinges on only an handful of grades. 3 papers, a midterm, and the final are all you are graded on. The papers, however, he expects a lot from the papers. He expects a lot of analysis using a limited number of difficult to understand sources. TAKE HIS ASSIGNMENTS SERIOUSLY

Loved this class with Prof. Bull. There's only 3 papers, a midterm, and a final, so make sure you do well on everything in this class. The midterm and final weren't that hard, but the papers are graded by the TA's, so pray you get a good one, (I had Hager and she was great). There's also participation, but it's an easy 100 if you show up.

analysis.name: Emily Burkhead
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 250 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The class itself is not horrible, you can preview by looking up "understanding analysis" and practice. Tests decide your grade, not hard if you know how to apply a theorem or prove it. She hates to grade higher for those who improved, and she grades harsh, bonus and curve are almost nothing, I regret taking her hunger game class only for a minor.

Taking Calculus 3 with this professor was the worst experience of my life. Studying for her exams brought me to tears. The test study guides are an extremely poor representation of the exams and she wrote most of the final so her students did bad on that too. Her class average is a C, while others are an A. Do not take this class! Save your GPA!!!

I gave her a 4/5 when I took her for MATH233. That was a lie. Tests and homework were graded harshly which would have been fine if she curved generously. Given what she said is "on track for an A/B/C" after each midterm, the curve should have been like +13% when it was actually +3%. Ragebait incarnate.

Carefully assess your abilities. There's no curve for this class at all. It's the only one among 233 courses that requires a weekly exam. Also, I've seen exams from other sections that had only five simple questions in 50 minutes, but Professor Burkhead's test contained more than 20 challenging and time-consuming problems, with no extra time given.

Save your grade and don't take 381 with Burkhead. Inaccessible and hard to approach with questions related to grading or asking her to explain concepts. Asked her many times to explain the material, and was often met with snarky remarks. Office hours are even worse, as she is not much help if you're lost.

analysis.name: Alyssa Byrnes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 113 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Incredible professor, my first time taking any sort of comp sci class and I love it now. Explains things very well and has a very clear and forgiving grading system. Very easy A if you show up to class and do the assignments on time, don't be scared by the "12-15 hrs/wk" they talk about I studied a couple hours for each quiz and ended with a 97.

Pass/failed. Didn't post recordings, which for material that has meticulous steps and reasons for them makes it incredibly hard to review a concept more than just seeing the end result. Tests made up 90% of the grade, and were taken entirely from homework questions. Rewarded cramming over really understanding the material imo. Still a nice person.
Everyone knows she's the best! COMP 455 is known to be hard, but she explained the concepts in a way that they stick with you forever.

This was my first time coding, and Dr. Byrnes was amazing! She explained things clearly and was very nice. It was fairly easy to pick up the material. EC is given if you turn in exercises early. Quiz practice questions are harder than the quiz questions. Practice memory diagrams, go to office hours, go to quiz review sessions, and you will be set!

Definitely the best professor to take COMP 110 with. As someone who had never touched a line of code before in my life, lectures were extremely interesting and the content never felt like too much. Assignments were dispersed throughout the semester and never felt like too much. Just practice memory diagrams before each exam and you'll do great.

analysis.name: Can Tian
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: It was straightforward and largely reiterated the material from ECON 420. Most students didn't attend lectures since the textbook covered the content just as well. Simply taking notes, completing the practice exam, and doing some studying was more than enough to ace the class. There were also a few homework assignments, all of which were easy!

This course really deserves a different professor given how important and applicable the content is for economics. Lectures are extremely uninteresting and provide no incentive to actually come to lecture and learn information - readings are better than lecturers. Not a lot of communication and you're on the hook for this class. Take with diff prof

Genuinely one of the laziest professors I have had in the econ department. Like, not once in the entire course did she pick up a marker or use an apple pencil to write something out. She straight up walks into class a minute before it starts, and shuts her laptop and bolts out of the room the minute class is over. Arbitrary grader. 0/10
LOL easy class. just study by yourself, no need to go to class.

Dr. Tian is such a nice professor and I loved talking to her after class. SO knowledgeable in MACRO and monetary policy and her 423 class is very well structured and time-efficient, with ready made and current slides and she ends class perfectly. Exams are harder than the practice but doable, I think she curves at the end. Great chill ECON elective

analysis.name: Esther Campi
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The comments speak for themselves. I wish she taught more classes so I could take her again. Possibly the best professor at UNC she's so awesome you won't regret taking her classes!

While Professor Campi's capabilities within the classroom are heavily reflected in her perfect rating, there is no rating that can encapsulate the quality of person she is on a daily basis. She is by far and away my favorite professor I have had at UNC, and is someone that I admire in every way I know how. I could not recommend her enough. 10/10

The comments speak for themselves so I am not really doing anyone a service by writing another. However, in case she reads these, I want Professor Campi to know that she greatly impacts each of her students in a wonderful way. I aspire to be more like her as a person and will always remember her 10 last bits of advice.

She is the best!!! Only took this class because of her other RMPs but I loved it! Very team-based and presentation-heavy, but NO TESTS! Would definitely recommend taking classes with her. She is very understanding and truly cares about her students. She loves participation and is open to any discussion students bring up.

Professor Campi is amazing! She really focuses on improvement rather than expecting perfection on the first go. She provides detailed feedback on every assignment and sometimes gives students the chance to revise mistakes and improve on graded assignments. She is extremely knowledgeable and experienced in the PR field.

analysis.name: Karl Castillo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 28 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: An A was a 95, Dr. Castillo is a very passionate professor, but his lectures were quite long and fast paced. No textbook, only slides, and each slide deck was anywhere from 40-70 slides, each class. The tests were a lot harder than I expected (took this class for an upper bio). Lot's of extra credit though, he wants you to succeed.

GROUP PROJECTS (4). COIL makes class feel like 2 classes. Doesn't communicate well. Exams are niche and questions are worded poorly. Lectures are boring. Cold calls. Loved him for 490. Highly disappointed and frustrated with 441. Quizzes every class. Feels like he doesn't care about students and only wants to do his personal research.

Dr. Castillo is a passionate speaker. He is insightful and holds office hours and will work to make sure his class succeeds. I have taken 4 classes with him so far and plan to take more! There are also extra credit opportunities if you go to class.

Dr. Castillo really cares about his students' learning the material. There are quizzes in every class but they're open note. Even though there were weekly assignments, I didn't feel like they were busy work. He is very clear on grading and the class is well organized. I would recommend this class if you're interested in the material
This class was about corals and it was so interesting. There is a project, but the topic can be chosen for wahtever you want. As long as you try, you will succeed.

analysis.name: Ralph Byrns
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 101 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class isn't very helpful, what he does say about econ in class is right from the book (that he wrote). But you need to go on Fridays for the weekly quiz, which is pretty hard. Lots of resources for help outside of class and lots of online assignments (which you have to pay for).  "Does that sound right?"  Worst class at UNC though so....

Coming into Professor Byrns' class I had no desire or interest in economics. In fact, I was only taking the class so that I could apply to the Kenan-Flagler Business School. Upon arriving into Byrns class, I became interested in econ as a result of his genuine interest and his amazing teaching style! He's not only a teacher but also a great mentor!

I consider Professor Byrns to be one of the most interesting people that I've met in my entire life. He did teach the history of economics (which can be dull), but he kept the class engaged with life skills and small tidbits that you'd never find elsewhere. I was so sad to see him leave UNC, but I know he loves to teach, regardless of the audience.

the only plus side to this class is the crazy amount of unexpected extra credit given at the end that prevents you from getting the horrible grade you think you have all semester. Minimal effort is need to pass this class with a C, and if you really want to learn you better read your textbook and ask your TAs for help, because byrns does NOT teach.

If you are serious about learning anything about economics, be prepared to teach yourself basically everything from the book. Unless you want a laugh, don't go to class except for Fri. Byrns is highly entertaining but if he spent half as much time actually teaching econ as he did trying to be funny, I might have actually learned something from him.

analysis.name: Cdc Reeve
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Honestly, THE BEST professors I've had here.  If you don't like reading or are closed minded you probably won't enjoy the class.  If you are willing to challenge yourself some then you will GAIN SO MUCH.  I could sit and listen to him lecture all day. Don't go into the class looking for a grade, look for an experience and the grade will come.

Great at simply laying out major problems. Enjoyable lectures that were well delivered. Many mostly well-chosen assigned readings in this course. I am sure his other classes are more difficult--PHIL 112 (sometimes taught by others) is an introductory/overview course. He knows his Greek! And he can rattle off extensive quotes from various texts!

Reeve is a great, clear professor who really knows what he's talking about. He is pretty intimidating though, so if you don't have a good TA, your questions may not get answered. He very clearly outlines the readings so you don't really have to read the books, but the exams are not easy at all, unless you're pretty good at philosophy already.

Reeve is a joy to listen to and he really knows his stuff (and is quite aware that he knows it). Readings can generally be skipped if you attend lecture, but they can help to understand the material. This class can be a challenge if you don't think the way Reeve does, but if you do you're golden

Reeve is quite possibly one of the most intelligent men alive. He is just bursting with information. He doesn't really care if you speak or not because he loves to be able to just share what he thinks and why. Do your readings, it'll help immensely. He only gives 2 grades a semester & no exams, so you'll need to do well but he wont let you fail.

analysis.name: Kyle Cessna
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor who is passionate about material and intent on helping his students learn. Students could turn essays in again after reviewing feedback which was extremely helpful. Occasionally a little confusing with class schedule or due dates, but would always correct it and ensure everything was fair for students.

Mr. Cessna is very passionate about philosophy and managed to make a dry course relatively entertaining. You can tell he really cares about students and wants to see people succeed. His grading criteria is very clear and he provides constructive feedback on submissions.

I only took this course because of the major requirement but thought Kyle was a great teacher. I am not super into philosophy and wouldn't have taken this if it wasn't required, but Kyle had nothing to do with that. He is accessible and willing to work with you if you are with him. The grading system was slightly confusing but overall good prof.

analysis.name: Celeste Seifert
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I think the class is really easy, and it's not hard to get good grades if you actually try. Yes, sometimes we have to do unnecessary busywork, but Professor Seifert is pretty accommodating for most things and is pretty nice.

Super easy A for me. Just do what you're supposed to and you'll be fine. Class was mostly developing a research project over a semester, which wasn't too stressful, and the grading wasn't too tough either.

Professor Seifert has by far been my least favorite professor at UNC. ENGL105 is meant to be any easy class for freshmen to take and get through but Seifert makes the class unnecessarily complicated. She is unbelievably condescending and rude to her students. For a grad student, she has a very high ego.

Don't take this class! They grade easy with a lot of papers, but if you want a teacher that will be at least a little bit respectful this is not for you. Celeste is rude and treats us like children. at points they were very rude when answering a simple question. I never wanted to participate in this class because of how discouraged I felt.

Easy class but professor is incredibly rude and condescending. Honestly treats students like they are in middle school. She is an easy grader but if you are looking for a respectful and mature professor I do not recommend. Also coming to class was the biggest waste of time, she would take 20-30 minutes on an activity that should take 5.

analysis.name: Silvia Ceballos
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ceballos is a great professor and makes 207 super easy to understand while also teaching you a lot of useful information. Exams are very fair and are designed "for a bad day", so she makes it very easy to do well in the class. Homeworks can get a little tedious but you work in groups, and they prepare you well for the exams too.

She is a great lecturer and takes the time to review everything you need for the class. Exams are very straightforward with lots of partial credit given just for attempting. Super caring and seemed to actually enjoy teaching.

I had her for both BMME 207 (circuits) & 365 (systems & signaling). She is an amazing professor that understands that the topics can be hard. Because of this, homework can sometimes be on the heavy side, but is always worth while and amazing test prep. Never grades harshly and always is clear for dates of tests or due dates.

I had Dr. Ceballos for BMME 207 and she was amazing! I was really scared about the class going in but she took the time to explain the basics really well. She had amazing methods for solving circuits which I had never seen before in other classes. The exams are based off of the homework she provides. I can't recommend this class enough!!!

Dr. Ceballos is an enthusiastic professor and helpful professor. Her notes are always organized and well-explained. Her homeworks prepare you extremely well for her exams, since her exams are always easier than the homework. There are times when she goes over her notes too quickly during class, but she posts them online in a timely manner.

analysis.name: Cecilia Martinez-Gallardo
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 47 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She is my favorite professo!! She is so sweet and you can tell she is very passionate about what she teaches. While she can be lecture heavy, her lectures are engaging if you are interested in the class. She has a great sense of humor, is incredibly intelligent, and will draw on her own personal life experience which I think is valuable. 10/10 imo.

She is super sweet and passionate about the material! The only thing is that she doesn't really grade anything throughout the semester, so you won't really know what your grade is until the end. The lectures aren't super discussion based, but mostly her just lecturing, but she explains concepts pretty well.

In the kindest way possible, CMG is very disorganized. She is very passionate about the topic however the whole class is confusing. Unclear grading criteria, putting incorrect answers on exams, etc. She is impossible to reach on email, and we don't even know what our grade is in the class. It sucks because she's a great person but not disciplined.

Interesting class, grade based mostly on low-stakes assignments. Do the readings/daily discussion questions, participate in class, and write a current event for basically half of your grade. The other half is a 5pg essay, group podcast, and 3 tests (multiple choice, short answer on final). She is super knowledgeable and made the class enjoyable!

She's passionate and very sweet but very hard to reach outside of class. Your grade is hidden the whole semester and you can not even calculate your own grade most of the time because she never grades most of her things. Midterms can be tricky, just study your notes hard because some of the questions are really specific.

analysis.name: Cecile Ruel
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Ruel is genuinely the sweetest woman. She's definitely a tough grader but pushes you to be the best you can at French. She has so much advice for learning a new language, but her lectures are a bit boring. The small classes force participation but since she only teaches from the textbook the classes can get repetitive and easily skippable.

I love Prof. Ruel- take her for a language if you can. Normally these courses are taught by PhD students and it is so much better to have her- she is a good grader. She's as French as they get and does a great job getting everyone to speak. Our class has such a fun time speaking about all things French but she still covers content needed for exams.
This course took exactly as much effort as it should have. Was a little difficult at times but none of the work felt unnecessary. Fair grader and funny, good energy in class.
Super nice and helpful, in class and during office hours! French 203 is pretty grammar heavy, but she does a good job incorporating cultural knowledge and conversation skills.

I took Roml-89 with Professor Ruel, she is kind but I did not appreciate her teaching style. Professor Ruel barely graded assignments, she also is unclear with instructions and talks in circles. Although the course is called French Coastal Ecologies, we barely focused on the environment of the coast and instead talked extensively about culture.

analysis.name: Celina Larios
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Celina is very fun! Energetic and engaging, she worked very hard to get everyone to participate in conversation and join discussions. Lots of readings, and participation matters a lot. Very little homework (other than reading before each class), and she's a very lenient and kind grader. Class content was boring sometimes but she made it enjoyable.

Profe Larios is so much fun. She creates a welcoming environment for students of all different Spanish levels to practice speaking. As far as 255 goes it is much more difficult than it was presented in 204.
Class time is fun but there are additional quizzes, projects, and large papers that are not related to speaking at all.
I had quite a bit of difficulty with SPAN203. Profe Larios worked hard to make sure her students understood the material. She was a fairly tough grader on things that I felt were subjective.

analysis.name: Celia Shiau
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: AVOID AT ALL COSTS. If you want to accept the greater challenge and see how well you can teach yourself, then this class is just for you. If you have common sense, then drop this class, this school, and this life. Just quit.

BIOL 545 was one of my favorite courses at UNC, largely in part to Dr. Shiau's teaching.  The 3-hour class structure was sometimes a little hard to sit through (not her fault), but she did her best to make the entire lecture engaging.  Literature-based teaching style was great and I would definitely take the course again.

Truly terrible class and professor. Dr. Shiau is super sweet and approachable in her one office hour, but cannot teach to save her life. Class was a waste of everyone's time as she could not convey a single idea. Textbook readings are awful and dense, but she tests from readings. If she's the only choice, take this class another semester.

Dr. Shiau was clearly passionate about the material, but lacked organizational skills. The class material was incredibly interesting and the small class size was great, but I often felt like she emphasized small details rather than the big picture. Overall, she is a great person, but the 3 hr lecture format of this class was not ideal.

Nice and knowledgeable, but exams were tough. Required you to know very specific details and processes from her slides, but she said that she wanted us to remember concepts from her class moving forward, which makes sense. Use GRQs to get a sense of the topic, and then gain more information in class. Not a lot of content, just a lot of specifics.

analysis.name: Yasmin Cedamanos
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: So amazing!! Please take this class if you have a chance, we learned SO much and Professor Cedamanos is an incredible teacher. Even if you struggle with Spanish she is so kind and accommodating while also pushing you to try your best. Learning Quechua as a language and a culture has been such a treat take this class!!! Fun projects as well!!

Span 105 moved very quickly, about 1 unit/3 days. However, Prof. Cedamanos was a very kind and approachable person. She is a picky grader, and very detail-oriented. You must participate several times each class to get a good grade! Much of the pacing is out of her hands, but she follows it closely, so make sure not to miss any assignments!

She is very nice and the content is not super difficult. The problem is that she grades much harsher on the pronunciation assessments compared to other teachers in the section. All in all she isn't terrible, just try to get Professor Lindquist instead if possible
Very great in class with clear lectures and examples. Helped a lot with gestures when learning. There was a lot of homework and the class did move pretty quickly.

analysis.name: Charlene Regester
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: She's very passionate. Pay attention to lectures because most of the test material comes directly from her mouth. If she can tell that you are trying then you will do well.

Dr. Regester is very knowledgable about African History! The class is very lecture heavy and does not have any slides, so going to class is important. Grading policies can be unclear at times. I found the topics to be very interesting and I learned so many  things about the African Diaspora.
Dr. Regester is willing to help you out as much as she can. She's incredibly knowledgeable about her craft but she doesn't dismiss your ideas and has no chip on her shoulder. And she's funny as hell.

Dr. Regester teaches you what you must know for exams, but you cannot miss class. All notes are spoken and you will not get them if you do not attend. The paper guidelines are unclear as she gave me an underserved grade because she did not like my word choice and had no comments on my thesis or supporting arguments. Find another gen ed to take.
Such a sweet and knowledgeable person but such a hard class. I really wish I did not take it even though at times it's been interesting.

analysis.name: Christian Lundberg
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are very funny and engaging, but he can go off track at times, which makes some concepts harder to follow. His presentations can also be difficult to study from. The class overall felt manageable, but much of the grading (including the midterm and final) was done by TAs, so your experience may depend on your TA.

He's just a genuinely great guy, and super personable. I'm taking one of his classes next semester. Probably one of UNC's best profs. His lectures are really interesting too, he's a great public speaker. I had a great TA as well, and just thought it was a good class. I always attended his lectures, even with attendance not being mandatory.

Christian Lundberg was my favorite professor out of the 3 for IDST132L. The class, however, is very TA dependent as the midterm and final are graded by them. Very fun class to listen to, most of the readings you won't have to read, but there are a select few (they will make sure you know which) that you should read.

Dense readings here and there, but he had the most interesting and applicable viewpoint. The midterm was to define terms, then recap a specific reading for each professor. You get to make an exam aid for the midterm and the final, and they give you the questions.

I took this for communication beyond Carolina credit, easiest class ever. Only 3 speeches graded by TA, and you pick the topic. Overall, I learned a lot and enjoyed this class! No homework other than preparing for speeches. The final was take-home and you write what you learned in the class. He also recommends his textbook but you don't need it.

analysis.name: Cinthia Arango Sosa
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I loved Prof Sosa! She's a really lenient grader and is so sweet and understanding. You definitely have to participate in class, but as long as you do, you'll get a good participation grade. It's a flipped classroom, but the exams were pretty easy if you've taken Spanish in the past (plus they tell you what's on the exam). Try to get her for 203!

I had missed out on two years of Spanish and was still able to keep up well enough, especially considering how little previous Spanish teachers had taught me. Every time I had to make up quizzes due to medical reasons, she was very understanding and accommodated for me. She was also pretty lenient with grading at some points. I highly recommend.

I loved her!  She is super sweet and a very understanding professor usually willing to take things late as long as you contact her and explain. She never called on anyone or forced them to answer. She brought us candy and food for our end of semester presentations which was not required of her. She is very approachable and just a sweet prof.

I have never enjoyed Spanish and this class proved it. Professor Arango-Sosa was amazing and was always willing to meet with me when I had questions. No matter how hard I studied, the exams killed me. A huge portion of your grade is participation. She doesn't care if you're grammatically correct, as long as you speak in Spanish.

She is nice, and has a pretty defined structure for the class. Occasionally, she struggled with the technology aspects of online teaching and she pretty much reads from the textbook, but she explains it well. Probably not the best SPAN 105 professor, but she is definitely better than a solid amount of them.

analysis.name: Massimiliano Cirulli
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Massi is a great teacher as well as a person. While he is strict, he is also funny. He makes learning another language cool and fun. His positivity and encouragement he gives to students make them want to learn more. Because Spanish classes at KU fill up crazy fast, this language is a good alternate. Italian is closely related to Spanish.

Massi is awesome! He cares so much about his students and puts in a lot of effort towards class. You have to do work outside of the class- as with any language- but it is easy if you stay on top of your stuff. He makes the class fun and everyone is involved during it. Attendance is key

Honestly, I didn't put in much effort and only took the class because it was a requirement. However, Professor Massi made it fun. He is an easy going guy, and the overall atmosphere of the class is relaxed.
truly caring and amazing professor

analysis.name: Menevis Cilizoglu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had Professor Cilizoglu at St. Olaf College, where she taught Intro to International Relations. It was a relatively laid-back class, but paying attention, doing the readings, and participating in class certainly helped. She's passionate about the subject matter and entertains student questions. However, her class isn't very engaging so beware.

Menevis teaches POLI150 for a small class (30-40 students) and it makes it super interesting because she always tries to engage in a debate. Her course is clear and easy to understand, and she is always available if you have further questions out of class. The multiple choice part of her tests are easy, the short questions are harder.

Love Professor Cilizoglu, fantastic professor who is well qualified. She does a great job at making class interesting while combining wit and humor. Test's were pretty tough but would take anything by her again.
Never taking again, will waste your time. Very unorganized.

analysis.name: Cicek Beeby
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took this class having been told it was an easy A with a different teacher. This teacher in conjunction with Matt Schueller present long and extremely dense powerpoints on overwhelmingly mundane history. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Working hard for a B-/B. With that being said, Beeby is more interesting than the other lecturer and teaches better .

Do NOT take this class. Material was extremely boring, and the midterm was full of ridiculously minute details that nobody could be expected to remember. She is a nice person but not a good teacher, gives unclear instruction regularly and is difficult to understand. I would recommend avoiding this class at all costs.

The only hard part about this class is trying to pay attention and take notes for 75 minutes straight, other than that, the material that would be on the test was extremely straightforward and the tests were exactly what was in the notes/ power points. The textbooks aren't really necessary and they are really expensive I wouldn't recommend buying.

This class wasn't too amazing, but it is a WB gen ed. It wasn't awful but the papers are tough and the tests are worse. Cicek was a pretty entertaining lecturer for the material but it wasn't enough, especially to keep my attention for an hour and a half. If you like ancient history, then go for it, otherwise you may want to look elsewhere.

Cicek did not make lectures very engaging and interesting, so it was very hard to pay attention. Her power points were vague. My friends and I absolutely dreaded going to this class. The tests are very hard, she expects you to know all the drawn plans of each city. This course could have been better if taught by someone else.

analysis.name: Joseph Cima
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The limit as x approaches a passing grade in this class basically doesn't exist. He has cool classical music playing in his office during office hours though, so take advantage of them. You're better off getting the cafeteria workers to teach you calculus than this guy.

He holds consistent office hours but his communication skills are so poor that it's pointless. He'd start on one topic and forget what he was doing midsentence and move on to a different example. He didn't know how to do half of the problems and mainly read frm the book. We had one test all year and ambiguous grading. Worst teacher I have ever had.

One of the worst math professors I have ever had!  This class is known to be hard, but his absent-mindedness and unrecognizable scribbles on the board did NOT help.  Had to drop this class.  He's crazy smart and has good stories, and he's nice (he pulled a box of kleenex out of his desk drawer during office hours one day) but he cannot teach!

Worst math teacher I've ever had. Always gets lost in the problems, can't use technology, made us all buy books that he wanted to use not the ones the book store sells. Unorganized. You never know what section you're learning anthe examples he gives have nothing to do with the homework and neither has anything todo with the tests. Enjoy

I frankly thought that he was the most horrible teacher there is!  I mean I didn't understand a word he was talking about.  You should only take that class if you are willing to teach yourself, which defeats the purpose of having an instructor, right?!  Anyways, never take his class...taking his class will mess up your gpa.

analysis.name: Clark Gray
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Lab assignments were pretty easy, but point penalties for tiny mistakes were large at times. Our reading quizzes were pretty challenging, but doable. He is very accommodating, and provides plenty of opportunities to make up points for late assignments. Overall, he is a great professor and this was a very interesting class!

Do not take this class if you are not good at weekly quizzes on lengthy papers. The quizzes are hyper specific and they are not open note making them quite tricky as they are a large part of your grade. The work wasn't necessarily bad, but Dr. Gray is not accommodating or flexible on any assignments.

Extremely picky about grading papers/labs and would take off points for the tiniest things. Also had extremely specific weekly quizzes that were closed note and based off of multiple readings that were laughably long. Kind of nice, sometimes? Kind of also passive agressive.

Do not take him for GEOG120. He is lazy when making notes for class and his tests are way too specific. Unless you plan on dedicating a large amount of time to studying for this class, do not take it.
Pretty straightforward class, interesting (but lengthy) readings and complicated quizzes. Grading was pretty inconsistent, but fair ins ome cases. He did not  fw me but was pretty chill to others.

analysis.name: Christopher Handy
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 174 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I'm not sure if it was because i've never taken any type of statistics class before, but I did not follow a single thing he said. The lectures felt really long and the exams were hard. He seems very nice tho. I would NOT recommend taking this class if you have never taken a statistics class before. There should be a stats pre-req for this course.

Lectures were not interesting in the slightest. Homework was difficult, but he held office hours in the econ aid center and would answer any questions. Mostly a boring class and requires prior statistics knowledge to keep up with how quickly he goes through topics. 200 person lecture with no connection to the professor. Curve is lifesaving.

Brutal class. Lectures are confusing and hard to follow—I stopped paying attention and just taught myself after class. Office hours helped, but I waited too long. Pre-class videos and the textbook are useless. Exams are awful and nothing like the practice, which has 150+ separate questions and is super tough. Only the curve saved me.

Overcomplicates, extremely boring lecturer. Class is glorified stats with the introduction of coding that he expects you to learn on your own. Grading criteria is unclear on tests and subjective. Teacher is spiteful, won't round your grade up or fix grading errors even if you are .01% away, he gets joy from seeing students suffer.

By far the most organized professor I've had at UNC. Gives incredibly clear guidelines, grades everything in a timely manner with plenty of opportunities for feedback. Provides plenty of resources for each exam and is always in his office happy to help his students. I love Christopher Handy.

analysis.name: Claudia Malhotra
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

For exams it's literally just hundreds of definitions, which is fine but she creates really niche arbitrary questions that I don't think trust ones true knowledge of Marketing. Very tough but also very nice at the same time. Would never take her again

Claudia is someone that was meant to be a teacher & it is so evident. She is so caring and understanding of her students & I genuinely appreciate her as a human being sooo much. Honestly, I won't say this class is easy, because I didn't find that to be the case. But taking her class was worth it because she is so knowledgable, passionate, & kind.

Amazing professor, cares so much about both her students and the material. Her passion and fun in class activities made this one of my favorite classes at UNC. Cases were a lot of work but graded fairly (loved new rubric system). Midterm/final surprisingly hard, definitely study and practice term definitions. Highly recommend, learned a lot!

Claudia is an incredible professor who clearly cares about her teachers and is very passionate about marketing. She always brought energy to the class and it was never boring. The class does have a lot of work and the case assignments can be tedious. The midterm I thought wasn't bad and final was harder. Both very heavy on memorization.

analysis.name: Jordan Claytor

review_highlights.comment: He was a good prof but the exam questions were designed to trip you up and some of the questions were very poorly worded. The written responses were easily misinterpreted and worth a lot of points, so I would say to make sure you read carefully!

Although Claytor is nice as a person, this can be easily overlooked when the exams are worth so so so much of your grade. From someone who is OOS and always had an A in high school bio/chem this is super difficult esp if you have other hard classes. course is entertaining but the lectures are almost useless and everything relies on self-study. Each question is 3 points out of 20, and one mistake means losing all 3—dropping to a B. This class isn't too bad, there is a good amount of work before and after class but it's pretty easily managable. Professor Claytor is great, teaches things in a way that is understandable and fun, and truly cares about students. BIO 101 is just a very difficult weed out class. Tests are weighted super heavy. Claytor made it enjoyable, but it is a lot of work and difficult to get an A.

analysis.name: Clay Williams

Professor Williams is honestly one of the best professors I have had. There are quite a lot of assignments in the course, but I always felt prepared. Clay gives incredible feedback and cares so much about your success. I truly feel like I'm a better creative person because of this class.

considering his first time teaching, did a not bad job! do expect assignments to kind of hit at the same time, but they aren't hard to complete and there are options to rework for a better grade. definitely got to take away a decent amount of skills!

Josh did give chances for corrections on midterm, but paper grades were unnecessarily nitpicky and unclear. This class ended my 4.0, and I never really felt like I had a real chance of getting an A.

You should immediately consider taking anyone else. His grading was unfair, harsh, & inconsistent. He also offers no actual assistance be it office hours or online. He made the notoriously manageable core PLCY class absolute hell, and ever other section had it much easier which was really unfair and disheartening. Not kind, capable, or helpful.

Trying to succeed in his class felt truly Sisyphean. You can go to office hours, read the textbook, pages and pages of the readings he assigned, and still not feel confident for his assignments. He was such a discouraging instructor. His syllabus said that effort does not mean success and boy was that true. Take anyone else for 581.

I think with more experience he could be really good professor because he knows the material well, was accommodating, and quick to answer emails and questions. However, I know from working in pairs with different people throughout the semesters that most people found his lectures hard to follow, which was the main issue.

analysis.name: Christopher Clark

This class is Minority Representation. There are 3 exams (none of them are cumulative) and he gives you a study guide a few days before each exam. There is one research paper towards the end of the class. Really interesting and fairly easy class. He goes over the readings in his lectures

Great professor, but lowkey not the easy A I thought it would be. Exam questions come from study guides. Essays were a time crunch since he tended to delay releasing prompts, but they were not too difficult. He has funny tangents in class. Great guy, make a lasting connection with him! Prof Clark is one of the most caring professors I've had at UNC. Although his classes are lecture-heavy, he throws in lots of engaging material (campaign ads, speeches, etc.) and plenty of jokes. Take a class with him if you can!!!

Prof. Clemente is the best ever. Super caring and kind guy who recognizes the common pitfalls and works to help you avoid them. He is Spanish himself and likes to share fun phrases or stories about Spain. He cares about you as a person and you learning Spanish. He is just awesome!!

This professor was one of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had. Professor Crothers is the most influential professor I've had at UNC so far. The feedback he gives on papers is also super helpful.
