Easy A. Whole grade is based on a "performance review" at the end of semester where you convince him why you deserve an A. Lectures are boring but definitely don't need to pay attention or really even show up.

Choose Kyle as your 105 teacher. 30 mins of work PER WEEK, easiest class you will ever take, 1 assignemnt a week, asnychronus classes, at the end he lets you argue for an A if you somehow dont already have one. He's also super super chill.

kyle was amazing! he is very kind, down to earth, and funny. he cares about his students and is very flexible with due dates and assignments. he also gives very good feedback and grades fairly. very chill and easy class, good for people who don't want much work to do for their 105 class.
Kyle might be the best 105 teacher. Allows late submissions, easy assignments that take 1-2 hours a week max. Also you can call him Kyle and not professor Cunningham

analysis.name: Harry Cushman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cushman is a very interesting and intriguing lecturer. Which is why it was so disappointing his class became so disorganized the second half of the semester. Several assignments were crammed into the last few weeks of class (one being a group presentation) with little to no description, rubric, or due dates. Incredibly frustrating and stressful

Only did pop quizzes the first month then didnt do any more, midterm is super easy you study off a jeopardy, class seems so intimidating at first but it gets so easy so quickly, final is not too difficult, final project is super easy you get a 100 as long as you put in minimal effort, be ready to ask classmates for missed notes

Professor Cushman if you're reading this I'm so sorry. I almost hit you with my car the other day on campus. I don't want you to know it was me because you're my favorite professor and I don't want you to hate me but I want to say I'm so sorry it was me who almost hit you. I'll be more careful I'm so sorry. I hope you have a great break!

I don't understand why all the comments are good. Dr. Cushman is a nice person and can be flexible, also knowledgeable about his field. But the syllabus is super disorganized and looking back, I learned zero stuff in the class and really thought it was a waste of time. To do the final project you really need background knowledge outside or prior.

i loved this class and really enjoyed the book. it felt like one large book club! if you are even considering this class, take it. in fact, even if you don't enjoy reading, take it. it was so fun getting to hear everyone's different perspectives and takeaways from the novel—that's what reading is all about, after all!

analysis.name: Tyler Curtain
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 57 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: You will not regret taking this course. He knows what he is talking about and makes class very engaging. Often makes you think outside of the box and dive deeper into hidden meanings of films. Make sure to participate, actually watch the films and memorize the facts he asks of the movies. Not being to check grades was no stress honestly.

Loved this class. Very discussion-based class, that's why participation and attendance matters. Usually a smaller class so he'll notice if you're not in class for a few days. Lots of reading but exams are easy and grading is lax. I enjoyed his class tho! Easy A if you're okay with reading and speaking up at least once a class.

I LOVED THIS CLASS. It was SO interesting, and I would recommend it to basically everyone. If classroom participation really stresses you out, you might find this class to be scary, but he is so interesting to listen to and the seminar is very good.

I audited this class, so grain of salt, but Dr. Curtain is kind and extremely knowledgeable about horror movies. He isn't afraid to call on people out of the blue and challenge their answers, but he's also funny and encourages discussion. Really enjoyed this class.

Genuinely a great class. Professor Curtain really makes you think about the films you watch, I have a whole new perspective of sci-fi film now. All you do is talk about the films/books in class, make sure to watch/read everything because he will cold call. All films except 2 books during the whole semester but easy reads. 1 midterm and 1 final.

analysis.name: Graham Culbertson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great class that provides a broad history of action films in a low-stress environment. Daily film viewing + discussion posts, plus three papers. For all assignments, if you meet the word count, you get an 100. The short video lessons were really informative, and Culbertson gives good feedback on papers. Really fun class, definitely recommend.

I love Dr. Culbertson. He's frank, witty, philosophical, and a lot of fun to talk to. I'm a STEM major, and it made me genuinely sad when I realized I probably wouldn't be taking another class of his.

Graham is v passionate & the BEST! I didn't know what to expect, but this quickly became my fav class. You read weekly, play board games in class, & write discussion posts. The final is playing a board game that u create. Graham truly cares ab his students & uses a low-pressure grading style that makes u rly want to put in effort. HIGHLY recommend
took it online over the summer. he is so chill and gives great feedback. he also does contracts based grading which is super nice. you can tell he is passionate about film and i learned a lot!!

Professor Graham was an amazing teacher! We had different units which were all very unique. Definitely not a traditional teacher in his grading contract-- but his system of 100 or fail made it a lot less stressful and allowed us to explore the content more! Provides a worldly view and always opened the class up for group discussion! TAKE HIM!!

analysis.name: Paul Cuadros
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cuadros was an awesome professor! The class was very consistent in work, which was a good schedule to follow, but also not overwhelming in work. Cuadros is very considerate with extended help and is very open to questions. I really enjoyed this as a fun journalism course.

Continually brought in bias in class, he was by no means impartial to anyone who went against his grain of thinking and you paid the price with a poor grade. It was either submit to his ideals, thinking or fail the class. No dissent, independent or critical thinking was allowed.
Paul Cuadros is a tough grader and expects you to turn in quality work, however, he is extremely caring and sees potential in all of his students.

Professor Cuadros is a gem in the J school, and if you aspire to be a journalist or reporter, you have to take a class with him. You have an article due every week but this class teaches you so much and Cuadros is super accommodating, caring & gives excellent feedback. He is a great person to know and he deeply cares about his students doing well.

An amazing, seasoned reporter with a love for teaching and developing his students' crafts. Tough work (one article a week, 3+ interviews, conducted remotely), but accomodating with people not getting back to you and granting extensions. Grading is based both on AP style and how he thinks it reads, so there can sometimes be "hidden traps."

analysis.name: Emily  Curtin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Climate Change and Health was an incredible class and while topics can be quite heavy, they are relevant and easily applicable to life outside university. Dr. Curtin is very approachable and her knowledge of various fields makes her a great lecturer. 390 is heavily based around discussion. Do the reading + participate and you'll do well.

I cannot recommend professor Curtin enough! I took anth of fitness culture with her and it was so fun! lectures are discussion based and very entertaining. You complete a research project of your choosing during the semester, and the workload is split up well throughout the semester. she is very supportive and wants you to succeed.

Very knowledgeable- all readings are on canvas or accessible through UNC. Gender, sexuality, and health is lecture based with student led discussions some weeks. attendance required but 2 absences no questions asked allowed. HIGHLY recommend to any med anth major/minor or anyone interested in the topic!

One of the best professors at UNC—this was my second class with Dr. Curtin, and I'd take a third! Lectures are engaging, and grading is fair if you put in the effort. The class focuses on understanding and thoughtful discussion over regurgitating forgettable facts. Highly recommend Gender & Sexuality and Bodies Under Capitalism (390 courses).

Dr. Curtin is so easy to talk to during class and office hours. She is slow to grade things, but most of the assignments are really straightforward, easy, and completion. Those that are not are not worth a huge percentage of the grade

analysis.name: Cyrus Sinai
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cyrus is absolutely the best professor I've ever had! He cares so much about his students and it's clear that he truly loves what he does. I especially like how he takes the time to get to know students and goes above and beyond to make the course relevant and interesting for everyone. Additionally, if you pay attention in class, you'll do well!

Cyrus is the absolute goat. He is willing to work with you on extensions, late work, anything you need. the man would probably donate a kidney if I needed a transplant. homework is extremely light since my class voted to move half the assignments to be optional. extremely easy tests: 1-pagers allowed, hard questions dropped, you can get points back

Nicest professor ever. Cares so much about his students and their success and is very passionate about the topics he teaches. Not a lot of work assigned, 1 assignment and reading reflection per week and only 1 midterm and final which you can use a one pager on each. Would recommend him to anyone. Take his class!!
I haven't finished the class yet, but i dont need to. It was that easy. I already got an A+ and its September.

Cyrus was an amazing teacher. Unfortunately it looks like he won't be back next semester but he made the class so engaging and enjoyable. Everyone I talked to also loved the course. If you ever have an opportunity to take a class with him do it!!!

analysis.name: Cynthia Current
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 81 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Current's class was almost unnecessarily difficult. She seemed like a nice person but she was very narrow-minded with how she wanted things to be written. When reading through comments on my papers, it felt as if she was marking them simply to have marked them. She rambles in lectures and is very hard on attendance. I don't recommend her class.

Worst professor I have had in all my time at UNC. Beyond unorganized, fails to lay out clear and succinct expectations for assignments and grades like you are supposed to know exactly what she wants when she doesn't tell you. Doesn't bother updating assignment information from previous semesters. Avoid! Find a professor who has their act together.

Dr. Current is super nice and the class is not too hard if you're doing the readings. Class participation is super important, but if you have anxiety about public speaking you can talk to them because they're very understanding.

Take 105 with a different professor. I cannot stress enough how passive aggressive and awful Dr. Current is. She will send you nasty emails ridiculing you if you miss a class or an assignment. She was non-understanding and rude even when I was mentally struggling and when I had COVID. She also rants about her opinions often instead of teaching.

Arbitrary grader. It is clear from her condescending emails/feedback that she thinks extremely highly of herself. She spends most of class on a rant about something random. She is very serious about attendance/doesn't regularly offer zoom. She does give extensions if needed. No one got less than a B, but ENGL 105 is supposed to be an easy A.

analysis.name: Cynthia Radding
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Required course for LTAM majors. Most of the class agree seems she just leaves us to teach. Discussion based on reading, be sure to give specific examples from text ( what was said on page __, etc). Only grades are attendance/participation, group project, & 20 page final. Very tough grader & dry. Uncomfortable silences. But is for student success.

Very very boring class. The material is extremely interesting but the lectures are very dry and just not fun to go to. They are mandatory and the recitation section is better but still like pulling teeth. The exams are in a nice format and if you study you will do well. Do not know if it is worth it though.

This is a good class if you show up most of the time and take notes. You can download the power points and use them to study along with the study guides that she gives for the midterm and final, which are not too hard and graded very fairly. She wants you to do well and isvery flexible, even let me re-take the midterm so I could get a better grade.

Her lectures are super hard to follow she usually just talks without stopping and has powerpoints with like 4 words per slide so if you dont get it when she says it, you will not get it ever. The good thing is that she gives you everything that's going to be on the test so if you study it you can get a solid grade. She is a very sweet lady

Every class for the entire class, she is talking at us, many times reading directly from a paper she had wrote on the topic in preparation for the class. Thankful for the powerpoint. The lectures were extremely boring. I learned more from doing the readings than from going to class. I would not take this professor again.

analysis.name: Cynthia Sturton
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 31 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is the worst COMP Class I have taken to date. Lectures are irrelevant to the LABS and there is little direction and guidance given. LABS are released late and then she doesn't accept late work. The reverse classroom is lazy teaching, Youtube teaches better than this professor. Be prepared to pay the school to teach yourself in this class.

Please do not take this class with her. Every time I step into this class, I fear something terrible might happen. Her lecture slides have less detailing and poor formatting, and it's a matter of whether you know the content or not. The labs are sometimes lengthy; only OH can save you on that. Other than that, please refrain yourself from this.

Cynthia seems like a nice person but is a terrible prof. The way she ran this class was disrespectful and unacceptable imo. She wouldn't accept any late work but would routinely release lecture videos and grades late. The labs (40% of grade) were also such a stretch from the class content and were the bane of my existence. Do not take this class :(

New labs are extremely difficult, time-consuming and the lectures are not very helpful. Sturton is not accommodating: when 50 people requested extension on a lab it wasn't provided. Mandatory videos, which are 40-80 mins long, are uploaded late in evening and you need to know the material for the quiz next morning. This is very bad class, avoid it

Idk what happened to this class but it is absolutely terrible. Irrelevant, harshly graded, and very difficult lab assignments. Everything in this class is graded insanely, including something as small as a project outline. Sturton is disorganized. Seriously don't take this class. My grade is sitting around a B and I've put way too much work in.

analysis.name: Cynthi Schauer
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I really think that Dr. Schauer is a smart woman, but she just has trouble explaining what's going on in her head. She gets tongue-twisted easily and ends up circling everything on the notes, so you really don't know what's important. Tests are too long for the time allotted. Her accent can be pretty amusing - she pronounces anions "EAN-iens."

The first two weeks a class she spent the whole class period trying to figure out how the projector worked, no lie. Bad at explaining things, textbook is useless, other than the useless textbook assigned questions, no other study material is provided. Clicker questions are nothing like the test. Practice exam is way shorter than the real exam.

She explains material in a nice simple holistic fashion in class, but then expects you memorize every single diagram and obscure calculation she ever mentioned for the test. The tests are too long, and though curved they are just too hard compared to the rest of the course material.

Worst teacher I've taken in the chem department. Awful, point blank. Takes forever on the easy concepts and can't explain the more difficult ones. Tests are stupid and it's often unclear what the question is asking. Very unfortunate that they don't find a replacement for her.

Dr. Schauer is not an effective lecturer. Your TAs are your best resource for information. Recitations for this class consist of students working on other classwork or websurfing while Schauer talks in circles. There are poll everywhere questions every lecture, otherwise everyone would skip. Students and TAs alike think she is very disorganized.

analysis.name: Cynthia Demetriou
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is amazing. By far the very best teacher I have ever had. He style of teaching is remarkable. She's clear in everything she says, upbeat, funny, and motivating. Inclusive of all students. Just the absolute best. I highly recommend her.

Among the best teachers I've had. Her style is remarkable. She's able to efficiently guide discussions, keep students interested, and she is clear in her instruction and expectations. She tests and grades fairly as well. I highly recommend her.
Junior Transfer Seminar is a pretty easy A. There is a presentation and 10 page paper at the end of the semester, but it really is not difficult. She is easy to get in contact with and REALLY nice.
Cynthia is a wonderful professor. I took her junior transfer seminar course and enjoyed it.

analysis.name: Oskar Czendze
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took HIST 153 with Professor Czendze, however, that was not an option to select. He is one of the most genuine professors and often brought candy to class for us :) There is a midterm early in the semester, a final, and a 1-2 page paper due roughly every other week. Take notes, pay attention to lectures, and do the readings - you'll be fine!

I took hist 153 with him but that wasn't an option to select -- great teacher, very knowledgeable and I really learned a lot. Definitely a lot of readings but its easy to get by with just skimming right before class. Pay attention in lecture too. One midterm, final paper, final exam, and ~6 mini papers throughout the semester based on readings.

Prof. Czendze is a very thoughtful and kind professor. I took "Holocaust Remembrance" with him which was fascinating. He encouraged lots of student participation while still guiding the discussion. The readings WERE a bit heavy at times, but they were genuinely interesting. If you at least skim and think about them, you'll be alright.
I took Hist 153, but it wasn't an option! it was a very interesting class, but there was just too much reading. nearly impossible to read before every class

analysis.name: Lightning Czabovsky
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: MEJO341 is a boring class but Lightning made it so much fun! There's no homework, and quizzes and exams are fairly easy, just be prepared to read. Only downside is it's an 8 AM but it lowkey doesn't feel like that sometimes (+ attendance technically isn't mandatory, he does give extra credits if you come though).

Lightning is the best! Goes out of the way to be accessible during office hours and help with assignments as much as you need. Gives great lectures as well and is very engaging. I wish I could take more classes with him, he's one of the best Hussman professors I've had.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Media Law is not the easiest class, but Lightning makes it so much better. Three exams + five quizzes + participation. As long as you do your readings, you'll be fine. He also curves the grade and offers extra credit, so don't worry if you didn't do well initially.

I've never rated a professor on here but I MUST rate Lightning. IF I COULD TAKE EVERY CLASS WITH HIM I WOULD. He makes the information so digestible, holds exam review sessions before each exam that basically tell you what to study and genuinely cares about the success of his students so. much. his dog Bert is adorable and he brings him to class.

I had the pleasure of taking Lightning for Mejo-341. He made law material understandable and digestible for someone who has no background knowledge of it. He had great communication, was open to questions, and quickly gave us our grades back. You can tell when someone is meant to be a professor---and Lightning is one of those gems!

analysis.name: Daniel Thornton
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 23 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: You don't know your grade until the very end. Nothing goes in canvas. Not even the quiz grades. It would be fair to assume it's mostly participation in class but he doesn't even tell you what the exam is weighted. It's easy if you participate and try, he's a good teacher and he really really cares about his students. No excused absences though.

Professor Thornton is amazing! Take this class if you can! As a first-year student, this class was amazing for meeting new people and getting to know a tight-nit group. Participation goes a long way and he often just calls on people. Highly recommend spending some time with the vocab and practicing the material, it made this class a breeze.

Professor Thornton is the goat. He is a great professor and I am so thankful I chose to take Dutch with him. Easily my favorite professor here at UNC. If you need to fulfill your language requirement, CHOOSE DUTCH WITH HIM!!! The class isn't really a gimme, but if you keep up with the work, you will absolutely be fine.

Awesome professor! He's super caring and helpful. He genuinely wants you to succeed! You have to go to class and participation matters, so talk in class. Overall, great class and would take again. Dan also knows a thing or two about the Netherlands, so don't be shy about asking him questions!
Love this class, very engaging, lots of time to practice Dutch, and very clear expectations for quizzes and tests. Provides good feedback and cares for his students.

analysis.name: David Ross
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 89 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He was the most annoying teacher. He talks everyday with a powerpoint, and talks about one slide for 15 mins. He asks questions in class and then when you answer he says "mm hmm" and then disagrees with you. He's so picky about giving As and if he gives an A it's an A-. There are group projects too. DON'T TAKE ENGL 105 WITH HIM, you will hate it.

I have few qualms with Dr. Ross as a person, but I would advise against taking his courses if you have a history with sexual trauma. He would often make derogatory and uncomfortable remarks about fictional women and almost every piece of media assigned included and poorly addressed the topic of sexual violence. Please be wary when registering!

Dr. Ross is simply a great professor. The lectures are certainly dense with ideas and cultural insight but are by no means boring. He's exceedingly well-read and well-spoken, and he gives very detailed feedback on papers (so you know exactly how to improve). Everyone on here complaining that he's a hard grader is just mad that they can't write.

He is very opinionated and you have the be an amazing writer for a first year class. If you are not a good writer and don't enjoy talking, do not take this class and if you do like discussions I also advise against it. There are a lot easier 105 classes that will allow you to enjoy the class while still earning a good grade. Do not take!

Ross is a lovely guy, but his grading criteria for English 105 is too harsh. Your grade is dependent on your natural skills as a writer. I spent hours revising my papers and could not get over a B+. For 105, this should not be the case. If you are Shakespeare, go ahead; he will improve you. If not, your grades will suffer.

analysis.name: Desire Kedagni
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The average on the final was a 72. He refuses to curve anything in the class. His actual teaching style was not terrible, and a lot of the exams reused questions from the problem sets, but the fact that he did not curve a single test with the justification of "if 4-5 people get an A, the grades work" was terrible. The average class grade was a C+.

I didn't like Econ 400, but Kedagni made me love econometrics! You have to go to class, since he takes attendance for a grade and includes concepts from lectures on exams. He's a chalkboard lecturer, which isn't everyone's cup of tea. My one gripe is that the midterms are way too long. However, their content isn't difficult. You just have to study.

Desire is a great professor and also a joy to talk to. He made econometrics enjoyable to learn and his problem sets, although somewhat challenging, are great review material. I would highly recommend you study and understand the problem sets and attend each class since he goes through important math proofs.

ECON 470 is very difficult, no matter who you take it with. Kedagni was a really nice guy, but resources were super limited outside of class. Thankfully, I passed/failed this course because the average on the final was a 70 with no curving whatsoever.
I took ECON 470 in fall 2023 and this course covers everything you need to know about linear regression. The pace of the class is very reasonable and Professor Kedagni's notes are easy to understand.

analysis.name: Denise Mitchell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: boring lecture and attendance not required so you can get away with not going. tests were pretty easy as long as you complete the study guide. tests were mcq, true/false, fill in the blank, and frq. has review days before exam where you can earn extra credit for the midterm. overall p easy class

For the semester long project, everything is peer-reviewed until the final research brief meaning that it could fail to meet her standards when it's worth the largest portion of your grade. Extremely strict on grading for exams and provides no flexibility in answers. Lost an entire point out of 30 for using a synonym instead of the actual word.

Tests were horrible. She grades very strict and the questions are too broad. She gives barely any material to study and grades so specifically. Other than the tests the class is fine but the tests make it awful. You can skim the readings that are assigned every day. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

Horrible class, harsh grader, way too specific on her test for no reason, class was all done in lecture and a waste of time to go to, her in class assignments did nothing to reinforce the class content.

I enjoyed this class! She is very particular when it comes to grading exams, specifically the essay portions but as long as you complete the study guides you will do just fine in the class. Attendance is preferred but you can get by skipping if you need it. Easy A if you complete all the study guides!

analysis.name: Paul Delamater
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. D is honestly one of my favorite GEOG professors! He explains concepts super well and actually seems to care and want to connect with his students. His class is pretty laid back and fun.

While there is nothing wrong with the course content, Delameter is very disrespectful and condescending in his feedback and when students ask questions. Never have felt scared to talk in a class before. For a class about technology, no question is a dumb question. Consider a student might be struggling with serious issues before you berate them.

Comes off as a pleasant and understanding person but your first conversation with him outside of class will make you change your mind immediately. He's so incredibly condescending and rude when you ask questions in office hours and doesn't actually care about helping you -- instead he just belittles. The TAs were the only redeemable part of him.

This was my first time really working with R, and Dr. D made it super approachable. Everything we did on a "major" grade assignment (hw or project) came straight from an in-class assignment or demo that we had access to. Very easy to do well if you take the time to pay attention to the coding. I thought the class was fun, and Dr. D is a good prof.

I love Dr. D and this class! I learned so much (you learn R) & he was really helpful with feedback & responding to emails & discussion posts. There's a semester-long final project, many coding assignments, demos, and in-class exercises. It's a lot but if you pay attention to his (sometimes boring) lectures and do everything on time you'll get an A.

analysis.name: Desiree Griffin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 139 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: All of this class is is group work, which is horrible because a lot of the group members don't do the work and you get penalized for it through your grades. Get a good group for the final project because I  had to end up doing primarily by myself. She's nice but I swear half the time she doesn't actually know the facts she just speaks like she does

She wants really specific and strong evidence for each case study. While that is not unreasonable, she sort of gives off the impression that there is only one right answer and grades harshly based on that. She expects extremely clear and detailed work while her questions in themselves are vague and feel like they're up to interpretation.

The class was great until the final. She introduced a new oral exam that was poorly structured. We had 4 minutes for 3 questions, but my interviewer, Professor Griffin, asked harder, extra, and off-guide questions that were completely unrelated to my client. Other students with TAs had simpler ones. It felt unfair and biased.

Dr. Griffin was an amazing professor. The grading for the case studies are a little strict, but as long as you are extremely detailed in your responses you will do well. Dr. Griffin is super understanding and goes above and beyond to support her students inside and outside of the classroom.

Go to class! Lots of points from the exit tickets and group activities. The semester-long project was cool. I like how she focused on applying the content rather than testing. I learn a lot from her classes! Only downside was the final was oral, and was graded kinda harshly imo.

analysis.name: Dharini  Bathia
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I don't have any issue with heavy accents but on top of that her PowerPoints don't outline anything. They have just questions without answers, and you have to try to decipher what she is saying with no visual aid. I am a visual learner, and not having the notes in writing on the PowerPoints in class made this class pretty much impossible.

Worst professor I've had. The class is easy, but she is very rude to students. Interrupted student presentations and was passive aggressive when the class expressed concerns about an unfair exam. You can do just fine in the class, but if there are other options for 581, I would absolutely avoid her. She's new to teaching so hopefully she improves.

Worst class I've taken in PLCY dept. Completely unclear grading criteria, awful instructions: 1 Q on midterm was only answered correctly by 1 person in the whole class and she said she "taught it well enough." Very rude, does not treat students with respect. Sure, I did learn something useful, but the environment was not supportive whatsoever.

Worst class i have ever taken at UNC., This woman single-handedly made me hate Information Science. INLS 201 was a nitpicky, terrible and useless course, She refuses to accommodate students, and seems to pride herself all the time. DO NOT TAKE!!!!

This class was only difficult because of the professor. Toni just speaks at you in class with language complexity that many students can't understand. She is chill but her class drags on and is just to get the requirement done. Toni is a great and accommodating person, and cares for the wellbeing of us as students.  English 105i in the social sciences wasn't the most interesting for me as a STEM major, but Toni's class is very easy to follow along with regardless of your major.  I highly recommend!!

If you have to take ENGL-105, take it with Toni!

analysis.name: Diego Riveros-Iregui
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 49 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class was so unbearable. Everybody was taking this as either a focus capacity or to fulfill their data science minor. They wanted us to be so dedicated to the topic so bad but no one cared. Such a boring class and attendance matters. Started picking on me for no reason towards the end of the semester in a 200 person class. Don't recommend.

Honestly I dreaded going to this class. Professor was passive agressive and randomly called on us. The lectures were a bit boring to me. Definitely requires some studying for the exams as the material is pretty dense, but making a good grade in the class overall isn't too difficult. Most exams were very similar to the practice ones he posted.

Tons of material, but his energy and lively teaching make it manageable. He's one of two instructors, and he clearly loves what he teaches. Great engaging instructor

Dr. Riveros-Iregui is so friendly and a very engaging professor. You can tell he wants his students to succeed in class and he'd specify on slides where they would be important in an exam. He gets upset when students don't focus in class or are distracted on their devices, and you get more out of class when you pay attention in lectures.

Seems like a chill guy, but lots of condescending comments. Blamed wifi. Expect you to devote your life to geography in a 100 level class for data science majors. THE WORLD DOESNT REVOLVE AROUND GEOGRAPHY. Expect you to come to class having done the readings but not doing that. So i just didn't go a lot of times. easy class though

analysis.name: Daniel DiSalvo
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining

Essentially, you read historical documents and take notes (not graded) outside of class and then spend the whole time in class discussing them.

Amazing professor! You can tell he really cares about his students and is willing to accommodate. The class is very discussion based but if you don't feel comfortable speaking up in class he gives multiple opportunities to get those points. He also gives multiple extra credit opportunities and helps students prepare for exams!

Dr. DiSalvo is a super cool guy and really knows American history and judicial history. Very informative class but could be a little dry in lectures. He clearly cared about his students and was easy to talk to and ask questions.

analysis.name: Duane Deardorff
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 92 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I think Dr. Deardorff is a lovely person, and he seems very sweet outside of the context of PHYS-114. He is very condescending and snappy in lecture, and is not the most effective at teaching the material. Most of his class is self-taught with the help of TA office hours because the TAs seem very sympathetic about how the class is run.

The exams are graded well (lots partial), so it is possible to get an A. However, Deardorf is one of the most condescending and rude professors I have ever had. Would not be kind to students when they answered incorrectly in class. When 9% of the class got a question right on an exam he told us we needed to study more...

duane would be a great professional juggler. he is not a good professional professor. extremely condenscending in both emails and lectures and manages to make simple concepts confusing. had a different lecturer for two months and the class did better than previous semesters on the second exam.

Avoid the scale up classes for your own good.  Basically nothing is taught in these classes and you are responsible for not only teaching yourself all of the material outside of class, but also a maddening amount of short and long lab reports and homework assignments.  Class attendance is mandatory for some reason, despite being completely useless.

He does not seem to care for our success. We do much of the learning ourselves so he is essentially the placeholder that contributes relatively little to our understanding. The actual learning is done during the 3-hour lab sessions. Would not recommend the class but there is a very limited selection of instructors here who teach this, so no choice.

analysis.name: Martina Di Francesco
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I have taken Martina for ITAL 101, 102, and 204 because she is THAT amazing. She is a caring instructor and makes class so much fun. She is so funny and really cares about you succeeding in the class. She is always making sure we are comfortable with the material and comfortable in her class. Can't recommend her more!
Martina is my favorite UNC professor. I changed my schedule to take ITAL 204 with her because she's that great. I learned so much from her and loved her class!! I can't recommend her enough!!

Martina is amazing and definitely one of the best professors you could get for any italian classes. The course is set up the same as 101 and 102 with homeworks due before each class, 4 tests, a small group project before each test, and two very easy quizzes in each unit. Would definitely recommend Martina to anyone taking italian!
She is so sweet! Never judgmental of your ability level & meets you where you are. If I could I would have taken her for all 3 levels.

Martina made learning a new language enjoyable and easy! I took 101 as a gen-ed but am seriously considering an Italian minor after taking her class. She goes out of her way to help comprehension and uses hilarious real world examples. Take Italian with Martina!!

analysis.name: Jennifer Diliberto

The best teacher!! So kind and caring! Class was fun and engaging, and I learned SO much. Not hard to get an A. She is so knowledgeable on the topics and wants to talk to you about them! Sweetest Professor ever! She clearly wants all of us to learn and gives encouraging, constructive feedback. This async class was very reasonable and very interesting. Dr. Diliberto is so sweet and cares about her students! She was good about asking for feedback twice throughout the semester to see what she should change. Lots of fun group discussions but never forced to participate in front of the whole class. She encourages you to think outside of the box but sometimes can be vague, but easy grader regardless.

analysis.name: Peter Doyle

Definitely have to teach yourself all the coding and video editing too.

You have to teach yourself, but he records everything and will try to answer questions in class.

Professor Doyle is very approachable and knows his material very well! Some of the material (especially HTML) is hard, but Professor Doyle is happy to give you help if you need it. Take MEJO-121 with him!

analysis.name: Doug MacLean

Amazing professor. Very kind, reliable, understanding, and smart.

GO TO CLASS even though he doesn't take attendance and you'll do fine.

Dr. MacLean has amazing organized lectures that completely cover the required readings for class. Grading is tough simply because he makes sure the average grade is a B-, but work hard with TAs on your papers and you'll do great.

analysis.name: Douglas Smit

review_highlights.comment: He basically never replied to student's emails. Important documents concerning students are not ignored by him at all. This is the most irresponsible professor I have ever met at UNC.

Professor Smit was my favorite professor this semester. He is funny and enjoyable to listen to. He relates hard-to-comprehend topics to simpler concepts in a way that's engaging and fun. He knows what he is talking about.

I noticed inconsistent grading between recitation sections. Additionally, communication could be improved, as emails often went unanswered and lectures sometimes felt difficult to stay engaged with.

Best first-year seminar, Archeology and Pop Culture. Watch movies and read articles each week on which you write an easy 200-word discussion post; some are optional. There's a group project you will present and a final paper; with effort, you will likely receive an A. Participation is encouraged but not required. Extra credit possibilities.

Smit is a great professor! Lectures were very interesting and fun! Important to attend because not a lot of info online. This is a super easy gen ed. 2 tests for the 1st and 2nd half of content and some reflections. Tests are easy if u take good notes and look at the study guide. I didnt do any readings and the tests were still easy.

analysis.name: Dongwha Shin

I could not recommend him enough.

Sweet professor who cares about his students. Only a couple of homework assignments throughout the semester that you can do in groups. Exams are heavily weighted but he curves a ton. Manageable if you can do practice problems and in-lecture practice. Confused by low ratings, he is such a nice guy who wants everyone in his classes to do well!

He is a nice guy but has no backbone. He made the exams but didn't grade anything (all grading done by his poor TA), so it took forever to get stuff back. Cheating was rampant on the final exam. You can tell he wants his students to like him, but he is an inefficient lecturer and bad with technology. He does allow cheat sheets and curves heavily.

Professor is sweet but if you want to deeply learn the material consider other instructor. Class is focused on applying concepts instead of learning equations, but if you want to take more advanced courses you need both.

I loved Professor Shin. Busi 408 is a challenging class, especially for me with no prior finance knowledge, but he made information digestible and less intimidating. Homework is group-based and there's lots of practice for midterm and final. Such a nice guy who obviously cares so much about the subject and his students.

analysis.name: Doria El Kerdany

review_highlights.comment: Took Arab 407 with Prof. Doria and currently in Arab 408. The topics are interesting and the class is easy. She's very caring and lenient but gives a lot of work. Doria means well, but it's hard to do well in her class. She constantly talks about how she's sad students are stressed, but grades on unclear guidelines & doesn't teach grammar. I did corrections AND extra credit, and she told me she wouldn't give me the points back because I already had a "good enough" grade. I wish someone else was teaching 204.

Professor Doria is the sweetest person. She gives a good amount of homework that is crucial to learning the material, so it is for good cause. She is very lenient with due dates if you speak with her about it and she is not at all a tough grader. If you want to learn Arabic and are excited about doing so, you should have no trouble in her class.

I really enjoyed my time with Prof. El Kerdany. She is very patient with her students and gives a lot of feedback on hw assignments for you to improve on. Participation in class is rly important to understanding the language and the rules associated with it. She also introduces you to Arab culture around the middle east which is really interesting.

analysis.name: Donald Reid
