He adapted the pacing of the class based on student feedback and gave students sufficient opportunities to ask questions and connect in office hours. Pay attention to lectures and do the practice exams, and you will know everything you need.

Having had difficulty in math my entire college career, andrew was by far the most impactful professor I've had in this field. He cares a lot and provides plenty of outside help to allow his students to succeed. He's a lil goofy but a great explainer. DO THE HANDOUTS AND PRACTICE EXAMS FROM OFFICE HOURS!!!!!!!

The first test was hard, but after we gave feedback he totally adapted his lectures for us. Even though this was a lecture based class he went above and beyond to make weekly lecture notes, problem sets, and practice exams. Overall, couldn't ask for a more dedicated and flexible teacher who wants students to succeed without handing it to them.

analysis.name: Andrew Turner
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures can be boring, but overall it is a chill class with interesting content and teacher. What started off as a filler class eventually became a fav. He doesn't grade harshly, and focuses more on conceptualization than gpa. He said before the final. “I'm not here to tank your gpa.” Not much work outside of the classroom, few assignments.

Prof Turner was a great, he was understanding and didn't mind absences (don't abuse this). He graded papers for completion and the 'term paper' on accuracy. His exams aren't bad but you must memorize a lot (took me 2-3 hr w/flashcards). I rec if you have a busy schedule bc he has no homework, but exams are weighed heavily but graded forgivingly.

Prof Turner is very knowledgeable and passionate about his work and that shows in his lectures. The content is quite interesting, but the lectures themselves can drag on and feel boring at times. Final grade is determined by 3 assignments and 2 exams which kind of sucks, but he is a pretty forgiving grader.

Pretty vague on what my grade was until it was finalized, but a chill dude who is clearly very passionate and respected in his field. Very niche topics but you don't have to memorize as much as other ARTH electives I've taken (only like 20-30 things per exam) and attendance didn't matter.

analysis.name: Andrew Boysen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: While some do say his voice is a little monotone, he's clearly passionate about the subject and really cares. He revamped the curriculum this semester a lot to make it more accessible and interesting to students, and his willingness to change and tinker stuff shows he's super caring of students. Exams are open note and online, albeit a little hard.

Prof. Boysen is clearly very knowledgable about the world of corporate strategy. I really enjoyed the assigned cases and the in-class exercises - they really helped me grasp the course concepts. Prof. Boysen was also always willing to meet with students (even outside of his scheduled office hours). He has been one of my favorite proffesors at KF!

Professor Boysen is a kind and caring person who repeatedly emphasizes we prioritize our mental health before all else. His attendance policy is relaxed, and he is encouraging of us to schedule office hours for extra help. Reading-heavy with lots of cases and a discussion-based class. I enjoy his sense of dry humor. He loves his daughter! )

I think 412 is overall j a boring class in general. But prof boysen is very respectful and knowledgeable in this field of study. He is also SOOO kind and often would bring small treats and gifts to class (which honestly makes my day)! Overall, choose a good project group, and you'll be fine
Professor Boysen was one of the kindest professors ever. He makes the class super manageable and I would 100% take another class with him. Definitely take him for BUSI 412!

analysis.name: Dr. David Dooling
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very funny, respectful, and intelligent. His lectures were really interesting, engaging (many people participated), and he used a lot of cool media as examples (music videos, artifacts, literally like Little Women and SpongeBob too). Gives good feedback and grades well if you try. Class became kinda optional towards the end. Fav prof at unc so far

Dr. Dooling has been one of the best professors that I have had. The class has reading checks every week which were pretty easy and 3 papers. There were no tests and if you ask for feedback before assignments are due he will give you it.
Dr. D is awesome! The class is easy if you do the readings and go to lecture. The essays/writing assignments are chill and have clear instructions. The TA's were very nice!

Loved taking 325 with him! He is very down-to-earth and always makes the content fun/engaging. Lot's of group collaboration, so prepare to talk. Class is so much better when you do the readings, btw. They aren't just busy work. Exams are open-note/textbook, but not too easy. Very relevant content!

If you can take any insightful and phenomenal class at UNC, take Comm 224 with Dr. Dooling. He is amazing, hilarious, caring, etc! The class is genuinely enjoyable and incredibly thought-provoking. Dr. Dooling is a fair grader but expects passion and effort. Take this class or any of his classes!

analysis.name: Andrew Yates
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 74 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Gives you a 20-question bank w/ answers for the test, and expects you to get 116/120 between midterm and final for an A. This makes the tests a complete joke (tip: don't just memorize the answers), but also forces you to study for the specific questions instead of reviewing actual class content, leaving you poorly prepared for future ECON courses.

Difficult to get an A but not hard to get above a B. Lectures were not helpful in doing the homeworks, which ended up being 80% of the coursework (there is a homework question on both exams). Overall, just not a great course to learn in and had to teach myself how to work out most of the homeworks/exams. Very passable class.

Prof. Yates is a good man but his quality of teaching is not. He moves quickly and his notes follow no sort of rigid structure which makes transcribing them onto your own paper extremely difficult. Handwriting is atrocious. By the time you figure out that he was writing a 'q' for quantity instead of the number '9' he has moved on to the next topic.

Very lecture-heavy with no posted slides or notes, so attendance is important. Grading is based only on homework and exams. six homework assignments and two exams. The exams closely reflected the study guide, and one homework-style problem appeared on the exam. Grading is done in blocks, so small point differences can affect final letter grades.

Very caring and funny guy, but wow this class is hard. Not a lot of materials besides lectures, textbook is not really used outside of recitations. If you prefer a more structured class, take MSA. Hard to get A-/A, but also hard to fail with how tests are graded. Definitely use the ULAs/econaid, but expect to teach yourself a lot outside of class.

analysis.name: Carlina Duan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Duan is amazing, I had no poetry experience before and she had such a welcoming class for all levels. You do have to go to class and attend all workshops, there is no test/exam and the final was reading our completed poems and she brought drinks and food. I recommend this class to everyone I know!
Professor Duan is very accessible but was not the most understanding. Assigns a LOT of work, one of my heaviest workloads I have ever had at UNC, and a lot of it is not productive work.

Incredible! absolutely amazing professor who cares about every individual student. I feel like my writing improved so much over the course of the semester. This class was never a source of stress, but you can get so much out of it because of the poetry workshops, and Carlina's constructive comments on every poem you write.
Professor Duan is an angel on earth, truly. She is incredible, caring, and kind, and fosters the safest space. Her knowledge is vast and her acceptance is unwavering.

analysis.name: Marco Duarte
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Duarte was an extremely caring and passionate professor. I found him funny and tried to make a boring class more interesting through real world examples. With that said, the class is very difficult. I could not follow along in lectures easily and it took me time outside of class to grasp the topics. Tests are very hard, but have big curve

Arbitrary grader. The topics are interesting, but he speedruns through them, and lectures have little to do with his horribly difficult math-heavy exams. Gets easily frustrated and mad when the class doesn't understand his teaching methods. I threw up one question into midterm 2, and he wouldn't let me retake it. Don't take this course, trust me!!

Class is insanely hard. That being said Marco works with you to ensure you don't fail. He has numerous extra credit opportunities, hw is graded for completion, and exams are curved extensively (30=C, 40=B, etc.). While this class is not by any means a guarranteed A I found it easy to obtain a B with pretty average effort. Just go to class.

This class will have super challenging midterms where you just speedrun solve everything you know, but the curve will SAVE YOU from getting below a B unless you skip class/put in 0 effort. Legit got a 14 on a midterm curved to C- LOL. Content is super interesting, pricing strategy/game theory, you actually learn something meaningful in this class.

I would avoid this at all costs unless you have to have it for credit. As far as a general 400 level econ elective this is a horrible choice. Class is ridiculously difficult, averages on exams are in the 40s. 80% of the class is graded on exams. There is curve on exams where a 30 is a C and 60 is an A. Overall just a miserable experience.

analysis.name: Emma Duvall
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Duvall was amazing! My favorite teacher during my first semester, definitely take ENG105 with her. Class was 3 projects, each with drafting assignments that prepare you fully for the final submission. She gave incredible feedback as well! Did not stress at all with this class.

super chill and easy class. Basically everything is completion if u put in a bit of effort. Attendance is not rly required either, she's pretty lenient with missing class as long as u email her beforehand, and it won't even affect ur grade. TAKE THIS PROF FOR ENGLISH

Emma made a class I thought I would hate one of my most enjoyable. She genuinely cares about all of the people in her classes. There are no exams, just 2-3 feeder assignments and a culminating project in each of the 3 units. She gives clear rubrics and feedback to help each student thrive in the course. If she teaches another section, take it.

Genuinely such an amazing professor and person. Class was not hard at all, and she made it clear she didn't want this class to be a stressor. Class consisted of some small assignments and 3 projects. Plenty of time was given, and she was very understanding on attendance (probably missed 5/6 classes from sickness). Great professor!

Emma is an amazing professor! She is extremely caring and kind, and absolutely wants the best for her students. The assignments are very straightforward, and she is an understanding grader. I loved this class. If you are able take ENGL 105 with Emma, do it!

analysis.name: Joaquin Drut
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great professor, really cares about his students and their learning. Willing to go the extra mile to make sure his students get the most out of his classes, and genuinely cares. Amazing professor, and would take again!

Was able to effectively dumb down physics concepts for freshmen in a humanities class. Lectures were occasionally excellent, sometimes okay. Not his fault imo but overall the class is horrible. Think of a bad attribute a class could have and it probably has it. I would rather rip off each of my toe nails one by one than take this class again.
Very approachable and willing to talk to you about the class and your problems. If you have trouble understanding something he will be able to help you.

Lectures are in-depth and engaging. Homework is a huge portion of your grade, so do not procrastinate doing it. Paying attention in lecture is important because the posted slides do not have the same level of depth or insight that you will need to do well on the final. Group project is quite a bit of work too, just make sure to start on time.

Dr. Drut was a fantastic professor. I've heard some people didn't enjoy his teaching style for PHYS 115, but for Numerical II I couldn't disagree more. He is genuinely the best physics professor I've had here at UNC by a wide margin. He's a clear lecturer and realistic about what we will and won't need in our careers, and encourages questions.

analysis.name: Dustin Sebell
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Some of the topics were interesting but I feel like half the time the class was sidetracked so bad by some random kid saying something so irreverent. And then Sebell entertains it and before you know it the class is over and you're sitting there wondering what you even learned. The levels of disorganization in this class should be studied in a lab.

Really interesting class. Attendance is mandatory but as long as you show up and do the readings it's an easy A. Pop quizzes here and there but short and not difficult. Participation encouraged but not required. 1 midterm, 2 papers, 1 final. Nice professor and fun class as long as you complete the readings and put some effort into the essays!

Really enjoyed this class, favorite of the semester. I found Prof. Sebell's discussions engaging, even if they often trailed off a bit or lagged behind the readings. Don't take if you don't want to read or don't like engaging in in-class discussions. I found what brought me success was just staying engaged in class & actively participating.

This class wasn't awful but it was just so boring. Every day in class it was just us listening to him talk about the dense reading we were assigned. There are random pop quizzes throughout the semester. I just wish the class was more organized as the syllabus is a joke for staying on track. There were times Sebell didn't even know when break was

Not a bad professor, just a boring class. But I am also not interested in the class topic at all. Beware of pop quizzes because lots of reading, and class consist one 1 exam, 2 papers, and a final. A reasonable grader, and easy to reach out to. I would recommend this class if you are interested in philosophy, but if not, I wouldn't take it.

analysis.name: Matthew Duncan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 20 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Minimal work outside of class and easy to get an A. He's also very caring for his students and offers lots of flexibility. English isn't always the most fun class, but he finds ways to make it engaging. He is very thorough with instruction and gives feeders leading up to the projects, which makes it so projects don't burden us with work to do.

Professor Duncan is a great professor. Just do the work (which is minimal and not difficult at all), participate, and you'll easily get an A. He does take attendance, but communicate with him and he's super understanding, and class was often asynchronous. I will say he is a tad bit strict, but overall, great instructor.

Prof. Duncan makes taking eng 105 more bearable. He gives you time in class to work on assignments so that you do not have homework. He also is very understanding if you cannot make it to class or have a question about one of the assignments. Each assignment can be resubmitted to get back points. I recommend!!

Professor Duncan was great! He gives great feedback and wants you to do well in the class. He is willing to work with you and is incredibly helpful, just make sure you actually go to class. I took this class as a major requirement but I really enjoyed it.

While Prof. Duncan can be a little serious and the class isn't super exciting, it is exactly what I needed as a first-year requirement. We had no homework and time in class to work on assignments. You will get an automatic A if you show up to class and turn in your assignments on time. You get to do a mock interview, which is super helpful.

analysis.name: Scott Duxbury
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Duxbury is incredibly kind and makes the homework very straightforward. I came in with no coding experience, and he makes everything doable. He's passionate, always willing to help, and his office hours are amazing. Plus, there's a ton of extra credit available.

i think you'd have to try to do bad in this class. Scott is a great prof - v caring, accessible, knowledgable, gives great feedback. i loved this class; it was genuinely interesting, and learned a lot w/out ever being stressed abt it. no exams, just reading quizzes (open note) and ~5 hw and a final project - all v doable w/out R/coding experience

Prof. Duxbury is such an amazing human being and lecturer. He's clearly knowledgeable and enjoys teaching. He introduced me to data science and motivated to pursue it as a major. Overall, take this class with him if you can! :)

Scott was an amazing professor. If you had any problems he was always available and throughout the course of the semester we would slowly chip away at our final. He gives great feedback and makes all the hw/quizzes very manageable. If you show up and do the work you will do fantastic. Highly recommend
Probably my favorite professor I've ever had at UNC. The class was a super easy A as well, definitely recommend!

analysis.name: Dwight Tanner
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dwight is literally the coolest professor I've ever had. He's super chill, very caring, and all around a pretty cool guy. The class required a lot of books, but they all were pretty good, and as long as you didn't procrastinate till the last day it's really doable. Definitely my favorite professor, would highly recommend taking one of his courses!
Taking ENGL 105 was relatively stress-free. There aren't too many assignments and gives good and fair feedback. If you are relatively good at writing, getting an A/A- isn't too hard.

I have him at Appalachian State University, and he has been awesome! He is very hip and relatable unlike a lot of other professors, and he is very caring about his students and their capability. When I had COVID, he was the best at reaching out to me outside of class and I really appreciated it. He is very inspiring and makes writing interesting.

Dwight is young and hip, and he is able to convey stuff in an exciting and engaging way. He is always funny and relaxed, totally approachable, and most importantly, he gave great feedback on writing assignments. There wasn't that much work and everything we did do was really interesting and allowed for a lot of creativity. 10/10 would recommend

Tanners a great guy, and really cares about helping you learn how to be a better writer. By far my best class last semester, if you can take him you should. show up to class, and when he assigns a reading you do it, because he will talk about it in class and youll feel stupid. Gives great feedback on papers, just make sure you do them on time.

analysis.name: Walter Bo Eberle
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Class consisted of discussions that he never offered feedback. Posts by students in the forum asking questions went unanswered, students also said emails went unanswered. Going into the final only the first discussion had been graded, nothing else.

Class consists of 1 weekly discussion post, a midterm, and a final paper. Super easy and he grades well, but hard to access outside of class especially since this class was asynchronous. Great TA though!
Bo rules. That is all. I only feel bad for him having to guide recitations where no one did the reading.

analysis.name: Parasara Duggirala
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This class is so tough -- I can't imagine how it's possible to succeed in his class. Not many people show up to his lectures because his slides are useless, so you should do a lot of self-studying. His exams are so tough that I can't even finish answering all questions on time. In general, I'm having horrible experience with this class.

This class made me think of self-harm at least thrice. As a student with perfect attendance, the discrepancy in difficulty between his lectures and homework is genuinely unfathomable. Staring into his homework is like staring into the abyss - try to comprehend it and you'll go insane. Don't do this to yourself. Take this class with someone else.

Don't take 455 with him. He makes the class unnecessarily difficult. Other sections with different profs had easier time with this course. Duggirala's 455 is illegally hard. One of friends even attempted s…. while taking this class.

While he is clearly very knowledgeable about the topics, he is not a good professor. Midterms and exams are more like IQ tests rather than testing to see if you actually learned something, and they are way too long. He has messy handwriting and lectures are completely useless. HW's take forever to complete and don't really help with understanding.

Just a bad professor. Not tough, not strict, just bad. He's clearly a genius in his field, but teaching is not his strong suit. Hardly elaborates on topics, interrupts students' questions, gives little to no explanation on practice midterm solutions (just writes "trivial" or tells us to read the textbook). Curve is legendary, but 455 is still hell.

analysis.name: Patrick Eberlein
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Wow you need to get this guy. He is fantastic. I really pity the other folks in the other classes because they do not get the opportunity to experience the greatness of Pat Eberlein. I have never been happier with a professor/ teacher in my life. Fair homework, fair tests, useful lectures. He also is a funny and kind character as well.

Far and away my best professor. Really helpful whenever you ask. He really teaches the class well and his tests aren't too hard. He tells you that what is on the test is all in the homework. He's being completely honest. If you study the homework, you'll be all set for the test.

I loved having Professor Eberlein. His lectures are easy to follow, and he is so knowledgeable on the subject. I would highly, highly recommend him. Also had him for Math 233, which we was great for as well.
Very helpful teacher. Knows the material well and gives clear explanations. The difficulty in his class has more to do with the material than any deficiency in his teaching style.
Great professor! Super willing to help out on homework (which you will probably need)

analysis.name: Angela East
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Kind and approachable person who is accessible, definitely take advantage of that; class was WAY harder than it should have been. Lectures: extremely hard to follow, and it often felt like she didn't know how to teach the material. The content taught barely matched the midterms, if it weren't for the practice exams I would have failed the class.

Ms. East was very sweet. She genuinely cares for the success of her students. However, I feel like her teaching style was not the best, as lessons were not always taught in a clear manner. I feel concepts could have been explained better in a simpler way; it sometimes would feel overly complicated. Her practice exams were very helpful!

Extremely inexperienced when it comes to teaching. She grades very harsh and unfair, will take off multiple points for small mistakes. She does not allow you to discuss any exam grades with her. She has terrible handwriting, making lectures difficult to understand. Does not take anything serious, she found it funny that her class average was 70%.

Felt significantly underprepared. She was accessible outside of class, but was always behind on lectures with rushed complex content! A nice person, but this class was extremely difficult. Still inexperienced. Appreciated how she supported the class. Caution taking this class though. Take the good and bad ratings with a grain of salt.

Prof East is one of the most caring professors I've ever had, she teaches really well, she is mostly organised and super adaptable. If you're gonna take 110, take it with her, she actually understands what it's like to be a student and she's flexible, considerate and has the best dad jokes. She's such a sweetie

analysis.name: Elaina Eakle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Enjoyed taking this class and it was easy. Not too many assignments. not a very harsh grader. she is very nice and cares about what she teaches. Movies watched were interesting and we'd have to complete a discussion post/group discussion about 2 films and write 1 tv show review. Exams were multiple choice and one short answer question.

I loved this class and Elaina was a great instructor! She genuinely cares about her students and encourages prioritizing your health over class. That being said you have to at least act like you care and go sometimes to get participation credit. The class was super interesting and looked at gender and sexuality in the context of current events!

Honestly all of her ratings are hyping her up but I didn't like her that much. The papers and tests were annoying and kinda hard in my opinion. You definitely have to try if you want an A she doesn't just hand them out. And just in general her vibe is kinda strange, monotone voice, and just seems like she would much rather be doing anything else.

It's not letting me select the correct class, but I took Comm 325 with Elaina. She is so sweet and also an extremely lenient grader, gladly grants extensions, and will do everything in her power to accommodate your needs if you just communicate. Lectures and exams are straightforward.

Elaina is amazing! For those taking her class virtually, she provides a textbook but her videos are great. Her tests are open note and easy A's (no time limit!). She gave me lots of feedback and met extra with me for our course paper (20%). She is super kind and really cares about her students. I would be ecstatic taking another course with her.

analysis.name: Connie Eble
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 38 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Eble was fine in the history portion of this class, but the difficulty of the class shot up when we reached old English. She expects you to know all about the grammar, but she doesn't explain it well at all. If you've had any old English before you'll probably be fine, if not, good luck. She's a tough grader, and not always clear in criteria.

I had Ms. Eble along with her colleague Ms. Brown for the freshman seminar "Interpreting the South from Manuscripts." Ms. Eble is a hard grader, but she will make your writing so much better. The class itself I found to be very interesting as it is completely discussion and raw-reading based.  My favorite class of the semester!

This is my second class with Eble and I'm enjoying it even more than the last. She's willing to work with you--if you have a problem, she'll show you grace! She's a lot of fun and extremely knowledgeable in her field. Plus, the classes she teaches are always very interesting.

she tends to over explain things, which makes her class pretty boring, but you hear the same thing so many times you won't need to study much at home. she is very knowledgeable and not strict with grades. she is very strict on attendance though

She was very boring.  One day it snowed and many students were missing.  She proceeded to take out the dictionary and for 1 1/2 hours, read words from the dictionary and talked about their origins.  A complete waste of my time!

analysis.name: Teacher Earl
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sends great pics in his emails!!! super entertaining guy..... the D he gave me turned into an A by doing super easy extra credit! he's so understanding and not as hard as you would think

Prof. Teacher Earl has a strange grading policy that saw me get a B- even tho I specifically requested a B+ at the beginning of the semester. I am not a smart boy, so the B- was fair. Great guy over all, and the only time I hated his class was when we had a substitute for the week

in love with every cell of his being. i wish I could take every class of his. thinking about applying to grad school at unc just so I can continue to see him. cannot recommend him enough! take a class with him, you will not regret it!

Teacher Earl truly got me out of my depressive episode. He brought so much light to my life, changed my whole view on the world through sociology. He is a beautiful person, not just inside, but on the outside too. <3 ;)
Teacher Earl loves to perform silly social experiments during class. Some of these include watching Hillybillies and the Crippled Camp. Interesting films with disturbing images.

analysis.name: Tyler Easterbrook
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tough quizzes! BUT, he grades projects leniently. The projects are fun too; do well on them (and talk every now and then in class) to get at least an A-. Tyler himself is interesting and fun to talk to. He made it a point to meet w/ every student before every project, which ends up being really helpful and says a lot about him!

Easterbrook was a great teacher. Effort is a huge thing for him. If you work hard, you will get a good grade even if you didn't do everything perfect. His lectures were really interesting and applicable to life. There were only like 4 projects and some reading quizzes. Very chill.
I loved Tyler's class! He was the most engaging instructor/professor I had this semester tbh. The class was mostly project-based and he was very willing to work with us with deadlines.

analysis.name: Megan Eagen
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Megan is a wonderful person. I had no experience or even much interest in Baroque Opera, but she made the topic and the class extremely interesting and engaging. She's extremely caring, and if she sees that you give a good effort, you will be rewarded. She helped me tremendously in office hours this semester and was really a fantastic professor.

Dr. Megan Eagen-Jones is an excellent professor. This was her first class in a large lecture hall, and she managed to keep things engaging. Her lectures are interesting, and she does a good job of highlighting the main points that she tests on. She genuinely cares about her students and offers really in depth feedback on the papers she grades.

I've never written one of these before but this teacher was so phenomenal I had to.  Megan is a fantastic proffesor who really knows her stuff.  She isn't out to trick you on the tests and gives very helpful quizzes.  If you give her a little effort anyone can get an easy A here.

There are pop quizzes, but they're not hard. Homework once a week. Best to do the readings (they're not long), but she goes over what you need to know in class. Really chill class, good pacing, ample opportunities for participation. She's really understanding. 10/10 recommend!

One of the best professors I've had at UNC. Her passion and interest in the material is clear, and that translates to clear, engaging lectures that touch on really interesting material. Approachable, friendly, and fair, she really does care about helping you succeed no matter your circumstances. If you have the choice, definitely take 255 with her.
